reviews.title: Cannot attach peripherals that require power and use both USB ports
reviews.body: I bought this hub so I could connect both an HDMI cord (to my tv) and various USB-A peripherals to my MacBook Pro. I originally only used two ports. One for my HDMI cable and one for my Bluetooth keyboard/mouse. For weeks this worked perfectly and I was completely satisfied. However, when I needed to also hook up a CD player to the other USB-A port, the hub couldn’t handle it. While my music did play, suddenly my mouse and keyboard had horrible lag. Not just a little slowdown, but seconds between hitting a key and it showing up on screen. It frequently even failed to register keystrokes and mouse movements. I checked everything. I changed batteries. I turned off Bluetooth, disconnected the keyboard/mouse device, got both going again. I switched the CD player and keyboard/mouse’s ports. I moved the CD player a foot away from the hub, to make sure it wasn’t interfering with Bluetooth reception. Nothing improved. I even took the (ridiculous) step of checking my CPU usage, just in case — it was well under 10%. Nothing I did caused the lag to go away. Except when I disconnected the disc player from the hub. As soon as that second USB-A port wasn’t in use, my mouse and keyboard worked fine. Given that I was only using three of the ports on this multi-port hub, one that promotes its amazing data transfer capabilities, well, not being able to handle sending video to a tv, receiving Bluetooth data from a mouse and keyboard, and playing a cd all at the same time is a complete fail. I later tried again when I wanted to connect a backup drive to the port. The problem repeated identically. At that point I wasn’t even using the drive yet. Simply connecting it was enough to disrupt the data from my wireless keyboard and mouse from functioning. Both the CD player and disc drive require power from the computer. They don’t plug into a power outlet. Apparently the hub can’t handle these kind of peripherals well. So I’m returning it and trying again to find a different option. I’ve always preferred to buy Anker because I trust them, so this is a real disappointment. Would I spend $35 again on a hub that can't do what it advertises? No. Would I recommend it to anyone else? No.

reviews.title: WARNING: Works well except for Mouse Dongle
reviews.body: I recently bought a second of these Anker 341 hub. First one I bought years ago and it is awesome: Been using it when travelling without any issues. I bought a second one as a permanent install for a device at home, and immediately had issues (like many others on reddit apparently) that the 2.4 GHz mouse dongle does not work (mouse needs to be within a foot of the hub). Anker customer service eventually admitted that there is "an interference between the USB3 ports and the 2.4 GHz frequency", but they did not offer a solution, and suggested that I return the hub. The solution I found online is to buy a short USB cable extension so that the dongle is away from the hub, and voila: the range of my mouse went from 1 ft to the expected 10+ feet. Clearly something changed in their design (old one still works great), and frankly that interference issue is not acceptable (deduct one star). And deduct one star for customer service not suggesting the cable extension. I am keeping mine as it fits for my usage scenario though, and I like the price, size and shape.

reviews.title: Solid Piece of Kit
reviews.body: This is a well-made, solid piece of kit. It’s a bit bigger than some of the competition, so less ideal for travel. But the longer braided cable with metal housing for the plug, and the aluminum body, makes for a device I imagine would hold up to years of use. I thought a lot about keeping it. Unlike many of the alternative hubs in this very affordable price range, it has 3 USB-C ports, 1 dedicated to power and the other 2 for data. I liked too that there was a physical button to turn the HDMI connection to a monitor on/off. That was particularly unique, and also something I didn't see elsewhere. It connected without issue to my 2026 MacBook Air 15" and remained fairly cool to the touch during my brief testing for direct Ethernet transfers between the laptops.

reviews.title: Excellent USB-C hub for my MacBook Air M3
reviews.body: I’m very happy with the UGREEN Revodok Pro 9 in 1 USB-C Hub. The packaging is very well done and gives a great first impression right out of the box. The hub itself feels solid, robust, and well built. I have been using it for about two weeks with my MacBook Air M3, and so far, I have not had any issues. It is truly plug and play: my computer detects all connected peripherals immediately, and everything works as expected. I also tested the display on/off button, and it works correctly. My current setup is the hub connected to my MacBook Air M3 with a 22” LG monitor through HDMI, while I connect a second 29” LG widescreen monitor directly to the laptop using a Thunderbolt cable. With the MacBook lid closed and both external monitors connected, I get: * 2560 x 1080 on the 29” HDR WFHD monitor * 1920 x 1080 on the 22” Full HD monitor One important thing to keep in mind: if you want to use three screens at the same time — two external monitors plus the MacBook screen — this setup will not work because the MacBook Air M3 does not support that configuration in this way. I still need to test the SD card reader and PD charging, but based on my experience so far, this hub has worked perfectly. Overall, great build quality, easy setup, reliable performance, and a very practical accessory for my MacBook. I definitely recommend it.

reviews.title: It Caused a Major Problem For Me
reviews.body: I was hoping to consolidate a couple of older USB hubs using this 9-in-1 USB-C hub. I had previously purchased a UGREEN SATA to USB-C external enclosure, put my working Western Digital 1TB SATA SSD drive into it and used it for over a week on my new laptop with no issues. I then purchased the UGREEN 9-in-1 USB-C hub to provide and extra USB-C port and other port connectivity, shutdown the laptop, replugged everything and the new hub showed up in the USB configuration, but the 1TB drive did not. I removed the drive and put it back into my old laptop which supported multiple disk drives, and got a hard drive detection error. The drive is dead. I did try the USB-A port with an older SATA hard drive and enclosure as well as the micro-card ports on the new hub and they work fine, but it cooked my 1TB SSD drive which would now cost $200 to replace. BTW, I had 38 years in IT and have been working with PCs and laptops since the mid 1980s. This isn't my first tech rodeo. Not happy...

reviews.title: Almost perfect- headset difficulty’s
reviews.body: I’ve been using this Acer USB hub for a few weeks now, and overall I’m really happy with it. I bought it mainly because my laptop doesn’t have enough USB ports for all my schoolwork gear and gaming accessories, and this hub has made things so much easier. Setup and use Right out of the box, it was completely plug-and-play — no software, no setup. I just plugged it into my laptop and started connecting my devices. The size is perfect for portability; I toss it in my backpack when I go between school and home, and it doesn’t take up much space on my desk either. Performance For most of my devices, the hub works flawlessly. My mouse, keyboard, flash drives, and external hard drive all connect instantly and run smoothly. File transfers are quick, and I didn’t notice any lag or drop in performance. The USB 3.0 speeds feel solid, which is great when I’m moving large files for class projects or videos. Build quality It feels well-made for the price — not cheap or flimsy. The cord is thick enough that I’m not worried about it bending or breaking easily, and the ports hold connections snugly. It’s clearly built to handle everyday use. The one issue The only thing keeping this from being a 5-star review is my headset. For some reason, when I plug my USB headset into the hub, it either doesn’t get recognized or the microphone cuts in and out. When I plug it directly into my laptop, it works perfectly fine. It’s not a huge deal since everything else works great, but it’s a bit annoying since I use the headset for both online classes and gaming. From what I can tell, the hub might not deliver enough power or stability for certain audio devices, which isn’t uncommon for smaller, bus-powered hubs like this one. Final thoughts Aside from that minor issue, I’m really happy with this hub. It does exactly what I need — adds a few extra ports, keeps everything connected, and is simple to use. For everyday accessories and school use, it’s a great buy. Just be aware that some more sensitive or high-power devices (like headsets or external hard drives) might work better plugged directly into your computer. Overall rating: 4 out of 5 stars Would I recommend it? Definitely — especially if you just need more USB ports for regular devices and don’t plan on using it for audio or power-hungry gear

reviews.title: Great product, solid build, and fast performance
reviews.body: I’m very happy with this Acer USB Hub. The build quality feels premium and sturdy despite being ultra-slim and lightweight. Data transfer speed is fast, and all four USB ports work smoothly without any lag or disconnections. The 2ft cable length is very convenient and gives enough flexibility for desk setup. title: Anker Laptop Docking Station, 13-in-1 USB C Docking Station, Triple Display

reviews.title: Works Great with Windows and Ubuntu/Linux
reviews.body: I have had no issues running this with my work laptop HP Laptop running Windows 10 and my Dell Inspiron 17 running Ubuntu 20.10/Windows 10. Both laptops charge, and all ports seem to work well. In general, the worst part of the USB-C format is the confusing amount of different laptops that seem to implement it in different ways. Not this product's fault; as I said, it works well with Dell and HP while my HP Laptop dock runs with both laptops, but under Ubuntu or Windows 10 on my Dell, it falls short. The HP Dock is a Thunderbolt dock, and my Dell is a Display port marked with a DP; the DP Port on my Dell does charge and allows all ports to work with this dock. I mention it because USB-C gets confusing, and mileage may vary depending on the laptop itself. My Hp is marked as Thunderbolt, and my Dell as Display Port, and this product runs wonderfully with both. I found I could get a 4k Display using the DP port on the back of the dock in Ubuntu, but I found it a little problem some and instead switched to using the two HDMI ports instead. Sometimes 4k would flicker, but that can be my older KVM Switch (1080P KVM). I don't mind the two 1080p screens as the dock makes it so easy to switch computers. I wonder why the HDMI port only seems to pump out 1080P and the display port 4k from my experience. Still, my HP dock didn't do 4k at all, so this dock outperformed it. I have even booted my Dell and HP Laptops with a live USB of MX Linux, and with no configuration, it worked. I just changed the display settings a bit. So to sum it up. 1) Easy to use - NO Drivers to install! 2) Works across Windows and Linux. 3) Affordable and better than my work HP Thunderbolt dock. 4) Works with USB-C marked PD or Thunderbolt. Finally, I would like to say the PD port can get confusing another port format for USB-C. At first, I thought it did not work as I plugged in USB-C devices, and it was not recognized. Then I upgraded to a new Samsung phone with USB-C PD charging support, and it charged and was recognized from the PD port on the dock. So the device has to support USB-C PD. As I said, USB-C is confusing. Now, what are you waiting for? Buy this best Dock on Amazon; it is excellent for Windows and, more importantly, great with Linux. If you have Thunderbolt, the big thing you get from a Thunderbolt dock is the quicker data transfer speeds, but you need to know your laptop supports it. For me, I don't care about my work laptop having maximum data transfer speed. As I said, Thunderbolt does work with this also from what I can tell. 1/26/2024 - I am updating this because I also wanted to note that this works great with the Surface Pro 7. The only exception is the built in wired network does not seem to get recognized, but I don't care. I am using WIFI anyway. So Sound, video, and all other devices work perfectly.

reviews.title: Works great most of the time
reviews.body: With this dock I can connect my laptop with a single cable to connect to a second monitor, ethernet, and power. It also has additional USB ports and an SD card reader, but I personally don't use any of those. Overall, it's super convenient. It's even better if you add a magnetic USB-C adapter, just make sure to get one that supports both high speed data and high power charging. I got a right-angle 240W+40Gb/s connector from Magtame (https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B0CWGHXVFK), and it works great with this dock. My one complaint with this dock is that every now and then, video out doesn't work. My laptop says it can see the monitor, but my monitor doesn't see the laptop. When this has happened, disconnecting my laptop, turning the dock off and then on again, and then reconnecting my laptop fixes the issue. It's only happened 5 or 6 times, and I have used the dock hundreds of times. (On a typical day I connect my laptop to the dock 2 or 3 times, and I've had it for almost a year and a half.) Overall, it's a huge timesaver.

reviews.title: DO NOT BUY THIS PRODUCT.
reviews.body: **UPDATE** Now my rear USB port has died--the only one of two standard ports that didn't hiccup and glitch. This thing worked FAIR (front USB port always glitchy) for about a year and a half--MINUS any Mac capacities--and now is essentially an aftermarket power brick. The combination of misrepresented functionality (no Mac support despite showing Mac use), faulty design (front USB unreliable, irregular power supply to dual monitors), and poor reliability (multiple ports and functions dead within 18 months) have serious undermined my former respect for this brand. DO NOT BUY THIS PRODUCT. (ORIGINAL REVIEW:) Disappointing. First, it was not clear to me when I purchased this that it would not allow me to extend screens from my MacBook. There is now a slide that shows that all Mac screens will be identical. It’s possible I missed that a year and a half ago at purchase, but I think I would have noticed. In any case, claiming this is Mac compatible is inane. I don’t know anyone who purchases a docking hub so they can see 3+ screens of the SAME THING. Mac users, beware. I was willing to attribute that to careless comparisons on my part—partly based on a very high opinion of Anker in general. BUT unfortunately the problems do not end there. Though there are two standard USB ports, the way in which this device is wired makes it difficult to use them. If I place my keyboard dongle in the front USB port, and insert a flash drive into the USB-C port next to it, there is suddenly an irregular lag to my mouse movements. I cannot work all day with my mouse lagging. Of course I can move the dongle to the rear of the unit, but now my printer cable is projecting from the front and that’s the whole point of having rear USB ports. In short, why design the ports in a way that they interfere with each other? ANOTHER ISSUE is flickering in my monitor screen sometimes. I looked online and the only solution I found is turning down the refresh rate because “60 Hz on each screen is a lot for the hub to handle”. I thought 60 Hz was pretty much standard so again I’m not sure why a device would be advertised as handling up to three screens if two was going to tax it. This problem also seems intermittent but it ought to happen never. LASTLY, just this past week, the device suddenly can no longer extend more than one screen on my Windows work computer. I’ve tried two computers and multiple cables but whatever I do Windows will not recognize that I have two monitors attached and allow me to extend them. Both monitors are actually live and connected but show the same image, so somehow the hub has lost the ability to differentiate between them. Now the hub is useless. I have disconnected my second monitor from the hub and connected it directly to my laptop. I have actually moved my keyboard/mouse dongle and attached it directly to the laptop as well. This removes all purpose for having a hub at all. And again, this is for my Windows work computer—my MacBook has all these issues but would not extend screens even when the hub was fully functional. I bought this because I had faith in the Anker brand and because it was slightly less expensive than the hub Apple promoted on its website. I regret this purchase. Now I have a $150 hub that combines only two of the five cable connections I connect and disconnect every time I move my computer from work to home. Very, very disappointed. Pay more to get a better and more reliable product.

reviews.title: Really some of the best docking stations on the market
reviews.body: Anker has been making quality products for years. They've become very proud of their goods of late, as they should be, but sometimes the price-to-value ratio seems out of balance. I got this one on sale, and after having worked with some units from the Chinese random-letter companies, it was refreshing to work with a unit again from Anker. I can just feel the quality. We're literally using all of the ports on the docking station. It works seamlessly between a Chromebook, Ubuntu, and a Windows laptop, so compatibility has not been an issue, and they all charge just fine. I've had no heat problems or noticed any noises. This is used for business and productivity, and I was looking for just 2 standard HDMI connections. It's REALLY hard to find good ones with lots of ports. Videos look great. Not sure it's gaming-performance worthy on secondary monitors, but for what we need it for, this Anker docking station is perfect.

reviews.title: Transformed my desk setup
reviews.body: Transformed my desk setup — just one important caveat for Mac users. This docking station has completely changed how my desk looks and feels. With just one cable, I went from a tangled mess of peripherals to a clean, minimal workspace. If desk organization matters to you, this hub is a game-changer. The 13-in-1 port selection covers everything I need — display output, USB-A, USB-C, SD card, ethernet, and more. Performance has been reliable across the board, and the build quality feels solid and premium for the price. That said, there is one important thing Mac users need to know before buying: dual monitor output does not work on macOS. This is an Apple limitation, not a flaw in the product itself — but I'll be honest, I didn't read the product description carefully enough and assumed it would work. I was caught off guard when it didn't. If you're a Mac user planning to run two external displays, please double-check compatibility before purchasing. Windows users should have no issues. Aside from that, I'm very happy with this purchase and would recommend it without hesitation to anyone who wants to clean up their desk and simplify their cable management.

reviews.title: Good Product/Great Customer Service
reviews.body: when i bought this hub i had a couple of problems with the hub right out of the box. i was busy fixing other things on other machines and missed the Amazon exchange window and reached out to Anker via their email providing them with a description of the problem, it was dropping a monitor and eventually was cycling my ethernet off and on constantly. their customer service returned my email on the same day and flawlessly provided me with things to check and eventually sent me a new device and a shipping label for the bad one. just hooked up the new hub and it's running like a new buick. this is my second all i one hub i bought from Anker and i will continue to buy their products in the future for the quality of their products and that of their customer service. Thank you Anker!

reviews.title: Works Flawlessly!
reviews.body: I wanted to get rid of my desktop and just use a laptop. I'm used to using a desktop at home and wanted to keep using my external keyboard, mouse, and two large monitors when I'm home. I bought an Asus laptop that is fast and has lots of storage. With this docking station, it works perfectly for me. I keep the monitors, keyboard, and mouse plugged into the Anker docking station. I have one USB-C cable that connects to my laptop. This one cable charges the laptop and connects it -- via the docking station -- to the monitors, keyboard, and mouse. When I travel, I unplug the one USB-C cable and I'm ready to go. When I return, I plug in the one USB-C cable, turn on my docking station and monitors, and I'm up and running as a desktop. I tried a cheaper docking station (LIONWEI USB C Hub) first. It mostly worked but required two USB-C cables (one to charge the laptop, one to connect to the docking station) and it was not stable. It would often glitch out and require me to reconnect or reboot. The Anker docking station has been very solid and, in 4 months has never glitched out or required any type of rebooting. Pro tip: I also use an "aucun Magnetic USB C Adapter" for the USB cable. This connects via a magnet so I don't even have to plug and unplug the USB cable, I just pull off the magnet.

reviews.title: Pretty good docking station with a few problems
reviews.body: The docking station worked pretty well right out of the box. A few observations: 1. The instructions, as many do now, are in multiple languages and a very small part was applicable. The key diagram and explanatory table were buried among all the other text, but it would have been helpful to have that information at the very top of the instructions, rather than in the middle of multiple languages. 2. I have an HP Spectre 360, and the charging function of the docking station is variable, i.e. sometimes it charges, sometimes it does not. I have to check periodically to make sure it's charging, otherwise I risk using all the battery reserve. It's a relatively minor issue and perhaps due to the detection by the computer of a non-HP power source. 3. Update: I had 2 HDMI monitors and a third was connected through a USB expansion device with an HDMI port. Decided to try using the display port instead of the USB expansion device, and when I plugged the third monitor into the display port using a converter cable for DP to HDMI, one of the other monitors would not show. No matter what combination I used, if I plugged the third monitor into the DP port, only 2 would show. So, I plugged my USB expansion device back in and voila! All three monitors showed again. I couldn't find any documentation online regarding this issue, so I have to assume that using the DP port along with the two HDMI ports negates one of the three. Interesting, but it decreases the score. Overall, the device is still a nice addition to my desk. Prior to now, I had a number of USB hubs strung together with a mass of wires like a bowl of spaghetti, so the docking station with multiple ports is a definite improvement.

reviews.title: Great Windows/Linux dock!
reviews.body: This is for the "Anker Docking Station, PowerExpand 13-in-1 USB-C Dock, 85W Charging for Laptop" ** Update March 9th, 2023 ** So pretty much everything in the original review stands, but there is one issue that I touched on originally about the display refresh rate and resolution that I can clarify now. To get the resolution how you want it, you need to set the monitors to the same refresh rate first, then once the resolution is set and applied, change the refresh rate. That being said, I'm not sure if the refresh rate actually changes or if it just says it does. ** End of update ** So I just got this about an hour ago, and everything just worked! Both in Ubuntu 22.04 and Windows 10. Here's my setup. Everything is plugged into the dock and only the single USB-C dock cable is plugged into the laptop. Laptop: Dell XPS 13 9370 1TB SanDisk USB-C SSD (for booting into Ubuntu) 2x Monitors + laptop monitor (One monitor is Ultra Wide 2560x1080 144Hz, other is 1080p 60Hz) - Note: I'm using one DP port and one HDMI port Wireless keyboard/mouse Speakers Ethernet connection for Internet First of all, I was using a Dell TB16 dock before this but I had multiple issues with it. Long story short, I don't recommend the Dell docks, especially if you use Linux. ** Long story about Dell TB16 Dock ** Using the Dell dock, my monitor would randomly go out, and the network only connected at 100mbps, the soundcard is super quiet (even at max volume), it's always on and can get noisy when it heats up (it has a fan), the cable is built into the unit (non-replaceable) and is only about a foot and a half long (coming out of the left side of the unit) and the unit itself is rather large. Also, I boot off a USB-C SSD drive for Linux (which allows me to plug the USB SSD into almost any computer and boot into my Ubuntu OS); For whatever reason, I could never get it to show up as a boot option when plugged into the dock, even with ThunderBolt boot support and pre-module stuff enabled. ** End of the Long story about Dell TB16 Dock ** Now the Anker dock on the other hand is about a 1/4 of the size of the Dell dock, connects @ 1GB with no problem, allows me to boot off my USB-C SSD, has a power button to turn it off when not in use, it's silent, works without having to install any drivers on either Windows or Ubuntu, comes with a decently long USB-C cable (3 ft?) to plug into the computer (which can also be replaced and yes it charges my laptop too) and the sound volume is great. There is one oddity that happened, but I was able to fix it easily enough and it's likely not a problem with the dock but a software issue in Ubuntu. When changing the resolution + refresh rate in Ubuntu, it didn't properly scale the resolution (the resolution was right, but much of it was cut off or shrunk down as if the monitor itself didn't change resolutions but the computer did), I had to change the resolution + refresh rate to something else, then to what I wanted to make it work. To be clear, it worked when I plugged it in initially, but changing it to my preference required multiple changes to set it in properly. Once set, it worked as normal. I highly recommend this dock!

reviews.title: Worked perfectly out of the box.
reviews.body: Zero issues with this versatile dock as it replaced a Belkin hub which was virtually cluttering up my desk. All of the cords run out the back of the unit including ones for an external monitor (HDMI), printer, external hard drive and power cord for my Windows 11 laptop. I only have a Bluetooth dongle for a mouse plugged into the front. Very clean look and I love the fact that there are two SD card slots and two additional USB C ports out front for charging devices. I snagged this puppy while it was on sale which was a bonus.

reviews.title: Warranty Support Is a Nightmare
reviews.body: 1 Star I was very happy with this docking station when I first purchased it. It worked well for several months, charging my laptop and running my dual-monitor setup without any issues. Unfortunately, the dock developed what appears to be an internal hardware failure while still under warranty. It stopped charging my laptop properly, and my monitors constantly disconnected and reconnected. To rule out every other possibility, I purchased an Anker Prime 14-in-1 Docking Station using the exact same laptop, monitors, cables, and power outlet. The new dock worked perfectly immediately, confirming that the original 13-in-1 dock was defective. What turned this into a one-star review was not the product failure itself. Electronics can fail. It was the warranty experience. I have spent over a week providing proof of purchase, completing troubleshooting, answering repeated requests, and following up multiple times. The process has been slow, confusing, and frustrating, with incomplete return instructions and unnecessary delays. I expected Anker to stand behind its warranty. Instead, I have had to escalate my case and file a Better Business Bureau complaint in an effort to have my warranty honored. Based on my experience, I cannot recommend this product. A good warranty experience is just as important as a good product, and unfortunately Anker has fallen well short of my expectations.

reviews.body: Tested its power capability as demonstratedin the video by running cpu stress test on 3 laptops all plugged into this device: Materials used - 3 laptops, Asus ProArt 13in, Lenovo T14 gen 2, Lenovo x13 Gen 1 - 3 Stattik 3ft 100W magnetic charging type c cables -1 Anker 10ft 240W type c cable - 3 240w rated Power monitor device for Type c Ran stress test on all 3 laptops, unplugged one halfway thru test to show how device works. At best, its capable of 200w Tops. It just redistributes power everytime you plug in new device. During testing, 2 of the 140w, closer to middle and 2 of 100w type c ports, stopped functioning. This was my second test and 2nd day of owning the device and it failed miserably. It is NOT durable and is prone to overheating and will shut off power to middle ports due to lack of vents. Why did I buy it and why did I do it? Bought to run 4-6 old lenovo T14 in a server config, I did not want power draw being an issue and wanted clean cable management. Turns out, I was right. This device can't power multiple device and give them sufficient wattage simultaneously. Please watch video

reviews.title: Impressive Power Management in a Tiny Footprint
reviews.body: Let's look at the numbers on this little block. Pushing 1000 watts total out of something just over five inches long sounds highly suspicious right off the bat. Seeing it in action makes more sense of the math, though. The gallium nitride chips inside are doing the heavy lifting, allowing the unit to manage heat way better than older silicon chargers. When my husband plugs in his Dell and I connect my MacBook Pro to the top C1 and C2 ports, we genuinely get the fast 140W charge we expect. We can simultaneously run the kids' tablets and our phones on the remaining ports without anything shutting down or getting dangerously hot. The listing doesn't explicitly mention UL or ETL safety certifications, which usually gives me a lot of pause with power devices. The thermal performance has been surprisingly stable in our house so far, keeping everything fully charged without turning into a space heater. The detachable base and the five-foot cord mean we can finally keep the little ones from yanking cords straight out of the wall socket. A very solid buy for a tech-heavy household.

reviews.title: Nice, nice nice. Big Power. fast charge.
reviews.body: 1000 W, what a beast! This is the best price for a very small unit and a lot of output. The whole household plugs in tons of stuff and then all charges fast. No regrets on this one. The two ports of 240 W could power a laptop.

title: Razer Basilisk V3 Customizable RGB Wired Ergonomic Gaming Mouse, Black

reviews.title: Yes! Beats the G502 Hero (which I liked) and the G502 X (by a lot)
reviews.body: Good god, what a mouse. I mean, it's not perfect; nothing is. But it's so good. I came from years of the G502 Hero; the grips on it were wearing out. I first decided to try a G502 X, as it was supposed to be an improved version of the Hero, essentially. For $25 more than the Basilisk, it pretty much sucked in my opinion. The only thing I could imagine picking it over the Basilisk for is weight. But if you care that much about weight, there are much lighter mice on the market. --- I'll review it as compared to the Hero (and a bit to the X), as that's what I know. They're pretty common, so maybe this will help people out if they're thinking about converting: Initially I wasn't so sure about the grip and the main mouse buttons. The mouse buttons have a rough texture, and I found with my Hero that when my fingers were slightly tacky/damp, they would stick slightly to the surface of the buttons in the same way a clean basketball shoe does to a court (i.e., not "sticky", but grippy). I liked that. But after using it for a while, I think it's totally fine and maybe even better. The feet seem the same to me as the G502 X, which is good. They're white PTFE. Very smooth. The scroll wheel is *fantastic*. Like, it's perfect. It seems to control the mode with an electromagnet, so it makes a cool click sound when the computer is restarted and such. And it even has a setting in the software where you can have it tactile by default, but with a quick flick, it switches to free-spin temporarily. Awesome. And when I move the mouse quickly side to side, there is absolutely no play in the wheel. Nothing. That was one of my annoyances with the Hero. The scroll wheel would wobble audibly and tactilely when in free spin mode with even moderately fast mouse movements. The click noise isn't as nice as I expected, but it's totally fine and better than the X (which was super loud and piercing). I'd put it somewhere between the X and the Hero. It's kind of like if someone built the X and then was like, oh, that sucks, and then made adjustments like a sane human. I believe the Basilisk switches are optical (the Hero is mechanical and the X is hybrid mech/optical), and so maybe that's approximately what happened. In short, I think the Hero is a pretty quiet click, and I think the Basilisk is a very standard click. Sounds like what I'd use as a mouse click if I were a foley artist. The Basilisk's weight is listed at 101g, and it feels quite nice. Not hard to control. I'm sure I'll get even better as we go, though. The palm section is actually quite high! Like, even more than the Hero. It feels pretty good so far. The Basilisk's cable is an absolute work of art. I mean, it's perfect. It's got a soft woven sleeve and is not stiff at all. I had the same kind of reaction to it as I did when I got my current massage shower head and found that no, the tube connecting the head to the spigot doesn't actually have to be stiff at all to do its job. The software is slightly annoying because there's a separate program for the lighting and the mouse (though they're styled identically and could ostensibly be packaged in one app). But its functionality is nice. There are 9 RGB zones around the bottom edge of the mouse, plus one on the scroll wheel and the logo under the palm. They seem rather infinitely adjustable. Neat! --- Hope this helps somebody!

reviews.title: Love the switch
reviews.body: I used the Razer Mamba Elite for many years and absolutely loved it, so I was hesitant to switch. This mouse was recommended to me as a replacement, and I have been pleasantly surprised. It feels comfortable in the hand, responds quickly, and the customizable buttons and RGB lighting are excellent. The scroll wheel is especially smooth and versatile. Overall, it has been a great change and I am very happy with it.

reviews.title: This Mouse Ruined Cheap Mice for Me
reviews.body: I’ve genuinely liked using the Razer Basilisk V3. The first thing I noticed was how comfortable it felt. Some mice are fine for about 20 minutes and then they start feeling like a weirdly shaped brick. This mouse has been much better for longer use, whether I’m gaming or just clicking around online doing whatever nonsense I got distracted by. What I like most is that it feels like someone actually thought about how a hand works. The buttons are responsive, the movement is smooth, and the scroll wheel feels so nice that it almost made reading comment sections worth it. Almost. While this mouse has not been life changing in a dramatic movie soundtrack kind of way, it has changed my expectations enough that going back to a cheaper mouse would feel like using a shopping cart with one bad wheel. Oh, and the customization. I am not out here trying to launch a space mission from my desk, but it is nice being able to set things up in a way that actually fits how I use it. Once everything is dialed in, it just feels easy. Overall, it has been a genuinely solid mouse and one of those upgrades you stop thinking about because it just quietly does its job well. Which, for a mouse, is honestly the dream. It just sits there, minds its business, and makes me slightly more powerful than I probably deserve.

reviews.title: One of my favorite mice and you will love it too
reviews.body: This mouse is just incredibly smooth. Even with its high weight the skates make it super easy to move around and the weight gives it control, resulting in superb aim. The material can make your hands a bit sweaty when death gripping it, but it’s very solid matte surface. You can grip test and throw this mouse across a room without it breaking. The shape this mouse has just fits right in your hand, and the rubber side grips make it super comfortable and easy to use, it’s basically great with any grip type. The skates are super glidey and quiet even when under the weight of this chunker of a mouse. It’s better for bigger hands of course, it’s harder to use with smaller hands but it’s doable. The scroll wheel is the best of any mouse, even the Logitech g502. It has a setting in the software where it can be a tactile scroll wheel when scrolling slowly, but becomes a freely spinning wheel when flicked fast. You can even switch between spinny wheel mode and tactile mode with the click of a button. I loved this mouse so much I upgraded to the wireless version, and I wasn’t sacrificing much leaving wired because the battery life was great on that one. 10/10 mouse.

reviews.title: Excellent & totally worth it.
reviews.body: Best mouse I've ever used. Every surface is comfortable to touch & adds to its controllability. The RMB & LMB are soft & responsive, and have a quick reset. Easy to hold & thumb rest allows for greater control during long use.

reviews.title: Good gaming mouse and does what it needs. Just wish it would last longer.
reviews.body: To be honest they don't make mice like they used to. I remember a time where you would buy gaming mice and they would last 5 years minimum. Now a days they last a year if you are lucky. So far this mouse has worked pretty good and seems like it is holding up quite fine. I also want to point out I haven't had this for a very long time and I suspect the build quality of the mouse should last a year if this was anything like my old razor mouse. The scroll wheel is pretty solid. I like how responsive it is. I have never seen a mouse scroll wheel quite like this. Scrolling speed is pretty good. Was able to do a lot of jagged movements and noticed the mouse handled it very well in minecraft. Ergonomic of the mouse are probably the best part. I haven't used a non trackball mouse that felt this great in maybe ever. The programmable buttons I haven't used for anything since I literally have nothing to remotely use them for whatsoever. RGB is decent. Not a selling point for me that is a selling point for some people I guess. With that said I am not sure if I can recommend this just because it seems pretty good but the way gaming mice have been going I don't see this lasting more than a year. I remember a time where mice would last like a decade now they break if you look at them the wrong way. I will say the big pro to a gaming mouse is the fact it is meant for gaming. Yes you are paying a lot of money for something that will break within a year but you pretty much have no choice just because these mice have a sensor in them that is significantly way better than most mice.

reviews.title: Great for the price.
reviews.body: The Razer Basilisk V3 is hands down one of the best gaming mice I've ever used. It's super comfy even during long gaming sessions thanks to its ergonomic design, and the customizable buttons are perfect for both gaming and getting stuff done. The RGB lighting looks awesome, and the HyperScroll wheel is surprisingly handy for switching between precise and fast scrolling. The sensor is super accurate and responsive, and the mouse just glides across my mousepad. I also love how easy it is to customize everything through Razer Synapse. Whether I'm playing FPS games, MMOs, or just browsing, this mouse works perfectly. If you want a top-notch gaming mouse with tons of customization and excellent comfort, the Basilisk V3 is totally worth it. Highly recommended!

reviews.title: Peak Gaming Mouse Energy
reviews.body: This mouse is basically the “I’m him” of gaming mice. It’s super comfortable, the buttons feel crisp, and the 26K DPI sensor tracks like it’s reading your mind. The RGB lighting goes full rave mode (in a good way), and the HyperScroll wheel is clutch whether you’re swapping weapons or doom‑scrolling. The 11 programmable buttons give you all the customization you could want, and the whole thing just feels premium. It’s fast, smooth, and honestly makes every other mouse feel a little mid.

reviews.title: Fantastic mouse for those who like it heavy.
reviews.body: I'm an avid PC user and rarely replace my accessories. My mouse especially was hard to replace, as every top end mouse seems to get lighter and lighter. However, after using the Basilisk V3, I can safely say this mouse has been a perfect upgrade from my 2013 Deathadder. It weighs roughly the same, being on the heavier side for a mouse, and that's perfect for me. It's built great, has a fantastic braided cable which is smooth to the touch, it doesn't catch on corners like the older Razer cables, and the RGB is stellar. I really like the ring of RGB that goes around the base, and it's incredibly easy to edit in Razer Synapse. The mouse is also extremely comfortable. I didn't expect a thumb rest to do much, but I'll honestly miss it if I ever have to upgrade. For the price, you really can't go wrong. This mouse is incredible for its price point and well worth investing in if you like to 'feel' your mouse movements.

title: Logitech G PRO X2 SUPERSTRIKE Wireless Gaming Mouse - Black/White

reviews.title: The best gaming mouse I’ve ever used
reviews.body: I’ve owned and tested many gaming mice over the years, and the Logitech G Superstrike X2 is, without question, the best one I’ve ever used. I don’t play competitively—I mostly enjoy adventure games, action titles, and other immersive experiences—but this mouse has made every gaming session more enjoyable. It combines incredible comfort, premium build quality, and features that genuinely stand out. The biggest highlight for me is the haptic switches. They feel amazing, providing a tactile, satisfying click that makes every input feel deliberate and precise. The feedback is unlike anything I’ve experienced on another mouse, adding a level of immersion that you don’t realize you’re missing until you try it. Combined with the outstanding responsiveness, every click feels fast, consistent, and incredibly satisfying. Another thing I absolutely love is how lightweight it is. It glides effortlessly across the mousepad and never feels fatiguing, even after hours of gaming. The shape is comfortable, the weight is perfectly balanced, and it almost feels like an extension of your hand. The wireless connectivity has also been flawless. It’s fast, stable, and completely reliable, with no noticeable latency or dropouts. It truly delivers the freedom of wireless without any of the compromises that used to come with it. Logitech has once again delivered a premium product. From the build quality to the innovative haptic switches, lightweight design, and rock-solid wireless performance, everything about the Superstrike X2 feels refined and thoughtfully engineered. It’s a mouse that makes you appreciate the little details every time you use it. Overall, this is easily the best mouse I’ve ever owned, and I couldn’t recommend it more. Whether you’re a competitive player or, like me, simply want the best possible experience while enjoying your favorite games, the Logitech Superstrike X2 is absolutely worth it.

reviews.title: Best Mouse I’ve Ever Used
reviews.body: I’ve had this mouse for almost a week now, and I can confidently say it’s hands down the best mouse I’ve ever used. It’s incredibly lightweight, the wireless performance has been flawless, and it just feels high quality overall. I am 35 years old and don't have the best reaction time but this mouse dropped my Human Benchmark reaction time average from 190 ms to around 160 ms. I wasn’t even planning on testing this, but one of my friends told me to try it and see if there was actually a difference. I tested on my old mouse, a Model O, and then back to the Superstrike X2 just to make sure it wasn’t in my head. The difference was still there. Everything just feels quicker and more in control, and the speed and click feel really make a difference. The feeling when you click it is incredibly responsive and smooth. The only thing I can compare it to is clicking an iPhone sleep button. Battery life has been very good also. After about six hours of gameplay, the battery only went from 82% down to 75%, which is impressive for a wireless gaming mouse. Can't recommend this mouse enough to everyone

reviews.title: Lightweight, buttons nice to press
reviews.body: I’ve been using it daily for about a month and a half now. First thing you notice is how insanely light it is, my hand doesn’t get tired even after long sessions. The buttons feel really nice to press. The magnetic analog switches are smooth and the fact that there are basically no loud clicks is actually pretty cool and satisfying. You can adjust the haptic feedback and trigger stops which is a nice touch. It’s comfortable tracks perfectly and the wireless connection has been rock solid. Battery life is good too. No major complaints so far

reviews.title: huge difference during long gaming sessions
reviews.body: The Logitech PRO X2 SUPERSTRIKE is easily one of the best gaming mice I’ve used. The first thing you notice is how incredibly lightweight it is—it glides effortlessly, which makes a huge difference during long gaming sessions. The responsiveness is top-tier, and the Lightspeed wireless connection feels just as fast and reliable as a wired mouse. The build quality is excellent, with a clean, minimalist design that looks great on any setup. The clicks feel crisp and precise, and the customizable haptics add a nice touch for those who want to fine-tune their experience. Battery life is also impressive, and the USB-C charging is a welcome upgrade.

reviews.title: Haptic is the future for mice.
reviews.body: I gave this mouse 5 stars simply because of the haptic triggers. Ive only ever used the razer viper pro mouse and for my large hands its the only one that fits comfortably. The superstrike is a bit smaller in my hand but nothing that would make me stop using it. Its heavier than the razer and to my surprise I actually like and prefer that. The battery life on the mouse is great. The settings you choose for the haptic triggers does affect battery life but its nothing major. Now the main reason I bought this mouse was for the haptic system it uses and ill be blunt and say its the best thing ever and I hope more companies adapt this. Being able to adjust the actuation points is fantastic. It will take a few days to get used to the sensitivity if you go all the way to one but once youre used to it you'll never want a regular mouse again. Overall I think its a fantastic mouse its a bit spendy but in my opinion the haptic system by itself is worth the price. The only issue i have with this mouse is the side buttons they are extremely squishy they barely click its very unsatisfying I would give the side buttons a half a star.

reviews.title: Lightweight, super fast and great for gaming
reviews.body: I’ve been using this mouse for a while now and honestly I’m really impressed. It’s super lightweight and feels very comfortable in hand, even during long gaming sessions. The response time is excellent — everything feels smooth and precise, especially in FPS games. Battery life is also really good, I don’t have to charge it often which is a big plus. The wireless connection is stable with no lag at all. The only small thing is that it might feel a bit too light if you prefer heavier mice, but for me it’s perfect. Overall, definitely worth it if you’re looking for a high-performance wireless gaming mouse.

reviews.title: Really great mouse, but terrible skates.
reviews.body: I absolutely loves this mouse. I usually have stuck to only using razer mice in the past. However I made the switch to this one and its honestly so great. I only really have one complaint and the rest is amazing. Pros: Battery life is honestly amazing. Its really quiet because it no longer clicks, its just haptic feedback like the ps5 controller. You can adjust when it actually clicks which is super cool just like a Hall effect keyboard, because it's the same tech. Mouse just feels great and the included grips are nice, but they do take some getting used to as they aren't what I was expecting. However I have come to like them. Cons: It's vey expensive for a mouse, there's a lot of competition and a variety of mice esp way cheaper. The stock skates are absolutely terrible, that's why I changed them jade's and now its perfect. No complaints after that. However for a mouse this expensive, I was hoping for better skates. I also don't really like the scroll wheel, to be fair I do come from razer mice so that might be why I hate it. It also takes some getting used to as the mouse is front heavy because of the switches on the mouse, but I bet you can fix that if you have a powerplay to balance it out. However I have this mouse for 2 months now and I absolutely love it and I wouldn't switch for another. The only thing I would change if you were buying this mouse today is to also order skates so you can replace them. Would be a 5/5 if it weren't for the terrible skates. TL;DR: Great mouse if purchasing, buy skates as well.

reviews.title: Huge Upgrade!!!
reviews.body: After just a week of using this mouse, I can confidently say this is the best peripheral purchase I have ever made. I initially wasn't in the market for a new mouse, until my scroll wheel broke on my razer mouse. I decided to just pull the trigger on the X2 Superstrike instead of purchasing another razer mouse. The mouse material feel is excellent, and the wheel is great as well. I've also seen some reviews disliking the skates on the X2 Superstrike, however I personally found them to be great. The haptic feedback mouse click seemed a bit gimmicky before I actually used it. Right off the bat, the mouse click feels incredibly responsive and similar to that of any high quality mouse. You get enough feedback and it doesn't feel that much different from a regular mouse click. But, you also have optionality to adjust a ton of settings, like accuation, feedback strength, etc. For gaming, with the right settings, this genuinely feels amazing, and that's before the performance upgrade. As many other reviewers have noted, it noticeably decreases latency on top of all of this. Another huge perk with this mouse I found, was that it's almost dead silent as well. No more loud clicking! My only critique with the mouse are the side buttons and the size. The side buttons are the only part of the mouse that feel "cheap". Because I use the side buttons often in competitive games, I notice it a lot more than probably most people would. I also have large hands, and this is the smallest mouse I have used. I got used to it pretty quick, but the mouse is on the smaller side. Nonetheless, if you are looking to upgrade your mouse and have the money, I would 100% recommend. This feels as impactful as going from a 60hz monitor to a 144hz+.

This is clearly where the mouse shines, and it delivers exactly what you’d expect at this price point in terms of core performance. However, the side buttons (the two next to the left click area) are a noticeable weak point. They feel cheap and somewhat out of place, especially when compared to competitors like Razer. Considering the price of this mouse, I expected a higher-quality feel across all buttons, not just the main ones. That said, since the primary clicks and overall performance are what matter most in actual gameplay, I would still recommend this mouse. If you can overlook the side button quality, it’s a strong option for anyone looking to move into wireless gaming. Sorry for the messy mousepad :)

title: zelotes Gaming Mouse with 8 Programmable Buttons,9200DPI Optical Wired Ergonomic Mouse, USB Corded Computer Gaming Mice for PC, Laptop,Mac, Black

reviews.title: gREAT AS A TEMPORARY BACKUP
reviews.body: In a pinch where in some situation your main mouse breaks and you need something that's similar to it but not entirely a carbon copy, this will get the job done. The form factor of this mouse is very particular in its design, catching inspiration similar to that of the Logitech G502. It forms and moves with the general weight of a 502. However the system how it adjusted its weight is more primitive but is still easily adjustable. It has a latch on the bottom that opens up to a couple sets of weights wrapped around foam which could be either removed one at a time or entirely. It's a great way to reduce a lot of load on your wrists. However you need to be careful with it because it's delicate and I've already damaged the phone, causing 2 sectors to become inoperable for weights. We need to be careful with them. Also the latch closing the weights container is very small. You might accidentally pop it open if you slam the mouse on your board. The DPI switch for the sensitivity is a nice addition though I wish I had ways to customize each distance from one another. You're permanently stuck with eight different speeds, but you could still adjust your overall mouse speeds through your windows settings anyway. The button layout almost like the 502 in terms of buttons, but it's missing 2 sets, so if you're used to all the buttons on that mouse, you're not going to get it here. Overall I had a great experience with this mouse. It glides smoothly because of its nice feet, the buttons aren't too mushy, the clicks are similar to that of any typical mouse. And the 8 programmable buttons are a nice addition

reviews.title: Good quality, budget friendly mouse!
reviews.body: The Razer DeathAdder Essential is a great choice for anyone looking for a quality mouse on a budget. it's size seems friendly for all hand sizes and its ergonomics are good, leaving me with no discomfort even after a 6 hour gaming session. The extra 2 programable buttons on the side are a huge help when adding shortcuts or changing keybinds. The mouse's design is also something not to ignore, the white version has a nice smooth sleek look and feel, with small hexagon pattern the bottom for your fingers to rest. Connecting the mouse to a laptop or computer is a very easy task, all you do is plug it in to a USB port, since it is a wired mouse. The mouse is just overall great to me, however some might want to opt for a mouse with quieter clicks if sound is going to be an issue for you. Overall 5 stars, it's a very good mouse, comfortable, responsive, precise, and very easy to use, highly recommend to anyone looking for budget friendly gaming or everyday use mice.

reviews.title: Comfortable Gaming Mouse With Great Performance

The build quality feels solid, and the overall design has that premium gaming feel without being overly complicated. Overall, this is a reliable and comfortable mouse that performs well. A great choice for anyone who wants a quality gaming mouse that can also handle everyday tasks.

reviews.title: Great Performance and Comfortable Design
reviews.body: This mouse works smoothly and feels very comfortable to use. The buttons are responsive, the scroll wheel is precise, and the design fits nicely in the hand. Great for both work and gaming. Easy to set up and excellent value for the price. Highly recommended

reviews.title: Overall, a great mouse. Has become my go to.
reviews.body: I got my first basilisk mouse on a Black Friday sale, and I got hooked. These are great, quality mouses that still use AA batteries. As someone who loves the MX series, and is sad that they’ve moved to Lipo, these mouses are much more affordable, functional, and still can be portable quite well. I love it.

reviews.title: Great mid range mouse option
reviews.body: My previous mice include the Razer Deathadder V2, Razer Basilisk V2 X Hyperspeed, and the Logitech Pro X Superlight. This is easily the most comfortable mouse I've used, the contours feel perfect and the extra button the side is well placed and feels like a natural addition. I've personally not found the weight an issue, though it is much heavier that most other mice, even ones that use a AA battery. I do prefer the external battery as I disliked having to plug in my mouse every so often to charge it, something that became much more frequent as the internal battery lost capacity. The new switches feel excellent, a noticeable improvement from the V2. Performance is good in all areas with the exception of the scroll wheel, which feels like it eats inputs for breakfast lunch and dinner. Basically when scrolling fast the Basilisk V3 seems to skip inputs. My V2 had similar issues and eventually I had to replace it when the scroll wheel started acting haywire and scrolling on its own or backwards. Something to keep an eye on. Appearance is unremarkable. The new RGB scroll wheel is appreciated, but fairly simple in customization. I have it set to static color but you can have it be reactive to clicking, color cycle, breathing, or a few other options with Razer Synapse. One small quirk is that if you have auto sleep on, it takes a bit to actually turn back on when using it again. Whereas the Razer Deathadder V2 was near instant in my experience, the Basilisk V3 takes a few seconds to get going, which sounds like nothing but does make a difference when it happens so often. TL;DR - It's a really good mouse at this price point, good performance and great comfort. Only negative is the scroll wheel and the weight if that matters to you.

reviews.title: Not as good as a 3S, but less expensive. Hopefully better quality switches than the 3S.
reviews.body: I like this mouse, but it could be better. I purchased it to replace a Logitech MX-Master 3S, which is a great mouse except the microswitch for the left button stopped being reliable after less than three years. While that's a reasonable life for some users, perhaps, it seemed inadequate to me. My use case is general pc use for searching the web, writing emails, and managing finances. The Logitech wasn't used every day. The 3S has a higher palm hump, which the Basilisk lacks and I really prefer. The Basilisk is similar in overall size to the 3S, so for the most part it fits my hand sufficiently well. Hump size is the main downside to the Basilisk. That, plus the battery is not rechargeable. What, in 2026?! But I've adapted to it, and battery life so far has been very good. It has the combo BT + 2.4 gHz connectivity with a dongle. Both choices work very well and reliably. I like the center wheel size and action a lot. I like the slip pads on the bottom of the mouse. It has a very handy and perfectly responsive third thumb button that I don't currently use but gamers may find it useful. reviews.title: Title: Fantastic Value & Durability – Still Going Strong After Constant Use!
reviews.body: I’ve been using the Redragon M602 Wired Gaming Mouse for quite a while now, and I am honestly impressed by how well it has held up. If you are looking for a high-performance mouse that doesn't break the bank, this is a top-tier choice. Design and Ergonomics: The first thing you notice is the ergonomic shape. It fits naturally in the hand, which is a lifesaver during long gaming sessions or even long workdays. The textured side grips provide great control, and the weight feels substantial without being too heavy. It feels much more premium than its price tag suggests. Performance & RGB: The sensor is very responsive and accurate. I haven't experienced any lag or jittering, which is crucial for FPS and fast-paced games. The RGB lighting is another highlight—it’s vibrant and looks great on my desk. The different lighting modes and DPI adjustments (which you can change on the fly) make it very versatile for different types of games. Durability: What impresses me most is that I’m still using it today and it works as well as the day I unboxed it. The buttons still have a crisp click, the scroll wheel is smooth, and the braided cable is very durable and hasn't frayed at all. It’s built like a tank. Pros: Super Comfortable: Great for palm or claw grips. Customizable: Easy DPI switching and beautiful RGB effects. Reliable: No double-clicking issues or sensor failures after extended use. Braided Cable: Adds a layer of protection and premium feel. Final Verdict: The Redragon M602 is proof that you don't need to spend $80+ to get a great gaming mouse. It’s reliable, looks awesome, and is built to last. I’m still very happy with my purchase!

reviews.title: Easy to program, amazing mouse for the price.
reviews.body: First off, for the price, this is a 5-star product across the board. I have purchased plenty of $50 mice and they just didn't last. The mouse buttons always gave out, and two or three years later I'd be shopping for a new one. The Redragon ones are remarkably cheap in price, but are lasting great and look pretty cool. I've previously purchased a few Centrophorus (M601), and when one got busted a few weeks back I went to order a new one and saw the Griffin (M602) for a few dollars more and decided to give it a shot. No software is needed to control the lights. There's a list in the booklet for how many presses to access various color settings, so that's super easy and I love not needing to install more bloatware on my computer. If yours came default to the "reactive" setting like mine did, never fear! There's much more soothing options. That said, it seems a little odd to have two buttons front and center for things like dpi and color. Once I've picked my comfort setting it's not something I plan to change often, and recessed buttons or perhaps interior ones would make the mouse more streamlined. The 602 has a very smooth, faintly grippy surface texture, and is far more ergonomic than the 601 with its bumpy texture. I'm not completely sure which texture I prefer, but possibly the 602. I am not personally using the 602 however, my husband is, because the ergonomic shape isn't designed for someone with really small hands and becomes counterproductive at that point. My old 601 works better for me. I believe he prefers the 602, so it's all working out. My only actual complaint about this mouse is that the lights inside aren't 100% covered. When it's being used from some angles I can see through tiny cracks next to the frosted plastic directly in and catch the glare of an uncovered LED, which was never an issue with the 601.

reviews.title: Impressive Quality Mouse for the Price
reviews.body: Before I start, I'll give my reason for the 4 stars rather than a 5 star review. There is no lift off calibration or setting, so the mouse will move if you slightly lift it off the pad. The mouse itself is very high quality and the ergonomics on it feel great. The entire mouse was a complete surprise to me. It is my first Redragon product and I am very impressed. I bought it for the low price and high quality look. The durability is very impressive and does not feel cheaply made. The scroll wheel feels great and not wonky. This thing has 9 programmable buttons?! Insane for the price.

reviews.title: Redragon Gaming Mouse beats all the other gaming mice
reviews.body: Redragon Gaming Mouse Beats Other Gaming Mice To start off with, I think that the Redragon gaming mouse is one of the best mice as of right now. I have owned this mouse for about 3 years and it is just as good as brand new. When looking at the price of this mouse compared to other gaming mice, this is cheaper, durable, longer-lasting, and has most of the features as the other expensive mice have. I would most certainly recommend any interested buyers looking for a gaming mouse to buy this product. First and foremost, I think that the Redragon gaming mouse is one of the best mice as of right now because it’s cheap and affordable. When looking for a desktop gaming mouse, you should always research and look for other products that might be similar, less expensive, and easier to use especially when it comes to gaming mice. One of the popular gaming mice that is competing against the redragon mice in the market as of right now would be the glorious model o. This mouse comes around $100 in the market and functions similarly to the redragon mouse. The redragon mouse comes in around $20 as of now due to inflation as well. There isn’t much of a difference between the two mice besides the shape, size, and price. Paying $80 more isn’t worth it if most of the controls, and key features function the same way. Some of the key features that the glorious model o can do as well as the redragon gaming mouse are drag click, butterfly click, has the same amount of sensitivity, and DPI. The main difference between these two desktop gaming mice is that the glorious model “o” feels much lighter and sturdier. The redragon mouse feels a little bit heavier however, it is a decent size for any beginners or experienced gamers. It also has side palm grips for you to keep your thumb, ring finger, and pinky finger on support giving you the most comfortable experience as well. Some of the features that both mice can do that interested buyers would look forward to is having the mouse double click, drag click, and butterfly click. Furthermore, this mouse is very comfortable and durable for a long period of time. The gaming mouse's texture is matte which makes the gaming experience even better. There are also side buttons to change the RGB color or lighting to whichever settings you’d prefer with 7-8 different color options. All of these features are adjustable just by downloading the app or software if needed. After owning this product for 3 years, I have not felt the need to buy another mouse yet at all because of how well-made it is. However, despite all of the pros mentioned, there are always a few flaws or cons since nothing is perfect. One of the cons I experienced by owning this product would be that when gaming, some of the clicks on the redragon gaming mouse don’t register due to how big it is. Even though it is recommended to have lighter-weight desktop mice when gaming, it makes it harder to click while having some clicks not register. Over the past 3 years of owning this product, I have noticed that there is also a solution to fixing this problem. I have improved my gaming skills and it has made clicking faster and much easier for me. I would most definitely recommend this product to gamers who are at least experienced a little bit and have fast clicking hands to enjoy the full experience.

reviews.title: A preference based knockout
reviews.body: To begin- I should state that I've been in the mouse community for a few years now and I've purchased mice from many different brands, big or relatively little. I've used Razer, Logitech, SteelSeries, Zowie, Corsair, Glorious, Pulsar, etc. I always seem to find myself coming back to either Razer or Logitech for specific needs that other brands don't necessarily offer. I have a lengthy history with Razer products, and that includes their Viper line of mice. I've owned the original, the mini, the ultimate edition, the 8khz wired release, as well as the Viper V2 Pro. There was one thing that kept my away from these mice for so long- shape. The original Viper mice, while excellent, weren't good for me comfort wise. The hump wasn't pronounced enough, and the curvature on the sides would cramp my hand every single time. I know, I know- why keep buying a mouse with a shape that makes you uncomfortable? Best answer: I like symmetrical mice, and other than shape, the Viper was/is amazing. Enter the V3 Hyperspeed! I was leaning towards 4.5 stars, but since I can't post a half star I'm comfortable rounding up. The V3 boasts a few changes that, in my personal opinion, are upgrades. The sides of the mouse are less aggressive with their curvature and I found them to be much more comfortable for my hands which are roughly 20x11. They've also done away with any worry of your ring finger clipping the side of your secondary click. They gave this mouse the same treatment the Deathadder V3 pro received. Weight isn't bad at all. It's around 82-83 grams with the included alkaline aa battery. I was able to get it down to a comfortable 70ish by using a lithium aaa and a separate aaa to aa conversion kit. This can be reduced even further by placing a small piece of aluminum foil between the battery(+) and the mouse's contact point. And another point to add- batteries. This mouse is NOT rechargeable, and it does NOT come with any included cables. For some this may be a deal breaker, but for me it's perfect. I don't mind rechargeable mice, but with 4K polling becoming the new " standard " I imagine constant charging could be a nuisance. However, there's a kit on here from PowerOwl that contains 8 aaa batteries and a charging system. I paid around $30 for the rechargeable lithiums and the aaa to aa converters in total. The converters came in a 10 pack so that was nice. This mouse is paired with my Hyperpolling dongle which can be purchased separately, or bundled together with this mouse when purchased from Razer. This. Thing. Is. Insane. When it comes to tracking accuracy I have absolutely nothing bad to say. The Focus Pro 30K in this mouse is the same sensor found in their flagships. Kudos to Razer for implementing that into their Hyperspeed line, which is widely recognized as their budget tier lineup. A few grievances of mine are that M2 ( right mouse click ) is considerably light. It might just be a case of heavy finger, but I found myself accidentally actuating the click at times. The side buttons are different in the fact that they are separated and have a bit of space between them. This is a good change, but I utilize M5 ( front side button ) as a Hypershift key, and it makes it a bit more difficult to hit M4 due to that split in distance. If you don't use Hypershift, then this should be of no concern. My copy has no creaking on the shell, no severe rattle, and the clicks are very crisp. I attribute that to the Gen 2 mechanical switches Razer are using in this mouse. For $70 you can't beat this, in my opinion! You're getting an insane amount of performance for a reasonable price. Pair this with a 4K polling dongle, grab some lithium rechargeable batteries, a few converters and you'll be fragging without the worry of cable drag in no time! Final score: 4.5/5 Amazing job, Razer!

reviews.title: Pleasantly surprised how good it is
reviews.body: For years I have been a fan of the Razer Viper series. I've had a wired version, and now 3 of the original wireless Viper ultimate's, and now this one. I liked the wireless so much even though my wired version still works I bought the first 2 ultimate's to replace it. This is so I had one at home and one at work. Well I lost one of them on a work trip and after years one of them stopped worked (not sure what happened) but it was pretty old at that point). I keep buying the old ultimate version because I like the side grips and don't mind the slight weight increase they bring. The old version is typically cheaper than the newer one anyway and I don't mind the slight weight increase it probably brings. While this version is slightly heavier than my old ultimate and doesn't have the side grips. It's still lighter than many mice out there and still easy to pick up without the side grips. I will spend a little more for the ultimate for my home mouse because I still like it better and it is lighter weight. But for work this is more than sufficient and was much cheaper. The viper series has been known to be one of the top rated mice on the market for years and I will continue to buy it for years to come. Also I don't care about the RGB so its nice this one doesn't come with any. The only downside of that is that its harder to tell when its low on battery. Guess you could say its a double edged sword. The only downside I have to this mouse is I think they removed the side buttons on the right which I frequently used to refresh web pages. But I don't feel the need to do that as often as I used to so I think its a compromise I am willing to make here especially for the price. This is still the most comfortable mice I've ever used, super smooth tracking, built quality is good, and you don't have holes in the mouse which would allow dust to build up inside (let alone if you spilled something in there or had food on your hands. For gaming I'm sure its pretty good although since I use this at the office I haven't tried that yet. But for the price I don't think you can beat this.

reviews.title: Leise Maus mit schickem Design und praktischer Akkustandsanzeige
reviews.body: Ich nutze die Maus jetzt seit einigen Tagen sowohl am Laptop als auch am Tablet und insgesamt macht sie einen wirklich guten Eindruck. Was mir direkt gefallen hat, ist das transparente Design – wirkt mal etwas anders als die üblichen Standardmäuse und sieht auf dem Schreibtisch ziemlich modern aus. Im Alltag war für mich vor allem die leise Bedienung angenehm. Die Klicks sind deutlich gedämpft, sodass man auch abends noch arbeiten kann, ohne dass das ständige Klicken nervt. Gerade im Homeoffice finde ich das echt angenehm. Praktisch ist außerdem, dass man schnell zwischen Bluetooth und dem USB-Dongle wechseln kann. Ich nutze sie tagsüber am PC und zwischendurch am Tablet, das Umschalten klappt unkompliziert und die Verbindung war bisher stabil. Auch die Akkustandsanzeige finde ich hilfreich. So sieht man rechtzeitig, wann geladen werden muss, statt plötzlich ohne Maus dazusitzen. Geladen wird per USB-C, was für mich inzwischen einfach Standard sein sollte. Die Form liegt bei meinen mittelgroßen Händen angenehm in der Hand. Sie ist nicht zu schwer und gleitet sauber über das Mauspad. Für längere Arbeitssessions passt das für mich gut. Insgesamt eine moderne und alltagstaugliche Maus mit leisen Tasten und praktischen Funktionen. Ein paar persönliche Vorlieben spielen natürlich immer mit rein, aber bisher bin ich zufrieden.

La batería también me ha durado más de lo que esperaba; con un uso diario, apenas he tenido que cargarlo.En resumen, es un ratón sencillo pero muy funcional, perfecto para quien busca comodidad, silencio y buena autonomía sin gastar demasiado. Para trabajar, estudiar o llevarlo en la mochila, es una compra muy acertada.

reviews.title: The mouse meets expectations and that is about it.
reviews.body: The mouse meets expectations and that is about it. The mouse works, is lightweight, similar shape to the g pro. The mouse is tiny, because I have bigger hands this made it difficult to operate it. That is mainly a me problem but I do want to mention it for others. Because the mouse is 40 dollars it has its drawbacks. Battery needs to be recharged every week or so, but the cable provided is hardly noticeable unlike the g pro. The mouse buttons feel heavy compared to other mice that I had. There is a lot of wiggle room when it comes to how far you have to press to get the actual actuation. (G pro, G pro superlight, g pro superlight 2, g502 x, model O) The mouse is base side heavy. So the weight of the mouse is not spread out. When you hold the mouse you can tell that you not actually moving the whole mouse. This makes fingertip grip harder to use because you really need to engage your palm to more easily move the base. Its still a light mouse so you can really get away with this. I have not needed to use the bluetooth yet so I have no idea how that latency is. The mouse is tiny, because I have bigger hands this made it difficult to operate it. That is mainly a me problem but I did want to mention it. I have had no issues with connectivity when using the USB into my docking station. The plastic case is cheap . I feel like I could easily bend the plastic just by pushing my thumb into it. Overall, I would say save your money and save up for a mouse that meets all of the criteria, but this isn't a bad mouse for $40

reviews.title: Perfect for my setup
reviews.body: I had to find a fast affordable replacement after my cat suddenly decided that my previous mouse was actual prey and absolutely demolished it. This one is a pretty good weight, which will hopefully save this one from an early demise. It goes to sleep fairly quickly to extend the battery life if you're using it wirelessly like I am, but there's no noticeable delay when you move it again and it wakes up. I have arthritis and typically use a palm grip as opposed to a claw grip on the mouse and it fits in my hand perfectly, plus the little grippy side where the thumb sits helps with control pretty well. The RGB default lighting actually matches the setup I have now, so I don't feel the need to change it unless I decide to change my lighting theme for my whole desk, but there's a little program on the redragon website that's pretty easy to set up and change what the buttons do and the lighting if you so choose. RIP old mouse, long live the redragon. Edit: Purchased July 2024 — Currently August 2025. For the past month or so, the mouse battery has been dying faster and faster. In the beginning, I really only had to charge it once a month with VERY heavy, daily use. Now, I've rarely been playing video games, mostly just using my computer for email and school, and I have to charge it at LEAST once a week. It's such a shame, it was such a good mouse. On the bright side, my cat can't knock it off very easily. RIP redragon too, I guess.
