title: Razer Naga V3 Pro Wireless MMO Gaming Mouse with Swappable Side Plates

reviews.title: I loved my Logitech. This is a viable replacement!
reviews.body: I am a user, and fond lover, of the G502 and G600. When I saw V3 Pro and the feature set, I really wanted to take a dive into the Razer ecosystem and give it a whirl. This one mouse had the features and potential to replace both the G600 and G502 on my desk. While using and trying the mouse, I can say that it does replace both and works as expected. The form may cause other pause, but it comes down to preference and usability. The G502 is a great mouse but was causing wrist issues despite the perfect for. The Naga V3 Pro is slightly smaller than the V2, but it has given me the form of the G600 which tends to be usable longer for me, with the features of the G600 and G502.

reviews.title: I don't like Razer, but this mouse slaps
reviews.body: I was really, really contemplating rating this less because of Razer Synapse 4. I couldn't get button remapping to work in any game at the start, it would only work after I closed Synapse entirely. Profile switching also didn't work. The software took so much finagling and trial and error manually deleting Synapse and re-installing more than once--I even tried deleting Synapse data online from my account via the Privacy Center to no avail. Midway through, I almost just resorted to keeping things on onboard memory and manually switching between games. It was brutal. Thankfully profile switching started working and button remaps followed suit. I don't know how I got it to work, but it works! It handles so well that the pain setting up the software can be forgiven. This is everything I wanted out of my old Logitech G600s, of which I've had several and daily drove for the better part of a decade. I'd always try but ultimately return other MMO mice because I'd always miss ring-finger button. I know I'm not the only one that felt this! It seems like Razer heard our cries and implemented it on this new Naga V3 Pro, even adding the two additional buttons by the left-click button like on the V2 Hyperspeed. My only gripes are that the side buttons aren't as pronounced and contoured as the G600, and the left- and right-mouse clicks are just obnoxiously loud. Travel distance and weight per click as well I'd say aren't great either--maybe better for older MMOs where each click needed to be more deliberate, but a lighter switch would be better for modern MMOs. I guess I'll get used to them. Despite all of that, the fact that in addition to the extra buttons this is wireless AND I can swap plates for other non-MMO games? I can learn to live with this. Logitech really missed out.

reviews.title: Another great Razer Product
reviews.body: I’ve been really impressed with the Razer Naga V3 Pro. My favorite feature is the removable side panels—it’s great being able to switch the button layout depending on what I’m doing. The mouse feels very solid and well-built, and the weight is just right for me. It feels comfortable and controlled without being too light. My only issue has been the 2.4 GHz wireless connection. I haven’t been able to get it to run as smoothly as I’d like, so I normally toggle it over to Bluetooth, which has worked much better for me. Other than that, it’s a solid mouse and I really enjoy using it. Definitely one of my favorite mice I’ve owned.

title: Razer Viper V3 Pro Wireless Esports Gaming Mouse, 54g Lightweight, Black

reviews.title: my review of the razor viper v3 pro
reviews.body: now for my background, i play r6 and csgo, and occasionally roblox shooters. i went from originally a 60g razer orochi v2 using a fingertip grip, and i went to this mouse with a traditional claw. i’ve had this mouse for a few months and i can say that this is a very good and universal shape for all sorts of grips. i have a medium size hand and i can comfortably fingertip and claw this mouse. the coating is lovely and the best i’ve personally felt on a mouse, and i tried the grips but they eventually wear out over time so i don’t recommend using those (the actual mouse texture is better than the grips anyway). now i know this sounds a little ridiculous but moving from a 60g small mouse not even including the batteries, i played a LOT better with this bigger one after adjusting and i’m honestly happy with my purchase (even though it cost quite a bit). it feels light in the hand for the size and the weight is flawlessly distributed. the skates are solid for being stock but you can always upgrade, the scroll wheel is pretty normal and has distinctive bumps per scroll but personally i like more smoother ones (i am probably just being nitpicky). the main clicks are lovely to hear and the little dongle included doesn’t take up too much space, i’d say only the actual cable itself does but this isn’t actually an issue. the dongle can also support up to 8k hz which isn’t necessary but it’s a “nice to have” feature and i use 2k hz myself to save battery life; speaking of battery life it’s pretty good and i suggest not using 8k since it drains it pretty fast but it lasts up to a week or two for me with regular use not charging (just remember to plug it in after use) the side buttons are a DEFINITE improvement from my old mouse and that was a perfect feature on the mouse. now, razer’s synapse software can be a little finicky sometimes but i suggest just configuring your settings and uninstalling it since it can take up some of your ram and overall performance. in conclusion, this is a really good option for gaming mice and it can fit a LOT of playstyles. this has all of the latest mouse tech (might be a little outdated for me to be saying that in the big 25 now) and each part of the mouse is very pleasant to use. i suggest this mouse if you have the money (it is pretty ehh value for money but as long as you have the funds it’s a s tier mouse)

reviews.title: Highly recommend for competitive gamers.
reviews.body: (Review from my 15 year old son) Honestly this mouse felt SO much lighter than I thought it would. I just upgraded from the Glorious Model O- Wireless Gaming Mouse, and let me say... the upgrade was WORTH it for sure. I pretty much only play Fortnite on Keyboard and Mouse, and I was having issues with my side buttons on my old mouse. I decided it was time to upgrade since I can't have those issues happening mid-game. The Razer Viper V3 Pro, is definitely a solid upgrade. The side buttons are so much more solid than the side buttons on my old mouse. Not to mention, the response time of the clicks was faster, and the accuracy of my aim with the better sensor was so much better. The scroll wheel is also very responsive and fast which is important for Fortnite. (I was able to easily quad edit in Fortnite when using this new mouse) The wireless connectivity isn't even noticeable at all. The response time is insane for a wireless mouse, and it surprised me a lot. I don't have a lot to say about the battery life yet, as this is my first day using it. I will say though, I charged the mouse to 68%, used it for an hour in Fortnite, and the battery was only 67% afterwards. Here are the few cons I can think of: When switching from whatever mouse you currently use, it will take a few hours or even a day to adjust to the lightness of the mouse. (mainly if you played on heavier mice before) It's not anything with the mouse itself, but just a matter of adjusting to the feel of the new mouse. The mouse comes with some grip tape you can put on the mouse, which honestly looks really cool in my opinion, and it really helps with making sure your aim is as good as it can be, since your hand won't slip off the mouse. (See image) (Note: mouse is charging) Razer also has a good software which allows you to adjust the mouse to match the feel of your old one which is really helpful to make sure you don't have to COMPLETELY start over with learning a sensitivity. Overall a really good mouse, no complaints to be honest.

reviews.title: Expensive, but great mouse.
reviews.body: The Razer Viper V3 has been an excellent mouse for both gaming and everyday use. It feels very lightweight and comfortable in hand, making long sessions easy with no fatigue. The shape is simple but very ergonomic, and it works well for both claw and fingertip grip styles. Performance wise, the sensor is extremely accurate and responsive. Tracking is smooth, clicks feel crisp, and there is no noticeable delay. The wireless connection is stable and reliable, with no lag or dropouts. Battery life has also been great, lasting several days of heavy use without needing frequent charging. Build quality feels solid, and the mouse buttons and scroll wheel all feel well made. Overall, the Viper V3 delivers excellent performance, comfort, and reliability. It is a great choice for anyone looking for a high quality lightweight gaming mouse.

reviews.title: Good claw grip mouse
reviews.body: I had a Logitech superlight and moved to the Viper v3 pro. It was the best decision that I have ever made. The mouse sensor in my opinion is more accurate the Logitech mice. The feel and texture and material of the mouse feels very nice especially the white coating option is phenomenal and has really good grip for a very low amount of weight gain. The size definitely favors mid-big hands and excels in the Claw grip. It isn't the lightest mouse on the market but it still in my opinion is more than light enough for most. The scroll wheel actually feels quite nice and i prefer it over the Logitech one. Though this mouse supports 8k polling I rarely find myself using it as it drains battery too fast, I would just use 4000/2000 if you want a high enough speed with a very long battery life. If you are looking for a high quality claw grip mouse then this is the mouse for you, if you don't have a claw grip I would recommend looking at other mice that might be for you.

reviews.title: Most satisfying mouse I have ever used; full stop.
reviews.body: As someone who loves the Superlight and has been jamming out with version 2 of it along with a Logitech Pro X TKL paired with it, it's been nice to swap back to my Black Widow V4 along with the Viper Pro 3. Right out of the box, and I am someone with medium to large hands, this mouse is just a pure delight to hold; it's not often I can say that my hands feel like they disappear when using a peripheral, but this mouse and the Superlight from Logi are the two mice that achieve that for me. Razer knew what they were doing here and it shows in the product; this will be my go-to mouse and I will alternate my Razer setup back to the Logitech set up as the mood strikes me to change things up week by week. When it comes time for the Wooting 80HE to arrive, I will most likely be pairing the Viper Pro 3 with that board due to just how consistently good it feels; I am 3 hours deep into a play session and the battery is down to 98% and I'm using the 4K polling rate; not going to bother with 8K just yet. It's hard to put into words here just how good the slight ergo shape of this mouse feels; I really have tried a number of different mice and this could be "the one"; I don't say this in a hyperbolic fashion either. It's rare that you use a gaming device where you just forget what you're using because it seamlessly blends into the play session. For anyone looking to try this out, the asking price is steep. For a low frills mouse in the aesthetic department it really isn't going to be winning wards for it's design change to be not as sharp as it's predecessor. I for one really dig the smoother design and the light hump towards the back of the mouse, the finger ridges, or whatever you want to call them, on the L + R mouse clicks, all come together to suit whatever combination of grip you want to employ here. I am using a light palm grip and find that going claw and then relaxing my fingers feel natural. The side buttons deserve a special award here; they are separated ever so slightly and their clicks are immediate / responsive. Truly the only gripe I have with my Superlight are the side buttons; Logitech really needs to take the oatmeal mush out of those and it will be a near perfect mouse for me. Really curious to see what kind of competition this will spur with other manufacturers; that said, and for now, this is the best of the best for something that is here, on Amazon, that you can order and have by tomorrow while it's in stock. To whoever nabs one, enjoy; curious to see other reviews pop up on here.

reviews.title: Best Gaming Mouse for Claw and Fingertip grip
reviews.body: TLDR: Good mouse, great quality for price, beautiful designs, 10/10 The Razer Viper V3 Pro is probably the best gaming mouse hands down. It’s ultra lightweight, feels amazing to move around, and extremely responsive. The clicks are a little on the louder side, the material is smooth and not particularly grippy, so if you prefer grippier mice, there are those grip stickers that you can put on. I have an average adult male sized hand. In terms of what type of grip you use (claw, palm, etc..) this mouse is definitely a claw or fingertip type of mouse. Palm grip doesn’t feel amazing on this mouse since it’s a little small in my opinion. There’s also no “ergonomic” shape like the razer deathadder, so if you’re a claw or fingertip type grip person, this is probably the best mouse on the market you can get. (Please do check measurements to compare with your own hand size) I got the faker edition due to his iconic style, and it’s a beautiful red with a stunning demon art design. Overall it’s a high end mouse with high end performance, the mouse is definitely equal value to the price. For league players out there: I ranked up from Platinum to Emerald after I got this mouse (not saying it does wonders lol)

reviews.title: Light with great battery life
reviews.body: I have had this mouse for about a year now and use it as my daily driver, and I love it. It is really light and glides across the mouse pad. The mouse wheel is not noisy at all and neither is the clicking of the mouse buttons imo. The battery life is good lasting more than a few all day play sessions, and a couple of weeks of light use. It comes with some little adhesive pads that you can place on the mouse which I would recommend using as the mouse is very smooth. My complaints are that the mouse gets clammy feeling after a while. Not a huge deal, but I have thought of buying another adhesive pad to go over the emblem because it gets to feel gross. I do clean it, but this is the only mouse I have ever had this issue with. Also the dongle is kind of a pain if you have OCD, it is hard to get it to lay flat down. Overall I love the mouse and think it is worth the money. I would just recommend buying an adhesive patch (I'm not sure what they are really called) to go over the razer emblem as that part can start to feel gross.

reviews.title: Surprisingly lightweight, good polling rate and no wifi-interference!
reviews.body: So far so good. I was impressed on how light this mouse felt when I used it for the first time. You can definitely feel the extra accuracy when you aim, by that I mean every small movement you make on your mousepad translates exactly as you would expect on the screen. My router and modem are right under my desk and I don't get any interference. I don't open the program that comes with it (synapse) because I used a wired headset with it (razer blackshark v2 X) and I don't want synapse messing the audio settings of my headset since the default option is pretty good. The battery works for a long time; I used it for like 3 consecutive days and when I open synapse to check battery is about 70% (I use 2k polling rate). Clicking sounds satisfying as you would expect from an expensive mouse. Your forearm gets considerably less tired. The side buttons and click buttons have not collected any dust or grime from my hands, unlike my old mouse did.

title: Logitech G502 X Plus Wireless RGB Gaming Mouse - Black

reviews.title: G502 X Plus -- A Worthy successor to earlier G502's for FPS games
reviews.body: The 2022 Logitech G502 X Plus was a very pleasant surprise. It is replacing a Logitech G-Pro that is roughly 80 grams weight on a Logitech Powerplay mouse pad (expanded cover for extra space and non-stop charging), primarily used for Overwatch2. Other gaming mice in my collection include earlier G502's, G903, Razer Death Adder + Copperhead, Steelseries Rival3 and Rival600, etc. Generally the best performers in FPS games are the lightest units with the best optical sensors, and the G502 X Plus definitely fits that criteria. Pros: -Comfortable ergonomic shape for marathon gaming sessions -PTFE mouse feet for super-smooth glide across mouse pads -The new optical hybrid switches are incredibly fast compared to the G-Pro's older Omron switches, with a nice crisp click and improved actuation. They will last much longer than conventional mechanical switches and correct double-clicking issues. My last G-Pro's right rear thumb switch suffered from double-clicking issues since they were the old Omron mechanicals that wore out from constant use. -Nice RGB lighting if you are looking for that kind of bling -This mouse wakes from sleep mode instantly (like the G-Pro series). The old G502 Hero Wireless required a full second to wake up, making the old sleep mode feature extremely inconvenient and annoying. -At 106 grams list weight, the G502 X Plus is a tad heavier for a gaming mouse. However, coming from an 80 gram G-Pro, I notice better aim stability without sacrificing flick aim consistency. With the Powerplay charging puck attached and USB receiver stored inside, the G502 X Plus hits 110g on my postal scale. The G502 Hero wireless is 120g with the same accessories. Cons: -No more adjustable weights like its predecessor G502, but to be fair, the whole e-sport industry has shifted competitive user demand to lighter weight mice for the fastest aim flicks possible. -Battery power drains faster with RGB lighting at full settings. This is mitigated by reducing RBG brightness to 85% and shortening idle-mode entry from 2 minutes down to 1. Using a Logitech Powerplay mouse pad, my mouse battery power hovers around 78% to 90% steady with RGB enabled. -The mouse's black finish tends to have shiny oil stains and wear marks over time. This is why I apply blue painter's tape to the areas most prone to this issue. EDIT Feb 2024 - I've replaced the blue painter's tape with automotive carbon fiber vinyl wrap for better visual appeal. Not recommended if you do not like the feel of textured carbon fiber, but it definitely gets rid of those shiny oil stains. Picture attached. -GHub software will not allow users less than 3 DPI presets, and all of these have to be different values at 50dpi intervals. I tried to "lock" my mouse at 1000dpi to avoid accidental DPI switching, but the software would not allow me to do this, so I ended up moving my DPI cycling button to the default profile button up top and removing the up/down DPI adjustment buttons next to the left click. This gave me two additional buttons for other programable functions (like Alt and middle-mouse click since pressing the mouse wheel down can feel awkward). EDIT -- GHUB finally fixed this issue. I can now run with just 1000dpi single setting. -The new hybrid mechanical switches have a different click sound compared to conventional switches -- not really louder, but definitely more metallic. Yes, this mouse is expensive, but the combination of lighter weight + excellent ergonomics + fast/crisp long-wear switches makes this model very hard to beat. If you are looking for a mouse with more weight and heft, then you may not be happy with the G502 X since the latest model has been redesigned for the e-sports crowd. The G502 X now combines lighter weight with an ergo shape, something that most ultra-light mouse offerings lack. NOTE: If you want the best wireless mouse experience, I recommend pairing the G502 X Plus with a Logitech Powerplay for non-stop wireless charging while using the mouse. For those that want a larger mouse pad than what the default Powerplay size offers, check out "Logitech powerplay mousepad expansion mod" on youtube. I have my set-up displayed in the attached images along with actual weight compared to the old G502 Wireless. Update 4/26/2023: The Glorious XL mousepad is the perfect thickness for this Powerplay expansion mod. EDIT: I just read a few other reviews claiming that the G502 X feels "cheap" because it feels too light. The whole point of lowering mouse weight is to minimize mass, thereby requiring less physical energy / effort to move the mouse quickly and accurately. This is how modern e-sports mice are designed, because a lighter mouse is a faster mouse, while a heavier one is a slower boat anchor that is usually on the losing end of an FPS fire fight. The G502 X Plus is only 10 grams lighter than the G502 hero, yet it is much easier to flick-aim than the older G502 Hero Wireless. Also, if you want RGB on the G502 X, you have to get the Plus edition, other wise you get no RGB. Yet one newer review complained about missing RGB LED's on his G502 X non-Plus edition. Going no-RGB is still a valid choice since it saves a few grams, extends battery life, and costs less, but just make sure you know what you are buying ahead of time. ;)

reviews.title: Exactly what you would expect from a direct upgrade.
reviews.body: TBH if your looking for a G502/HERO/Lightspeed replacement there is no complaints in my opinion. Its just a hair bit wider then the previous 502s almost unnoticeable but if you hold them together there is a slight difference. The battery life for it so far has been good for me only been having to charge it like once a week it feels like. It feels like a upgraded 502 lightspeed which is what is. I like that they gave us a option to replace the thumb button with a flat cover that matches the mouse curve so you dont have to have the thumb button for those of us like myself who accidentally press it and never actually use it. Compared to what we paid at launch for the g502 it feels comparable for value and performance. The scroll wheel feels like a nice upgrade from the deep groves to more of a slightly grooved surface thats easy to catch with your finger without issues. The only thing could probably complain about is lack of weights for those who like the weighted options is not super light but its definitely not as heavy as the previous models so people who like the weight of the 502 hero or lightspeed with weights it is gonna be lighter. I like how they changed the charging cable over to the C type charger just like the G733 headphones it still slides it like before but its alot easier to slide in and out and the cable has a good hold when plug in without that feeling like you might rip it if you pull to hard. Other than that software wise minus the RBG change on the body of the mouse it does everything the same as the HERO and Lightspeed models so its pretty much a direct upgrade and replace without having to relearn or figure new stuff out.

reviews.title: Great gaming mouse
reviews.body: I've been using the Logitech G502 X Plus for about a week now, and it's been excellent so far. I came from an older gaming mouse, and the difference was noticeable right away. Everything feels incredibly smooth and responsive, whether I'm gaming or just using my computer for everyday tasks. Setup couldn't have been easier. I plugged in the wireless receiver, turned the mouse on, and it worked immediately. It was truly plug and play. Installing Logitech G HUB was simple too, and customizing the buttons and RGB lighting only took a few minutes. The mouse feels very well built and comfortable to use, even during longer gaming sessions. The clicks are crisp, the scroll wheel feels solid, and the sensor tracks flawlessly. I also really like having the extra programmable buttons. They've already become useful for both gaming and general productivity. While I can't speak to the long term durability yet, my first impression has been extremely positive. I honestly don't have any complaints so far. If it continues performing this well over time, it'll easily be one of the best gaming mice I've owned. If you're looking for a high quality wireless gaming mouse that's easy to set up and performs exactly as you'd expect, I'd definitely recommend giving this one a look.

reviews.title: My New Gaming Sidekick: The Logitech G502 X Plus!
reviews.body: Alright, let's talk about the new star of my desk setup – the Logitech G502 X Plus Wireless Gaming Mouse. As someone who spends a good chunk of time in front of the PC, this isn't just a peripheral; it's practically an extension of my hand, and honestly, it feels like it was designed specifically for me. First off, the wireless freedom is a game-changer (pun absolutely intended). Ditching the cable is just chef's kiss for decluttering and those intense gaming sessions where every millisecond counts. And the LIGHTSPEED Optical connection? Flawless. There's no perceptible lag, no hiccups, just pure, unadulterated responsiveness. My old M720 Triathlon is still great for everyday use, and it's my go-to when this beast needs a charge, but for serious pixel-peeping and headshot hunting, the G502 X Plus blows it out of the water. The HERO 25K Sensor is no joke. I'm talking pinpoint accuracy that makes navigating my Alienware 38 Curved and 34 QD-OLED monitors feel like butter. Whether I'm trying to land that perfect shot or meticulously editing a document, this mouse tracks like a dream. And the LIGHTFORCE Switches? Every click feels crisp and satisfying, giving you that tactile feedback that just confirms your action. No mushiness here, just pure, responsive clicks. Then there's the LIGHTSYNC RGB. Look, I appreciate a bit of flair, and this mouse delivers without being over the top. It adds that perfect touch of gaming aesthetic, syncing up with the rest of my setup, like my Gimars RGB Gaming Mouse Pad. It just makes the whole experience feel more immersive and, frankly, cooler. This mouse just fits. The ergonomic design feels great in my hand, even during those extended sessions. It's not too light, not too heavy, and the button placement feels intuitive. It's built for comfort and performance, and you can really tell. In short, if you're serious about your PC experience, especially gaming, the Logitech G502 X Plus is an absolute winner. It's fast, accurate, comfortable, and looks damn good doing it. My gaming setup feels complete with this bad boy. Highly recommend it to anyone looking for a top-tier wireless gaming mouse!

reviews.body: Good mouse, i like it. the buttons are useful, its ergonomic for long sessions, the lighting is cool (even if you can’t see it while using it) and i put some glass skates on and some grip tape to protect the grey rubber grips it already has. the wireless or wired option is great and the battery genuinely lasts a really long time, i charge it like once a week and it charges quick too. only complaint is the software you need to use to set up your dpi settings and lighting and all that is GARBAGE it’s soo bad! they really need to improve the software so for that reason its 4 stars, its that bad.

reviews.title: Gamer Requested and Gamer Approved
reviews.body: I bought this as a gift for a gamer who specifically requested this mouse, so expectations were already pretty high. It ended up being a great gift and they were very happy with it. They especially liked the feel and responsiveness for gaming, along with the wireless design and RGB lighting. When someone who games regularly asks for a specific mouse and loves it once they get it, I’d say that’s a win!

reviews.title: Avoid. The G-Hub software simply does not work.
reviews.body: Title says it all. I bought 2 of these, figuring I could sync profiles between my desktop and laptop gaming systems. The mouse is mechanically well built, but there are plenty of mice that are mechanically just as good. If you're buying a gaming mouse with all the extra buttons, then you probably play more than one video game... which requires software to change the "profile" or button functions for each different game... and that's where this mouse falls apart. The G-hub software seems designed to do everything Except what you want to do: -You want to change button functions? By Yourself? Gosh, even if you do figure out the interface and psychically intuit that the keys have to be drag/dropped onto the buttons to change them, they still won't change. I mean, why would you need to? We scanned all software on your hard drive and sent the list to our marketing dept, and they auto-set profiles that work great! They promise! -You want to unlock the profile so you can change the button settings? Aw, too bad choom. It's locked because, um, we felt it was necessary to lock the buttons for some reason. Like you might accidentally open this software and accidentally drag/drop functions you didn't really mean to change. Best to leave it locked, for your own good. -You want to change profiles? Oh, sure you can do that. Until you navigate away from G-hub and then it "helps" by auto-changing the profile back to Default! No worries, our marketing team has your back. I mean, they are gaming experts! You should SEE their score on Candy Crush! -You still want to change profiles? Why? I mean, we auto-detect the application for you! Spent a lot of money on that, choom. Why you wanna mess that up? -Want to sync your gaming profiles across two computers? Yeah, we know you tied your G-hub software to your logitech account and thanks so much for that data pipe from your computer to the cloud, but really, our marketing department NEEDS that so they can gather data from your system. You know, to uh... track performance and issues and stuff. We're afraid there just isn't the bandwidth to move your settings to the cloud and over to a whole other device. Sorries, but like we said, our software auto-detects and auto-sets the prefect settinz 4 U! We are soo accurat, and xcelnt qualitee! Promize! So the G-hub software is crap designed by idiots, but don't listen to me. I only have a BA in Computer Science and 24 years experience working in IT, and played video games since Dungeons of Daggorath on the TRS-80. But be my guest and google "Manual for G HUB?" for yourself. Do yourself a favor - buy 3 mice for this price and throw the two worst ones away. You will STILL be money ahead, and have a way better experience. At least until Logitech hires an actual software interface designer.

reviews.title: G502 HERO but less wires. Weight (or lack thereof) could be a pro/con
reviews.body: Fantastic mouse that cleaned up my setup while keeping the in-hand familiarity of the wired G502 HERO, shape and free spinning scroll wheel and all. Battery life is very long subject to personal usage differences of course, I plug it in when the battery indicator turns red maybe for a few hours and it's back up to full and that's maybe one a week or so with moderate to heavy usage. Wireless performance is fantastic, no issues there. The weight of the mouse is *very* light, that can either be a pro or a con: If you want something you can move effortlessly for high speed gaming performance you'll love it. If you're like me and likes a weighted sturdy mouse, and used the G502 HERO with all of the weights installed, you might not be happy. However, there are 3rd party weights you can buy here on Amazon that seamlessly integrate into the magnetic lid underneath for the dongle storage. With one of those installed it's no longer flying off of my keyboard tray and it's just as comfortable as the old version without the limits and mess of a wire.

reviews.title: Excellent wireless mouse for gaming
reviews.body: I got this when it was on sale and boy oh boy I LOVE using this mouse for playing games! Very accurate, no lags whatsoever, easy to configure using the desktop app of Logitech. The rgb lights are just perfect adding accent to the mouse’s design - I hate too much lights in the mouse as if it becomes like a christmas light. It has on and off switch but it does go auto sleep if you left it on so another plus to that feature! Charging takes a bit but faster than other wireless mouse. Battery life is great (would last for more than a week playing games a couple hours a day) I have big hands and mouse felt nicely (not too small and not big either) Only comment I will add is that I don’t think it was worth the full price but if you see it go on sale for like 25% or more, heck yeah add to cart and checkout right away!!!

reviews.body: Accurate nice size for a palm grip especially for bigger hands, notice the button under the scroll wheel to switch the wheel's rigidity. The infinite scroll thing is a gimmick. Overall great mouse for gaming or productivity, I wish it had a bluetooth + wireless dongle option.

title: Logitech G PRO X Superlight 2 Wireless Gaming Mouse - Black

reviews.title: Lightweight, Fast, and Worth It
reviews.body: The G PRO X Superlight 2 is an excellent gaming mouse. It’s incredibly lightweight, tracks flawlessly, and feels very responsive in fast-paced games. The battery life is great, the shape is comfortable for long sessions, and the build quality feels premium. It’s expensive, but if you’re serious about gaming, it’s absolutely worth the investment.

reviews.title: Crazy light and perfect for gaming
reviews.body: I have been using this mouse for a couple weeks now and honestly it has been amazing. The first thing you notice is how light it is. It almost feels like nothing in your hand which made a huge difference for me in FPS games and even just normal computer use. My aim feels smoother and my wrist does not get tired after long sessions. As someone who games in the mornings before studying or rotations, it has been a really nice upgrade. The clicks feel super crisp and responsive and the wireless connection has been flawless so far. No lag, no random disconnects, and the battery life has been better than I expected. The shape is comfortable even after hours of use and it fits well for both claw and palm grip. Setup was simple and the software was easy to use to adjust DPI and buttons. Overall this is easily one of the best mice I have owned. It feels premium, performs great, and actually made gaming more enjoyable for me. If you are thinking about upgrading your mouse, especially for competitive games, I would definitely recommend this one.

reviews.title: Crisp, Precise, and Worth Every Dollar!!
reviews.body: The Logitech G Pro X Superlight 2 is easily one of the best mice I’ve used. It’s extremely light without feeling cheap, and the sensor performance is outstanding. When paired with a glass mouse pad, the glide is insanely smooth and tracking feels incredibly clean and precise. Because I have larger hands, I added grip tape and highly recommend it for anyone in the same boat. Without grip tape I had to grip the mouse tighter than I liked, but with it, control and comfort improved immediately. Combined with the crisp clicks, reliable wireless performance, and long battery life, this mouse delivers exactly what it promises. Pricey, but well worth it.

reviews.title: Exceptional Performance and Comfort
reviews.body: As an avid gamer, I can confidently say that the Logitech G PRO X SUPERLIGHT Gaming Mouse is a game-changer. From its lightweight design to its impressive performance, this mouse has exceeded all my expectations. First and foremost, the weight of this mouse is a standout feature. Weighing in at just under 63 grams, it’s incredibly lightweight, allowing for swift and precise movements during intense gaming sessions. Whether I’m engaging in fast-paced FPS games or executing intricate maneuvers in strategy games, the mouse feels like an extension of my hand, offering unparalleled control and agility. The HERO 2 Sensor with a staggering 32,000 DPI ensures pixel-perfect accuracy, translating every subtle movement into smooth, responsive cursor action on the screen. Combined with the LIGHTFORCE Hybrid Switches, which deliver ultra-fast click response and exceptional durability, every click feels satisfyingly tactile and precise. The 4K polling rate further enhances the responsiveness of the mouse, minimizing input lag and ensuring that my actions are registered instantaneously. This is crucial in competitive gaming, where split-second decisions can make all the difference between victory and defeat. In addition to its performance, the design of the Logitech G PRO X SUPERLIGHT is ergonomic and comfortable, featuring a streamlined shape that fits snugly in the hand. The ambidextrous design ensures that both left-handed and right-handed gamers can enjoy the same level of comfort and control. Furthermore, the customizable button layout and onboard memory allow me to tailor the mouse to my preferred gaming style, with up to 5 programmable buttons for easy access to essential commands and macros. Overall, the Logitech G PRO X SUPERLIGHT Gaming Mouse has truly elevated my gaming experience. Its combination of lightweight design, exceptional performance, and ergonomic comfort make it a must-have for any serious gamer looking to gain a competitive edge. Whether you’re a casual gamer or a professional esports athlete, this mouse delivers in every aspect, making it well worth the investment. Highly recommended.

reviews.title: Lightweight gaming mouse. Mouse size is decent for small hands.
reviews.body: Been using this mouse for about 6 months for work, school, and gaming. The mouse size is alright. I have small hands, and my hand doesn't get sore or strained using it for several hours. It has decent ergonomics. The clicks are much quieter than a Razer Viper V3 Pro. The sound clicks are as "loud" as linear switches (which are fairly quiet) if noise level is a concern for you. I prefer quieter, but tactile clicks, which this mouse does quite nicely. The mouse clicks don't bother me when I'm working at night. Battery life lasts quite a long time for this mouse. I can use this mouse for a couple of days (or even a week, if I'm taking breaks) without having to charge it. On Logitech G HUB, it says the battery life lasts for approximately 96 hours. You'd have to download Logitech G HUB to customize macros and set sensitivity on the mouse. If you're using this mouse for mainly gaming, make sure to go to "Device Settings" and under "Lightforce Switch" set it to "Optical Only". This will decrease battery life, but will utilize the full performance of the optical switch and has lower latency. My only gripes are the Logitech G HUB is glitchy sometimes and certain game profiles don't automatically switch over, like when I tab in and out between the desktop and Fortnite, and the software doesn't automatically switch to the "Fortnite" profile, and the side buttons feel a bit mushy when building and editing in Fortnite. The side buttons could be a bit crispier. Overall, this mouse does the job and excels for gaming, especially FPS and fast-paced games.

reviews.title: Sleek, Compatible, and Improvements to FPS Gaming Performance by a Long Shot!
reviews.body: I recently upgraded my gaming setup with the Logitech Gaming Pro X Superlight 2, and I couldn't be happier with my purchase! This mouse has truly elevated my gaming experience to a whole new level, especially with the dramatic increase in my FPS capabilities. First and foremost, the wireless capability is outstanding. The Superlight 2 offers a lag-free connection, providing the responsiveness needed for competitive gaming. The design of the mouse is sleek and ergonomic, fitting comfortably in my hand for extended gaming sessions. The lightweight construction is a game-changer, allowing for swift and precise movements without any fatigue. The HERO sensor technology that Logitech markets and promotes, I thought it was just another silly gimmick when I read its specifications at first glance. After a couple of gaming sessions, the sensor on this mouse delivers incredible accuracy, ensuring that every movement is translated with precision on-screen. The Pro X Superlight 2 keeps up flawlessly with extremely good pinpoint accuracy. Also, the Battery life is impressive, lasting for extended periods without the need for frequent recharging. This is particularly useful during those intense gaming marathons where every minute counts. When it comes to the smoothness and curved ergonomics of the build, it truly feels solid, and the buttons have a satisfying click. It gives me confidence that this mouse will withstand the test of time. The Logitech Gaming Pro X Superlight 2 has exceeded my expectations in every aspect. It's a top-notch wireless gaming mouse that combines cutting-edge technology with a sleek design. If you're serious about improving your FPS gaming and want a mouse that delivers exceptional performance, the Pro X Superlight 2 is the way to go.

reviews.title: Logitech still hasn't gotten their quality control in line over the last 6 years of making mice.
reviews.body: About 6 years ago I bought a g pro wireless, the first one had an issue with double clicking with the primary left click AND the middle click. That developed after ~4-7 days of use. Logitech RMA'd it and sent me a new mouse. This second mouse immediately had issues with the left click where it was mushy and had significant travel past the actual click sound. They RMA'd this one too. Finally by the third mouse I got one that worked good, no double clicking, no middle mouse button issues..... for maybe 2.5 years. 0.5 years past the warranty period. I lived with the mouse button issues for a while until it became unbearable to the point where I can't reliably move the camera anymore in league of legends, or rotate the camera in many 3rd person games/3d software. I decided to get this mouse (G PRO X SUPERLIGHT 2) to replace the aged g pro wireless. It seems logitech has learned absolutely nothing in their quality control department over the years. This mouse that I just got ALREADY has scroll wheel decoder issues where it scrolls in the opposite direction briefly before scrolling in the correct direction. Secondly, it has a squealing noise as a scroll upwards that is already unbearable to listen to. I've had enough of logitech mice. I hate the situation because I love the G pro's shape and feel. The silver lining is that there are MANY competing mice now that offer great performance for less, or about the same amount of money which copied the shape and feel. This will likely be the last logitech mouse I buy and am returning it. Razer Viper V3 pro here I come. These issues I have with quality aren't the only things that are a negative about this mouse. Compared to its predecessor, the g pro wireless, the mouse buttons are much louder and slightly heavier. I didn't mind the noise nor the heavier clicks as they were only marginally heavier to press, but this is a big complaint many gpw/gpx1 -> gpx2 users have complained about. Maybe I don't mind it because I tried putting TTC gold 80M switches in my old GPW but promptly switched back to my broken middle mouse button because the TTC gold 80M's are massive (and LOUD) BRICKS you have to press down to actuate the button. Insanely heavy, horrible switches, absolutely horrible. The worst switches the world has ever seen. I challenge anyone complaining about the GPX2's switches to try those absolute monsters out. But I digress. Another issue I had with the mouse was the removal of the DPI button, which wasn't the end of the world because I created a macro I found on reddit to cycle through them. It worked fine for the small number of occasions I needed to switch the DPI but the one button was easier.

reviews.title: Great for fps, ok for work, same issues as other mice
reviews.body: Using this for work and various video games (cs). Very light mouse, almost feels like air. Build quality is excellent, the materials are pleasant to the touch. The sensor is very precise and smooth, this mouse wont let you down in a clutch. No issues with battery life (multiple full days), just keep a usb-c cable nearby. My phone charger is multipurpose now, phone/headset/mouse. The only issue is the middle click (mouse3): when held down, it can register multiple clicks when slightly changing pressure. For gaming, no big deal; for working, very lame (can close/open multiple tabs by accident). From forums/reddit, this is common to most (if not all) superlights. I've used the superlight for several months now with no new issues (other than the middle button). Before this, I've had at least seven wired and later wireless g703s. Something usually breaks within a year or so (left/right double clicking, mouse wheel issues, etc.). I expect the same for the superlight. That's gaming, cant help it. Might sound bad, but both g703 and superlight are excellent mice. With heavy use, it is inevitable that something breaks eventually. If looking for cheaper mice, g703 is a heavier alternative. pros: -"super light" -great sensor -no issues with logitech drivers -logitech good customer service (can RMA, I got like 3 free g703 after issues with the purchased ones) cons: -no dpi shift button -inconsistent middle mouse, can register multiple clicks while holding m3 down (without letting go) -scroll wheel feedback is somewhat weak

reviews.title: Solid Mouse, But Time for a Price Drop
reviews.body: I got the G PRO X SUPERLIGHT 2, and it's pretty great. First off it's insanely lightweight, which is a great touch if you're into quick movements. Feels good in the hand and is super responsive. The battery life is solid too, it holds charge for a decent amount of time, and when you do need to charge it, it's fast. Build quality seems sturdy, like it won’t just fall apart if you’re a bit rough with it. That said, for how good it is, there are a lot of other mice out there offering similar stuff at cheaper prices now. I still like it, but honestly, it might be time for Logitech to consider bringing the price down a notch with all the competition around. It’s still worth it, just... a little less of a splurge would be nice.

reviews.title: Phenomenal value
reviews.body: I was really blown away with this mouse to be quite honest. For what you pay, you get awesome value which is something that is lost today in most consumer of products. This mouse is a tad bit smaller than the Superlight 2 in width and length, and has a slightly lower hump in the back. The skates feel really decent just be sure and remove the very fine plastic covering from them like i didn't for the first week (they were hard to see & i didn't know they were on) I really enjoyed using this mouse because despite the click latency which really isn't a big deal unless your competing, the mouse performs amicably. reviews.title: Based on Parade PS188 - must use 140W capable laptop to get 125W charging
reviews.body: One of the first compact portable hubs with PD3.1/EPR charging capabilities. It is based on the Parade PS188 USB 3.2 w/DisplayPort hub solution and is is a re-brand of the OEM WinStars WS-UHP3415L model. I reached out to MintHouz to get more details about the hub, and they responded quickly and with deep technical detail which was greatly appreciated. The specs don't call it out clearly enough, so here is what it should say: - The Minthouz hub reserves 15W of power which is a good approach. The power to charge your laptop will always be 15W less than what the hub negotiates with the connected USB-C power supply. For example, with a 100W PSU, you can charge the laptop at a max of 85W. This ensures the power supply is not overloaded when you use the USB ports on the hub. - If you connect a 140W power supply to the hub, but a laptop that can only accept 100W max (20V @ 5A), then the laptop will only charge at 85W. This is because the hub will only negotiate a 20V link to the power supply to match the connected laptop. This is the intended behaviour for similar 140W capable hubs. - The only way to get 125W charging is to use a 140W power supply and a laptop like a MacBook Pro, Framework, MSI gaming, or Thunderobot -6 that ships with a 140W or 180W USB-C power supply in the box.

reviews.title: Exceptional
reviews.body: This Minthouz 5-in-1 docking station's current price of £29.99 is a bit steep but the product's quality can't be faulted, so it warrants a higher price than flimsy lower-spec 5-in-1 hubs. For example, this docking station has a high-quality braided nylon cable. Braided cables are more durable and resilient than their non-braided competitors. They withstand bending and tangling extremely well. Conseuently, they last longer than inferior cables. The docking station has an aluminium shell. That's an ideal material for the job, because aluminium is light yet structurally strong, plus its conductive properties make it an effective heat dissipator. The spec of the docking station is excellent. The USB Gen 3.2 ports (one USB-A, one USB-C) allow super-fast data transfer. There's also a Gen 2.0 USB-A port, which is ideal for connecting a keyboard or mouse (USB Gen 2.0 is more stable than higher Gens for this purpose). The Gen 3.1 USB-C 140W PD (power delivery) port is a cut above the usual PD ports on docking stations (the present norm is 100W USB-C Gen 3.0). The HDMI port can deliver 4K@60Hz video - in other words, resolution of 3840p x 2160p, at a refresh rate of 60 frames per second. Bear in mind that in order to achieve 4K@60Hz, the connected monitor must be capable of that performance, as must the HDMI cable you use. Standard HDMI cables deliver a maximum resolution of 720p or 1080i at a maximum refresh rate of 30Hz. High-Speed HDMI cables are capable of 4K resolution have a maximum refresh rate of 30Hz. If you want to enjoy 4K@60Hz, you need to use a cable rated as Premium-High Speed HDMI - these are capable of 4K resolution with high dynamic range (HDR) at 60Hz refresh rate. This docking station works flawlessly. Build quality is premium. Spec is exceptional. It's worth paying a wee bit extra for that sort of quality.

Dieser USB-C-Hub bietet einen HDMI-Anschluss, welcher 4k bei 60 Hz unterstützt. Abgesehen davon sind die Anschlussmöglichkeiten eher begrenzt. Es gibt noch zwei USB-A- und einen USB-C-Anschluss. Außerdem einen USB-C-PD-Anschluss für die Stromversorgung. Mit Tastatur, Maus und Monitor sind also schon fast alle Anschlüsse belegt und nur noch ein einziger USB-C-Anschluss bleibt frei. Andere vergleichbare Produkte bieten hier noch deutlich mehr Anschlüsse. Die USB-C-Verbindung zum Laptop ist fest verbaut und leider sehr kurz. Ein etwas längeres Kabel wäre hier sehr sinnvoll. So benötige ich in den meisten Fällen noch ein extra Verlängerungskabel. In Anbetracht der begrenzten Anschlussmöglichkeiten ist das Produkt auch entsprechend klein und kompakt. Das ist natürlich gerade für unterwegs praktisch. Der Hub passt problemlos in die Laptoptasche, ohne viel Platz wegzunehmen. Insgesamt hat mir das Produkt vergleichsweise zu wenige Anschlussmöglichkeiten. Andere Produkte von vergleichbarer Größe haben da etwas mehr Anschlüsse. Dennoch bin ich mit dem Hub zufrieden. reviews.title: Handy hub for USB and HMDI functions
reviews.body: The hub from Minthouz is nicely presented in card packaging and feels sturdy and of good build quality. The braided trailing USB C connection lead is quite thick which helps enable the power and data throughputs this hub provides. The main outer casing is aluminium which not only protects the internals but also offers good heat dissipation. As well as outputting 4k @ 60hz, the hub provides two USB C and two standard USB A sockets. The first USB C is designed to pass power only (no data) @ up to 125W - this depends on the supply device and the device drawing the charge. The centre USB C and USB A sockets are USB 3.2 gen 2 ports providing data transfer of up to 10Gbps, while the final USB A socket is USB 2.0 capable of up to 480Mbps. This hub certainly adds much needed connectivity to certain laptops which are sometimes supplied with a lone USB port. At the advertised price of £40 this is not a cheap device but one that can make life a lot easier for those that need it.

reviews.title: I don't know how I ever lived without it.
reviews.body: I'm very happy with this device. My laptop doesn't have an ethernet port and only has one USB-C SuperSpeed port, so I bought an ethernet to USB-C cable to connect my ethernet switch to the Anker and into my laptop's USB-C port, and it works great. I don't need a fast internet connection for the things I do, so my service is only a 50mbps symmetrical up/down connection, and that's what I get even while transferring files from my external between other devices, charging my phone, and using composite devices. I bought the Anker 100W Compact and Foldable USB C Charger for it and it charges my S24 extremely fast. It's very well built, yet super lightweight. I love the sleek, slender design. It's the perfect size to easily slide into a pocket, store in a desk drawer, or keep handy in a laptop case or backpack. Using it is easy. Just plug it into your computer and plug your devices into it. Just make sure you have a power supply for it if you're charging or powering other devices, using external storage, or running anything else that taxes USB power. I have had ZERO connectivity issues with it — no random disconnect/reconnect blips, no failed transfers for huge amounts of data that have taken up to 45 minutes, no static his or crackle when my headset is running through it... no problems at all. It's actually kind of spooky now that I think about it... I can't recall a time I've ever had a similar device that didn't have some nuance that got under my skin, like a loose connection, random disconnections, having to reinstall the drivers all the time, or having to troubleshoot just to get it connected for the first time. The most stress I've put it through was with my keyboard connected, ethernet running through it, my S24 charging and transferring about ~20gb of pictures and videos to my 2T external HD at the same time that my laptop was transferring about ~500gb of media and documents to the HD, too, and I was surprised by how warm it DIDN'T get. My only complaint is trivial and unique to my situation — I wish output cord was longer. About six inches would do. My laptop sits up on an adjustable stand that clamps to my desk, and the end where the output cord is hangs a few inches off of my desk. This puts extra stress on the USB-C port and can wear it out faster or damage it. I haven't had a use for the HDMI port yet, but I eventually will. I use all of the other ports for my work and personal devices, though. These include: a 2tb external hard drive; a Poly Blackwire 3320 Series headset; a dongle for a wireless mouse/keyboard combo or a wired keyboard and a dongle for a wireless mouse; my Galaxy S24 charges and transfers files through it super fast; I have several thumb drives ranging from 20gb to 512gb that I regularly use; I recently bought an RCA/S Video-to-USB converter to digitize old home movies I plug into it, too.

reviews.title: Do you have an external drive that has a short cable?
reviews.body: I have a LITE-ON USB 2.0 External CD/DVD Writer Model eUAU108, manufactured in 2013, with an attached cable that is slightly less than 4 inches long. This model was an improvement over prior models, in that it requires only a single USB 2.0 connection, whereas previous models employed a Y-cable to enable connecting to 2 USB ports simultaneously for additional power. I have always felt that this drive was marginally capable of running on the 500 mA specification for USB 2.0 ports. I think this is the main reason for the ultra short cable - to minimize the voltage drop. The short cable worked OK when I was using the drive with a laptop, but attempting to use it with a computer attached to the back of my flat screen monitor is a major problem. The USB ports are about a foot above the desktop, making it necessary to support the drive in some manner. This has always been problematic. I tried using the only USB extension cable that I had, a cheap dollar store cable, and it did not work at all. My next thought was that I should purchase a higher quality, and obviously more expensive, USB cable, but I still had reservations. Would a longer cable, even of a higher quality, work? Why did LITE-ON force a short cable onto the consumer? They could have provided a USB port instead of an attached cable. I then thought of using a powered hub, which could solve the voltage/power issue, but I still wondered if there might be other signal quality issues that a longer cable might cause. I believe I was starting to overthink the matter at this point! I started looking at the market of powered hubs and discovered that there was quite a variety, from no-name cheapies to surprisingly expensive higher end units. It was easy to eliminate the no-name cheapies because there were brand names I was familiar with that were very affordable. Then I discovered that some of the hubs were rated at 10 Gbps! Gotta have that feature, right? Even though I don't have a single device faster than 5 Gbps, I justified this feature on the basis of future-proofing. I figured it would only be a matter of time before I had devices of that speed. Later on I discovered that all the USB ports on the computer attached to the back of my monitor are 10 Gbps capable – five are USB 3.2 Gen2 (10 Gbps) and one is USB4 (40 Gbps!) - additional justification for going with a 10 Gbps hub. As I looked at the 10 Gbps offerings I quickly discovered that many, if not most of them, were from RSHTECH/Rosonway. They have quite a variety of well designed, useful devices. So many options that I found it helpful to generate a table of features to more easily compare them. I finally decided to go with the RSH-H7C4 for the following reasons: • 10 Gbps on every port • both USB-A and USB-C ports • push button switch (vs. rocker type), with an indicator light, for each port • all ports support USB Battery Charging 1.2 protocol (BC1.2), delivering a maximum of 1.5A at 5V (7.5W) per port [standard USB ports limit current to 0.5A (USB 2.0) or 0.9A (USB 3.2)] • 36W (12V/3A) DC power adapter • detachable 3.3 foot USB-C host cable (when I need to connect to a USB-A host I use a cheap adapter I purchased at a dollar store; some of the Rosonway units include a dual-headed cable with both A and C plugs!) • two year warranty It's a beautifully designed unit with a solid, weighty feel to it. Rounded edges and a thin accent band of non-anodized aluminum around each end give this hub a modern, classy appearance. With the case being narrow and slightly rounded on the bottom, one might have concern about its stability against the pushing and pulling of the connected USB cables. While it might technically be more stable with a completely flat bottom, it is surprisingly stable as is due to its weight and mass. Not at all like some of the lighter weight plastic cased devices that I have. It would take a deliberate effort to tip it over; I don't think that will be an issue. I actually do tip it over to accommodate one of my situations: the cable on my DVD drive is so short that the drive cannot lay flat when the cable is inserted into the port on the hub from above. I have to lay the hub on its side (see video). The included USB cable is heavy gauge, very thick. With my limited experience in the world of USB cables I have made two observations: 1)there is a tremendous range of cost, quality, and capabilities among the many cables on the market; 2)an extra USB cable frequently comes in handy. It would make sense to me that RSHTECH would provide a suitably high-grade cable with their hub in order to support the 10 Gbps data rate and the BC1.2 current draw capability. The fact that the USB cable is detachable is a bonus! It can be used elsewhere. I could even change it into an extension cable by the use of a gender-changing adapter. The indicator lights are a beautiful blue, quite small, but tastefull in my opinion; apparently too small for some reviewers, but I have no complaint. I would rather have them understated than overstated. The first testing I did was to connect the aforementioned LITE-ON CD/DVD writer to the computer hanging on the back of my monitor using the RSH-H7C4 hub and its included USB cable. (When the LITE-ON drive is directly attached to this computer I never have problems because the power requirement of the LITE-ON drive is easily satisfied.) I briefly tried the hub in “bus-powered” mode (without the power supply attached). I was able to read files on the DVD writer with no problem. (This was just a brief, not comprehensive, test because my main concern was testing the more power intensive task of burning a disk.) The next testing was in “self-powered” mode (with the power supply attached). I successfully burned and verified an ISO image. I then disconnected the power supply and tried to burn the image again in bus-powered mode. The burning went without any error messages, but the verification process failed. Another attempt in bus-powered mode failed during the burning process. Returning to self-powered mode (with the power supply attached), I was again able to successfully burn and verify the ISO image. It appears that when the DVD writer is attached through the hub and cable, burning a disk requires additional power beyond what the computer port is supplying (in order to power the circuitry in the hub and to compensate for loss over the length of the three foot cable). USB Battery Charging 1.2 protocol (BC1.2) seems to do the job here. I am pleased with that! I have solved the short cable issue; I can now lay my DVD drive flat on the desk and have dependable operation. Additional testing with a much older computer, a Dell Inspiron Mini 1012 (vintage 2010), revealed an unexpected limitation: the DVD writer was unable to be recognized as a boot device by the Inspiron Mini when connected to it through the hub. As far as I can tell, this is a limitation of the older BIOS in the Inspiron. There is no way to make this system recognize an optical drive connected via a USB hub at boot up. After the system is booted the drive is able to be used with no problem. It is my understanding that the more modern BIOSes of today handle this situation in a more sophisticated manner and can detect hub-connected optical drives at bootup. I verified this by bootup tests on the computer attached to my monitor and on a modern netbook. Both of those systems were able to recognize the DVD writer at bootup with no problem when it was connected via the hub. The Dell Inspiron Mini 1012 has USB 2.0 ports that theoretically should supply enough power for the LITE-ON CD/DVD writer, but I have always felt that it was marginal. I would like to be able to supplement the power. The RSH-H7C4 is only a partial solution here. It can be used with the Inspiron for burning disks since that is a process that occurs after bootup, but in the case where I need to boot from this DVD writer I might have to first transfer the DVD image to a bootable USB thumb drive and use that instead. While not a comprehensive evaluation of the RSH-H7C4, my tests have assured me that some of my problems have been solved. I can comfortably lay the LITE-ON CD/DVD writer on the desk instead of trying to figure out how to suspend it a foot up in the air in order to attach it to the computer hanging behind my flat screen monitor. I can also use the hub for more dependable disk burning using my Inspiron Mini 1012. I am quite impressed with the RSH-H7C4 hub and RSHTECH/Rosonway. I've always been very excited by little “boxes” and devices that solve computer interconnection (and other) problems. The companies that come up with these solutions are frequently very clever. RSHTECH will now be one of the first companies I look to for such solutions. A brief look at their lineup shows devices such as: • USB switches (to share USB ports between two computers) • powered and unpowered USB hubs, some with card readers and HDMI ports • powered USB extension cables • unpowered USB extension cables with built-in signal booster chips • USB HDD/SSD enclosures • docking and cloning stations • 10 Gbps USB connected M.2 NVME/SATA SSD enclosures • 10 Gbps USB connected Magnetic M.2 NVME SSD enclosure with 100W PD RSHTECH puts an effort into including enough hard facts and specifications in their product descriptions to enable consumers to easily understand a device’s capabilities and limitations. This fact, and my favorable impression of the RSH-H7C4 hub, give me confidence to expect good performance and value with any of their products.

reviews.title: Great Hub, Great Value!
reviews.body: Review of Rosonway 7 Ports USB 3.2 Hub 36W I purchased the Rosonway 7 Ports USB 3.2 Hub 36W and tested it in two separate configurations. First with my Surface PC laptop operating Windows and second with my Mac Mini 4 operating Sequoia. The Hub, which is powered with a 36W(12V/3A) DC power adapter, comes with 7 Ports, 4 USB-C 3.2 ports and 3 USB-A 3.2 ports. It claims speeds up to 10Gbps on every port. The Hub is small and sturdy aluminum device with independent electronic switches on each port and a blue LED indicator to display power status. This enables power management over all connected devices. When I connected it to my Surface laptop PC it worked seamlessly. I was able to connect to my external mouse and keyboard, 4 thumb drives and an external backup drive. The computer recognized all the drives and could rapidly access the external backup even with all these peripherals attached and running, the hub did not get hot (only warm as would be expected). I then put the hub through an extremely tough challenge. I connected it to my Mac Mini 4 through one of the rear-facing thunderbolt/USB C ports. I then connected all my peripherals to the hub. I did not use any of the other available Mac Mini ports, only the Ronsonway Hub. I connected the following peripherals: external Kensington Trackball mouse, a Seagate Portable 4TB External Hard Drive, two thumb drives, external speakers, a Xencelabs Quick Keys, and a backup UPS device and a second hub (7-Port USB C Hub Splitter 10Gbps with 3 USB-3.2, 4 USB-3.0 Ports) – this hub was connected to a Logitech camera. All of the peripherals worked perfectly. I could open and read all the external drives (the Seagate and the 2 thumb drives) the webcam, mouse and Quick Keys all worked without problems. Even with all these peripherals including the second hub attached and running, the hub did not get hot (only warm as would be expected). I couldn’t be happier with the performance of this compact, but powerful, hub. I made a brief video if you want to see the hub and the attachments I made to the hub. One final thought, I believe this hub is a terrific economical option for expanding a laptop or desktop to accommodate an amazing array of peripherals. This hub demonstrates that a single USB C connection to a Thunderbolt 4 port on my Mac Mini, can simultaneously and seamlessly accommodate a wide array of desktop components.

reviews.title: Awesome 1-Stop Solution for Travel Power and Data Connectivity!
reviews.body: This device is the perfect accessory for someone needing to connect multiple devices using a single interface.
