title: USB C Hub 7 Ports USB 3.0 Hub with 4*USB-A&3*USB-C (4ft)

reviews.title: Easy USB port expansion for my desk
reviews.body: I picked up this 7-port USB C hub because I had simply run out of USB ports on my docking station. Between my mouse, keyboard, speakers, webcam, and all the newer devices using USB-C, I needed an easy way to expand what I could connect without replacing my existing setup. The 4-foot cable is particularly useful on my desk because I can position the hub where it is convenient instead of having everything crowded around the back of the docking station. I have been using it for the wireless dongles for my mouse and keyboard, along with my small Polycon speakers and webcam, and everything has worked perfectly for me. I like having four USB-A ports and three USB-C ports available in one place, especially as I am accumulating more USB-C devices. The aluminum housing feels sturdy, the non-slip base keeps it from sliding around, and the small LED lets me know it is powered. One thing to pay attention to is that the USB-C port marked 5V is for power input only, not data transfer, so it is not an additional data port. That is clearly stated in the description, but it is worth knowing before plugging something into it and wondering why it isn't recognized. I think this is a practical solution for anyone who needs more USB ports without rearranging their entire computer setup. The long cable and combination of USB-A and USB-C ports make it especially useful on a desktop workstation. For my particular setup, it has done exactly what I needed and saved me from constantly swapping devices between limited ports.

reviews.title: Versatile and Well-Built USB Hub
reviews.body: Very pleased with this USB-C hub. Having seven ports in a compact enclosure is extremely convenient, especially when connecting multiple peripherals to a laptop or desktop with limited USB connectivity. The four USB-A and three USB-C ports provide a useful mix for both older USB devices and newer USB-C peripherals. USB 3.0 speeds are also fast enough for transferring files to external storage and for everyday devices such as keyboards, mice, USB adapters, and other peripherals. I particularly like the straightforward plug-and-play operation. There was no complicated setup or additional software required—just connect it to the computer and the ports are immediately available. The compact design also makes it easy to keep on a desk or take along with a laptop, its heavy weight keeps it from moving around when attached devices move around, a problem I've had with lighter-weight models. Overall, this is a very practical USB expansion solution at a great price. The combination of seven ports, a good mix of USB-A and USB-C connectivity, compact size, and USB 3.0 performance makes it a useful addition to any computer setup. Highly recommended!

reviews.title: Nicely Designed USB Hub
reviews.body: The XIAOBI USB 3.0 7 Port Hub looks really nice. It is aluminum and has 7 ports, 3 USB C and 4 USB A all rated at 5Ggps. It does require a 3 Amp 5VDC power supply (not included -1 Star) of some sort if you are going to be using external hard drives and the like. I am glad I got this hub because I had two other 10 port USB hubs connected I thought were connected to USB 3.0 ports but when I started speed testing this hub, I noticed they were only transferring at USB 2.0 speeds. I connected all hubs to legit USB 3.0 ports and the speeds increased by 5 times. Almost all the things I have connected to the USB hubs work fine at USB 2.0 speeds, dongles, wireless headset etc. but if you transfer files on to a thumb drive or an external hard drive; you want the USB 3.0 speed. With the other two 10 port hubs connected; when I connected this hub to my system it started to do squirrely things. The Logitech mouse & keyboard didn’t work and thumb drives would not register on some hubs but would on other hubs. I think this is a problem of my system; too many USB ports connected so I removed this one. I connected this hub to my windows 11 laptop as the only hub and it worked perfectly with no problems. So, if you have a power supply and only use this hub; you should be fine. I really do like the looks and speed of this USB hub.

reviews.title: No more cord chaos in the living room entertainment center
reviews.body: I didn't realize how much I needed to clear up my messy living room hub center for cords until I plugged in this 7-port USB 3.0 hub from Xiaobi. The solid aluminum alloy build feels genuinely sturdy and doesn't slide around thanks to the non-slip rubber base, which also keeps my TV stand safe from annoying scratches. With seven ports available, I can easily leave the grandkids' Xbox, PS4, external media drives, and peripheral receivers plugged in all at once without constantly swapping cables. Transferring large video files and photos takes just seconds with the speedy 5Gbps data transfer, and the 4-foot cable gives me plenty of slack to route it neatly behind my entertainment center. It even comes with a handy dedicated 5V power input port on the back to keep all my devices running super stable under a heavy workload. At this price point, getting a slim, travel-friendly, and wide-compatible hub that works seamlessly across multiple systems is an absolute steal for the value.

reviews.title: Solid hub, passes USB 3.0 speeds with no loss.
reviews.body: For being a USB 3.0 rating, this is a good hub. Solid metal construction with a tapered angle front for easier access. Rubber strips on the bottom of the HUB keep it in place. It has a tight form factor, up to seven devices without over crowding while keeping the overall width to a minimum. The input USB C port is on the rear of the chassis, along with an external power input (optional). For my desk design, the rear ports don't work out well, plugging the cables into the rear of the HUB chassis, pushed it out away from the rear wall of my desk. Side input ports work out better for me. Throughput speed is what you would expect for a 3.0 USB rating, there is no discernable loss of speed using the hub, it seems to pass data without any loss of packets or bandwidth. For a 3.0 hub, the price point makes it a good value.

reviews.title: Useful Mix of USB-A and USB-C Ports
reviews.body: I like the combination of ports on this hub. With four USB-A and three USB-C connections, it gives me more flexibility than hubs that heavily favor one connector type. The ports are spaced well and easy to access, and the metal housing has a solid feel. The 4-foot cable is one of the more useful features for my setup. A lot of hubs have short cables that limit where they can be placed, while this one gives me enough length to position it where it is actually convenient on my desk. It is also worth noting that this is primarily a USB data expansion hub. The additional USB-C connection on the back marked for power is there to provide supplemental power to the hub; it is not another data port or a charging port for connected devices. Overall, this is a straightforward way to add several USB-A and USB-C connections while keeping everything organized in one compact hub.

reviews.title: Nice Hub
reviews.body: This is a really cool design. I was actually surprised by how small and compact it is when it arrived, but in this case that’s definitely a good thing. It manages to pack a lot of utility into a very small footprint without taking up a bunch of unnecessary space. The design makes really efficient use of the available room, and I like that you get quite a bit of functionality without having another bulky item sitting around. The speeds also seem nice and fast in my use, which makes it feel even more capable for something this compact. Overall, I’m impressed with how much they managed to fit into such a small design. It’s clever, space-saving, fast, and practical. A lot of utility in a surprisingly small package.

reviews.title: Excellent USB 3.0 5GBps Hub
reviews.body: This thing is great, it has 4 USB-A (3.0) ports and 3 UCB-C ports that support 5Gbps speed. This thing is solidly built, the frame is made of aluminum and it has a nice little desktop profile slant to it so it will look nice sitting on a desk top or as I will be doing, connecting it to sit on top of my Desktop Tower etc. I am going to be able to get rid of 2 cheap plastic hubs I had been using and boil everything down to this hub. reviews.title: Excellent powered USB Hub
reviews.body: This is a well-made powered hub. Delivery was same day (awesome) and arrived undamaged due to excellent packaging. Upon testing, all of my ports worked with no problem. The silver color matches perfectly with my iMac (see photo) and it sits very nicely under the iMac screen on the pedestal. I like the slanted design, which makes it easy to plug and unplug your USB cables. There are plenty of ports, including 6-USB and 3-USB C ports. All USB ports can charge as well as be used for data. 3 of the USB ports move data at 5 GBS and 2 of the USB ports move data at 10 GBS. 2 of the USB-C ports are for charging only and 1-USB C port is for charging and data. I plugged in a USB portable thumb drive, and it was recognized immediately with no issue. I am not running any other disks off of this hub at this time. Not only that, but I was pleasantly surprised by post sales support. I had a question on submitting my warranty registration using their website. They only design issue I have is that the power plug and USB C connection cable comes out the side of the unit. I would have preferred it to be off the back of the unit in order to hide the cables better. I would purchase this Hub again.

reviews.title: Provides the power requirements of your USB devices while extending the available ports.
reviews.body: I had a problem. My monitor array at home includes a Thunderbolt hub that includes two DisplayPort and one VGA connector, and my laptop at home includes one HDMI and one additional VGA connector, but this totals only 6 screens when my laptop's primary screen is added in. My monitor array, on the other hand, includes yet another 6 screens (all but two of them are 1080p). These screens are driven by a set of mostly DisplayLink display adapters, although I have a few others that required manually installed drivers (with varying success), and some that don't advertise DisplayLink but whose drivers installed automatically anyways. Six USB-A Display adapters require a lot of power, and I ran into the limit of my workstation and Thunderbolt hub's power capacity at only 4 additional displays, and every single USB-A and USB-C port on my laptop and my dock were used up, leading to a messy snarl of wires and cables that wire ties just didn't resolve. What I like: 1. It allows me to connect my entire array of video extenders and power my entire array of monitors. It substantially cleans up the mess of cables connected to my laptop and hub by putting many of them in one place. 2. Its aluminum finish looks good on my desktop. 3. Its power supply is rated for 65w, telling me I can connect more devices before its capacity is exhausted. 4. It has a sturdy construction. What I don't like: a. Ummm, that's a tough one. Maybe it takes up additional desk space and there are a lot of cables connected to it, but hey, that's kind-of the intent. Nah, I can't say I dislike that. Caveats: - Your results may vary if you plan to use this to drive a large array of screens. My laptop has 64GB RAM and a second video card with another 6GB video RAM. I have a newer laptop at work with 128GB RAM and a second video card with 16GB video RAM that can't run my home array without overheating.

reviews.title: Takes up a little more space than you might think, but it definitely does what it advertises.
reviews.body: I found the product description intriguing, since I've been looking to update my existing USB hub. The fact that this hub had twice as many sockets as my existing hub, and a good mix of USB-A/B and USB-C sockets, made it a great choice. I have it mounted under my desk with mounting tape because it's lightweight, and it allows me to organize the cables without having to trail most of them across my desk. The unit itself has a nice, small profile, but the fact that it needs a power pack instead of just a regular cable does add to the space it takes up. Overall, it's provided me the opportunity to connect more devices and power/charge devices that were previously plugged into power adapters. So far, it's performing well, has given me more charging capacity, and I still have space left for additional devices if I decide to add more. Overall, it was worth the cost of this particular item.

reviews.title: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ The best USB hub I've purchased!
reviews.body: This USB hub is absolutely excellent. After trying several USB hubs before, I can confidently say this one has been the best so far. It works flawlessly, handles my devices reliably, and has performed exactly as expected. The connection is stable, the ports work perfectly, and the overall quality feels much better than other hubs I've used. I'm very impressed with the performance and reliability of this product. If you're looking for a powerful, dependable USB hub with plenty of connections, I highly recommend this one. A fantastic product that truly delivers!

reviews.title: Great powered USB hub
reviews.body: It seems I always have a bunch of different USB connections that I need for my work computer and after researching I purchased this and it works flawlessly. There’s a large large brick off to the side of it the powers it, but that is the only drawback to this unit it is otherwise a great purchase.

reviews.title: Performed well until it didn't, but replaced promptly without hassle.
reviews.body: This USB hub worked well for 9 months then it started intermittently not communicating, then it would reconnect. All I had connected at those disconnect times were Logitech dongles for a keyboard and trackball. Difficult to diagnose, I thought the screen was freezing, perhaps a graphics card issue. Occasionally Windows issued the "USB device not connected." When the hub completely failed, the diagnosis was easy. I contacted intpw via email as suggested on their website, after a couple of efforts at diagnosis they agreed the unit was defective and replaced it promptly through Amazon. The service tech suggested that Logitech dongles should be placed as far apart at possible on the hub, they are known to interfere with each other if too close; don't know that I've ever had that problem, but took the advice. So yeah, it would have been nice if it didn't fail, but stuff happens and they replaced it. This thing is really well made, an aluminum extrusion with the board rigidly mounted inside, shielded and physically protected.

reviews.title: Low profile, fast, and stylish
reviews.body: There is not much to say about this. It has a low profile and lets you expand how many USB ports you have. The first four USB A ports, starting from the left, have 5Gb/s speeds. The next two have 10Gb/s speeds. What you should know is that of the three USB C ports on the right, the first one has 10Gb/s speeds, the next two are just for power and do not handle data. If you have a phone or tablet that lets you charge it through a USB C port, you can plug it into one of those ports and it will charge. What you should know is that you need to plug this into a high-speed USB 3.2 port to get the fast speeds. It comes with a USB C to USB C data cable for plugging into your computer. Since it only gives you one USB C data port, you're not gaining any additional USB C ports since you use one from your computer and only get one in return. The cable isn't that long, so you'll be limited in where you can place it unless you invest in a longer cable. But the price is good, it looks nice, and is very functional.

reviews.title: Solidly built powered USB hub (with a few wrinkles)
reviews.body: This hub has a very Apple-esque design and appears to be very solidly built. So far, it seems to perform well and as expected based on its specs. A couple of things though that are not made clear to purchasers based on the description provided: 1. The hub is provided only with a US 2-pin mains power lead. In other countries you’ll need to use a plug adaptor, else provide your own native mains cord with an IEC-C7 “figure 8” connector on the other end. At least the power brick uses that style of connector, the mains plug is not hard-wired. 2. The instructions warn you that WiFi dongles (such as those used to communicate with wireless mouse and keyboards) should not be plugged into the hub due to the risk of interference. Meaning one port on your laptop/PC will have to be used for such dongles if you have them. Not a dealbreaker, but it would have been nice to know this prior. 3. The instructions say only one HDD or two SSDs can be connected to the hub (presumably for power draw reasons). The maximum load is 900 mA (4.5 W) but it’s not clear if that is per data port (the USB standard) or in total across all data ports. This hub provides only one USB-C and two USB-A 3.1 Gen 2 data ports (10 Gbps). That’s a bit light-on these days. The remainder are USB-A 3.0 ports (5 Gbps). The two “power delivery” (non-data) USB-C ports are handy for charging devices, total power delivery max 45 W. So all up, a rating of 4 stars.

reviews.title: Fantastic Typing Experience
reviews.body: This keyboard offers a truly premium feel at an excellent price. The build quality is solid, the keys are responsive and comfortable, and typing on it is a pleasure. Everything feels well made and reliable, making it great for both work and everyday use.

reviews.title: Great Keyboard!
reviews.body: The keyboard feels solid and sounds much better than I expected for the price. The keys are smooth, the compact 75% layout saves desk space, and it still keeps the function row and arrow keys. The wireless connection was easy to set up, and switching between devices has been convenient. The RGB lighting looks good without being too bright, and the battery has lasted well with the lights turned down. The software could be a little easier to use, but I did not need it for basic settings. Overall, it is a comfortable and good-looking keyboard for gaming, work, and everyday use.

reviews.title: Great for both work and gaming
reviews.body: I bought this keyboard after spending some time looking for a wireless mechanical keyboard that I could use for both work and gaming, and I’m really happy with my purchase. What I like most is the feel of the keys when typing and the sound. It has that characteristic mechanical keyboard sound that is very satisfying without becoming annoying when I’m working for several hours. I also think the 75% size is perfect: it takes up much less space on my desk without sacrificing the keys I actually use. I also really like the way it looks. It feels stylish, solid, and much more polished than I expected. The wireless connection has worked very well, and being able to switch between devices is really convenient. I mainly use it for work and do a lot of typing, so it was important to me that it be comfortable as well as nice-looking, and so far it has completely met my expectations. When I bought it, I didn’t realize that the letters were printed on the front of the keycaps rather than on top. It only took me a few hours to get used to it, though, and now I actually like it because I think the lettering may wear off more slowly. The only thing I didn’t like is that it doesn’t have a dedicated “Home” key. It has an “End” key, but not “Home.” That said, the software makes it incredibly easy to remap keys and customize their functions, so it works perfectly for me anyway. I also like that you can choose from several colorful lighting effects, although I usually keep the lights turned off because I find them a little distracting while working. The keyboard is somewhat heavy, so I would consider it more of a desk keyboard than something you would want to carry around, which is completely fine for my use.

reviews.title: 10/10 would buy another one, perfect gift
reviews.body: The AULA F75 Pro isn’t just a keyboard — it’s a life upgrade. From the moment I unboxed it, I knew this thing was built different. The build quality feels premium in a way that makes everything else on my desk feel insecure. The weight, the finish, the layout — chef’s kiss. But the sound? Oh man… pure mechanical ASMR. Every keystroke is a buttery, creamy “thock” that makes typing feel less like a task and more like a treat. It’s so smooth and satisfying I found myself typing things I didn’t even need to type — emails, notes, grocery lists, lorem ipsum paragraphs — just to hear it sing. Key layout & switch orientation: One thing I absolutely love is how the keys are south-facing, sitting slightly inward instead of pointing outward toward you. It gives the whole board a cleaner, sleeker look and makes the RGB shine through in a softer, more premium way. Wireless performance: flawless. Zero lag, zero hiccups, zero drama. It connects instantly and stays rock-solid whether I’m gaming, working, or just vibing on YouTube comments. Battery life: absurdly good. I swear this thing runs on wizard energy because I keep checking the percentage and it keeps refusing to go down. RGB: The lighting is vibrant without being over-the-top, and the multi-function knob makes switching effects, brightness, and colors stupidly satisfying. One smooth twist and you can go from a calm ambient glow to full-on gamer neon. It’s intuitive, responsive, and makes controlling the RGB feel extra premium without the need of a software which is a plus. Overall? This keyboard is elite. Legendary. A masterpiece of clicky, thocky engineering. If you want something that feels incredible, sounds incredible, and looks incredible, the AULA F75 Pro is the one. I absolutely, genuinely loved this product.

reviews.title: Unbelievable quality on this thing
reviews.body: Just, WOW! This thing is HEAVY but feels like it was made out of butter. The exterior casing is made out of what feels like dense '90s style plastic which doesn't show fingerprints. If I didn't know better I thought it was metal covered in some kind of coating. The keys on this thing are the smoothest I have ever felt in my life. Just pure buttery smoothness, but a really nice clickety clack when you start typing. There isn't a spring sound like a lot of old keyboards from the '80s up to the mid '90s, but the clacking sound is still very satisfying and retro in its own way. The lighting patterns are just out of this world. I expected it to just light up, but it has quite a few different patterns like rippling, pulsing, and my favorite is some kind of mode that makes the colors jump around. The fact that the lettering is on the front of the key instead of the top is really cool. So far the Bluetooth and 2.4 GHz connections have both been really good, I haven't tried it plugged in but I'm sure it would be good. Seriously, the quality on this thing is unreal and exceeds my expectations by several miles. I thought I was just getting a fairly decent plastic keyboard that would weigh about the same as most others and have springy sounding keys. This thing reminds me of some kind of professional music gear. If you aren't sure, just get one, this is seriously one of the highest quality items I have ever received from Amazon from a non-top-tier brand.

reviews.title: Very Impressive
reviews.body: I'm impressed. Coming from a 4 year old Corsair mechanical keyboard with cherry mx switches, I had high hopes that this keyboard would get the job done. It lacks dedicated media keys, but you still have media keys by using the function key. The battery is excellent to start; I hope it lasts just as long as my Corsair did. The weight is a little beefy despite it being mostly plastic and thicc. The size is perfect if you intend to use it on your lap or TV tray. There are many different LED modes as well, which is nice, as well as the fact that you can set these modes without having to install some sort of app to control them. While I primarily use the 2.4 connection, I do like the fact that it supports 3 bt devices. The response rate is very good and on par with the Corsair. You will have to get used to the arrow key layout with end, pg up, pg dn, and delete being in one single vertical row. Probably the most intriguing thing that made me want to even look at it was the front etched keys, which were perfect for my use case. I usually rest the keyboard on a shelf slightly higher than my shoulder when I sit so the keyboard is closer to my eye level than my hands. These keys make it easier to quickly see and press some custom commands I have instead of having to pick up the keyboard, sit it on my lap or tray, and then use my commands. The key presses are also very muted from the cherry mx switches, which is a plus and slightly more satisfying. Overall, I'm Impressed. (update as of 3-15-26) Nearly a year later, the battery's lifespan has decreased to about 50% of its original capacity.

reviews.title: Click click clickety-click!
reviews.body: I’m honestly really impressed with the AULA F75 Pro Wireless Mechanical Keyboard. Right out of the box, it feels like a premium product. The build quality is solid and has a nice weight to it, so it stays firmly in place and doesn’t slide around during use. One of my favorite things about this keyboard is the sound. The clicking is super satisfying without being overly loud—it just has that perfect mechanical feel that makes typing enjoyable. The RGB lighting is another standout feature. At first, I didn’t realize there was software available, but once I found the link at the bottom of the product page and installed it, the level of customization blew me away. You can really dial in the exact colors and effects you want. Overall, this keyboard exceeded my expectations. Great feel, great sound, and excellent customization options. Definitely a solid buy.

reviews.title: So, awesome I’m jealous!
reviews.body: I bought this keyboard for my husband and switched the keycaps to fit his aesthetic as well as so he can read a bit better. (He’s new to the computer club used to be console and he’s got bad eyesight from the military.) so in the picture the keycaps are changed but not the switches! The original keycaps it comes with is a grey with the letters, symbols, and words on the side. Even though I swapped them out I want to state they are absolutely excellent quality, super soft matte feel, and low profile. I kept the keycaps for future use instead of tossing them or offering them up to my family. Which is what I usually do with manufactured keycaps. So, that’s how good they are! That and they honestly are an absolutely gorgeous color in person despite just being greytones. Now onto more of the benefits this keyboards the forth of fifth I’ve customized (I just customize as a hobby for friends and family) This one though is the first of this brand and oh my gosh do I regret not buying this brand sooner! Mainly for myself because of all the bonuses with this keyboard. Haha. Firstly, the keyboard came in awesome packaging and when I realized it can be used wirelessly too! Absolutely fantastic! I didn’t check for that before purchasing so it was a super awesome surprise! And the quality too my husband has absolutely loved getting to use his new keyboard and he got so giddy with the RGB too. I feel like building wise too this is a great keyboard for beginners. If you want a nice keyboard that has easy hot-swappable capabilities this is definitely where to start! And the volume button is such a bonus too. It makes accessibility count with this keyboard. That along with how compact it is too it takes such little space. To put into retrospect his desk is only I think 38 inches width and he still has plenty of room on each side of his desk for his snacks and drinks because of how little space the keyboard is. Literally no issues have come from the keyboard, it even with his wonky usb ports (a custom built computer composed of old/used parts.) it works well and doesn’t have any connectivity issues. So, to put all the perks together: -compact and comfortable -easy to swap keycaps around and switches —switches it came with are the perfect click for those who don’t like it to be an overbearing sound. —perfect for beginners of customizing keyboards. -Volume nob to control volume with easy access rather than fighting around your desk to get to the speaker control. -has wired, Bluetooth, and dongle capabilities which cleans up wire management. — Battery life is great so charging doesn’t happen as often and it lasts even longer with rgb turned off. - I almost forgot: also, has amazing presets of rgb colors that are fun and is perfect for zoning out to when you are having writers or artist block. Now, for the jealousy caption. I need to save up to get me one too! Because, this keyboard is everythingggg and I am definitely in need of an upgrade from my wired keyboard as well as all the perks of this keyboard. Definitely, looking forward to customizing one for myself down the line! This company is for sure my go too for keyboards. I highly recommend! For now I’ll just enjoy seeing the smile on my husband’s face every time he looks at his keyboard while we game together! The best Christmas purchase I’ve ever made!

title: Logitech G413 SE Full-Size Mechanical Gaming Keyboard - Black

reviews.title: Light, bright, responsive, and with a wonderful profile layout
reviews.body: Best keyboard I've ever owned. Sturdy case, sleek profile, the layout makes this keyboard incredibly easy to clean without the need to dismantle the keys in the process. The White LEDs are bright and easy to see in the dark, unlike many backlit keyboards that can make it harder to read the keys. The responsiveness both in typing and in the tactile feel of every key clacking on release is a delight. I was skeptical when the sale brought the price below $35, but I could not be more impressed with the quality upon arrival. As a friend has been using a slightly different G4 model for 5 years, I have every expectation that I will be using this keyboard for years to come. Very happy customer.

reviews.title: Worth 60 bucks easy, on sale it's an absolute bargain.
reviews.body: I ordered one of these after my place of employment got tired of keyboards failing constantly. After several months of outright abusive use by my co-workers, they still performed flawlessly with a lovely sense of tactile feedback, soda spills aside. One failed only after half a thermos of coffee was spilled into it, but that's to be expected from anything not waterproof rated. After ordering one for myself to use at home, I LOVE typing on it. It's my first true mechanical keyboard, and it's pleasant to just tap away, typing whatever I feel like. Each key feels like it's got two levels of depression (almost like me): First a clear 'catch' when the key activates and types, and then another more firm one when you reach the bottom of the key well. I've yet to have it double-type anything even when my clumsy fingers wanted to, although it hasn't saved me from butterfingering my keystrokes in games. As far as gaming goes, it's not PERFECT. It does make an audible noise when typing, so when you are frantically spamming the strafe or jump keys, it's going to sound like clicking the mouse over and over, but it's really no worse than your average mouse. If you're wearing headphones and blasting your speakers, you won't notice it. If you're in a silent small room, you can't avoid hearing it. Find your medium. Its clearly more meant for office work, but I find it good for gaming, and it's sturdy and heavy enough it doesn't move around at all or feel like it'll die if I drop my phone on it.

reviews.title: Great Mechanical Keyboard for gaming or surfing the web.
reviews.body: Satisfying but quiet clicks, decent lighting, solid construction, and amazing responsiveness give this keyboard a 5 ⭐ from me. I game pretty much everyday and Logitech is the only keyboard/mouse company I find worthwhile AND affordable. As a major plus, it's also very ergonomic and easy to use for long periods of time.

reviews.title: Perfect for me. Really like it.
reviews.body: Just got it so not a complete review. But so far, I really like it. I'm not a gamer, but just needed a keyboard upgrade and this is perfect. So far :) Note: True, there are no painted letters/numbers on the keys. Once usb plugged in, everything is seen with the backlight on the keys. I figured out the reason: painted letters and numbers wear off after a while. This see-through letters/numbers (presumably) will always remain. You don't use the keys unless plugged in anyhoo! So, I see no problem! It's very nicely weighted and has a nice feel on the keys. Great for the $35 price I paid!

reviews.title: Not the best choice for Mac; satisfying click but not for quiet environments
reviews.body: I can't tell you how well this works for gaming, but if you're looking to buy this as a Mac keyboard for standard daily use, definitely read on. This keyboard is far better for a PC. It doesn't have matching keys for a Mac keyboard, so you'll have reduced functionality with key commands. These are differences I've come across so far: - Instead of a CMD key on both sides of the space bar, this keyboard has only one on the left of the spacebar that functions that way, and it's not in the position of the usual Mac CMD key. (see my pic) - There's no volume control on this keyboard, so you'll have to have your Mac keyboard available to change volume unless you keep volume control visible on your menu bar. - Screen dimming requires holding this keyboard's fn key and then using F1 or F2. - Some special function keys on this keyboard don't do anything on a Mac. Here's what I do like about the keyboard: - Satisfying click. The keys are like old school keyboards with large keys that actually had feel to them. The volume of the click is kind of loud though, so if you need to maintain a quieter environment this keyboard won't do. - The attached 10 key is nice to have. - It's corded so no batteries required. - The keyboard is sturdy feeling with just-right weight to it - The key backlighting is adjustable - No quick trigger keys means no accidental double lettering - Because the keyboard rises high off your desktop compared to modern keyboards, make sure you have a seating position that lets you keep your hands lower than normal. Overall this keyboard is probably great for gaming or for PC users who don't have to keep it down while using it. If you're a Mac user, especially one who needs a quiet environment, you should look at different models.

reviews.title: Great keyboard with backlight with mechanical keys.
reviews.body: This is a mechanical keyboard. That means it is noisy where it has the traditional keyboard sound. I personally love it! The key are far more responsive than the soft-touch keyboards that are mostly used today. The clicking of the keys could be distracting to someone sharing an office, however, if you work in a private office, this keyboard is great. Also, the keyboard is backlit which makes it that much more useful when working late nights in a darker environment. It is constructed of metal and has a slip resistant base that stays put on my keyboard slide.

reviews.title: Excellent Keyboard for Everyday Work
reviews.body: I've been very happy with this keyboard for everyday work use. The mechanical keys have a great feel and make typing much more enjoyable, especially during long periods of writing and data entry. The build quality feels solid, and the keyboard has a clean, professional look that fits well in an office setup.

reviews.title: Not for me
reviews.body: I am not impressed, compared to an old and cheap Steelseries Apex 100 (Fuhlen rubber dome) I've had since the late 2010s. This keyboard has taught me that I really dislike backlit keyboards. Even on its lowest backlight setting, it is distracting, and the keycaps are not visible with it off. I haven't used a good mechanical keyboard in quite some time but I did not enjoy the typing feel of this one. The keys are subjectively spongy and stiff. Sadly, it is boxed up for return and was not meant to be. I will still give it three stars as the build quality seems solid and I think it would work well for someone who is not bothered by bright backlighting and enjoys the distinctive feel of these keys.

reviews.title: Amazing
reviews.body: Very good

reviews.title: Great keyboard
reviews.body: I am using this keyboard right now to type this review. I got one of these for work, and I like it so much I bought another one for home. The brown switches have tactile feedback, but no audible click. The feel and sound of these keys while typing is very satisfying. This keyboard is a bit noisy, but I haven't heard any complaints about that so far. I much prefer this mechanical keyboard to my old membrane keyboards. I am still getting used to it, so I make a few typos, but the frequency of them is diminishing. Build quality is excellent, the chassis is aluminum. There is no pointless, annoying RGB backlighting. Only the keys light up, which makes it easy to use in the dark. I would recommend this keyboard. It's more expensive than membrane keyboards, but I think it's worth the extra money.

reviews.title: Muy buen producto
reviews.body: Excelente, suave al pulsar las teclas. Algo de ruido, pero me gusta el sonido. No tiene teclas programables. Se siente duradero.

reviews.title: I liked it so much I used it to write this review!
reviews.body: I wanted to wait a couple months before writing this review, give myself time to decide my opinion. Well, I would say it is excellent, one can usually rely on Logitech to provide a good product and this is a prime example. The noise level is not the loudest I have heard from mechanical keyboards. Besides, if you want the responsiveness of a mechanical keyboard, you have to expect and accept a certain level of click-clack. I use it mostly to play games and secondly to write stories, as such it works well. While I do not play professionally, or online, nor care to, during my usage I have not noticed any lag or ghosting. In particular, I like the while lighting, it is not strong, but not weak either, allowing me to see the keys in any lighting situation. Which I appreciate, as the popular RGB keyboards are a bit too "loud" for me. It is also very tight and small for a mechanical, and fits comfortably on a small desk. I highly recommend this keyboard!

reviews.title: Fue un regalo
reviews.body: A la persona que se lo regale le encanta la marca logitech y se puso muy feliz asi que creo que esta muy bien

title: VGN N75 Wired 75% Compact Mechanical RGB Gaming Keyboard with Media Knob

reviews.title: Another very good mechanical keyboard by VGN
reviews.body: The VGN N75 is a compact wired mechanical keyboard that packs a lot of useful features into a space-saving 75% layout. Between the hot-swappable switches, gasket-mounted construction, RGB lighting, programmable controls, and dedicated metal volume knob, it offers a strong combination of gaming performance and everyday usability. Positives: - Compact 75% layout: Keeps the essential keys while taking up less desk space, leaving more room for a mouse and other gaming accessories. - Dedicated metal volume knob: The physical media knob makes adjusting volume quick and convenient without interrupting gameplay or other tasks. - Hot-swappable switches: Support for both 3-pin and 5-pin mechanical switches makes customization easy without soldering. - Smooth Dynamic Silver switches: The pre-lubed switches provide a smooth keystroke, quick actuation, and responsive feedback that works well for both gaming and typing. - Excellent RGB customization: With 16 million colors and 18 lighting effects, the keyboard offers plenty of options for creating a personalized setup. - Programmable through V-HUB: Key assignments, macros, shortcuts, and lighting can be customized to match different games or productivity needs. - Gasket-mounted construction: The gasket design gives the keys a softer and more cushioned feel, which is particularly noticeable during long gaming or typing sessions. - Improved acoustics: Five layers of sound-dampening material help reduce hollow or harsh keyboard noise and give the keystrokes a cleaner sound. - Durable PBT keycaps: The textured PBT keycaps feel solid and should resist shine, fading, and everyday wear better than standard ABS keycaps. - Stable wired connection: The wired design provides consistent, low-latency performance, which is especially useful for competitive gaming. Negatives - Wired only: Unlike some VGN keyboards, this model does not offer Bluetooth or 2.4GHz wireless connectivity, so it is less flexible for users who prefer a wireless setup. - 75% layout takes some adjustment: Users accustomed to a full-size keyboard may need some time to adapt to the more compact arrangement. - Customization requires software: Getting the most out of the programmable functions and RGB options means spending some time configuring the V-HUB driver. Final Words Overall, the VGN N75 is an impressive compact mechanical keyboard for gamers and everyday users. The hot-swappable PCB, responsive Dynamic Silver switches, gasket-mounted structure, five-layer sound dampening, durable PBT keycaps, and customizable RGB lighting give it a premium feel without taking up much desk space. The dedicated metal volume knob is another useful touch that makes everyday control more convenient. The biggest limitation is that it is wired only, but for anyone who prioritizes a stable connection and low-latency performance, that may actually be an advantage. For gaming, work, and general typing, the VGN N75 offers a strong combination of customization, comfort, durability, and performance in a compact design.

reviews.title: Bought it for my son, he liked it enough to take it to college
reviews.body: Got this for my son and he liked it enough that it went with him to college, which is about the best review I can give it. It's a 75% layout, so it keeps the function row and the arrow keys but drops the number pad off the right side. That's the whole point of this size, it takes up a lot less desk space and leaves more room to move the mouse around, which matters if you're gaming. He said it took a day or two to get used to where a couple of keys ended up, since things like the arrows and delete get shifted around to fit. After that it was second nature. On the rare times he needs a number pad he just plugs in a separate one, but for everyday typing and games he doesn't miss it. The look is the first thing you notice. Grey and teal keycaps with a few brighter accent keys, and a gold metal volume knob up in the top corner. It's solid and has some weight to it, so it stays put on the desk instead of sliding when you're leaning on it. The knob spins to change volume and clicks to mute, which is handier than you'd think once you're used to it, no reaching for a slider or a function key in the middle of something. The switches are hot-swappable, and that's the feature worth understanding. Each key switch pulls straight out of the board and a new one drops in, no soldering, no opening anything up. What that means in practice is you're not stuck with how it feels out of the box. If you decide down the line you want something lighter, heavier, clickier, or quieter, you buy a set of switches and swap them yourself in a few minutes. It comes with the little combo puller tool for pulling both the keycaps and the switches, so you have what you need to do it. The ones it ships with are smooth and fairly quiet, pre-lubed at the factory so they don't feel scratchy. The keycaps are the good PBT type that hold up and shouldn't get that greasy shine cheaper keycaps develop after a few months. It's wired only, no Bluetooth or wireless dongle. For a gamer that's a plus, not a drawback. A wired connection is more stable and has less lag than wireless, which is what you want in a game where response time counts, and it's one less thing to keep charged. The braided cable is a decent length. There are flip-out feet on the bottom if you want it tilted up at more of an angle, and the label says it works with Windows, Mac, Linux, and Android. He's been happy with it and uses it every day. Good pick for someone who wants a compact board that looks sharp and that they can actually tinker with later instead of replacing.

reviews.title: Good, but not my daily driver
reviews.body: I got this for my daughter and she likes it. The compact size is nice, but getting everything into a 75% layout means some keys aren't where I'm used to finding them. That's been more of an adjustment than I'd personally want to make. The keyboard itself seems well made. The RGB looks good, the colors are nice, and I really like having the volume knob. I'm also not a huge fan of the key press feel—it's a little softer than I prefer. So there's nothing really wrong with it, it's just not a great fit for me personally. My daughter is perfectly happy with it though, which is who I bought it for anyway.

reviews.title: great keyboard, compact size, wish it was wireless
reviews.body: nice mechanical keyboard. nice clickity clack sound (probably not for use in quiet environments). build quality is good. plenty of RGB options along with brightness adjustment. wish it was wireless. compact size is great (more space for mouse in my case). i have an external number pad i use in rare circumstances. PBT (polybutylene terephthalate) keycaps which should not become shiny over time like cheaper ABS plastic keycaps. be sure to get VGN Hub software to make the most for the keyboard. VGN Hub software lets you easily customize the keyboard. looks really nice in person. hard to tell from any picture.

title: Redragon Mechanical Gaming Keyboard Wired, 11 Programmable Backlit Modes, Hot-Swappable Red Switch, Anti-Ghosting, Double-Shot PBT Keycaps, Light Up Keyboard for PC Mac

reviews.title: Great keyboard, definitely happy with the purchase - great price too.
reviews.body: Easily the best keyboard I've ever bought, and I've bought some high-tier brands in the past for over a hundred dollars. It comes with a keyswitch tool, extra switches, and does not feel cheap in quality. It also sounds nice when typing. It's that kind-of "muted clack" sound. Hard to describe such things but that's my best shot at it. The size is standard array and my fingers feel good on it. I was able to switch out my keycaps for WASD (I prefer circular key caps for those) and the caps do not clash with the other caps what-so-ever. The wireless bluetooth and plugged in modes both work well; I was able to use it wirelessly for about 3 days of near-constant use before having to plug it in. Honestly, I just left it plugged in since then so not sure how well the battery is on a recharge. The lights are appealing, the keys look nice; the color scheme is kinda abstract but I'm not mad about it. Overall, great keyboard, and it's held up for a couple months now with no degradation. Thanks Redragon. Appreciate a good product.

reviews.title: But should you?
reviews.body: I would highly recommend this keyboard and company. It worked great for some time and then within the 2 year warranty period, my num1 key started acting up. I use my num pad just enough for it to be bothersome. I reached out to the company with the issue and supporting documentation and they were kind enough to get me a new one sent out, same model and everything. I love the sound of the keyboard, the ergonomics are fantastic, the size is comfortable, it responds that way you think it would/should and is compatible with every program I use. Great product! And YES, you should buy it!

reviews.title: Bought both keyboards so I could compare
reviews.body: (TLDR): The “LED” one (less expensive) works/sounds just as fine, the only real difference is the “QWERTY” one has brighter and more vibrant backlighting. If you just care about functionality/affordability, get the cheaper one. If you care more about aesthetics, spend a lil more! - - - - - I have two fellow gamer friends who desperately needed new keyboards, and since I already bought them keycaps, I decided to look for affordable mechanical keyboards for them. Amazon recommended these, reviews seemed promising, but I had another issue.. what’s the difference?? Why is one $10-15 more?? Nothing really explains the difference here and Google couldn’t help me with wtf LED vs QWERTY was (I thought they both were?? 🤨 Idk still learning about keyboards, bear with me here) A few reviews said one was brighter than the other, but other than that, I was unsure why one cost more. One friend only cared about functionality as they work from home, but the other friend very much cares about aesthetics and has a nice gamer setup. So figured, I’ll just get both! So here’s a breakdown of all the notable but pretty settle differences: RBG LED (White Logo) On Box: Sindri Red Dragon Price: Cheapest Option (great for what you pay for, best affordable option) Sound: Red Switches, not “silent” imo but not too loud either (I think this one sounded SLIGHTLY clackier, but friends couldn’t tell difference, maybe I just watch a lot of keyboard videos to notice lol) Base: Black “Metallic” appearance (bottom keyboard in light pic) Felt slightly lighter, not all that noticeable though Lighting: Not nearly AS vibrant, but still bright enough (top keyboard in dark pic) When you first plug in, the light is stagnant. Functionality: No lag so far, smooth typing, perfect for casual gamers or work use RGB QWERTY (Red Logo) On Box: Rudra Red Dragon Price: Slightly Pricier (still great for what you pay for tbh) Sound: Red Switches, same, not “silent” imo but not too loud either Base: Black Plastic appearance (top keyboard in light pic) Felt slightly heavier. Lighting: Much more vibrant (bottom keyboard in dark pic, pic doesn’t do justice, it was significantly brighter) When you first plugin, the light is flowing. Functionality: No lag so far, smooth typing, perfect for gamers and work use - - - - - My review is already long af, but I’ll have my friends update me on overall usage overtime. The “aesthetics” friend plays way more games on their PC, so I’ll be able to tell heavy gamer use for the QWERTY one. While the “functional” friend will be using it for work, as they work from home, so I’ll tell more daily use for the LED one. 👍 I’ll ask more about the settings as well as time goes on, for now, they’re just happy with their new keyboards!

reviews.title: Cheap price for a great Keyboard
reviews.body: This Redragon keyboard is a cheap and very well-rounded keyboard. Keys are smooth with a very satisfying mechanical sound. A lot quieter than pervious mechanical keyboards I've had int the past. The RGB lights are vibrant and have a couple different options for customization. I just bought it recently and the keyboard program to customize the lights is not the best. Those are the reason I'm leaving a four-star review. Other than that, I think this is a great keyboard for the price!

reviews.title: Works Fine. Not too big. Great value
reviews.body: Works fine so far. Love me some red switches. A nice, satisfying "thock". It is not too big even though it has the ten key pad. Illumination options are fine. Good quality and value if it holds up. Got it on sale for $25. That is the price of a decent membrane keyboard. This is mechanical switches so better value.

reviews.title: Sounds great, feels great
reviews.body: Sounds great, feels great. Nothing fancy. I did notice the the keys are quite responsive and don’t need to be pressed down all the way to activate. Very comfortable to type and game on. The material isn’t anything fancy but it gets the job done. Just a simple usb port and I can even connect to my Xbox. Great compatibility and very happy with the product

reviews.title: Very nice bit of kit
reviews.body: Very nice bit of kit, I've used this keyboard for over a year and the only issue is one of the number keys stopped providing a backlight. It still functions as a number key but no light. At first, I thought I needed to replace the key connection. But after doing that. It still is not providing a backlight.

reviews.title: Decent for a deal, but could be more durable.
reviews.body: I wouldn't buy this keyboard for more than thirty dollars, but it goes on sale enough that I believe it's worth buying for the twenty or so dollars the bring the price down to. I've had this keyboard for over a year, and it's worked flawlessly for most of that time. There's not much to say about it, functionally. It's a standard full-sized mechanical keyboard. It's not quiet, but I like how clicky it is, personally. Now, for the reason I don't recommend you buy this for full price. About nine or ten months into owning this item, the keys started to behave finicky. The 'R' key no longer lights up and the 'A' key has a problem with double inputs. I'll give the keyboard this, I use it a lot. I'm a writer and a gamer, so I've really put it through its paces. I'm also not as anal about maintenance as I probably should be. If you regularly dust and clean under the keycaps, it would probably last you a good deal longer. If your like me, someone who puts your keyboard through heavy use, I would go with something more durable. If you only intend to game with it, it should be fine for about a year, which for twenty dollars is a fine deal.

reviews.title: Reliable keyboard
reviews.body: My favourite brand of inexpensive mechanical keyboards. I have three, one very old, and all work just fine.

reviews.title: My sons LOVE it!
reviews.body: My 12yo son LOVES it for the multi-coloured light effect and my 17yo son nabs it at every opportunity! I've marked it down a star as I find the keyboard 'clacky' to type on but for gaming that's not a requirement.

reviews.title: Works great, lasts forever, LEDs not very bright
reviews.body: The keyboard and mouse work well. The keys are good quality. They both have been working for years with no problem. They LEDs are a little dim though; they’re not the brightest I’ve seen.

reviews.title: Not as advertised
reviews.body: The cable is different than advertised. The RGB is a single ugly static mode. The only customisation is to turn off or on specific keys RGB. For example the Q key is always an ugly yellow static backlight that can be turned off but not changed colours. The keyboard is hot swappable but good luck getting any of the switches out with how tightly they are fitted. This means that the board is effectively NOT hot swappable.

title: AULA F75 75% Wireless Mechanical Keyboard, Hot Swappable Creamy Keyboard, Pre-lubed Linear Switches, 2.4GHz/Type-C/BT5.0, RGB Backlit Gaming Keyboards(White&Brown)

reviews.title: LOVE my first mechanical keyboard
reviews.body: This is the first mechanical keyboard that i got and i absolutely love it. It definitely makes the typing experience more relaxing - the keys have the perfect creamy think to it. If you type really fast it sounds like pebbles in the creek ^.^ I did some research before getting a keyboard since i wanted something of a good quality but was prepared to drop $100+ on it. Very pleased with the quality of t his one - it feels very sturdy, the keys have just enough resistance to effortless typing. With the knob you can switch different color modes and adjust the brightness or control volume. It also allows pairing with 3 devices (and switch with a brass of a button, well, 2 buttons but u get it) via Bluetooth and it’s very convenient since i can use it with my computer, iPad and steam deck. I use Mac book and the translation from cmd , option and, control buttons are a bit confusing since the keyboard is for windows, but once you get used to it it’s ok. All my friends without mechanical keyboards now want one and all my friends with one approved the buy =DD Oh, and I obviously replaced the keycaps - now the light mode really looks magical.

reviews.title: Amazingly creamy clicky clacks on a budget!
reviews.body: For a stock budget keyboard, I am *in love*. The sound is gorgeous; deep and thocky and super creamy. Sounds like rain on a tarp in the best way. It is super comfortable to use and the keys take very little pressure to press, so typing on this is a breeze. It feels sturdy and heavy and substantial, not cheap, light and rattly. This definitely feels like a quality keyboard and I highly, highly recommend it to those who are particular on their keyboard sounds!

reviews.title: Good for work
reviews.body: Creamy, adorable, lights are amazing, perfect size, lovely blue! It’s just an amazing product. It comes with a key switcher thing and extra keys in case. It also has a usb so you don’t have to plug it in and it is amazing with computer and has no glitchy features.

reviews.title: Smooth and Satisfying Mechanical Keyboard
reviews.body: This keyboard has a great feel right out of the box. The pre-lubed switches provide a smooth, satisfying keypress, and the sound is pleasant without being excessively loud. The 75% layout is a great balance between compact size and functionality. It keeps the important navigation and arrow keys while taking up considerably less desk space than a full-size keyboard. The wireless connectivity is also convenient and makes for a cleaner setup. The hot-swappable design is a major plus for anyone who enjoys customizing their keyboard. Being able to change switches without soldering gives you plenty of options to personalize the typing experience later. The keys feel responsive and consistent, whether I'm typing or gaming. The overall construction also feels solid, especially for the price. Overall, this is an excellent mechanical keyboard with a smooth typing experience, useful wireless functionality, and plenty of customization potential.

reviews.title: Keyboar
reviews.body: I mean you can't complain with the price. It is a good quality keyboard for the pricepoint and it doesn't look bad either. I bought this as an alternative to my work membrane keyboard and switched out the switches to a more silent one as these were too loud. The battery life is decent I find I can get around three work days of battery life with the RGB on before needing to charge. The quality and durability are OK for the price point. It has slight give to it when you put force on it, and sometimes the keys become slightly misaligned and wobbly. Overall, a good keyboard with decent features.

reviews.title: So pretty, amazing sound, easy connection⭐️
reviews.body: Obsessed! The pink and cream color combination is gorgeous in person. It’s so clean and cute and the RGB makes it even prettier. It comes with the strawberry mint switches and the keys feel so good to type on (buttery?) and the sound is so satisfying and thocky. I also love how easy it is to switch between devices. It feels really sturdy and it’s honestly one of my favorite desk purchases! 5/5 ⭐️

reviews.title: Amazing keyboard, sturdy, lovely sound
reviews.body: i am very picky about my keyboards but this is the second AULA keyboard i have gotten and i am in love once again. the videos and pictures don’t do it justice it looks and sounds amazing, i love creamy / thocky sounding keyboards and this one is perfect. the resistance on the keys is great, the sound is great, the whole thing is great so i definitely recommend getting this if you’re thinking about it, it is worth the money 100% it is so nice to type on and i use the usb connector ( my cats are going through a wire chewing stage) and its great. i also love the adjustability of the keyboard, i always have the back end sit up higher, the material is solid and it feels super weighted which i love. there are a bunch of different color options i didnt show all of them in the video but i normally have mine on white or off.

reviews.title: AULA F75 Review Glacial Blue Reaper Switches
reviews.body: I’ve been using the AULA F75 keyboard as my main keyboard, and it has been a great upgrade from my previous one, especially considering the price. I mainly use it wired, but I also tested the Bluetooth connection and it worked perfectly fine with no issues. The overall connectivity has been excellent, and I haven’t had any problems using it with my games. The RGB lighting looks really nice and adds a lot to the keyboard’s overall appearance. I do wish there were more RGB customization options and selections available, but the included effects are still enjoyable and look great. The Reaper switches feel and sound amazing. In person, the keys have a really creamy sound profile, while in videos they seem to come across as a bit more thocky. The typing experience feels smooth, satisfying, and enjoyable. The multifunction knob is one of my favorite features. I mainly use it for controlling volume, and having quick access without needing keyboard shortcuts is extremely convenient. It’s a small addition, but it makes everyday use much easier. For gaming, this keyboard has been great for me. Everyone has different preferences when it comes to switches and keyboard feel, but personally, I really enjoy using it while gaming. The responsiveness, comfort, and connectivity have all been solid. Overall, the AULA F75 is an excellent upgrade at its price point. I’m very happy with it so far, and I’m definitely interested in trying out other versions of this keyboard in the future. For now, this has been a fantastic choice, and I would recommend it to anyone looking for a quality mechanical keyboard without spending a lot.

reviews.title: No APP, But Great Keyboard
reviews.body: Unfforunetly this keyboard doesn't have an app for mac, Have to use other software to for tweking stuff on the keyboard( whihc is a pain). But I love this keyboard, feels great,its heavy and it sounds like im making popcorn, Its not very loud which is a good thing nor is the sound sharp. Quality is 5/5.

reviews.title: Must recommend
reviews.body: Genuinely beautiful keyboard I’m in love with it, there are multiple options with lighting and it’s a great value for money.

reviews.title: If you are willing to spend for it, just dont give it a second thought. This is a BLIND BUY !
reviews.body: The AULA F75 White is an absolute stunner. The build feels premium — solid frame, no flex, and that clean white finish just makes the whole setup look next-level. The typing feel is insanely good — smooth switches, zero wobble, and that thocky sound that’s just addictive. Connectivity’s flawless too — whether wired or wireless, it wakes instantly and stays super responsive. The RGB is bright and crisp without being overdone, and the keycaps have this nice matte texture that feels great under the fingers. But honestly, the best part? That white aesthetic. It’s sleek, minimal, and makes your desk look so clean and futuristic. It’s the kind of keyboard you keep glancing at just because it looks that good. If you’re into performance and aesthetics, the AULA F75 White nails both. Absolute gem for the price.
