title: Logitech MX Mechanical Wireless Illuminated Keyboard Tactile - Graphite

reviews.title: Never thought I'd love a keyboard so much...
reviews.body: It's taking a little getting used to the slightly different arrangement of some keys but man... overall, this keyboard KICKS TAIL!!! I love how it lights up, I'm always working in low light or the dark and my eyes aren't what they used to be so I just can't tell you how much of a difference it makes. I also feel like the key symbols won't/can't wear out because they're backlit. Typical keyboards have letter and words wear off over time, but I don't see how that's possible with this keyboard. It's not a "gamer keyboard" it's just a great basic keyboard with all the functions you need. Keystrokes feel amazing! Not sure how to describe but when you're typing it just feels really nice. A real quality built product and worth every penny. I'm considering buying another before they don't make them anymore... LOL Oh, the battery lasts forever on this thing too. You can turn it OFF when you're done for the day and you can set the keyboard to pair/work with multiple computers (even have keys configured differently if you like). The backlight shuts off when you remove your hands from the keyboard or stop typing for about 5 seconds, but its got this really cool "motion detection" feature that once you put your hands over the keys again or start typing it lights right back up! I'm telling you if you're in the market for a new BLUETOOTH keyboard and are willing to pay a little more for a NICE one... this is the board to have!!! I really love it. I'll give you the 1 thing I didn't like about it as I began using it... The FUNCTION ROW of keys has no space above the NUMBERS or Number pad, etc. So it's super easy to hit the wrong keys sometimes. I'll often go to use the "home" key and end up hitting the key to switch between machines, or the biggest one is the "lock" key the farthest top right key over the number pad's "minus/dash" key. I often go to hit the "minus/dash" key and end up locking my windows (having to sign in again). HOWEVER, using the Logitech software that is used to configure the keyboard I was able to just disable that lock key. I don't need a KEY for that anyway. When I want to lock my Windows session (log out) without shutting down, I'll just do it the normal way with my mouse (Start > Power > Lock). No big, been doing that forever anyway. Anyway, this keyboard is awesome. Especially, once you get used to it. Most times I get a new keyboard and have to get used to the key arrangements and different spacing anyway. Might as well do it with a great keyboard. 😊👍🏻 P.S. I have always been a Microsoft keyboard/mouse kinda guy. I didn't think much of Logitech until I got the MX Master 2 Mouse, which is now also my favorite ever. This keyboard goes with that mouse it's sold in bundles they're of the same product set.

reviews.title: Satisfying typing experience
reviews.body: I love this keyboard. I use the same monitor for my gaming PC and for my work Surface Pro. I had a wired keyboard which I had to unplug from the gaming PC and plug into the docking station every morning and then do the reverse after my work hours. It became tedious after a while, so I decided to upgrade to a wireless keyboard that can switch between multiple devices without having me crawl under my desk to do so. This one seemed not too expensive, had full width, and reviews were decent. I'm very pleased. Switching between devices is handled with 3 dedicated buttons for this specific purpose, no crawling required. I used the dongle to pair it with the gaming PC, and Bluetooth to pair it with my work computer. Now I can work from the kitchen or the yard if I want to. It's slightly louder than I expected, but is by no means clickety like some others I've used. Typing is now completely satisfying. The texture of the buttons is soft and the feedback is addictive and makes me want to type forever. As an unexpected bonus, I was able to connect the keyboard to my phone and type in mobile apps with a full keyboard!! What a novel and refreshing experience. The only complaint from my daughter is that it doesn't have colored backlight. It's just plain white.

reviews.title: It's Logitech. Can't beat it.
reviews.body: If you need a keyboard that fits in a crowded desktop or you just like a clean and neat desk looks, and if you work with applications that require precision on what you type, coding, CAD, the feel and precision of a mechanical keyboard is what you need. Love it. I've heard it's great for games too, but I don't play games at all, so I can't tell, but I bet durability required for games is similar to software coding, tons of strokes per minute. Games are certainly more rough, due to adrenaline, that can be hard on a keyboard. Not my thing, I need precision, and compact format.

reviews.title: Beautiful keyboard
reviews.body: So I just received and began to use this keyboard today. I am pretty blown away by how nice it looks, how good it feels, and just the experience overall. Compared to my previous keyboard, I already like this a fair amount more. For reference, I was using the Corsair k57 RGB wireless. Also a quite nice keyboard, but this has a much more premium feel. It's also much more professional looking, which is why I chose it as I plan to use this in an office environment. Some thoughts below. -The clicks are super nice, I've never used a "clicky" switch with feedback like this before and I quite enjoy it. Probably my favorite feedback I've had from just typing on a keyboard. The various corsair boards I've used in the past I typically chose a quiet and/or a linear switch. -Overall a very nice, professional look. I wouldn't expect any weird looks with a keyboard like this in a professional environment. -Pairing was easy, plugged in the receiver and it instantly connected; no other input needed. Even the sister product to this never did that for me, the MX master 3S mouse. I had a bit of a struggle trying to get that to pair using the included receiver, as I recall. (Otherwise one of my favorite mice, also coming from a mostly corsair brand background). There is also bluetooth pairing, if preferred. (or if the receiver refuses to work, like my MX master 3S.) One minor negative is the backlight. The first problem was even getting the keyboard to light up at all. The keys for the keyboard backlight simply did not seem to function at all, no matter if I had the FN key held or not. Puzzled, I installed logitech's software and looked for options there. No luck. A bit annoyed at this point. Luckily, their software offered me access to an upcoming beta version of their software, "Logitech Options", so I downloaded that to poke around and see if there were more settings there. As it turns out there were. Oddly, they didn't work though. The keyboard refused to light up, the keys meant to dim or brighten it doing nothing at all. As I began a search to see if this was a common issue, the backlight finally came on. No idea what changed. Pretty standard white LED backlights. Lots of pissed off customers on forums about it though. Apparently, Logitech has been pretty silent about the issue. I'd be pissed too, if my $200 keyboard didn't have a functioning backlight due to software issues. With that rambling anecdote, the backlight itself is just fine, about what I expected for a professional keyboard like this. Just clean white LEDs. In summary, a very nice looking, nice feeling premium keyboard. Pretty unassuming in a professional environment. Easy setup. Quite happy with it. Edit: The backlight does not seem to remember brightness settings between use sessions, so if you will get super annoyed or angry about having to hit brightness up each time you use, that's something to consider. Most annoyingly, if the room is deemed "too bright" by the sensor, the backlight will not turn on at all. Understandable, but I'd still like the option.

reviews.title: Worthy Upgrade
reviews.body: I replaced a Logitech 860 with the MX, the quality and feel of the MX is very good. I love the feel of the keys. The key setup is more tighter than the 860, but after a couple days I’ve became accustomed to it and I like it. The difference in the feel and quality is significantly better than the 860.

reviews.title: Very disappointing for a $150+ keyboard.
reviews.body: I was very disappointed when I started using this overpriced keyboard. First of all, the build quality is inexcusable for a $150+ keyboard, especially from a brand like Logitech. The space bar and the backspace keys squeak horribly every time I press them. I understand that can be fixed by applying some white silicone grease, but I shouldn't have to do that with an expensive keyboard right out of the box. In addition, the rubber foot across the back of the keyboard has already started to peel off. I purchased the tactile (quiet typing) version, and while it isn't the loudest keyboard I have ever typed on, "quiet" is not at all how I would describe it. Someone in the next room or cubicle would definitely be able to hear you typing on this. I wonder how loud the "clicky" version is... And now, to address the backlight issue: Several reviews have mentioned problems with the backlight. It seems to function "as intended", but the design choices really make me scratch my head. The backlight will turn off just a few seconds after you stop typing, and doesn't turn on again until you press a key. That means that if you aren't constantly typing, the backlight will be turning on and off in a way that is very visually distracting at the bottom of your vision. If you take your hands away from the keyboard, you will not have the keys illuminated to help orient your hands when you start typing again. In a dark room that means you can't see anything on the keys. Even the timing of the backlight is inconsistent. Sometimes it turns off while I am still typing, sometimes it stays on for a minute or two with no input, like it got stuck. At first I thought I just had to adjust the timeout settings on the Logi Options+ app. Nope! No options! Just a couple of annoying, distracting backlight animations (like, random keys illuminating, why would anyone want that?!). I'm not sure who signed-off on the design for this thing or what they were thinking. Furthermore, the caps lock key has a distracting blinking whenever it is on, especially annoying if you are gaming and caps lock is set to something like toggle run/walk. The keyboard is Bluetooth only, which seems to work fine. But I would have liked to have the option to plug it in like a normal USB keyboard. As far as I know the USB plug is only for charging, but also leaves an always illuminated and fairly bright "charging" LED, very obnoxious if your computer is in your bedroom. In short: Don't waste your money on this. I will be returning mine.

reviews.title: Great first mechanical keyboard
reviews.body: I just finished my first long work session with this keyboard. I'm glad I bought it. It's very easy to type on. It's my first mechanical keyboard of any kind. I went with the quieter version. You still get the clicking sounds, just not super loud. I finally understand what people mean when they say typing on a mechanical keyboard feels more satisfying compared to non-mechanical ones. Highly recommend this keyboard if you're looking to get into mechanical keyboards. Definitely won't be my last.

reviews.title: Beware the USB dongles
reviews.body: Original review: It's a keyboard an it works After hearing people rave about mechanical keyboards, I decided to get myself one. I am not sure how representative of mechanical keyboards this one is, but I find it to be very similar to everything I have used before. The keys don't feel "clicky" at all. In fact, I am constantly running into an issue of resting my hands on the keyboard, and "mushing down" a key by mistake (in other words, "wwwwwwwwwwwwwwwww" because my finger pressed a key without me even noticing). I think I can get used to pulling my hands away from the keyboard to keep that from happening, but I find it weird that I now have to do this. I assumed the keys would be harder to press, not mushier than the cheap-o keyboards I have had. Another issue I have had is that the keyboard is not flat. I have tested it on multiple surfaces, including a glass table. I ended having to prop one side up with some paper. Not too happy about that. For whatever reason, this does not have a print screen key. Luckily you can remap it using the Logi Options+ software. Honestly, at this price, I am not sure I would recommend this keyboard. Ok, so why 4 stars? It does have some positive points. First, it looks pretty sharp. Second, aside from not sitting flat, it feels solid / well-built / quality. It is small, yet it is heavier than most keyboards. I am used to keyboards lasting "forever", so I will update here if/when I run into issues. Third, switching between different machines works flawlessly. Fourth, it allows me to bring my settings to all computers (e.g. remapping the screen capture key). Fifth, it has a rechargeable battery and it lasts long enough that I never have to worry. I do have a charging cable right on my desk, so every once in a while I just leave it plugged in, so I have never seen it go below 85%. What else can I say, it is a keyboard and it works. ----- Updated review: beware the USB dongles. Logitech mouses and keyboards (e.g. "MX Mechanical", "MX Master 3s", "MX Anywhere 3") connect either via Bluetooth, or via a USB dongle. However, the USB dongles are not all the same. For example, the "MX mechanical" keyboard only connects to a "bolt" dongle; and the "MX Anywhere 3" mouse only connects to a "unifying" dongle. Unfortunately, there is no clear guide / summary for which devices go together. You just have to check each device before buying to see what dongle it uses. Devices in the same generation are *not* guaranteed to use the same type of dongle. Here is my experience: I setup for myself a MX mechanical keyboard + MX Master 3s mouse and everything works fine. Both devices connect to a "bolt" dongle, so I have a "bolt" dongle on my laptop, and another "bolt" dongle on a desktop computer. I can switch between laptop and desktop with a press of a button. The keyboard/mouse itself is fine, the review can be seen above. My wife saw my setup and wanted the same, but she didn't want the MX Master 3s mouse ("it is too big"), so I got her a this same "MX Mechanical" keyboard and a pink "MX Anywhere 3". As it turns out, the mouse does not come with a "bolt" dongle, it comes with a "unifying" dongle. So now I have one "bolt" dongle which connects only to the keyboard, and one "unifying" dongle which connects only to the mouse. Thus, to "fix" this situation, I either need to use Bluetooth for everything (which I was trying to avoid to begin with), or I need to purchase 1 extra bolt dongle and 1 extra unifying dongle, so that each computer has both a "unifying" and a "bolt" dongle. Let's hope I have enough USB ports, or I will also need a USB hub. Even if you are aware that different dongles exist, you still need to be careful. If you buy a "MX Anywhere 3", you get a "unifying" dongle, but if you buy a "MX Anywhere 3 for business", then it has a "bolt" dongle. This is, by the way, how I ended up with a "unifying" dongle - while browsing the products, I opened up two tabs, one with a black MX Anywhere 3, and one with a pink MX Anywhere 3, except one of them was "for business" and the other was not. You might think this mess would warrant giant disclaimers ("DOES NOT HAVE A BOLT CONNECTOR"), or some kind of guide for which devices go together, but nope. For extra hilarity, Amazon bundles a "MX mechanical mini" (bolt) with a "MX Anywhere 3" (unifying). The whole thing is confusing, misleading, and just terrible user/customer experience. If I could start over, I would just get something else.

reviews.title: Lovely Product - but US layout not clear in product description
reviews.body: Product is excellent, but be aware this is a US layout keyboard. If you want a UK layout (or European) you need to look for this specifically on Amazon.

reviews.title: Best office keyboard to date
reviews.body: This keyboard is pretty amazing. I own a HHKB, and a Pok3r. I build and customize my own keyboards. I bought this mainly because of the Logitech Flow feature. But first, I wanted to talk about the keyboard itself and why I think this is the best office keyboard to date. The build quality is amazing. It's sturdy, and the internals are very tight, which means, no rattling, no added noise or reverbiation. As a result, this is a very quiet mechanical keyboard (I can only speak for the brown switch version). The keycaps are made out of recycled plastic, but they don't feel cheap. They are quite smooth and easy to type with. The typing experience is very consistent and smooth (see type test photo). My typing speed is consistent with my other keyboards, but for me, it's definitely feels much better to type with tactile silent switches compared to my other keyboards. Even though this keyboard is a low profile keyboard, there are flip up feet at the bottom of the keyboard to lift it up a little more to get a better angle if that's what you prefer. The lights are nice, but what makes this keyboard really stand out is when it doesn't use the lights at all. Without the backlights on, this keyboard can do 10 months on 1 charge, which is completely unheard of for a mechanical full size wireless keyboard. I've had this keyboard for a couple of days on the whole time, and by now, my other wireless 60% would have died and required a recharge. There is only one issue with this keyboard which is customization. For Macros, only some of the keys (F Keys and Cursor Targeting Group) can be customized vs what I am used to, which is being able to customize every single key. For customizing the physical look itself such as changing the switches or the keycaps, this keyboard cannot be customized like that. The spacebar doesn't use standard stabilizer stem widths. You can replace every key cap except for the spacebar. You also cannot change the switches unless you know some soldering which is not recommended. As for the reason why I bough the keyboard. I absolutely love it! The logitech flow option allows me to move from my multiple computer setups with only one keyboard and mouse. I often multitask, I have a computer running 24/7 as my "smart tv" as well as my personal laptop, and my work computer. Considering how I can flow through all those computers from one set of mouse and keyboard without having to physically switch the mouse to use that specific computer is absolutely game changing. I feel like I am using one computer, even though they are all completely seperated. Whenever a product can make someone's life easier, is when you know you have something truly revolutionary. For work and every day use, this is absolutely the best office keyboard to date.

reviews.title: An Excellent Successor to the Venerable K800 Wired/Wireless Keyboard - Different but AWESOME!!
reviews.body: I really like this keyboard!!! In fact, I would say that this is a good/reasonable successor to the magical, venerable K800 Wireless and Wired I (like most) have an old wired K800 (attached to my work laptop), and was sooooo sad to see that I couldn't get another one. I took the leap and purchased the K800 wireless as a backup (what I writing this on..) for my personal laptop, and it truly is such a wonderful easy feeling keyboard. Again, logitech has discontinued the wireless one - enter to MX Keys (full size) I think that this one has that old school IBM-style feel, yet waay more robust, heavy (surprisingly), and modular (regarding key caps and triggers) I think, if past is prologue (as it invulnerably i..) this product to will either disappear, or get worse - I will by a 1 or 2 for safe keeping

reviews.body: This is a US layout keyboard on sale in the UK... but no mention of that on the description.

reviews.title: Excellent keyboard with a few minor issues
reviews.body: This keyboard is a solid little keyboard. It’s very well built and has a satisfying feel and noise while typing. I really like how easy it is to switch between different computers. I have it set to use both my desktop PC and my MacBook Air when I dock it on my desk. It knows which is which and changes the keyboard layout accordingly. Everything just works. The battery life is excellent and it charges up really quickly over usb c. The Logitech Options app is really easy to use with everything laid out in such a way to just make sense. Also; the back lighting is simple but still nice. Ok onto my complaints. First I wish the key caps were a better material. They get glossy really quick from the slightly dirtiest fingers. I dunno if that’s due to the dark grey colour or the material itself. But for the price it should have better key caps. Second; I wish this thing had full rgb backlighting. The white is nice; but full colour would be better. Ok that’s it. So overall this is a great desktop keyboard that you could also take with you if you wanted to use your laptop or iPad on the go with it. It’s great for multi device use and the typing experience is really nice!! If you’re coming from the keyboard that came with your Mac or PC… or want something small and portable; this is definitely for you!

title: AULA F99 Wireless Mechanical Keyboard,Tri-Mode BT5.0/2.4GHz/USB-C Hot Swappable Custom Keyboard,Pre-lubed Linear Switches,RGB Backlit Computer Gaming Keyboards for PC/Tablet/PS/Xbox

reviews.title: Love it!
reviews.body: Bought this for my wife’s WFH setup. She fell in love with the Creamy Switch craze on TikTok and this was a reasonably priced keyboard that fit the bill. I found a cute sakura themed keycap set to replace these, but she said she’d have been happy with the blues and purples that came preinstalled. It looks great, feels and sounds fantastic, and does everything you’d want from a keyboard. She loves the size, specifically that it includes the number pad. Not enough decent keyboards do these days. People want minimalism in everything, but the functionality of a dedicated number pad is hard to beat. Connecting is super easy. We’re using the hardwired USB-C option, but I was able to use Bluetooth on my laptop at work while I was testing and installing the other keycaps prior to giving this as a birthday gift. She loves that it’s such a lightweight feel of typing, even noticeably so to someone without the heavy handed typing of myself, having grown up on IBM and Alps switches which allow for some decent banging. I’m not a keyboard snob or really a deep enthusiast, but some of my friends and coworkers that care more than I do really loved it as well. It’s a crowd pleaser, and that wonderful little subdued THOK on each tap is soothing as foretold.

reviews.title: Perfect for work and the sound is ohh so goood!!!
reviews.body: I LOVE this keyboard!! After spending two weeks researching I decided on the Aula F99 and I am so happy with my decision. I’m not a gamer but wanted a full keyboard for work and this checked all the boxes. The sound is so creamy and reminds me of marbles or smooth stones. It’s so fun to type on and the RGB is kinda fun too. Bluetooth connected with ease, so did wired. Haven’t tried the dongle yet but so far it’s been plug and play play with no issues. Feels sturdy not cheap. Sounds great out of the box. Ordered the Gatreon Milky Yellow switches but I may not even need them cuz I’m kinda digging this sound already. It’s soooo satisfying. Great value!!

reviews.title: First mechanical keyboard ever - love it!
reviews.body: Perfect right out of the box. Set up was effortless. I love the simple and minimalist look and layout of it. I decided to swap my old HP wireless keyboard that I use for work out for this one and while it's a tad bit louder than I expected for snall office settings, I still love the sound and feel of it. It is definitely "stockier" than expected for plastic. Bit on the heavyside in comparison to a standard HP keyboard. Feels good and solid though. I've been using it all day and have no complaints so far. Small side note: if you're a dingus like me, the ÷ key on the number pad is the same as /. Took me a minute to figure that out because I'm so used to / + - * 🤣

reviews.title: Bought it for my husband and now it's mine
reviews.body: First I want to say that I initially bought this for my husband as he had bought a walmart clicky brand keyboard and was finally growing tired of the clicky sound lol. Well as the keyboard enthusiast I suggested this one as it was simple and a few of the review videos had sounded promising. When it arrived the first thing I noticed was the heft, this was made with durable material and not light weight at all, which put some ease to my mind that it wasn't just made of cheap plastic. The size was just perfect, I couldn't be happier, and when I typed for the first time the creamy and thocky sound just itched the right place in my brain. I could not get enough of it. I love that there are 3 types of way that you can connect, BT; Dongle or wired. I always prefer wired. The keycaps are nice, although I prefer rounded keycaps to the sharp square ones, I did replace the factory keycaps and I just fell in love with this more. The switches sound nice and deep and honestly, this is almost perfect for me, I'll be playing around with this keyboard especially since it's hot swappable and I might try other switches. For those just starting out with interest in the keyboard area, this is a great first start with a not too expensive price point! I did end up having to buy another keyboard for my husband since I stole this one, it was definitely worth it though! Can't wait to mod this one a little more!

reviews.title: Decent keyboard
reviews.body: Coming up on almost a year of owning this keyboard. It was just what I needed. I love the feel of the keys, the sound, the 3 different options to connect, the weight and the number pad. The battery life wireless is okay. I wish there was a power button. Sometimes you accidentally touch a key after turning off the computer and the keyboard feels like it stays on forever lol. I use it for my WFH job and light gaming. I bought it last April and now it’s February and I’m starting to notice connection issues (non responsive) and sticky keys. It’s been acting a bit possessed lately. I work with a lot of VDIs so that could also play apart in the weirdness but it’s been more and more frequent lately. I use the Bluetooth option, I will try to hardwire to see if there is a difference. Will update my review if it poops out 🤔🤔

reviews.title: Amazing Keyboard for WFH
reviews.body: I’ve had this keyboard for almost 2 months now and wanted to wait to write a review until I had used it for a while. I’ve got to say this keyboard is awesome. recently got a WFH after only ever working in an office so I knew I wanted to invest in a nice keyboard. I spent at least a week researching and reading reviews on keyboards and didn’t realize how hard it would be to find nice keyboard with a num pad but I kept coming back to this one because of the amazing reviews and of course I love the way it sounds! For the average person yes this is a little bit on the pricier side but to me it was totally worth it, I like that it has 3 forms of connection (Wired, Bluetooth, and USB), there are a million different RGB options and it sounds amazing and it comes with super easy instructions and you can change the key caps if you want nicer keys. I will say, as you can see in the video I have two keys where the lighting under them doesn’t work/ change color, but I still have it 5 stars because it doesn’t affect the function of the key board. Another slight inconvenience is that you do have to charge it with the wire after a few days if you’re using Bluetooth or USB and it doesn’t give a low power warning but besides that it’s perfect. I also want to note that I have seen that this key board had gone a little viral on TikTok and I did purchase before it was trending so I would say if you are coming here from TikTok no, it’s not a scam it’s actually a great keyboard!

reviews.title: Great keyboard for the price
reviews.body: The Aula F99 is a "96%" mechanical keyboard that comes in around the $90 price point normally, but can get as low as $60 on sale. That form factor means that it does have a numpad and arrow keys as well as home, delete and page up/down keys, but those keys are moved up in-line with the function keys and the numpad/arrow keys are squished up closer to the main keys with the arrow keys set a little further down to make space. Having a numpad was a must for me because I like to play games that often use the numpad for important functions, and I also prefer typing numbers on a numpad when the occasion arises. At this price point, this is probably one of the best options for people who want a numpad and/or arrow keys but still want a keyboard that looks and sounds more like a custom keyboard you see in YouTube shorts of people doing sound tests. It has linear switches meaning there's no "bump" or clickiness to them, I'm not 100% sure what exact switches they are because there is some conflicting information online. I think mine has "Star Vector" switches? Regardless, the switches are quite light on force and very quiet, which brings us to the sound. This keyboard sounds great for the price. It's a little on the clacky side, but the switches have no scratchiness to them and are obviously pre-lubed, and there appears to be some kind of sound-deadening material inside the case as there is none of that hollow pinginess you get from something like a cheap Logitech mechanical. Overall it is a massive improvement from the Logitech keyboard I had previously to this one. The case is plastic but seems to be fairly high quality. The keyboard is surprisingly heavy which is very confidence inspiring and gives you a very stable feeling typing experience. It also has RGB lighting on all of the keys but the keycaps are not shine-through meaning the lettering doesn't light up. If that's a big deal to you, I'm sure you could swap them out for something else later as it does come with a keycap and switch puller, which also means you can change the switches if you want. It also has 3 different connection modes: "Wired" which uses a USB-C port on the board for connection (and it does come with a USB-C to A cable in the box), "2.4 GHz" which uses a little wireless dongle that sits in a little slot on the top edge of the board when not in use, and it's also able to connect via bluetooth. I haven't tested the battery life as I use this keyboard at my desktop computer with the wired connection, but having the different modes and a physical switch to change between them means you could have this board connected to multiple different devices and switch between them whenver you want which is cool and useful if you need that. I'm fairly new to the world of mechanical keyboards, this is only the second one I've ever owned, the first being a Logitech board that didn't sound or feel nearly as good as this one. As I type this review out on this very keyboard, I find myself liking the sound and feeling more and more. I'm sure there are things about it that someone with more knowledge and experience could pick apart and criticize, but overall I am very happy with this keyboard and would definitely recommend it to anyone who's not an expert and is looking for something better than the offerings from companies like Logitech and Razer.

reviews.title: Great for both gaming and working and is very satisfying to use!
reviews.body: This keyboard is absolutely amazing! It has such a wonderful creamy clicking sound that isn't overly loud but still satisfying to use. Though I did instantly replace the keycaps with some very cute cats ones, they do feel very nice and have a wonderful texture. I love that you can adjust it to be in a more ergonomic position! Also the battery lasts for such a long time I am legit shocked every time it tells me I need to charge it lol. I use my computer and keyboard a lot as I am both a gamer and do all my work from my computer, so it gets a lot of use. And yet there has been no sticking, no issues, and is a lot nicer to use for longer period of times. Something else of note is that this keyboard was practically made for us who have small hands. My hands are very small and my last keyboard was sometimes annoying to use because I was unable to easily reach as many keys. This one is perfectly compact to where it does not feel crowded but also is super easy to use all while having the numkey pad! Also I love the customizations you can do with the keyboard colors and lighting! This was actually recommended to me by a friend. I went to her house and used it for a minute and was so stunned by how nice it felt I ordered this right there and then. I literally cannot recommend it enough!

reviews.title: Ojalá siga así por mucho tiempo. 😄
reviews.body: Excelente teclado por su precio. Tiene muy buena calidad de construcción, las teclas se sienten cómodas y agradables al escribir y jugar, y la batería me ha dado un buen rendimiento. Además, la iluminación y el diseño le dan una apariencia muy premium. Hasta ahora ha superado mis expectativas y ha sido una de mis mejores compras. Lo recomendaría sin problema.

reviews.title: Uygulaması çok güzel ve hızlı sipariş
reviews.body: Sipariş pazar günü verilmesine rağmen aynı gün elime geçti. Klavye den ilk izlenimlerim gerçekten güzel olduğu yönünde. Çok yumuşak bir sesi var. Ve uygulaması başarı ile çalışıyor. Kesinlikle memnun kalacağınız bir ürün tavsiye ederim

reviews.title: Teclado surpreendente
reviews.body: Teclado incrível, com teclas macias e som agradável, construção excelente, com bons materiais, bem robusto e pesado. Tive teclados como razor blackwidow e ele é superior. E o melhor, vem padrão abnt2!

reviews.title: BEST KEYBOARD!
reviews.body: The best in class Keyboard I have ever used! The Typing Experience just feels awesome! Earlier, I was using Dell Wireless! Saw some Video on Social Media, and Man'O'Man! FELL IN LOVE WITH THIS KEYBOARD!

reviews.title: Best Keyboard in My Collection!
reviews.body: I have had this keyboard for a month now, and wow! It is by far the best keyboard in my collection. I love a nice creamy typing experience, and this more than delivers. I had been searching for a full keyboard that was versatile and easy to use. I bring it back and forth from work, and with my wedding planning, I've put it through it recently. There are 2 different heights that you can set the keyboard to for wrist support, and thanks to the larger keys, I can have a full set of nails and have 0 issues typing. My only complaint is that the light that indicates the battery is always red, even when fully charged. I'm not too sure why this happens, but it doesn't bother me. Great brand. Great quality. Beautiful design.

title: Kisnt KN85 Wireless Mechanical Keyboard, 75% Layout, Bluetooth/2.4GHz/USB-C, Custom RGB Backlit, Hot-Swappable Linear Switch, Creamy Sound for Gaming/Typing (Retro Beige)

reviews.title: Genuinely the best budget keyboard out there
reviews.body: I can’t recommend the kisnt KN85 enough. The RGB is bright (although the software isn’t great), It’s a good weight for a plastic keyboard, the colors it comes in are attractive, and the price is amazing. The most important part (to me) is the switches. They are Bsun purple switches, a smooth, creamy linear switch that sounds amazing. I genuinely use these in my other boards. It is made of plastic, but the plastic is sturdy. It is bluetooth, 2.4 ghz, and wired. Overall, this keyboard is worth it. I love this keyboard, i’ve bought two of them!

reviews.title: Best board for the price, BY FAR !!
reviews.body: Great board especially at this price point. This really raises the bar for entry level products and makes it much more accessible. This thing will impress most seasoned enthusiast. I could see this thing attaining a similar status to the Aula F75. You get really good acoustics, great switches (lubed BSUN Purples), gasket mounting AND hotswap. I've been typing on it for a few days and the sound tests you see online are very accurate, board sounds very creamy and poppy, which makes for a very satisfying typing experience. The RGB on this board is really bright and has some cool preset animations. Definitely NOT office friendly, I took this thing to the office one day and had to swap it for a normal keyboard because it is quite loud. I enjoy the sound but I don't think my coworkers did. lol Unfortunately I did notice that the space bar seems to make a really loud thunk which doesn't match the sound of the rest of the board, but you can fix this pretty easily with a rubber O-Ring or some foam inside the space bar. And sadly I did not get any spare keycaps with my order, as I've seen other buyers receive in their reviews :( Overall though, really good board and significantly raises the bar for entry level products. This thing will outperform boards that cost twice the price. I am very happy with my purchase and will be buying one for my gf too

reviews.title: Super impressive for the price.
reviews.body: I'm shocked at the quality of this keyboard for the price. The main case is plastic but a is very good quality plastic. Obviously, it's not going to be aluminum at this price. The quality of the keycaps is also excellent. They are the more premium PBT plastic rather than the cheaper ABS plastic and they feel great. It even has more features than my other higher end mechanical keyboard as this one not only has wired USB (obviously), but also 2.4 Ghz dongle (which secures nicely in a little cutout of the bottom of the keyboard and held in magnetically), and a whooping 3 Bluetooth channels so you can pair this keyboard with many different devices at the same time. I love the layout as well. It's a little smaller than a TKL layout keyboard, but without any compromises. Typically, I don't like 75% or less because you lose too many useful keys or they have them in a weird place, but this keyboard's layout is perfectly done. You still have all of your Home, End, PgUp, PgDn, Insert, Delete, and Print Screen and Pause/Break keys. The only key missing is the Scroll Lock key which is never used anyway so this is perfect. It has nice RGB that lights up under and around the keys. Also comes with some extra switches and even a decent keycap and switch puller tool. Even comes a thin, cheap, plastic dust cover which I appreciate. My only complaint whatsoever about this keyboard is that I'm not too crazy about the switches, but that's really a personal preference thing. They're certainly not terrible and I can definitely see other people with different preferences liking these, as actually a lot of other reviewers did really like the switches. But I'll probably be swapping them out, which is another great thing about this keyboard is that they are hot swappable. For those wondering about the sound - the stock keyboard is clacky rather than thocky.

reviews.title: It's pretty good!
reviews.body: Chances are, you've found this keyboard after reading a number of Reddit threads or watching a review or 2 on Youtube, and I can confirm they're all very correct to recommend this keyboard. It's kind of obvious that it's not trying to be high-end, as evidenced by the all plastic build, basic and other creature-comforts that are left out, like volume knobs and little near-useless LED screens, but it is still a solid, well built keyboard with a decent-enough feature set. But, it's a keyboard, so if we're being real, its the tactile feel of typing on this thing along with it's really nice, satisfying "creamy" sound (at least that's what I've heard it called, though I still don't quite get why) that makes you want mechanical keyboard like this and this one does the thing real well while also looking pretty dang nice at the same time (I got the gray gradient version with side-printed keycaps. The battery life using the included USB 2.4G wireless dongle is exceptionally good and it also has RGB backlighting with 20 preprogrammed lighting modes, if you're into that thing, but I've got it set to a static color and it looks good enough for me. All of that at this price point makes this a really, really, really good option and one that I can absolutely recommend.

reviews.title: Amazing, and truly worth the price.
reviews.body: It's a truly amazing keyboard, it feels great, looks great, and sounds great. I have only one issue with it, it's loud, but that's only an issue at night. The ergonomics feel pretty good, and the switches are very nice and responsive. Everything feels high quality, especially for this price. Very worth it and affordable. The backlight is a nice touch, it can be disabled and enabled, along with changing the color and speed. Note: "Mom if you're seeing this, I wrote this review" -your son.

reviews.title: The best value for a budget keyboard, hands down.
reviews.body: This keyboard has been an absolute dream, and the price cannot be beat. It uses bsun switches (I'm honestly not sure which, I've done some digging but can't find them), of which I got the linear version. These switches are nice, there is no noticeable scratch, a crisp bottom out, and the stabilizers are actually silent with no rattle or ticking. There is a variety of foam included, but they leave a bit of room in the case which keeps the board from sounding muted. There are NO SCREWS, so modding this thing is a breeze (might need a small flathead tho) and you have a lot of options straight out of the box. It also comes with a hotswap board, so you can lube the switches (already lubed, but do what you want) or change them out entirely. There are also FLIPPY FEET (2 STAGE!!) so you can adjust your typing angle. I have heard people complain about the software that comes with the board, but it turns out it is fully compatible with the Signal RGB app. Now I can assign any pattern I want, even outside of the presets! The lighting is very prominent since the LEDs are south-facing. 3 of the lights do not work in the software, but they are on the edge of the board with the modifier keys so they are not noticeable. My ONLY gripe is that the keycaps are not very durable. I have been using mine for a few months now and the tops of the WASD keys are starting to become shiny and smoother. These are likely not PBT, but they are a very thick ABS so the sound stays deeper and fuller. However, a PBT set from a name brand manufacturer costs more than this entire keyboard, so this is an incredibly minor complaint.

reviews.title: Amazing keyboard for the price
reviews.body: This keyboard sounds even better than the reviews claim. Before buying, I came across a few comments suggesting that some of the internal padding had been removed or that the overall quality had declined as the keyboard became more popular. After using it myself, I can confidently say that those concerns were unfounded. The build quality is excellent, the typing experience is incredibly satisfying, and the switches feel fantastic. Every keypress sounds and feels premium, making it a joy to use for both work and gaming. So far, I’ve only tested the 2.4GHz wireless mode, so I can’t comment on the wired or Bluetooth performance. However, based on my experience, I have no hesitation recommending it. For the price, this keyboard offers outstanding value. It was absolutely worth the wait, especially considering I ordered it from the US and had it shipped to South Africa.

reviews.title: Comfortable, creamy sound, easy set up.
reviews.body: Set up was a breeze, simply plug in. It charges in a few hours. This keyboard is really nice. I like the “creamy” sound other viewers have described. A VERY light touch is all you need to type. I won’t say it’s sensitive, it just requires a light touch of each key. That is something I need to get used to. I have a laptop set up on a riser, and needed a keyboard that will fit in the small space beneath it. This was my choice after reviewing MANY keyboards. I also wanted a laptop with raised keys, a mechanical keyboard. I like the “old school” feel of it. Weight: it’s heavy. I won’t be traveling with it, so that doesn’t matter to me. But I love the heaviness of it. Feels secure in its spot. Ergonomics: there are two levels if you want to change the angle. Three is you count not using the little feet at the back. I also have a padded hand/wrist rest for extra comfort (NOT INCLUDED) but the keyboard itself is comfortable to use. Color: I would have preferred black to match my desk accessories and laptop, or blue my favorite color. I went for the least expensive option as the color doesn’t change the effectiveness of the device. Lights: it’s advertised as a gaming keyboard. I’m not a gamer, nor will I ever be. You CAN turn off the lights. Simply read the paperwork that comes in the package to know how.

reviews.title: Buen sonido y calidad por el precio, pero software y patas mejorables
reviews.body: El teclado superó mis expectativas en lo esencial: sonido “thock” muy placentero, pulsaciones firmes y tres modos de conexión que funcionan sin problema. La construcción se siente sólida; el plástico es grueso y limpio al tacto, de mejor calidad que en otros modelos de su rango. Puntos a favor: Excelente sensación y respuesta lineal. Sonido grave-cremoso desde fábrica, sin necesidad de mods. Muy buen valor por el precio: se acerca a prestaciones “custom” de gamas más altas. Puntos a mejorar: El software de administración fue inútil en dos PC. La página es confusa, y aunque el teclado fue reconocido, no ofrecía opciones reales de configuración. La parte trasera utiliza un plástico más sencillo, y las gomas antideslizantes están pegadas con cinta doble faz que comenzó a despegarse desde el primer día. Me preocupa que se pierdan o necesiten ser reemplazadas pronto. No incluye numpad: ideal para gaming y escritura, pero puede ser limitante para quienes usan mucho la entrada numérica. Conclusión: Una excelente puerta de entrada al mundo “custom” por su sonido, tacto y conectividad, siempre que no dependas del software ni necesites un teclado completo. Nota aparte (no influye en la calificación del producto): el rastreo tardó cuatro días en actualizarse; el paquete llegó sin daños, pero el proceso logístico, la comunicación y el profesionalismo por parte del vendedor pueden mejorar.

reviews.title: Fantastic Keybaord
reviews.body: Excellent Product

reviews.title: BEST KEYBOARD I HAVE EVER USED. WORTH EVERY PENNY.
reviews.body: Honestly, I am absolutely blown away with the quality of this kisnt KN85, it's hands down the best keyboard I have ever owned. First of all, the sound quality of the key click is insane, this thing is so thocky with the bsun switches, PBT double shot key caps, gasket mounts and multiple layers of dampening foam/silicone, genuinely such a pleasure to type with. It is even hot-swappable if you want to change or upgrade your switches. The battery life is amazing, first use never charged out of the box lasted over a full week of heavy daily use. I find it very hard to find any fault with this keyboard whatsoever. One note is that the LED's are south-facing, so shine-through backlit keycaps won't work, I like double-shot caps for the thock, so this doesn't bother me one bit. But seriously, I have never been so happy to be typing at my desk. It has changed my whole experience. I watch reviews of £200-£500 keyboards, and I still think this is better. All I will say is get it fast, as prices are constantly rising due to demand.

reviews.title: It's really solid
reviews.body: looks and feels amazing, setup was easy and battery is lasting along time which is great. but the sound of the keyboard is so creamy, it really does sound like a premium keyboard. I also love the beige color scheme its very clean yet retro and the letters are bolded and of course its not a lousy 60% so you can enjoy all the key functions without having to press FN all the time

reviews.title: Better than expected
reviews.body: Awesome keyboard that punches above its weight. Stock switches are louder than I'd like, but hey it's a custom keyboard, so just swap them out easily for anything you like. For the price it's great keyboard. ONLY major issue is I like separate numpad controllers (I put these on the right of my mouse so it's quicker) but Kisnt only make these seperate numpads for the two other colour schemes that exist. The beige and green scheme is missing.

title: Razer BlackWidow V4 X Mechanical Gaming Keyboard, Yellow Switches, Black

reviews.title: Best Keyboard I've Had
reviews.body: Zero complaints, satisfying sound, a lot of cool features. Very satisying feeling when typing, not loud or clunky at all. You can tell the quality of the build by the weigh it feels and it's weight. I love also the volume wheel, so cool!

reviews.title: It's a good board
reviews.body: Ok, so after spending a couple weeks with this board I can tell you- A couple of things I wasn't really aware of- 1) Just how much pressure I'm used to applying at rest on keys 2) How much I relied on outside esc and ctrl keys for orientation These keys are very sensitive compared to the old BW I've used for years. I've been accidentally entering a lot of keystrokes at rest. They are very quiet and soft stroking compared to the green switches in the older Black Widow I've retired. So if you want clicks, feedback or resistance look elsewhere. Believe it or not my main hesitation for getting this board was the outside left row of programmable keys. I was afraid that it would be in the way and get confused with my escape and control keys, which yes has been very challenging to get used to, but it's no fault of the board itself knowing what I was getting. I pulled up all those caps on that row and replaced with wider pudding caps for brighter distinction. Programed those keys to mirror their neighbors, esc ,Ctrl etc so that when an erroneous keystroke is made it should at least still be the function I was looking for, albeit orientation may be off from wasd. So anyway I'm having to look down a lot more at the keyboard and retraining my mind to orient off the *F key

reviews.title: Durable and well built. Survived a liquid disaster.
reviews.body: I have the green switch version. Durable and Chroma lighting is excellent. Put O rings in the keys to dampen slightly. Key feeling and clicks are a matter of personal preference. Spilled coffee on this one twice. I thought the keyboard was toast after the last disaster spill. Keys weren't functioning and the leds were out. I took it apart and rinsed it out the affected areas heavily with alcohol. Blew the liquid out with compressed air/compressor. Works fine now. After taking it apart I could see how good the quality was. Keyboard backplate is actually solid metal. 2 screws under the top two rubber foot pads. Careful, the pads tear easily. 18+- screws under the keys. Remove the keys to find them all.

reviews.title: Great Keyboard, would buy again
reviews.body: Had it for a bit over a week now and it's been great. I originally had the Razer blackwidow V1 with the green clicks switches and it was great the thing finally crapped out on me a few weeks ago. The thing lasted me forever, was super durable and felt very responsive. My biggest complaint was it was hard to clean. So I decided to go with the newest version and try the Yellow switches. I didn't like the softer yellow switches at first but have come to like them and this keyboard solved the cleaning issue. My biggest problem was actually the Macro keys on the left hand side. With my old keyboard I used the edge of they keyboard to orient my hand without looking when gaming, this makes it hard to do that because my fingers end up on the macro keys. I've started to retrain myself to position properly but it wasn't easy. Other than that this keyboard is fantastic.

reviews.title: Works great, looks great
reviews.body: Awesome keyboard!

reviews.title: great keyboard
reviews.body: absolutely love it great keyboard. really good for the price lighting on the rgb is amazing. so far it feels really durable.

reviews.title: Shoddy Construction, Unresponsive key issues
reviews.body: Before I got this keyboard, I was using the 2016 edition razer blackwidow ultimate. That keyboard still works perfectly, and the only problem I had with it was that the keyboard was LOUD as heck. Enter the blackwidow v4 x with yellow switches. At first i was extremely happy with the look, feel, and materials of the keyboard, it felt very premium, and the keys were MUCH quieter. I bought it in December of 2023. By March 2024 I noticed an issue with the "P" key being unresponsive. Meaning when you press the key, there was a chance of it not registering the keypress. So if you press the key 10 times, it may only display about 5 or 6 times. Not that bad for gaming since the "P" key is hardly used. However when typing it could get very annoying. I attached a video showing me trying to press the button 3 times, followed by a space, then the button 3 times, then a space etc. You can clearly see it does not register the keypress quite often. Eventually I decided that since I paid $100+ I was going to get a working product. My RMA process started on April 20, 2024, and after many days of back and forth emails with razer trying to convince them it was a hardware, not software, issue they gave me a shipping label to send out on April 26, 2024. I received the replacement about 3 weeks later on May 17, 2024. Today on May 18, 2024 I noticed the same unresponsive key issue with the "2" key above the "W" key. This IS a big deal for gaming since it is used very often. I dont want to go through the RMA process again, and im pretty sure I cant get a refund from amazon after 4 months so this keyboard will likely just be tossed in the garbage where it belongs. A lot of time and money wasted on a sub-par product. Been using Razer keyboards and mice since about 2012 but its probably time to try a different brand to try since their quality seems to have gone down. Shame.

title: RisoPhy Mechanical Gaming Keyboard, RGB 104 Keys Ultra-Slim LED Backlit USB Wired Keyboard with Blue Switch, Durable Abs Keycaps/Anti-Ghosting/Spill-Resistant Computer Keyboard for PC Mac Xbox Gamer

reviews.title: ★★★★★ Great first impressions!
reviews.body: Just received my RisoPhy RGB Mechanical Gaming Keyboard and I'm already impressed! Unboxing was smooth — everything was well packaged and arrived in perfect condition. Right out of the gate, the mechanical switches feel fantastic — satisfying and responsive with great tactile feedback. Typing this review on it now and it already feels way better than my old membrane keyboard. The RGB lighting looks amazing — all 104 keys are individually backlit with tons of color and lighting mode options. Instantly upgraded the look of my desk setup. Build quality feels solid and premium — no flex, no creaking, and the keycaps have a nice, smooth texture. It's a standard full-size layout with number pad, so it was easy to jump right in with no learning curve. Can't speak to long-term durability yet, but based on first impressions, this keyboard seems like an excellent value. Will update if anything changes, but so far I'm very happy

reviews.title: Great mechanical keyboard for productivity
reviews.body: Bought this keyboard for my office, as a replacement for a wireless, membrane based keyboard that was starting to show its age. The value of this keyboard is excellent. Based on the feel, it seems to be a true mechanical keyboard with switches, and not a simulated one using a membrane contact with a clicky mechanism. The feel is great and the pressure is just right to prevent most accidental touches to adjacent keys from inserting extra letters. Nice and clicky, maybe not the best for noise if you're in an office with other people, but the feel is great and if you work in a private office like I do the noise won't matter much. I had thought the RGB colors would be distracting, especially for an office, but actually they are fairly subdued and actually seem to help with positioning (I am a fast hunt-and-peck 3 finger typist, so this actually matters a lot to me). I have a much more expensive Razer mechanical gaming keyboard at home, and the main difference I see between them, other than cosmetic differences, is that the Razer keys seem like they have a hair trigger and require very little motion to produce keystrokes, while this keyboard is a bit stiffer and requires the keys to be depressed a little harder in order to produce a keystroke. So if you are relying on a hair trigger response for gaming, this maybe is not the best choice, although for a casual gamer like me it's more than adequate. But for actually getting work done, the hair-trigger of the Razer keyboard makes it really hard not to make typos, and this keyboard is a lot better in that regard. One minor nitpick is that the font used to label the keys is a little odd, and the "6" really, really looks like a "G", which can be a little off-putting at first. But that's just a minor quibble. Final verdict: Definitely worth buying, unless you're an absolutely elite hardcore gamer.

reviews.title: Great for those with long nails.
reviews.body: I got this keyboard for a couple of reasons. I type at night, and when I wake up early, I'll do schoolwork. It's backlit and I can see the keys in the dark. There are a few settings to have the keys act or light up differently. And, because I have medium-long nails - the keys are large enough, and there is enough space between them, to accommodate my medium-length gel nails. I got raised keycaps to stick on the keys of this keyboard but they are not necessary for the length of my nails. Its appearance is as depicted, not too big, not too small. The keyboard connected easily to my laptop and is just as easy to set on top when not in use. It unplugs from the USB outlet easily, making removability a cinch when I decide enough is enough (not often) and pack everything up and put it away. It's very responsive, typing exactly as I type or game. None of the keys have stopped working or gotten stuck, even with my long nails. I love the sound of the keys clicking, again not too loud nor too soft. It gives me a 90s vibe while typing, and I can hear if I've hit the keys. Overall, I'm very glad I decided to buy this keyboard. It's perfect for my needs.

reviews.title: Nice, blue switch. led mechanical keyboard that doesn't break the bank.
reviews.body: If you're looking for a slim, low profile, led mechanical keyboard with blue switches, then you will be happy with this. The keyboad is exactly as described in the listing. The keyboard housing is made of plastic which makes the keyboard lightweight. The keys have a nice tactile feel with a nice "clicky" sound. The build quality is good, but doesn't compare to the solid feel of my Motospeed or Red Dragon keyboards. Included with the keyboard is a little plastic keycap puller. The led's are nice and bright and can be turned off. The CON is that each key is a set color, so if you're looking for a keyboard whose keys can change to various colors, you might want to skp this one. I personally did not care for any of the available 9 light modes. The 9 modes were definitely not exciting in my opinion and with keys being a preset color, I found some of the modes quite distracting. You can increase, decrease the brightness or turn off the leds. If you're looking for a keyboard where each key can display a multitude of different colors, this is keyboard is not for you. As for the the sole purpose of using this as a mechanical keyboard, then you won't be disappointed. I purchased this for use at work because I love the tactile feedback of mechanical keyboards. I didn't not test the liquid resistance of the kayboard but there are cutouts on the bottom for liquid drainage. No key ghosting was detected during its use. Again, if LED keyboards is what you fancy, I don't think you will be pleased with this because the keys are a preset color and can't be changed. As for the function of being a mechnical keyboard, this works well for the price point.

reviews.title: Mechanical Gaming Keyboard – Over a Year of Flawless Performance!
reviews.body: After using this mechanical gaming keyboard for well over a year now, I can confidently say it's one of the best purchases I've ever made — not a single issue has come up the entire time. It's seen heavy daily use for both gaming and typing, and it's held up beautifully, including one memorable incident where I accidentally spilled soda right onto it; I was able to quickly disassemble it, clean it thoroughly with water and some rubbing alcohol, and it came back working like nothing ever happened, which speaks volumes about its build quality and durability. The RGB lighting is absolutely vibrant and stunning, with multiple settings and effects that let me customize the look to match my setup, whether I'm going for a subtle glow or a full-blown rainbow light show. The mechanical blue switches are honestly the sweet spot — they offer that satisfying, tactile clicky feel that's so satisfying for typing, while still being incredibly responsive and snappy for gaming, and thanks to the full anti-ghosting on the 104 keys, every single keypress registers perfectly even during the most intense, fast-paced gaming moments. With its rugged build, gorgeous RGB, fantastic switches, and full-sized layout, this keyboard has completely exceeded my expectations — I couldn't recommend it more to anyone looking for a reliable, high-performing mechanical keyboard!

Decided to give this keyboard a try. It’s awesome! So much easier to type with my long nails. The colors are so pretty. I love that you can change them to do different things. The best part is the clicky keys. The sound is so relaxing. I would 100% recommend this keyboard. The colors are bright ant vibrant, the clicks are calming. reviews.title: Feels like the legendary Model M, sporting it strong points and its quirks.
reviews.body: If you missed the old,clicky Model M from IBM, this keyboard emulates it pretty well. One must consider though, that it may emulate it too well. If you have fat fingers, you will find yourself making the same typos that you mad in high school when you learned to type on one. However, this is no deal breaker in my opinion. The speed at which I can type has vastly improved with the solid tactile feedback that tells you without a doubt that you press was registered. Setup couldn't be easier, just plug it into any USB port and away you go. Recognizes immediately as a 104 key with perks. Having the media controls and other immediate functions right there is nice too. As far as the design goes, it is very rugged and ready for the millions of keystrokes you will put on it as a writer. You will find a kind of typing joy you haven't experienced in quite a long time. No soft-touch or sickle keyboard will match the feel from what you get here. The only thing I find really off is the shallow height of the back stands. I think that they should be redesigned to be a bit taller. I cut a little piece of flat trim to set them on and that made the angle perfect. All-in-all, this keyboard is a joy to type on. I don't use it for gaming, because I see this as a waste of a premium feeling keyboard, wearing out the ASWD area and ruining it. I haven't had such a good keyboard in years and I'm not destroying that way. The one caveat I would warn you about is that if you use it on a KVM switch that is USB powered, this keyboard draws quite a bit of power to run the back light. be aware that you may get video background issues. Mine works just fine if I turn the backlight down low.

reviews.title: High Quality, Gorgeous LED Backlighting, Perfect Price
reviews.body: This mechanical keyboard is amazing for gamers looking to pick up a high-quality blue-switch mechanical keyboard. When I consider and review this product, I keep the following factors in mind: Functionality and Use - 5/5 The overall functionality of this keyboard is perfect, leaving me with minimal complains as a high-frequency and intensity user. As a proficient typist, I frequently type over 120 WPM and use combinations of hotkeys to complete tasks efficiently. This keyboard has supported this level of use during work/office settings, and feels highly responsive and crisp during high-intensity gaming moments, due to the blue key-switches creating a noticeable "click" with each keypress. If you have roommates or family, you may want to consider the clicking sounds of this keyboard while typing. The fact that they will likely hear your typing due to the pure "clicky-ness" of the key switches may present itself as an issue to some. Personally, this is not a factor that applies to my circumstances. Build Quality and Durability - 5/5 After 1 Month of intensive use, I have not noticed any issues so far in terms of key-press responsiveness, structural integrity, or wiring/USB issues. The keys hold in place well and the LED's have stayed consistently bright. Product Design - 5/5 The design of this keyboard is minimal, but effective. Exactly what I was looking for when shopping for a keyboard within this general price range. The all-black style allows the LED backlights to really *pop*, even in bright light/daylight. The inclusion of a "Fn" key allows for the same hotkeys and macros most would be used to with other keyboards, such as volume control and media playback, amongst other things. QoL Features - 4.5/5 This keyboard comes with 9 different LED-backlighting effects, such as lighting per keypress, "breathing" effects, WASD + Arrow Key backlighting, and more to complement a variety of use-cases. It would be nice to have the option to customize the LED backlighting colours themselves, as the backlighting options are pre-set; however, the crisp glow and colour choice are visually appealing and I am happy with the options provided. Value for Money - 5/5 Overall, I am highly satisfied with the purchase of this Keyboard and would recommend it to any gamer, office-worker, or avid tech geek like myself. For such a low price-point, you are getting a physical product that is equal in quality to that of a name brand like Razer or Corsair, without paying for the related bloatware and branding. Anybody looking to pick up their first mechanical keyboard, you cannot go wrong with this!

reviews.title: Good quality, affordable mechanical keyboard. Surprised by its quality given its price range.
reviews.body: Very satisfied with this purchase. Head and shoulders above my membrane Logitech K120 Wired Business Keyboard, and without breaking the bank too! To be honest, I feel lucky to have gotten this keyboard at such a low price. At this price point, I could not find a single mechanical keyboard that met all of my requirements but this one. In fact, even some of the more expensive mechanical keyboards didn't meet all of my requirements. For starters, the keyboard uses the UK layout with the pound sign and hash symbol key in the right place—very important for me. Second, this is a full-size keyboard with a numeric keypad at the right. This was important for me as I wanted a keyboard that did all of the same things as my previous keyboard, the only difference being that it is mechanical—a requirement that this RisoPhy mechanical keyboard fulfils precisely. (I should note, too, that most of the mechanical keyboards at this price range and even some more expensive ones, being shorter in width, lacked a numeric keypad.) Then there is the feel of the keyboard. The product description says that it uses "BLUE switches", seemingly modelling its switches on the classic tactile and clicky Cherry MX Blue switches. (It is unlikely that the keyboard uses actual Cherry MX Blue switches, given the price range, but rather its own knock-off versions of the switches.) While this may not be what some gamers are looking for (looking for something smoother and offering the same resistance all the way down without a slight bump as you press each key), this is perfect for me, as I was looking for a keyboard that produced nice responsive, tactile feedback, mirroring a classic typewriter effect. Some people may be put off by this, thinking that it makes the keyboard too noisy, and while, yes, there is a clicking noise with each key press, it honestly isn't that loud (though because there is still an audible clicking noise, I can understand criticisms saying that this keyboard is inappropriate for an office environment, for example, where such a constant clicking noise can cause distractions.) The keyboard is nice to type on, which is my primary use for it rather than gaming. A feature I don't care as much for is the rainbow backlighting. From my tests, the "9 different backlights" settings mentioned in the product description work exactly as expected. Also working as intended (at least from my tests on Windows 11) are the "12 multimedia combinations", effectively function keys that perform operations, such as, open a calculator and open Windows search. The major downside to this keyboard that I can think of is that the keyboard switches are not hot-swappable (though at this price point, this isn't a disappointment but just something to be expected.) In all, if you are looking for a keyboard that meets some of the same requirements as I was, at this price, I am unaware of a better keyboard on this website than this one.

reviews.title: Parfait pour les frappes rapides
reviews.body: Comme dit dans un autre commentaire, il est parfait quand c'est ce qu'on veut. J'écris énormément et j'ai une frappe très rapide. Quand on frappe vite, le top c'est un clavier mécanique de ce type, et c'est très rare d'en trouver à moins de 100€! [FRAPPE] J'ai une préférence pour ceux avec un retour son (comme sont les claviers à switch/commutateur bleu) et bon un anti-ghosting: on peut frapper vite, avec exactitude et si besoin corriger dans l'immédiat. Que ce soit pour du gaming ou de la frappe écrite très rapide, c'est un excellent clavier. Par contre, clairement, je ne vois pas des personnes qui tapent occasionnellement supporter ce clavier, qui est bruyant... comme un clavier à commutateur bleu! Quand je suis au téléphone, j'essaie parfois de taper un truc discrètement: je me fais griller systématiquement et on me dit de ne pas fracasser mon clavier... les gens sont habitués à des claviers silencieux. [SOLIDITÉ] Le clavier est vraiment excellent: je l'utilise depuis 1 an, de manière intensive. La touche espace est un peu usée (lustrée mais on voit toujours la barre horizontale) mais toutes les touches sont encore parfaitement lisibles, ce qui est exceptionnel pour de l'ABS et mon utilisation intensive! Des heures de frappe par jour, au moins un nettoyage par semaine (pas délicat, avec un produit, et des brosses pour enlever les masses de poils de chats... et les miettes ^^ ). [ERGONOMIE] La surélévation est un peu trop marquée pour moi: elle créé une casse du poignet qui fatigue, mais le retour tactile est énorme. Comme dit, le rétroéclairage est à un dosage parfait: ni trop peu (aide au repère rapide en cas de besoin), ni trop (fatigue des yeux). Les pattes arrières qui ont tendance à se replier, mais je suis une grosse brute et ça me gêne moins que sur de nombreux claviers. [CONCLUSION] Clavier adapté à une personne qui cherche du matériel solide, efficace, de bonne qualité à petit prix et surtout un clavier mécanique avec un retour son marqué. Pour moi on n'est pas loin du clavier parfait!

reviews.title: MUST BUY 10/10
reviews.body: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ 5/5 Stars The AULA 99 Wireless Keyboard has been an amazing addition to my setup. The tri-mode connectivity is incredibly convenient, allowing me to switch seamlessly between Bluetooth, 2.4GHz wireless, and USB-C wired mode depending on what I need. Pairing was quick and easy, and the connection has remained stable with no noticeable lag. The keyboard feels premium and well-built, with responsive keys that provide a satisfying typing experience for both gaming and everyday work. The compact 99-key layout saves desk space while still keeping all the essential keys easily accessible. Battery life has been excellent, and I love the flexibility of being able to connect multiple devices. The customization options and overall design give it a modern, high-end feel that stands out from other keyboards in its price range. For anyone looking for a reliable, versatile, and comfortable wireless keyboard, the AULA 99 is a fantastic choice. Great quality, great performance, and absolutely worth the purchase!

reviews.title: Amazing Value for Many Features
reviews.body: Keyboard is amazing, has all of my needs met. It's a full keyboard with NUM pad, has a backlight that can be adjusted either by color, by pattern, or by brightness, AND connects to multiple devices simulataneously. The keyboard is *NOT* quiet. But it's a "thocky" sounding keyboard. The taps are thick, muffled, and soft. I do wish the booklet that came with it had better instructions. I couldn't find in it how to switch the backlight pattern and had to ask Alexa on the product listing after it arrived. But the booklet does show how to program the buttons, install the software, and switch between connection modes. I'm definitely a fan for the price. Other keyboards with these features can be up to $70+ so this is basically a steal and such a great product for the value. I'd get more but because it connects to multiple devices, I only need one!

reviews.title: Works. Just okay
reviews.body: This keyboard is adorable, has great soft (not super quiet, but soft feeling) key presses, its responsive, and it has great connectivity options. Its a happy medium between a full size keyboard versus a compact layout, and it's so easy and smooth to type on. That said, the RGB backlighting does not work for me. I've followed the instructions sent with the keyboard, followed the troubleshooting instructions from AULA and from Amazon, used AULA's software for this keyboard, tried factory resetting, and googled for help videos or anything I could find. Reached out to AULA's support, and they were unwilling to assist and just directed me to Amazon. All I could find on Amazon was the seller's support information. At this point I'm just accepting that it's a defect and something must be wrong within the keyboard, and I'm not savvy enough to diagnose their hardware issues nor do I have the time or will to demand a refund or replacement. The keyboard works great without RGB, but it was a big feature for me when purchasing this as it was mostly an aesthetic purchase. Yeah, I could have picked other options, but I chose this because of the price and I wish I hadn't. So, knocked two stars off for me. TL;DR - it's just a keyboard that you can use on multiple devices. If you just want simple for a good price, this is for you, cause it's a solid option. Don't expect support from the seller or be surprised when the extra functions don't work.

reviews.title: Gaming and Office
reviews.body: This keyboard is pretty amazing. It's very easy to set up and use. I use it for both office-type work and online gaming. It is not a quiet keyboard, typing makes some sound, which I personally prefer. I love the extra controls like the dial for volume. The LED lighting has a lot of customization, even including adding a custom color, if you install the " AULA S99 三模RGB版 " software, but there are also shortcut keys to just quickly flip through the preset modes/colors. It has multiple options for connection(BT/GHz/USB), and they all work smoothly & without error that I've encountered. I like that there is the option to keep it on consistently if it's plugged in(USB), but I wish there was the option to do that while running on its charge too(BT/GHz). If it isn't plugged in, it will go to sleep with inactivity, but that's really my only complaint. I have not noticed any type of lag or input errors when using it. If anything, it's a little extra sensitive and, when first using it, I was typing some double letters by accident, so it is very responsive. I found it to be perfect even for fast-paced online competitive gaming, which says a lot for a small and affordable company/product. For the price, it's a no-brainer. AULA, PLEASE MAKE A MOUSE TO GO WITH THIS THAT HAS CUSTOMIZEABLE LEDS AND A COUPLE BUTTONS ON IT PRETTY PLEASEEEEEE. <3

reviews.title: Cute, has a few quirks but good keyboard

I may test if charging is for some reason a USB-C to USB-C requirement as well. My keyboard in the picture is up on a keyboard riser so it isn’t actually that tall or angled.
