title: Cherry KC 200 MX Wired Mechanical Office Keyboard MX2A Silent RED Switches

reviews.title: Very good for the price
reviews.body: This is certainly a bargain priced mechanical keyboard but that doesn't mean it's bad; in fact, it's excellent. I got the model with silent red switches. I already own a Cherry silent red without the number pad but I wanted a full size. This one is ever so slightly less silent, likely due to an aluminum frame (a plus) rather than plastic. But it is still quiet enough to use in the bedroom at any hour. It is wired only. I actually prefer a wired connection rather than fooling with Bluetooth or dongles. To save space there is no plastic "frame" around the keys but this is just a matter of looks and you may prefer it, as the aluminum base is very attractive. It did take a little positioning to reach a stable state but that may have been my desk as much as the keyboard. There are tabs to raise the back but I don't use them. The keys are clearly marked and have a good feel to them. Let's see if with use they take on a shine; it's too soon to tell. This is a keyboard I will use a lot as I do most of my work on my home desktop setup. So far the typing experience has been exactly what I expect from this type of switch; there is enough of a tactile feel to be reliable but of course it's limited by the damped switches. (I do love the positive solid feedback of the very loud, clicky blue switches but my home office is in the bedroom and that doesn't work out.) The only thing I can't speak to is the software for remapping the keys. This can be downloaded from the Cherry site. But it doesn't run on my Linux system so I can't make use of it. However I really see no need to remap any of the keys, and if I really need to do that, there are other ways. I definitely rate this keyboard at 5 stars. It is great value for the money and gets you into the wonderful world of mechanical keyboards without breaking the bank. I have had great luck with Cherry products and this one is another winner.

reviews.title: I can't believe the improvement over other switches. It's crazy!
reviews.body: If you thought other companies made good key switches, then you are in for a surprise with this keyboard. Cherry absolutely nailed it with these new MX2A switches. I purchased the version with the Cherry MX2A Silent Red switches. Now, I basically hate linear switches. Really, I usually can't stand them, but these new silents reds are the smoothest, and most buttery feeling switches I have ever felt. I have been using mechanical keyboards my entire life. Since before the patent ran out on the Cherry MX switches and the only mechanical keyboards you could buy had Cherry switches. Now, everyone makes their own switches, with all kinds of "features" like hall effect, rapid trigger, analog, adjustable actuation, magnets, etc.. Here's the issue with all of those though, they feel like crap to type on and are super loud. I have spent thousands on keyboards over the years. I still have over 15 mechanical keyboards sitting in storage that I stopped using. I am not exaggerating either. To give you an idea of where I'm coming from, my favorite switches used to be Cherry MX Brown. Now they are Cherry MX2A Silent Reds. I haven't even mentioned how quiet they are too. Unbelievably quiet for a mechanical keyboard. It's definitely the quietest mech keyboard I have ever used, which is saying a lot. Some people may think the keyboard is fairly basic, and in all reality, it is. It doesn't require software, doesn't have RGB or any lights (besides the led for caps lock and such), it doesn't have a removeable cable, or a super high polling rate over 1000Hz. Visually and functionally speaking, the keyboard is simple. But that a huge positive in my book. It does have full N-key rollover, so if you do use it for gaming, there won't be any issues there. I don't need to install any bloat to use the keyboard. I don't need to configure anything. It's just plug and play. It's fairly compact for a full-sized keyboard too, so be aware of the slightly more compact layout. My only real complaint is that it does not have 4 rubber feet on the bottom to keep it from sliding around. There are 2 rubber feet on the bottom front, but on the bottom rear, the feet are hard plastic, so it doesn't stay in place super well. There are rubber pads on the bottom rear feet that fold out, but I don't use a keyboard angled, so they are useless for me. Other than that, one thing, this keyboard is perfect for me. Am I going to use it for my hardcore gaming sessions? No. I actually purchased it for office work, and it's going to be perfect for that. However, will I be purchasing another keyboard with these same exact switches for my gaming pc? 100% YES! Look, you may not like the design of this keyboard, or its simplicity, but do not sleep on these new Cherry switches. Cherry is back with a vengeance, and if you're looking for a new keyboard, get one with these new Cherry switches. Whether it be this keyboard or not. The switch is king, and Cherry is back on top. Update: I now own 3 of these keyboards, lol, all with the Cherry MX2A Silent Red switches. One for the gaming pc, one for the work office, and one for the home office. They can't be beaten when it comes to typing quality. No regrets.

reviews.title: Great Office Keyboard
reviews.body: I got this keyboard 3 weeks ago and I am very impressed. I used this at work and it suits my needs perfectly. It is extremely elegant and the keys are so satisfying to press. It feels very solid and hopefully should last a very long time. I share an office with one other person and the silent red switches are perfect for my environment. I would definitely recommend this keyboard to anyone who wants a simple but effective office keyboard.

reviews.title: Good first mechanical keyboard
reviews.body: Great productivity keyboard. Satisfying “thunk” on usage with fast throw. The switches being reds are easy so it doesn’t take much effort and it’s a good mechanical keyboard if you are coming from a cheaper style membrane or scissor style keyboard but want to venture into the world of mechanical keyboards. Not perfect but pretty good especially for the money.

reviews.title: New favorite office keyboard!
reviews.body: I have always had mechanical keyboards but they are loud and are not appreciated by coworkers in nearby offices. This keyboard solves the problem and sacrifices nothing to do so. It turned out to be quieter than I thought it would be and feels great for all day typing!

reviews.title: Great keyboard with no complaints.
reviews.body: Has held up extremely well! My typing speed has held up through a fairly intensive use for this while using Discord fairly heavily, while writing 3+ hours per day and while gaming on fairly heavily (Helldivers 2, Deadlock, Counter-Strike). The keys are a little heavy but in a way that seems well-built rather than is exhausting to type with. It's very nice to type with and gives good feedback. The keys spring back in a very responsive manner and provide a very good typing experience. The layout and feeling of typing with it overall has been really nice, no complaints of things like function keys. The dedicated calculator function key is unexpectedly more helpful than I had given it credit for and all function keys work with Linux.

reviews.title: Beautiful keyboard, but too cramped/crowded.
reviews.body: Almost perfect, but the function key row is terribly integrated. It's too close to the number row. Same issue for the arrow keys and number pad. They're all too close together and I hit adjacent keys. Since every other keyboard in the world has separation, due to muscle memory I find myself hitting the function keys when reaching for the number row. I have giant hands though, so may be less of a nuisance for normal-handed folks. They should have made the keyboard a quarter inch taller and half inch wider and fixed this.

reviews.title: Smooth and easy keys.
reviews.body: When I started looking for a keyboard all I wanted was easy push keys and this one fits the bill. I love the raised keys and the buttons are very smooth and easy to press. I work at a computer all day and love this keyboard. It has significantly eased my finger fatigue. Would recommend 👌 Also the keys are very quiet. I have had this keyboard for several months now and its still like new.

reviews.title: Swapped from a Razer Ornata v3, no regrets
reviews.body: I was using an Ornata v3 before this, which is pretty close in price. I wanted something I could use for both work and gaming. Here's a comparison that might help if you're looking for where this excels against the Ornata and similar competitors: No lighting: I'm tired of everything having freaking lights on them! I could just disable it in the settings I guess, but then I'm just paying for a feature I'm never using. Only keys with a light are Capslock and Numlock to let you know they're on. Keys: Good tactile feel and not too loud. Just enough of each to make you feel like you're typing. I use it for both gaming and work and it handles both jobs well. Very responsive for gaming. Some might consider it a little loud if you're in a cubicle with someone and you have to type a lot, but that's what headphones are for I guess! You won't find a more quiet mechanical keyboard that stll has that tactile typing feel, so you'll have to choose which you value more. (feel > sound for me) Size: A big more compact that some keyboards, but that's a plus. No lost real estate around the edges, just well-spaced keys and easy typing. You don't feel cramped at all if you're a touch typer. It has some heft to it. I often sit with it on my lap and it's fine. Not bouncing around like leaf, but doesn't cut off circulation to your legs. Durability: Again, it has some heft to it. When I pick it up I have a habit of snagging a key and pulling the cap off. I actually broke a key or two on my Ornata because the cap connectors are flimsy plastic posts and trying to find replacements was a nightmare. These keys are well-made and durable; haven't lost one yet. Only negative to me was the Calculator(???) button in the top-right. When I have it on my lap I was accidentally pressing it against the edge of my desk a lot and opening calculator app(s) mid-game; very frustrating. It was a simple job to go into windows settings and remove the mapping to the key (google for instructions) and now it's not an issue for a recliner like me. Anyone having it sit on their desk will likely never have this issue. I was a little leery of the price point when purchasing, but I'm seeing the value in the design, layout and build quality. I don't regret my purchase at all. In the last couple years I've gone through Razer, Steel Series and Logitech keyboards all around the $100 price point and this is by far my favourite. Highly recommend it.

reviews.title: perfect for work
reviews.body: perfect for silent work environments, very nice to the touch

reviews.title: Great product and service
reviews.body: Extremely happy with product

reviews.title: Great but over-priced on Amazon
reviews.body: Excellent keyboard, works very well for gaming. The problem is the price: when I bought mine for $101 CAN, they were decent value for the money. Now a year later they want $216 CAN for them, and...that's a little absurd.

title: RK ROYAL KLUDGE R98 Pro Wired Mechanical Keyboard, 96% Creamy Gaming Keyboard RGB Backlit with Number Pad and Volume Knob, Gasket Mount, MDA Profile PBT Keycaps, Hot Swappable Pre-lubed Linear Switch

reviews.title: As per Description!!
reviews.body: I’ve been using the RK Royal Kludge R98 Pro for a little over a week, and I’m honestly impressed with how much value this keyboard delivers. The moment you take it out of the box, it feels solid and well-built definitely not your typical budget keyboard. Typing Experience (5/5) The gasket mount design combined with the pre‑lubed linear switches makes typing incredibly smooth and quiet. It has that “creamy” feel everyone talks about. No pinging, no rattling just clean, soft keystrokes. The MDA profile PBT keycaps are thick, durable, and comfortable to type on. Design & Layout (5/5) I love the 96% layout. It saves desk space but still includes a full number pad, which I use constantly for work. The addition of the volume knob is a nice touch and works great for quick adjustments. RGB & Customization (4.5/5) The RGB is bright, vibrant, and offers a ton of effects. Customizing it is easy once you get familiar with the shortcuts. I only wish the software was a bit more intuitive, but it’s definitely not a deal‑breaker. Performance (5/5) For gaming, it’s responsive and stable with zero noticeable latency. Hot‑swappable sockets are a big win if you ever want to switch to different switches later. Overall If you’re looking for a keyboard that feels like a premium custom build for a fraction of the price, the RK R98 Pro is a fantastic choice. Great for both work and gaming, excellent build quality, and a super satisfying typing experience. Highly recommended!

reviews.title: Amazing gaming keyboard
reviews.body: So, i dont usually write reviews, but i felt i had to for this keyboards. the creamy clicks are AMAZING (its my first time having it so im super impressed.) the tiny screen is actually pretty simple and easy to use, you can customize the backlight color and style, speed, etc. the knob works perfect. feels great. it came with extra keys, a usb-c to plug in if you prefer wired, and a key remover. everything feels amazing, very high quality. its obviously not 10 pounds, but carries some heft that feels super secure. its got little folded stands to prop your keyboard up if desired, which i think is super nice. i love the color variety (i got the brown, for reference.), it can be hard finding a nice keyboard that is still stylish and pretty. im extremely satisfied, especially with the price being only 70 usd for this nice of a keyboard. i still have yet to use it, but im pretty confident it will be nice. ill update if anything happens!

reviews.title: I am surprised how much I actually like this keyboard
reviews.body: I recently purchased this item a couple of weeks ago and so I think it was a good purchase. First of all, they keyboard is super smooth and because of the switches, you do hear some clicks but they're not that loud, just enough to be satisfying. The product feels well-crafted with quality in mind. The keyboard stands; are the perfect size, not freakish large so typing for long periods of time is comfortable. I also like how they send you the "end" key in the box so if you don't like the volume knob, you can put the "end" key back in. I type 80 words a minute, especially when I am writing programs, I pleased on how well the keys on this board respond and the entire feeling of when a key is pressed. When I type superfast on things that are super important, I don't want my keyboard to fail me. Now, there are a few things I don't really like about it but overall, like I said, this is a great keyboard. - The volume knob: Hey, it works but personally, I feel that it is too close to the "pgdn" key so you really can't grip it like a knob. I kind of wished it had groves or something on the dial making it easier to turn. Right now, I just got to try and turn it little by little by spinning the know from the top down to the "-" key. That's about all the room you got. - Key position: This one is more of my fault. I am more used to full sized keyboards and not the space saving ones with less keys. The part that messes me up is where the arrows, shift, and enter is all smushed together. If this might also, be you, check out the S98 model instead. - Drivers and App: I can't really download this because the website is blocked at work for gaming lol. I don't know if the site is listed as gaming or if it is just because of their name. I know, this is totally not their fault haha.

reviews.title: Absolutely Impressed!
reviews.body: I upgraded my home gaming setup with this keyboard after considerable research, and it’s been a joy to use for both gaming and typing. Strengths: Premium typing experience: The pre-lubed cream linear switches and gasket mount deliver a “thocky” feel and satisfyingly smooth keystrokes. Typing and gaming are both quiet and comfortable, with five layers of foam dampening any hollow sounds. Customization: The included software lets me remap keys, create macros, and adjust more than 20 dynamic RGB lighting modes quickly. I loved being able to easily tweak the look and functionality. Build quality: PBT double-shot keycaps with an MDA profile feel sturdy and resist wear; they’re grippy and comfortable for long sessions. The detachable aluminum volume knob is a treat for instant control. Layout: The 98-key layout keeps the numpad and arrow keys but eliminates wasted space—a space-saving solution perfect for both gaming and work. Universal compatibility: Works perfectly with Windows and Mac out of the box, and includes both a 2-in-1 keycap/switch puller and extra switches for future customization. Bottom Line: This is an exceptional value for anyone who wants a customizable, quiet, and responsive keyboard for gaming, work, and creative projects. The smooth switches, full-featured software, and premium build make it a standout in its price range. Highly recommended for enthusiasts and everyday users alike.

reviews.title: Solid keyboard for the price
reviews.body: So I upgraded my desk setup to include this keyboard. I did minimal research but I knew I liked the color and the number pad. After having it for several months: 1. The keyboard is indeed "creamy" and smooth 2. The lighting is fun and the quality of the board is very nice. 3. It has a good weight and the volume knob is very helpful. 4. I am glad I didn't go smaller 5. The key swap capability is nice but I don't use it a whole lot. Overall a good keyboard to replace my Bluetooth work one. I definitely think this a worthy upgrade if you're in need of one.

reviews.title: Amazing keyboard - so far
reviews.body: I was looking for a keyboard that had a nice compact profile, looked nice, has a volume control knob, AND sounds great when typing. THIS keyboard literally hits everything I was looking for. It's just the right size and weight - it looks and feels premium. The keys have that creamy/clacky sound I was looking for. The colors of the keys are great - but that being said - the backlights don't seem as bright as other keyboards I've owned, but that's not really a big deal to me - but it might be to some people. Overall - I love this keyboard - now I just hope it lasts. I've read some reviews that make it seem like it might not, but I'm hoping it's durable. As of this review, I've only had it for about an hour, so I'll update this review if anything changes with time.

reviews.title: Where sound, price, and comfort meet.
reviews.body: Absolutely worth the money, and even got it on sale! As I was looking for a replacement for my Logitech G512 that had finally started to show its age, after nearly 5 years of daily wear and tear from both games and general typing, I stumbled upon this board after seeing the shop it was inside of. I've been using it now for close to a week, and it has sealed the deal for my desire to build a keyboard once I have the means to do such. Each keycap having a small variance in its elevation by just a few millimeters may not sound like much, but it allows for a much smoother flow in typing and touch feel as you move through the keys. Additionally the sound the keyboard makes with the lubed switches below each key, effectively a quiet thunk-click is just beautiful. Its also much quieter than the G512 was, and is less noticed by people when I am speaking with them over the phone for work. So major win there! Solid 5/5 stars, if you need a keyboard for a good price and solid function - fully recommend.

reviews.title: Loved it so much I bought 2 of them
reviews.body: This keyboard is great, little heavy and only connects via USB, but as far as everything else you'll be pressed to find a better keyboard at this price range that is as satisfying to type on, cause the "creamy" switches sound like something that punches WELL above its weight. Nothing necessarily ergonomic about it but it does have a satisfying color to it and the lights aren't exactly offensive in terms of "too bright" If you're looking for wireless don't get this one, look at RK's other offerings but if you're okay only hooking up wired for work or other reasons this is going to be the one you want.

reviews.title: Very good
reviews.body: Very good & my son loves his new keyboard

reviews.title: Légère fatigue mais très qualitatif
reviews.body: "+" - Injection qualitative des plastiques de touches, - Apparence flatteuse et châssis robuste, - Branding peu agressif, - Super réactif, - La définition du rétroéclairage RGB est excellente et les scénario LeD sont bons, - Format 98% vraiment cool. - Peu de vibration parasite, - Excellent rapport qualité/prix, - Jeu de remplacement de quelques switch et touche de remplacement de la molette si besoin. "-" - Certaines touches (Shift, Caps Lock, Tab) gigotent un peu, - Molette de son est lisse et difficile à tourner. Pourtant, elle est pourvu d'un mécanisme de haute qualité. - Le clavier est haut, sans repose poignet une fatigue est inévitable. - Toute tentative de nettoyage est vaine : démonter le clavier par strate est difficile. "i" - La distance d'activation est très courte, ma main au repos au dessus du clavier peut suffire à déclencher des commandes. C'est un moyen efficace de rendre le clavier réactif mais diminue le confort d'usage selon moi. - Le son "creamy" n'est pas de tous les goûts, mais c'est un bon compromis entre feeling mécanique et discrétion. Il est plus bruyant que des cherry brown ou les touches "brown" des claviers mécaniques logitech. J'aime beaucoup l'esthétique et la sonorité de ce clavier, je le recommande aux acheteurs éclairés ! :) Ma note était de 4/5, mais la marque m'a spontanément contacté pour mieux comprendre mon retour. Je pense qu'ils ont un service client absolument exemplaire.

reviews.title: Beste Tastatur für das Geld
reviews.body: Die RK ROYAL KLUDGE R98 Pro hat mich vom ersten Moment an überzeugt. Die Verarbeitung ist hochwertig, die Tastatur wirkt stabil und das kompakte 96-%-Layout bietet alle wichtigen Tasten inklusive Nummernblock, ohne unnötig viel Platz auf dem Schreibtisch einzunehmen. Besonders begeistert bin ich vom angenehmen Tippgefühl. Die bereits geschmierten Switches laufen butterweich und klingen dabei angenehm satt. Dank Hot-Swap lassen sich die Schalter bei Bedarf problemlos austauschen. Die RGB-Beleuchtung ist hell, vielseitig einstellbar und sorgt für eine tolle Optik. Auch der Drehregler ist im Alltag sehr praktisch, beispielsweise zum Regeln der Lautstärke. Insgesamt bietet die R98 Pro eine Ausstattung, die man sonst oft nur bei deutlich teureren Tastaturen findet. Für Gaming, Homeoffice und den täglichen Einsatz ist sie eine ausgezeichnete Wahl. Das Preis-Leistungs-Verhältnis ist hervorragend – ich würde sie jederzeit wieder kaufen.

reviews.title: Best keyboard ever!
reviews.body: I used to type 60wpm, now its 90wpm in only 1 week of having this keyboard. Its amazing for work!

reviews.title: Good product
reviews.body: Let's get straight the points. Advantages: - PBT keycaps. I don't know how to describe it but it feels great. Oh, the colors are nice too. - Support both Windows and Mac - The sound is nice - The Space button feels nice, very stable - Have PrintScreen (PRTSC) button (because I use this button a lot so this is a pro for me) - Have Numpad keys. As an accountant, this numpad never fails me lol. Disadvantages: - Requires a great force to press, but you can enhance this by replacing to other keycap layouts. I'm a typist, therefore I really care about this. - The brightness is okay, but I expect to have brighter LEDs. Oh well, that's all. This is a decent product. I recommend people buying this product. Please make sure that you choose the right product for your use. Thanks for reading.

title: RK ROYAL KLUDGE S98 Wireless Mechanical Keyboard w/Smart Display & Knob

reviews.title: Super creamy keys!!
reviews.body: My first mechanical keyboard and sounds exactly how I imagined! It’s nice solid , creamy click noise! So satisfying!!! I loved the key color combo! The RGB lights are customizable, down to each key! Super cool. I am overall impressed with my purchase, as I was hesitant to buy something I wouldn’t like the sound of. I was also hesitant because there are so many options but I am glad I picked this! Good value for your money. The keyboard is heavy and feel super sturdy, doesn’t feel cheap. The keys were very responsive to touch and the Bluetooth was easy to setup with my windows laptop. The only thing I don’t like is the look of the keys, they do have a sheen/texture to them I don’t like but honestly, overall, I don’t mind it at all! Great buy!

reviews.title: Excellent Keyboard With Minor Software Issues
reviews.body: This is my first mechanical keyboard, and I finally understand what all the hype is about. The sound is incredibly satisfying. It has that nice mechanical sound without being overly loud or obnoxious, but it also isn't so quiet that you lose the satisfying typing experience. The typing feel is probably my favorite part—the keys feel incredibly smooth and satisfying, and so far everything has felt flawless. The build quality is also really impressive for the price. It has some nice weight to it and doesn't feel cheap or flimsy at all. The smart display is a fun addition. Is it necessary? Absolutely not. 😂 But it's definitely nice to have. You can use it for things like Bluetooth connection and volume settings, and you can also customize it with your own photo or GIF. The one area that could definitely be improved is the software. It's not particularly user-friendly, and finding the correct software to customize the keyboard took me longer than it should have. Once I actually found it, though, it wasn't too difficult to figure out with a little patience. The software itself also feels a little chunky and dated. That said, this has zero effect on the actual performance of the keyboard, so it's a very minor complaint. I've had absolutely no issues with wireless connectivity. I've used both Bluetooth and the included cable and haven't experienced any disconnections, lag, or other problems. One thing to note is that you'll need to use the included cable when connecting the keyboard to the software for customization. The battery life has also been surprisingly good so far. I haven't actually had to charge it yet, so I can't speak to the full battery life, but I work from home about 9 hours a day and also casually game in the evenings. After two days of that, the battery has only dropped about 5%. Overall, I have very little negative to say about this keyboard. The software could definitely use some improvement, and there could be better information provided about where to find and how to use it. But that's a very small complaint compared to everything else this keyboard does well. For my first mechanical keyboard, I'm extremely happy with it. Everything about it has exceeded my expectations. 5/5 and definitely recommend!

reviews.title: Great design. Great functionality. 100% Recommend if it fits your general specifications.
reviews.body: tl;dr: I am EXTREMELY happy with this keyboard. Build? Beautiful. Sound? Amazing. Functionality? PERFECT. Price? FANTASTIC. If this keyboard fits your specifications for your desk and you happen to work with two different computers at the same time, get it ASAP. More details: Previously I had a significantly smaller RK 68 which was great for me. It was perfect for what I wanted, a small profile and clacky keyboard. Unfortunately, I spilled soda all over it and it died so I had to get a new one. Fortunately, it was this keyboard. In my search for a new keyboard I had a couple things I was looking for: - A green color way to match my set up - A nice clack to it. - A numpad attached. Clearly it's not something very specific. But during my search I came across other features that I had no idea I wanted. But this one hit pretty much what I was looking for so I decided to give it a try and boy did it blow my expectations out of the water. == Design == Pros: This keyboard looks sleek. Before, to build something like this I had considered paying my friend to build it from scratch but the colorway and the key placements are just so clean. With multifunctional keycaps, they've added the second function on the side of the keycap so you can easily see the primary and the secondary without it feeling too cluttered. The back lighting options really make it fun to customize. They give you default options you can run with and each of those options you can tweak to your liking in terms of color. The digital display seems more like a part of the design the way it links to the volume knob, rather than an after thought like some other keyboards. This provides another option for you to make the keyboard your own by letting you upload a gif to just loop by default. Cons: No complaints really, except the digital display occasionally pops off slightly, requiring you to press it back in but it hasn't become too much of an issue for me yet. Also, uploading the gif to the keyboard takes a good amount of time (something like 5 minutes) , so if they could fix that speed that would be amazing. Oh one more complaint is that it's too tall. I had to get a wrist mount just to feel comfortable typing on it. == Functionality == Pros: MAN, this keyboard is PACKED with features I never thought I would need. Aside from the aforementioned backlight customization, something that has made my life so much better is hidden behind the digital display. It's base functionality of controlling the volume of your computer works like a charm but it's when you get into the submenus that you can really see where it shines. You see, I am someone who bounces between a macbook pro for work and a windows PC for play and so I'm constantly bouncing between the two. Before, I had a mac specific keyboard and a windows specific keyboard, both occupying space on my desk. This keyboard has eliminated that need in a sleek and elegant way by allowing me to hardwire into my desktop and bluetooth to my macbook. From there, I can easily use the digital display + volume knob to switch my connection between the two. Heck, if I needed to add another couple I could. It seems like I can have up to 5 different devices connected (3 bluetooth, 1 wired, 1 wireless dongle). So if for some reason I had another device, I could easily switch between the two. You might ask yourself, but what about the difference in layout between macs and windows machines? Oh my friend, you see... THEY THOUGHT OF EVERYTHING. Through the same digital display, you can swap the layouts between the two types. I was totally fine with that until I read the manual a bit more and found you could even use a hotkey JUST for that. Remember the secondary functions of the various keys? If you look on the side of the 'A' and 'S' keys, you can see that they read 'WIN' and 'MAC' respectively. So to switch formats, all you have to do is hit 'Fn' + 'A' or 'S' to switch between the two. This really pushed my like for this keyboard to love. Cons: The only thing I can really think of is a nitpick and is possibly even already a function, I'd just have to read through the manual a bit more. It would be nice to be able to use a shortcut to bounce between the different keyboard connections like you can switch formats. == Sound and Feel == Pros: I am having a BLAST typing this review. Every keypress feels so satisfying as the switches engage and disengage making you really feel connected to the keyboard. The sound is more thocky than clacky which is extremely pleasing to my ears, especially after coming from a clackier keyboard. Cons: While this keyboard is probably 50 percent quieter than my last keyboard, it's still definitely louder than a membrane keyboard, so if you're looking for silent, this isn't what you want. But if you're looking at mechanical keyboards, then this most likely isn't you. == Price == I feel like this keyboard is well worth the 89 dollar price tag for what you get. I feel like even a couple years ago, you'd have to pay 300 bucks to someone to custom make something like this with the design options. Sure, it's not as bespoke as the true customs, but I feel like it holds up just as well. Overall, I'd give this keyboard a 'have no fear, buy away' if your needs are similar to what I've mentioned above!

reviews.title: I love this keyboard
reviews.body: I recently got into keyboard building and I chose this keyboard for my first build. I love that it’s basically full size but has a compact feel. I choose the sky blue option that came with the pale green tactile switches. I enjoy the feel of a tactile switch, but the switches that came stock were a little too high pitch for me. I swapped out the switches for some hand lubed Leobog Greywood v3s (sound test in video). The keyboard has a surprising amount of weight to it, and the knob and screen are very useful. Pros: South facing RGB Sounds amazing (imo) after I swapped the switches and put new keycaps on The LED screen and the knob are extremely handy and a really cool feature Battery works REALLY well - when the RGB is off Tri-mode feature - I personally have some issues with the Bluetooth with one specific computer of mine (they won’t connect unless the keyboard is on and in the right mode before I turn my computer on) but I don’t have this issue with any of my other devices and believe it’s likely due to an old Bluetooth adapter. Cons: Battery - I did a full test of this and the battery with RGB on is honestly terrible in my opinion. I started my workday with a fully charged battery, and it had drained to 28 percent after 10 hours Software - Can’t seem to be able to change the clock from 24hr format to 12hr format Software for the keyboard itself is definitely lacking, and there were little resources I could find on how to use it All that being said I don’t regret buying this keyboard at all. It’s a major upgrade from what I had before, and I’m extremely proud of my first build.

reviews.title: All the mechanical keyboard I need
reviews.body: First mechanical keyboard I’ve owned, can’t imagine I’d need anything different. Bought two of these, one for my workspace and one for my wife. We both needed accurate and responsive keys for frequent data and password entry, the lights and display are just bonus points. I change out my display for random gifs and RGB weekly using the web portal, easy enough once you get the hang of it, takes 5-10 minutes to upload a gif. Can confirm battery lasts about a week with moderate workday use. Keys are on the quieter end of clacky, not as obnoxious as some mechanical keyboards I’ve used in the past. Key travel registers about 75% from fully depressed which took me a tiny bit of time to adapt to. More often now, I’ll think I missed a letter because I didn’t press quite hard enough, but look back to find it registered after all. Comes with a few replacement switches, key puller, and usb-c cable which is nice. I’m sure there is better quality for more money out there but I’m not the demographic for it, this is all the keyboard I think I’ll ever need.

reviews.title: A must have for anyone looking for an amazing sounding keyboard!
reviews.body: When I first got a gaming PC, I figured I didn't really need a super expensive keyboard and that a cheap one that sounded "clicky" and had lights was fine enough. I also didn't want to bother with charging a wireless keyboard. However, I started to hear from YouTube videos and TikToks about "creamy" and "thocky" keyboards. I immediately started to do research, because I was obsessed with the sound. This is one of those rare purchases that I cannot stop thinking about how happy it makes me. I have absolutely no qualms with it. Here's what I love: The sound is excellent. Videos that I watched were a good indicator, but as other reviews have said, they really do not do the keyboard justice for how it actually sounds. The letters themselves are very creamy, while the function buttons (spacebar, shift, enter, backspace, etc.) have a much deeper "thocky" sound to them. If you're on the fence, at least try it and return if it's not for you. The functionality is incredible. There are a ton of lighting options that you can play with. You can mess around with them in the software on your PC. But because this keyboard has a small LCD screen, you can also change them directly on the keyboard itself. I have mine set to light up the entire keyboard cyan from whichever key I press, expanding out. Speaking of the LCD screen, you're able to upload GIFS or images to the screen, which is a really cool feature. As far as connectivity, you have every imaginable option available to you. I have my gaming rig connected via the 2.4USB wireless adapter. You can also connect up to three devices via bluetooth. And of course you can opt to hardware in. I love the the keyboard has both a USB-A and USB-C port. I am a huge advocate for technology having USB-C as an option, as it is much more convenient, provide faster transfer times, and faster charging times. Speaking of charging, the battery life on this keyboard is excellent. I seem to get about a week's worth of charge with extreme use daily. I know that the keyboard is hot swappable, meaning you can swap out the switches, which ultimately determine the sound of the keyboard, but personally, I haven't messed with that, as I love the way it sounds now. Overall, this is an excellent keyboard. If you're in the market for a wireless keyboard that sounds great, this is the best option out there! I typically don't like spending a ton of money on stuff unless I am absolutely sure of its value, and let me put your mind at ease that this keyboard is worth so much more than what the price tag shows.

reviews.title: To many firmware glitches - basically unusable for any serious work
reviews.body: Today, I initially wrote a negative review of this keyboard due to issues with missed or repeated keystrokes, or keys continuing to fire until another key was pressed. However, after extensive investigation (because I really wanted to keep this keyboard for its mechanical build), I finally discovered that the issues were caused by an obscure, lingering USB driver from a device no longer connected to my PC. That driver was behind all the trouble. I hope this revised review is published before the original one, which is no longer valid. After 15+ years of using Cherry MX Blue switches on a single keyboard that eventually got damaged, I was in search of a replacement. This keyboard seemed like a good option - more compact than my full-size board and featuring “tactile” pale green switches. I hoped they would resemble MX Blues in feel, just without the audible click. Unfortunately, these switches aren’t really that much (or at all) tactile. I don’t understand the claim. There is a point somewhere along the key travel where pressure slightly decreases, but you’d need to press very slowly and have an extremely sensitive touch to notice it. In actual typing, it feels - at least to me - indistinguishable from a regular linear switch. That said, I’ve gotten used to them and didn’t have much trouble adapting after so many years with MX Blues. And the 'thocky' sound still sounds nice. The build quality is solid. The board is sturdy, heavy, and a definite improvement over my old keyboard. I’m not particularly interested in the display or LED lighting. I don’t see the point - especially since the keycaps aren’t translucent, so the lights don’t help in the dark. Omitting those toddler-toy-like features and lowering the price - or populating that space with more keys - would be more useful, in my opinion. I used the included keycap puller to swap the positions of the 'Home' and 'Del' keys, then made the change in the RK software. It took just a few seconds. These settings are retained even if you unplug the keyboard or uninstall the RK software entirely from your PC. All things considered, in terms of mechanical construction, this is a very good keyboard. I do wish the switches were more tactile, but that’s just a matter of personal preference. These switches are still decent, and I’ll probably swap them out in the future for some Kailh clicky switches.

reviews.title: Good keyboard but little support for Mac
reviews.body: The keyboard part is awesome and the keys feel good with a satisfying clack that isn't sharp or too loud. I use this on a Mac and it does have a Mac mode. However, I find it hard to use with the wireless dongle (doesn't work on my Mac) and just have to use it wired. Fortunately, it does have a supplemental USB-A port for my wireless mouse transmitter. The screen is OK and the volume knob is useful. I think this is a Windows keyboard and Mac compatibility was added afterwards as the F keys don't work even in Mac mode to adjust volume or activate programs like a native Mac keyboard. Still, the keyboard is worth keeping even if the program needed to control the LED lights and other functions is Windows only.

reviews.title: Tastiera ottima, peccato mi sia arrivata palesemente usata
reviews.body: Premessa. La tastiera mi è arrivata nuova ma palesemente usata. La confezione era sigillata da un secondo adesivo applicato sul precedente, la tastiera aveva delle ditate, il libretto come in foto, il cavo di alimentazione addirittura pizzicato, tutti i sacchettini rovinati. Insomma, se acquisto un prodotto nuovo quello dev'essere nuovo, altrimenti avrei preso un usato garantito spendendo meno. Posso capire un eventuale reso nei tempi di recesso ma almeno il cavetto andava sostituito. Andando alla tastiera Top di gamma della Royal Kludge. Non vengono dichiarati la tipologia di switch montati, arrivata con i tactile e sono comunque ottimi, non mi era capitato di provarli. Molto piacevoli e che fanno un minimo di resistenza per poi abbassarsi in modo deciso. Non mi dispiacciono affatto. La superfice dei tasti si presenta leggermente ridotta nella parte piana, il che aiuta a non premere erroneamente tasti indesiderati. Il suono è abbastanza piacevole, un po' asciutto ma non fastidioso probabilmente influenzato dalla struttura rigida della tastiera. La scrittura è agevolata dall'ampiezza ridotta della superfice dei tasti seppur non abbiano l'inclinatura ergonomica che offrono altre tastiere di pari fascia, ma il tono su tono su alcuni tasti li rende non di immediata individuazione. Manca la retroilluminazione. Assenza che trovo inspiegabile in tastiere che passano i 100€ di costo ma vedo che, escludendo i classici marchi da gaming, si trova poco. La tastiera ha due livelli di altezza con piedini gommati, ma è abbastanza alta. Personalmente la uso senza rialzo. Full RGB, totalmente modulabile tramite software ma con la possibilità gestire il tutto tramite lo schermo integrato. Buona luminosità e colori intensi. Possibilità di connessione via cavo, incluso nella confezione, via Bluetooth e con chiavetta. Quest'ultima con una sede magnetica laterale. Presenta anche due tasti fisici. Su un angolo troviamo la selezione di collegamento tra via cavo o chiavetta e poco più in là il tasto di accensione e spegnimento. Il comando del piccolo monitor è comodo e si legge bene, così come i led per il Blck Num e il Caps Lock presenti anche come led vicino al tasto Esc. Ben individuabili al tocco anche i segni su F, J e 5. Il piccolo monitor ha una funzione di menù per diverse impostazioni navigabili tramite una pratica rotelle. Livello batteria, data, tipologia di connessione, caps lock e block num, se è in modalità Win o IOS. Insomma, mostra ciò che serve ed è ben leggibile. È possibile anche caricare delle GIF limitate a 60 immagini. Un po pochine e va a togliere le altre info. Opzione carina ma resto dell'idea che, avendo a disposizione un piccolo monitor aggiuntivo, si dovrebbe poter sfruttare meglio. Per esempio con le temperature di esercizio dei componenti, la percentuale di utilizzo, ecc.. Il software è completo. Offre di salvare 3 mappature differenti dei comandi e gestire in modo totale l'illuminazione. Non molto intuitivo, devo ammetterlo. C'è un menù di cui non ho chiaro l'utilizzo e non viene fornita alcuna informazione né nel manuale cartaceo ne per quello disponibile sul sito (Entrambi in inglese). Ottima tastiera, nel complesso quella con cui mi sto trovando meglio delle diverse che provate (e ne ho provate diverse nella fascia 50/150€). Peccato davvero per la mancanza della retroilluminazione oltre che, vedendo che è presente su altri prodotti, la mancanza di poterci abbinare il poggia polsi magnetico.

reviews.title: Great mechanical keyboard and seller delivery support
reviews.body: The keyboard works flawlessly and has a really great mechanical feel and sound. The keyboard delivery was very prompt and thank you to the team for providing a hassle free online purchasing equipment

reviews.title: Comfortable and Stylish
reviews.body: This is a great and reasonably priced keyboard. The key sound/feel is super pleasing, and the quick switch between devices/volume/effects with the dial and screen is awesome.

reviews.title: Good keyboard, with nice click sounds and fun to type!
reviews.body: Good keyboard, with nice click sounds and fun to type! The build is sturdy and the keyboard is heavy. I am expecting it to last long. I liked the small screen for configuration. There is a time display on the keyboard, which I don't find useful. Once charge last about two weeks with bluetooth connectivity.

reviews.title: The sound and typing experience is amazing.
reviews.body: This is my 2nd Royal Kludge keyboard and I am very impressed. I've had mechanical keyboards from Logitech, Keychron, Corsair, Drevo and Redragon and I like my RK ones more. This one in particular is just super satisfying to type on. I love the creamy sound from the keys, it's unlike anything else I've owned so far. The green and clay-red color scheme also looks awesome. Keycaps are soft touch but not shine-through which is a bit of a disappointment but not a deal breaker. The little screen and knob is easy to use and actually useful. It's nice to change settings in a menu vs using function keys, and being able to check the time when enjoying full screen entertainment is also handy to me. My audio setup is also able to use the knob as a volume control which is an added bonus. All three connectivity modes work well for me - Bluetooth is reliable, 2.4Ghz is fast and reliable, and wired mode is also fast and reliable. Range on BT/2.4Ghz is average, but since this isnt really an HTPC keyboard I don't think it matters much. My only complaint is the battery life. RK claims they have a gigantic battery in this keyboard but I only get 2-3 days of use between charges, and it takes a loooooong time to charge so it ends up being plugged in a little more than I'd like. If I keep the RGB lighting on the 2nd lowest setting, I can get another day or two of usage but I wish I didn't have to charge this keyboard once a week. I really like this keyboard overall and I'd definitely recommend it! It's a good keyboard for full price but RK has sales all the time so I'd wait for a 20-25% discount, where it becomes a killer deal in my opinion. Edit: 3 months in and still very fun to type on and 100% reliable. I just keep the backlighting off most of the time now to conserve battery and it lasts a while without the backlight on 2.4Ghz link (2-3 weeks light use). Only thing I don't like after a few months of use is having to press fn + PgDn for the End key.

title: SteelSeries USB Apex 5 Hybrid Mechanical Gaming Keyboard – Per-Key RGB Illumination – Aircraft Grade Aluminum Alloy Frame – OLED Smart Display (Hybrid Blue Switch)

reviews.title: Great Keyboard and Great Features!
reviews.body: This keyboard is probably the best one I've ever had. It is built so well. It is made mostly of some sort of aluminum. It does not bend at all and it just feels very nice. I have had a keyboard that was so cheap that it bent even when I was typing normally (I don't type very hard), so this was a nice change. The metal volume dial is very high quality, and yet again, just feels well-built. There is also a little button that controls 4 things. It will pause and play your music, skip to the next song, go to the previous song, and open up menus in the OLED display. The OLED screen is very nice. It could be a little brighter, and the larger pixels make it harder to display certain things. But, what makes up for that is that with the program you can install, you can download apps that will change what the screen says. My 2 favorites are Discord and System Monitor. They RGB lighting is really nice. Each light can be its own color and with the program, you can make your own lighting configurations. The keys sound very nice. They are clicky, but too clicky. They are also easy to press, but not so easy that I could see myself accidentally pressing one. It also comes with a wrist rest. It magnetically attaches and feels very smooth and high quality. Overall this keyboard just feels very premium and super high quality. I would recommend it to someone who wants a good keyboard with some very nice features from a good brand and does not mind spending the premium cost.

reviews.title: Outstanding, with a possible caveat
reviews.body: Five months into owning this keyboard and it's easily my favorite keyboard I've ever had. Reasonably heavy so it easily stays in place even banging out page after page of typing documents, but doesn't feel like a slab of lead. The entire assembly is well put together; the keyboard has a nice, satin texture across the body and the keys, which feels great under the fingers, though it does show some oils more easily so I recommend regular cleaning/wipedowns. This keyboard uses an odd hybrid system between mechanical/membrane, some proprietary/trade secret Steelseries BS, though honestly, if this wasn't pointed out to me after the fact I probably wouldn't have caught on. This uses cherry stems and switches, and the keys are naturally a cherry profile, so finding aftermarket replacements/decorative keycaps is easy as well. The keys feel responsive and clicky, delightfully so, when gaming or typing for general purpose. But there's a catch; it's a hybrid, so not truly mechanical. It does feel very good, but I have concerns that the membrane will wear down in time as opposed to a true blue mechanical keyboard, which will stay responsive and snappy for a lesser eternity where membranes begin to show wear after a year of heavy use. Time will tell. The lighting is phenomenal - the LEDs are bright, responsive, and have great color depth and range compared to a lot of RGB hardware out there. You can use Steelseries' own software to customize and program this keyboard outside of the 5 existing presets saved onto the board's memory, but you can also use other third-party RGB control software like SignalRGB. All in, it's a quality keyboard for a great price; one wire connects everything, you have a stop/start button, a wheel for volume, and a built in profile-swap button, which is entirely unnecessary but quite nice.

reviews.title: SteelSeries Apex 5 – Almost a 5-Star Keyboard, but Not Quite (4.76 on My Scale)
reviews.body: The SteelSeries Apex 5 left a strong impression. It’s a well-built keyboard with some excellent features and clever design choices. The cable is thick, long, and even has a nice touch — the SteelSeries logo on the USB plug. The RGB effects are top-notch, with smooth transitions both on keypress and when idle. I was genuinely excited about all of this... until I noticed what was missing. And for me, that’s a big deal. Let’s break it down.😁 ### What Makes It (Almost) 5 Stars – The Good:😃 - Excellent Media Controls: The volume wheel is fantastic: easy to reach, smooth to use, and includes a click-to-mute function. The menu button also works similarly to the playback controls found on many headsets with built-in microphones or hands-free kits. Super convenient. - Onboard Controls – No Software Needed: You can manage brightness, RGB colors, effects, profiles, and more — all from the keyboard itself. No software required. Only macros can’t be directly viewed or edited in menu, which is a small detail worth noting. - Smart OLED Display: It shows the status of Num Lock, Caps Lock, Scroll Lock, and whether the Windows key is disabled. Very handy (though there’s a small catch — more on that below). - Customization & Visual Feedback: Besides full per-key RGB customization and reactive effects, pressing the “Fn” key (the SteelSeries logo key) lights up related function keys in red for quick reference. It’s super helpful… but again, not perfect (you can’t change the color — more on that too). - Profile Memory Built-In: You can save up to 5 profiles directly on the keyboard and toggle them on/off without cycling through all of them. I personally use just two: one for gaming and one for productivity. ### The Not-So-Good – My Gripes😒: - No Dedicated Context Menu Key: This is my biggest issue. A full-size keyboard should include the dedicated menu key (the "right-click menu" key). SteelSeries replaced it with their custom “Fn” key, which really disrupted my usual workflow. I ended up switching to Shift + F10 to keep things consistent across devices. - Fn Key Can’t Be Reassigned: The SteelSeries logo key, which replaces the context menu key, is fixed — it can’t be remapped. Personally, I’d have preferred having the Windows key only on the left, and using the right one for Fn, keeping the menu key in its usual place. - OLED Button Always Lit: The brightness of the button next to the OLED screen cannot be dimmed or turned off. If you’re working in a dark room or watching movies, this little light will keep shining at you — kind of annoying. - OLED Icons Overlap Custom Logos: If you upload a custom image to the OLED screen, the status icons for Num Lock, Caps, etc. may overlap your logo. Not a dealbreaker, but it limits how creative you can get with personalization. - No Visual Feedback When Windows Key Is Locked: Unlike other lock states (like Caps Lock), there’s no lighting change or visual indicator on the keyboard itself when the Windows key is disabled — just a small icon on the OLED. Feels inconsistent. - Function Key Highlight Color Can’t Be Changed: When pressing “Fn,” the related keys light up red — but that red is not customizable. If your RGB theme is red, this effect becomes basically invisible. - Slight Input Delay: There’s a small delay in key activation. I don’t notice it while typing or working, but for competitive gaming, it might matter. Rtings.com confirmed this in their testing too. - Non-Replaceable Hybrid Switches This is the most serious issue. The switches aren’t standard and can’t be replaced by the user. If a key fails, you’re stuck with relying on warranty, support… or scavenging another board. Not great. ### Neutral Points – Might Be Good or Bad Depending on You🤷🏻‍♂️: - Actuation Distance: I switched from a keyboard with ultra-light 0.8 mm actuation, and I kept typing extra characters. The Apex 5 feels much more precise and helped reduce typos — a big plus for me. - Key Feel & Keycaps: The keycaps aren’t made from premium material, but they feel decent. Coming from linear switches, the tactile feel took a bit of getting used to — but I adjusted quickly. - Magnetic Wrist Rest: I don’t use it much, but the magnets are strong and hold it firmly in place. - Macro Labeling (M1, M2, etc.): Some keys are labeled as macro keys (M1, M2...), which can be confusing at first — but you’ll get used to it. - Customization Without Software: You can change basic RGB effects and profiles directly from the keyboard. The software adds more depth, but it’s nice that you’re not forced to use it. - USB Plug with Logo: A small but smart touch: the SteelSeries logo on the USB plug helps you spot which device you’re plugging in. - No Physical Lock LEDs: The lock indicators (Num Lock, Caps, Scroll) have been moved to the OLED screen, and you can set those keys to change color when active. Some might miss the old-school LED lights, but I’m fine with it. ### Final Verdict 💸😇 The SteelSeries Apex 5 is a well-built, visually polished keyboard with great RGB, useful media controls, and a solid set of features for gamers and professionals alike. Still, a few oversights — especially the missing context menu key and the non-replaceable switches — keep it from being a perfect 5-star device in my eyes. If those flaws don’t bother you, then this keyboard is an easy recommendation. Just know what you're getting — and what you're not

reviews.title: Great entry mechanical keyboard with solid feel and comfort
reviews.body: I bought this for my 14-year-old, and it’s been a great keyboard for both gaming and schoolwork. The hybrid switches feel clicky and responsive without being overly loud, and the RGB is bright and customizable enough for their setup. The included wrist rest adds real comfort and doesn’t slide around. No issues with software or macros so far. It’s a well-rounded keyboard that feels more premium than its price suggests.

reviews.title: Awesome!
reviews.body: Excellent individual RGB keys. Cool but small LCD screen (But it displays my CPU temp, so I'm happy). Volume control is super handy, and it's compatible with SignalRGB. Not to mention this keyboards clicks sound amazing! If you're into the old school keyboard sound.

reviews.title: Nice keyboard - Amazon Refurbished just sucks
reviews.body: I have only had this keyboard for a few days at the time of this review, but from what I can tell it is a solidly built keyboard with a nice feel and decently responsive keys. I did have to knock off a star though as the keyboard I received was in poor condition with two of the keys having keypress detection issues. This however was NOT the fault of SteelSeries as I bought this one from Amazon Refurbished. Do NOT buy this keyboard from Amazon Refurbished. They do only the bare minimum to make the keyboard presentable, and do not open it to check the internals before shipping it. Or else they would have seen the gunk inside that was causing the key press detection issue. Thankfully, user maintenance was easy. Simple matter of taking off the key caps, taking out the cover screws, and the mainboard screws. Then I was able to clean it with a little alcohol and reassemble it. Works like it was new. Just didn't expect that I would have to be the one doing the refurbishing on day one. But that's why I gave it 4 stars, pretty easy to perform user maintenance on it to ensure that it continues to function. Which boggles me why Amazon didn't do that.

reviews.title: Great keybaord!
reviews.body: Got this to replace a $250 Razor keyboard that went out after four years with largely only work-related use. I have keyboards from the '90s that still work. Razor customer service didn't even respond to me. That being said, I'm happy with this one. Less than half the price and works just as well. So much, I bough one for my son as well!

reviews.title: Amazing keyboard!
reviews.body: Amazing! It has many cool features and sounds amazing. It’s full sized too so you don’t miss out on any extra keys.

reviews.title: Mi primer teclado mecánico. Totalmente satisfecho
reviews.body: Excelentes materiales de construcción, amplias opciones para configurar prácticamente cualquier cosa del teclado y gran comodidad. Pasé de un teclado de membrana "gamer" Logitech G213 a este SteelSeries Apex 5 y la diferencia puede notarse. Desde los efectos RGB ampliamente configurables a través del software SteelSeries GG hasta el tacto en las teclas y el reposamuñecas (que está hecho de un material de plástico suave al tacto), todo es súper cómodo y de gran calidad. Algo que me gusta bastante de este teclado es su pequeña pantalla OLED en la esquina superior derecha, que puede configurarse con algún dibujo, algún GIF o con alguna de las integraciones que tiene con algunos juegos o programas. Yo particularmente la uso para monitorear mi sistema y ver la temperatura a la que se encuentra mi CPU y GPU de manera rápida y sencilla sin tener que ejecutar MSI Afterburner o RivaTuner SS. Sin embargo, tal y como vi en la propia página del producto y en algunas reseñas en YouTube, se podía visualizar la canción que estuvieras escuchando en el momento, pero por lo que pude investigar esto solo es posible si usas TIDAL y bueno, yo utilizo Spotify, por lo que esto no me agradó tanto. El sonido del teclado es notable y puede llegar a ser molesto si no estás acostumbrado o si vives con alguien más y sueles usarlo en las noches a no mucha distancia del resto de personas. El video que adjunto es muy fiel (considero yo) al sonido que obtienes una vez el teclado está en tus manos. Algo que me gustaría mencionar es que, a pesar de que el teclado venía bien empaquetado junto con otros productos, la caja del teclado en sí venía con algo de cinta extra en varios lados, lo que me hizo dudar un poco en si el producto era nuevo o usado, pero al abrirlo me di cuenta de que era nuevo o estaba en condiciones prácticamente perfectas, por lo que me quedé más tranquilo, pero ese detalle de cinta extra en la caja no me agradó demasiado.

reviews.title: Everything is good about this
reviews.body: The keyboard is amazing. It has per key illumination which the software is very cool with. It gets recognised by signal rgb software so it syncs everything together. The feel is good it has mechanical clicks with membrane so doesn't feel like your bottoming out the keys.

reviews.title: Very Satisfied
reviews.body: I wanted a kind of middle road price RGB keyboard and I am in love with this one. The keys feel very satisfying and loud and clicky. The RGB support is great, I use signalRGB so that was a major selling point that it worked for that. I do wish it had better side controls for audio and even though you can pause spotify or whatever with the top right button it only pauses your last application which can be anything so that can be a bit annoying. The scroll wheel does work well for volume control though. Overall I do like it a lot, good colour and feel. Recommend for those who want something nice but dont want to drop 200

reviews.title: Awesome.
reviews.body: Never knew what I was missing out on before I got this. So. Worth. It.

title: AULA WIN68 HE Mechanical Gaming Keyboard 60%, Hall Effect Magnetic Switch, Fast Trigger Mode Adjustable Actuation, 8000Hz Polling Rate, RGB Backlit, Wired Black Keyboard for Laptop/PC Gamer

reviews.title: Budget HE keyboard that gives you all you need...
reviews.body: AULA WIN68 HE is my first ever HE keyboard, after years of being in the world of mechanical keyboards and exclusively favoring the brown switch (tactile) I always watched many videos and people praising HE keyboards and the edge they give to you in gaming primarily. We all know of the famed Wooting 60 HE which started this trend in gaming world both the price and being only 60% give's it only a small and competitive market for a few individuals that can afford it or need it for professional e-Sports. As primarily a single-player gamer I was blow away with how much HE switches changes your experience of playing and gives you for the first time ever something that gamepads had over keyboards, and that is you don't need to push the key all the way for it work, both only a slight push fulfils the given command that you want (MMOs and racing games benefit from this the most). The web software is one of the best features of this keyboard and it allows you to customize every single key however you want it, every key supports rapid trigger as well as customizing the dead zone as well as primarily the sensitivity of the keys. The standard version that I have allows you to customize the sensitivity from 0.8mm to larger if you prefer (default being 1.70mm, while mechanical boards clock at 2.1mm). Keyboard is hot swappable and you can change your magnetic switches really easily. Brightness and RGB is also good with no complaints in that department (you can customize it in the web software). The build quality is also good and think that board was upgraded to PBT switches since when typing on them the feel sandy and rough, sound quality is quite since magnetic switches are linear switches (both better in every way), and the keyboard is wired only which I prefer since I am using it on my personal PC and have no need to use it elsewhere. HE keyboards are definitely the future and every professional or enthusiast e-Sport gamer simply must have this keyboard because it gives them and edge in every way that mechanical keyboard simply cannot give at the moment! I recommended this board for anybody who is on the fence over coming to the HE world.

reviews.title: best gaming keyboard
reviews.body: feels nice and colors are great super durable and size is amazing not too heavy and typing feels so smooth and connects perfectly like any other keyboard love the fact that you can change how little you have to press in order for it to register. 10/10

reviews.title: Best for gamers or HE keyb enthusiasts
reviews.body: Very silky smooth, sounds absolutely amazing and feels even better, the software drivers were kinda hard to find n looked like a scam but were not and work perfectly, though you don't need the software for much unless you care about the actuation points and all that special stuff, which you probably do since you're getting a HE keyb, came with everything in box everything works, very high quality feel its heavier (In a good way) than my old keyb I bought for around 60 usd. Got just the standard black keyb but the rgbs all show through the keycaps really good and none of them are buggy or broken. All in all its very worth it if you're a gamer or just care about hall effect keybs in general. It's a 60% so you obv don't have all the keys of a 100% but it's definitely good for saving space. But that's why I mainly recommend to gamers or people who are looking for specific features.

reviews.title: Great Quality
reviews.body: Perfect for Gamers! My son has a 200.00 keyboard and actually prefers this one. Great price and quick clicks.

reviews.title: Solid Build, Great Sound, and Impressive Lighting Options
reviews.body: I’ve been using the AULA WIN68 HE keyboard for a while now, and it’s been a great experience overall. The compact size is small enough to save desk space but not so small that it feels restrictive—everything is still right where you need it. The function key functionality is seamless, making it easy to access all the extra commands without breaking your flow. The typing sound is crisp and satisfying without being too loud, and the build quality is excellent—solid and heavy enough that it won’t slide around, even if you accidentally bump it. The RGB lighting is another standout, offering a wide range of patterns and configurations to match any setup. While the software initially seemed a bit sketchy, after doing some research and testing I was able to find a great actuation point that feels perfect for my typing style. One thing I’m still unsure about is the “different switches” option in the software—it’s visible, but I’m not entirely certain what it changes, if anything. Considering the overall quality, sound, build, lighting, and features, this keyboard delivers an impressive experience for such a budget-friendly price. Overall, I highly recommend this keyboard to anybody looking for a budget-friendly gaming keyboard! I've attached a picture with my Logitech G305 mouse for a scale reference.

reviews.title: Deeper Insights Than Apple Watch – WHOOP 5.0 Delivers Serious Data with Minimal Hassle
reviews.body: After a ton of research into wearables that go beyond basic step counting and heart rate, I chose the WHOOP 5.0 (with the 12-month membership) specifically because I wanted way more detailed, actionable data than what my Apple Watch provides. And it's delivered big time. The band itself is incredibly lightweight and comfortable—I barely notice it's on my wrist all day and night. I only take it off for showers, which is a huge win for continuous tracking. The real game-changer is the charger: it snaps right on top while you're still wearing it, so there's zero downtime or lost data. That's a thoughtful design that makes staying consistent effortless. The metrics are fantastic—sleep stages, recovery scores, strain, HRV, respiratory rate, and all the deep physiological insights feel accurate and meaningful. What surprised me most was uploading my recent physical lab results directly into the app; WHOOP factored those biomarkers right into my overall data and trends, giving even more context to how my habits affect my health long-term. The GenAI-powered WHOOP Coach is another standout—you can chat with it to ask specific questions about your results, get personalized explanations, or dive deeper into why your recovery dipped or how to optimize training. It's like having a smart coach in your pocket. The app is clean, intuitive, and clearly well-thought-out—everything from daily summaries to long-term trends is easy to navigate and feels intentional, not overwhelming. My one complaint is the clasp. It might just be my unit, but it feels a bit finicky and harder to close securely than it should—sometimes takes a couple tries to get it to click properly. Not a dealbreaker, especially since the rest of the experience is so seamless, but it's worth noting for anyone picky about quick on/off. If you're serious about health optimization, recovery, and getting beyond surface-level tracking, the WHOOP 5.0 is worth it. The subscription unlocks all this depth, and after a few weeks, I can't imagine going back to less insightful devices. Highly recommend for data-driven folks!

reviews.title: MAJOR DESIGN FLAW DO NOT BUY
reviews.body: DO NOT BUY THIS!!! Purchased and came very quickly like next day but the UBar clasp design is so poor it broke when I tried to switch wrists after about a day wearing the decice, when I put it back on the UBar that secured the device was bent so that it wouldn't secure properly to my wrist. The entire wearable is held onto your wrist with a UBar attachment that is secured on either side by 2 millimeter (no exaggerating) size holes. These will inevitably fail and after wearing for a total of about 29 hours and simply attempting to switch once it's a major design flaw. It was difficult to figure out how to secure to the wrist and charge from the beginning and while relatively comfortable to wear, wasn't giving the readings I would want without an upgrade. The customer support is essentially an AI that responds via email and then eventually redirects you back to Amazon. Also this is membership based that auto renews annually and is several hundred dollars. I was willing to give a try and see if it was worth the renewal since the 1st year was included with the device and I felt like I could simply change to another wearable if I didn't feel it was worth it. I finally got a real person to respond who redirected me back to Amazon for refund because they couldn't provide any alternative to the band flaw. Super disappointing I was excited to try this and bought for myself for my birthday and will have to do more research on what actually works for wearables because this is NOT a good product

reviews.title: Whoop has some good stats, and some fake hype too
reviews.body: WHOOP will be at you day and night; the device is very frisky when it comes to telling you your basic health stats and behaviors. However, I would like to add a few caveats: 1) The AI or algorithm that they use SOUNDS like it's personalized to you, but the conclusions and statements the device makes are based on collected, aggregated, and thoroughly-predigested data. That's not to say its inaccurate, but it's not "personal" in a real sense--the sense that a series of physiological and blood tests would deliver. that would be specific to you. You are more likely to get recos based on standardized data. 2) The app is really busy. There are so many charts and data points and subcategories that it becomes difficult (for me, anyway) to find precisely what I'm looking for. I have to ASK (query) to get to see my running stats, for instance; I can't seem to find them otherwise. 3) The loads of data and so-called personal recos are designed to keep you interested and committed, andf that's basically a good thing, but it's also to hook you into paying an annual fee FOREVER. Compared to a high-end sports watch (Garmin, Suunto, or even Apple) you will be paying ad infinitum for something others offer for free. That said, I've only had my WHOOP for about a month, so I'm expecting a fresh batch of data when I hit the 30-day point, and perhaps I'll find more of it useful when I get there. Right now it's a pleased enough with the info provided, though I do wish it "agreed". more with my watch. Not quite sure whose stats to believe! ***UPDATE*** A few days short of two full months. I DO like their AI; when I correct it ("No that wasn't a run I was digging in the garden / walking the dog") it accepts and adjust response accordingly. Nice. Though I still find the data provided kind of scattered around the site, with no simple menu to help locate something. And WHOOP is OBSESSED with "Strain;" even after reading their explanations I still can't compute their approach. Accuracy still a big ? mark, as it only occasionally matches what my Garmin watch reports. Who to believe??

reviews.title: BEST OPTION FOR YOUNG KIDS!
