I love that I control who can communicate with him (just me and his dad). I recommend it!

reviews.title: Works well for my 11 year old son who
reviews.body: So far so good. We got this for my 11 year old son who is just not ready for the responsibility of a phone yet. He is constantly at ball practices or with friends, so we wanted him to be able to contact us if needed. The watch is a little big on his wrist, but understands me so since it has so many features in it. We did have some trouble with the connectivity at first, but that seems to have been worked out. The parent app is easy to use and set up. It functions as expected. The cellular plan is a little expensive - but since the watch itself is a good deal (compared to some other smartwatches), I don’t mind paying the cellular fee. Is it the most amazing product I’ve ever seen - no. But does it work well enough so I don’t have to hand my 5th grader a phone with access to the entire world on it - yes. So I’m happy enough!

reviews.title: Great for our 10 year old
reviews.body: My husband and I were unsure about this watch when we first got it for our ten year old, but we absolutely love it now! She has had it several weeks now, and in the beginning it just took some getting used to. We thought the service wasn't working, but we found out if you turn it off and turn it back on it usually picks up the network again very quickly. Our daughter loves it and it is very user friendly. We feel comfortable leaving her at practice now knowing she has a way to contact us if she needs to. If you're looking for a way for your child to communicate without the dreaded smart phone, you cannot beat this watch, especially for the price! I will give an update in a couple more months, but we love it so far!

reviews.title: A kid's smartwatch that actually works.
reviews.body: After trying the TickTalk 5 for a few weeks, the short battery life and lackluster GPS I needed to find another kid's watch for my 8 year old to wear to school and trips. I looked at several other brands and even tried an Apple Watch but it wasn't what I was expecting. After Googling around I found a post about the JrTrack 5 and how other parents seemed to like it. I read the reviews and read the specs and it ticked all the boxes. Cosmo uses their own carrier service which you have to use. They offer at least four different plans to chose and gets cheaper the longer term of service you chose. It's a little bit more each month but at the time of this review it was unlimited call, text and data which was better than most of the month to month sim card companies out there. Activating was straight forward. You use the Cosmo app and set it up at a parent. Here you can add the contacts of people who will only be able to call or text them. If you're not on the list it won't go through to the watch. The watch uses TWO GPS chips for locating. We went to Universal Studios and I was able to do spot checks just to see if it worked and it zeroed in exactly where she was each time. Even in the airport terminal it was able to find her. With the GPS you can set up "SafeZones." These are geofenced areas that will alert you when your child has either entered or left the user adjusted area. Battery life so far is good. Even though we charge it each night, we can get just about two days out of a charge. You can set a schedule to tell it not to ping the location say overnight etc. This saves on battery life. The watch has a camera on it but currently does not offer video calling even on Wi-Fi. Normally that's not a problem, but the watch has an SOS function where it starts pinging the location and turns on the microphone so you can hear what's going on. It would be very very helpful to have the camera turn on also so that I can see what is happening also. Hopefully it'll come out in a future update. All in all, it's been a great watch. Call quality is loud and clear and most important she loves to use and wear it. If your kid doesn't want to use it then what's the point.

reviews.title: Peace of mind for a good price
reviews.body: So far, so good! It's already a big step up from our last tracking watch. The GPS is much smoother and my kid loves the picture/video messaging. Haven't had issues with phone calls so far. There's so many features available -- my kid finally isn't complaining about having to tote it around! It's a perfect size for kid, not too clunky. Fair pricing on their plans. All the people who recommend it were right--it's great! The charger works perfectly--a big improvement from our last watch service!!! It's a relief to have something reliable to keep an eye on my active kid!!!

reviews.title: Disappointing reliability; inconsistent pricing and performance
reviews.body: I purchased the JrTrack 5 hoping for a reliable way to stay connected with my child, but unfortunately, it has not met our expectations. The primary reasons for this are ongoing connectivity issues and unreliable GPS tracking. I’ve frequently experienced scenarios where the watch fails to make or receive calls, often resulting in a busy signal or a connection timeout when I need to reach my child most. Additionally, the GPS tracking is often lagging or inaccurate, which defeats the main purpose of having a safety watch. The voice call quality is also inconsistent and often sounds muffled, making it difficult to communicate clearly. We ultimately switched to the TickTalk 5, which has been significantly more reliable. The signal strength, call clarity, and GPS accuracy on the TickTalk 5 are far superior for our needs. I wanted to like the JrTrack 5 for its price point and features, but for a device intended for safety, the technical unreliability makes it hard to recommend. Beyond the technical issues, I’ve found their pricing model to be frustrating—the watch seems to be constantly on sale at different, fluctuating price points, which makes it hard to trust the value of the product.

reviews.title: Setup takes time. Be patient. Overall, pleased.
reviews.body: I purchased two. The first one was a nightmare to setup. In the end, an incorrect IEMI number was to blame; however, it took a week to resolve. Therefore, I lost a week of paid service as the watch was unusable for that amount of time. The watch also had to be updated right out of the box. It would not update with less than 30% charge. There was 0% charge on the watch right out of the box, and it took awhile for the watch to get to 30%. (Batteries don’t hold charge as long as I’d like. I have instructed my kids to leave them on the charger except when they leave the house in an effort to keep the watch from dying.) Pairing the watch to the parent app wasn’t as smooth as it should be. The screen protectors included in the box are cheap and don’t stick well. I have ordered sturdier protectors from COSMO. Hopefully, they will work better. Initially , when my children tried calling me from their watch, my phone would go straight to voicemail every time. Customer service said that they’ve seen that a lot. It has to do with the call filters on my phone. I contacted my carrier and all spam filters were removed. I now receive their calls; however, I suppose I’ll receive more spam calling now too. I have been working with COSMO customer service for a week now. One thing I can say is that they are very polite, patient, and helpful. My case was escalated to a higher level of service because they initially could not figure out why my watch would not pair to my parent app (IEMI). Second level of service communicates through email so if you can’t answer your email right away, it does take some time to get things resolved. However, the service person was very pleasant to work with. Because of all the issues, my kids have only been able to use the watch for a day; however, it’s working well. We’ll see how it holds up over time. For now, although more expensive, I’ll pay the month to month service fee just in case we decide this isn’t for us. I do appreciate that they can’t access harmful content online and they are limited to contacting only the approved people who I have added to the parent app. That’s just what I was looking for! Too many online dangers and extra screen time for kids these days. So far, this has fixed those issues for our family. Besides the difficulty getting it set up, we’re relieved that we can monitor their contacts and location via GPS on this watch.

reviews.title: Poor connectivity and call quality
reviews.body: We've used this watch for about 6 months now and while we're not completely unhappy about it it's got a lot of room for improvement. First let me lay out what's great: my son loves taking pictures and sending them to us. You can limited access to people that can call/text and receive messages and calls, helping provide a safe environment for your child. I think the battery is fine, it provides a full day charge, you just have to remember to charge it overnight, but this isn't a problem for us. Now what I don't like, and it's sort of a deal breaker, and I wouldn't have purchased if I had known this: The connectivity. We're located in a suburb with generally good reception so that shouldn't be a problem, but connectivity is really poor. The watch really struggles to provide accurate and timely location updates. Many times it will take up to 10-15 minutes to provide the location of the watch when active tracking is on, which really defeats the purpose of the watch, and is really frustrating. The second one is the call quality, which is basically to the point of unusable. We've tried everything, including their support desk (which is really great by the way, but in the end it didn't resolve anything), but basically it's impossible to have a call with the watch. It won't pick up what is being said, cuts out and/or just won't work. My son can generally hear us, but we just can't hear him, no matter how clearly or slowly he speaks right into the watch. It's not connectivity, because it's even when we're connected to the Wi-Fi in our home, but outdoors it's even worse to the point of being unusable. When the location tracking works (hit or miss) the watch serves its purpose of allowing peace of mind of knowing where our son is, but not having the ability to call him/talk to him and the very frequent drops in location data availability prevent me from giving this watch more stars. It has all the ingredients to be something awesome, but I think they cheaped out on hardware, resulting in a product that's just not cutting it for us. Other families we know have the same issues, so it's not just us. If the company would improve their hardware and address these issues I'd probably give their updated device a shot, but until then I'd hold off going with this watch.

title: Garmin vívoactive® 5, Health & Fitness GPS Smartwatch, 42mm, Black

reviews.title: Finally found the Fitness Watch that works as advertised!
reviews.body: I have tested numerous “smart watches” in my quest to find a decent replacement for my ever faithful and reliable, Fitbit Versa 4. I purchased it almost four years ago to replace the original Fitbit Versa. But then Google took over Fitbit, and I was looking for a reliable alternative to the Fitbit products. I tried a Samsung Galaxy watch 7 that lost steps by the thousands each day. I tried an Apple Smart Watch that sometimes had to be charged more than once EVERY DAY! I tried a Parsonver (less expensive) but even though it was advertised and labeled IP 68, (indicating that it would withstand submersion in water) I actually received an email from the company before the watch was even delivered advising me to be careful even showering or washing my hands with it on! SERIOUSLY???? And the step counts were not even close to correct! Then I tried an Amazfit BIP6 (also advertised as IP 68, but clearly IS NOT) and thought I had finally found what I was looking for, until it completely malfunctioned after only 3 weeks of use. So Amazon replaced it with ANOTHER BIP6, and that one lasted almost 5 months before it began to seriously malfunction and the touchscreen no longer worked. So my new search began and I decided to give Garmin a try as my walking and swimming buddies swear by their Garmins, and the results that they get with them compare favorably to my old Fitbit. I have now only had the Garmin Vivoactive 5 for about a month, but so far, it is AWESOME! It tracks extremely well with the Fitbit, and I have had no issues whatsoever with water infiltration. If that changes, I will be back to downgrade my rating, but so far, so GREAT! This proves that you don’t have to buy the most expensive models of ANY brand of fitness watch to find one that does what you need it to do. Most of them have more functions than you will ever need or use anyway. I bought separate, different color bands to customize it and love that you have a lot of choices for watch faces, so pick the one that works best for you! (Although - once again, Fitbit has a much better and more user friendly watch face selection portal!) The one potential “glitch” I thought I had finally discovered with my Vivoactive 5, but which turned out not to be an issue, occurred when I was flying internationally. I was returning from Europe to the US on an evening flight where the time in the US was six hours earlier. So both my FITBIT and my Garmin thought that when enough flight time had elapsed, they went past midnight and started their metrics over as a new day - meaning steps completely zeroed out and started over. But not long after I landed at 7 pm US time, my Fitbit picked back up with the previous day’s step tally, but my Garmin still showed the reduced step count tallied as a “new day”. I was disappointed with this until I checked the metrics in the Garmin app and noted that the “two day tallies” indicated on the watch itself were actually (appropriately!) counted and displayed as a single day step counts in the app. So yes, I am sold on the Garmin. But I do still have to wonder why if FITBIT - even early versions - could have successfully addressed ALL of the issues I have found with so many competitor brands, why can’t all the others? Maybe I shouldn’t have been so wary of Google taking over Fitbit when I started investigating other Smart watches, but I learned a lot about different brands and their bogus IP 68 and 5 ATM ratings! So to reiterate, Garmin is exactly what it says it is, and Fitbit is as well. Do your comparisons!

reviews.title: Love me a Garmin
reviews.body: I've been using Garmin for running for years now. They've improved a lot! This one does everything I need and more. I like the body battery, sleep info. The 5 syncs up to GPS much faster than my 4 to run or walk. I love the music, however, my headphones sometimes disconnect to the watch while running. Not sure if it's the headphones or the watch. It's pretty easy to use if you've had one before. It has changed on the strength where you hit the bottom button vs tapping the watch to enter weight/reps (don't have to do that anymore, not that it was a problem). Overall I'm super satisfied. reviews.title: The best fitness tracker I've used
reviews.body: I'm coming from an Apple Watch Series 5. I had gotten frustrated with the battery life and sleep tracking and wanted to see if a more fitness-focused watch would be a better fit. I'm not a big runner or someone who does a lot of intense exercise, but I do like to track my exercise and sleep and get nudges to move when I've been sitting down for too long. I also like to get notifications on my wrist without needing to pull out my phone. Compared to the Apple Watch, the first major thing I noticed was this is nowhere close in terms of smarts. title: Garmin vívoactive® 5, Health & Fitness GPS Smartwatch, 42mm, Ivory

reviews.title: Finally found the Fitness Watch that works as advertised!
reviews.body: I have tested numerous “smart watches” in my quest to find a decent replacement for my ever faithful and reliable, Fitbit Versa 4. I purchased it almost four years ago to replace the original Fitbit Versa. But then Google took over Fitbit, and I was looking for a reliable alternative to the Fitbit products. I tried a Samsung Galaxy watch 7 that lost steps by the thousands each day. I tried an Apple Smart Watch that sometimes had to be charged more than once EVERY DAY! I tried a Parsonver (less expensive) but even though it was advertised and labeled IP 68, (indicating that it would withstand submersion in water) I actually received an email from the company before the watch was even delivered advising me to be careful even showering or washing my hands with it on! SERIOUSLY???? And the step counts were not even close to correct! Then I tried an Amazfit BIP6 (also advertised as IP 68, but clearly IS NOT) and thought I had finally found what I was looking for, until it completely malfunctioned after only 3 weeks of use. So Amazon replaced it with ANOTHER BIP6, and that one lasted almost 5 months before it began to seriously malfunction and the touchscreen no longer worked. So my new search began and I decided to give Garmin a try as my walking and swimming buddies swear by their Garmins, and the results that they get with them compare favorably to my old Fitbit. I have now only had the Garmin Vivoactive 5 for about a month, but so far, it is AWESOME! It tracks extremely well with the Fitbit, and I have had no issues whatsoever with water infiltration. If that changes, I will be back to downgrade my rating, but so far, so GREAT! This proves that you don’t have to buy the most expensive models of ANY brand of fitness watch to find one that does what you need it to do. Most of them have more functions than you will ever need or use anyway. I bought separate, different color bands to customize it and love that you have a lot of choices for watch faces, so pick the one that works best for you! (Although - once again, Fitbit has a much better and more user friendly watch face selection portal!) The one potential “glitch” I thought I had finally discovered with my Vivoactive 5, but which turned out not to be an issue, occurred when I was flying internationally. I was returning from Europe to the US on an evening flight where the time in the US was six hours earlier. So both my FITBIT and my Garmin thought that when enough flight time had elapsed, they went past midnight and started their metrics over as a new day - meaning steps completely zeroed out and started over. But not long after I landed at 7 pm US time, my Fitbit picked back up with the previous day’s step tally, but my Garmin still showed the reduced step count tallied as a “new day”. I was disappointed with this until I checked the metrics in the Garmin app and noted that the “two day tallies” indicated on the watch itself were actually (appropriately!) counted and displayed as a single day step counts in the app. So yes, I am sold on the Garmin. But I do still have to wonder why if FITBIT - even early versions - could have successfully addressed ALL of the issues I have found with so many competitor brands, why can’t all the others? Maybe I shouldn’t have been so wary of Google taking over Fitbit when I started investigating other Smart watches, but I learned a lot about different brands and their bogus IP 68 and 5 ATM ratings! So to reiterate, Garmin is exactly what it says it is, and Fitbit is as well. Do your comparisons!

title: Samsung Galaxy Watch 8 Classic (2025), Black, 46mm, Bluetooth Smartwatch

reviews.title: Premium Look with Excellent Features
reviews.body: The Galaxy Watch 8 Classic looks and feels premium right out of the box. The display is bright and easy to read, the performance is smooth, and it connects quickly with my Samsung phone. I also like the health and fitness tracking features, and the battery easily lasts through a full day of regular use. It’s comfortable to wear, stylish enough for everyday use, and packed with useful features. I’m very happy with this purchase and would definitely recommend it.

reviews.title: Phenomenal(ESPECIALLY IF YOU USE A DIABETIC CGM!)
reviews.body: The negative: Qi wireless charging removed with the watch 8 generation. That means you can't charge the watch from a power-sharing compatible phone(like my S23 Ultra). ....really, though, that's all the negative. Power-sharing has always been fiddly anyway. The neutral: I get about 1.5 days per charge, with battery protection on(max charge @ 90%), and ALL the bells and whistles(including always-on display). If you want it for sleep tracking every night, have a charger at your desk during the day to keep it topped-up. Slightly smaller screen/chassis ratio than expected. The body feels like they COULD have made the display a smidge bigger, but ymmv. That would have impacted weight, durability, and battery life, so it's probably for the best. The good: Feels good. Substantial. Beefy, but not clunky. Get a metal band to replace the sweaty faux-leather/rubber one. Fast. Responsive. Voice commands using google. Built-in digital compass. Gestures(shake your hand in a...suggestive fashion to clear notifications because...um...you're busy...feeding geese 0_o ). The rotating bezel is back, absent on the other variants of the watch 8 generation(and a deal breaker for me). Best of all, though, as an insulin dependent diabetic, the ability to check my blood sugar without unholstering my phone is PURE GOLD. If this applies to you, Google "gluroo watch app". Recap: Not perfect, but it still phenomenal. Not cheap, but I've worn it every day for a month. Every day, I think to myself: "WORTH IT".

reviews.title: Samsung Galaxy Watch 8 Classic (2025) 46mm — A Worthy Return to Form ★★★★★
reviews.body: After putting the Galaxy Watch 8 Classic through its paces over the past few weeks, I can confidently say Samsung nailed the comeback. The rotating bezel is back, and honestly, that alone made me hit "buy" — but there's so much more to love here. Build Quality That Feels Premium The 46mm stainless steel case has real heft without feeling clunky on my wrist. The brushed finish looks sharp whether I'm in a t-shirt at the gym or wearing a button-down to a meeting. The sapphire crystal display has shrugged off everything I've thrown at it — no scratches yet, despite my best (unintentional) efforts. The crown bezel clicks with that satisfying tactile feedback Samsung fans have been begging for since it disappeared. That Display, Though The Super AMOLED screen is gorgeous. Bright enough to read in direct Florida sunlight, vibrant when scrolling notifications, and the always-on display sips battery rather than gulping it. Colors pop and text is razor-sharp. Health Tracking Is Genuinely Useful The upgraded BioActive sensor is the real star. Heart rate tracking is accurate compared to my chest strap, sleep tracking finally feels reliable (with actually actionable insights instead of just data dumps), and the new wellness features — including the energy score and vascular load metrics — give me a real sense of how my body is recovering day to day. ECG, blood oxygen, and body composition all work as advertised. Performance and Battery Wear OS with One UI Watch is snappy. App launches are instant, transitions are smooth, and I haven't experienced the lag that plagued earlier generations. Battery comfortably gets me through a full day with the always-on display enabled, and closer to two days if I turn it off. Fast charging tops it back up while I shower. Fitness Tracking GPS lock is fast and accurate on outdoor runs, workout detection actually catches the workouts I forget to start, and the suite of supported activities covers basically anything I do. The running coach feature has been a pleasant surprise. The Ecosystem Bonus If you're in the Samsung world, this watch is a no-brainer. Pairing with my Galaxy phone was seamless, Samsung Pay works flawlessly, and notifications mirror perfectly. It also plays nicely with non-Samsung Android phones, though you'll lose a few features. Minor Nitpicks The proprietary band connector means you'll want to budget for first-party or compatible straps. And while battery life is solid, power users tracking long workouts with GPS will still want to charge nightly. Bottom Line The Galaxy Watch 8 Classic is the watch Samsung should have been making all along. The rotating bezel transforms the experience, the build quality justifies the premium price, and the health features have genuinely changed how I think about my recovery and sleep. If you've been waiting for Samsung to bring back what made the Classic line special, the wait is over. Highly recommend.

reviews.title: Fit, Form, Style, and Functional.
reviews.body: I love the style, the look, and the feel on my wrist. It's a little heavier than I expected but once I startes wearing it, I don't feel the weight. I like the seamless pairing and compatibility with my Samsung S23 Ultra Smart Phone. I am still getting acquainted with all the features since I've only had it on for less than 2 weeks. I love the vibrant colors on the screen, the many choices to change the face, the ability to change the font size is a nice feature. It works well with the Samsung Health app that's already on my phone, the Echocardiagram feature is pretty cool (not for medical use), battery life is good, I like the fact that I can check my text messages. I haven't tried the AI Assistant yet, but given time, I'll adjust to it gradually. BTW, I am a Senior Citizen so it may take a little while longer to enjoy the full benefits this smartwatch offers. I've tried other less expensive smartwatches in the past but this one hits all the marks for me. I am well pleased so far.

reviews.title: Strong health features and keeps time.
reviews.body: The options on this watch are insane! I bought it for the health features and I find comfort in being able to check my blood pressure and ekg. The sleep monitoring is great. If you are pushing a cart in a store and you are walking the watch doesn't see it. But it has picked up walking and bike riding automatically for exercise tracking. If your phone updates overnight then it disconnects until you restart your phone which means no alarm. Overall happy with this watch I haven't figured out why but a couple of times the watch battery has been dead in the morning but most of the time there is over 40% in the morning so not sure what happened the other two days. The watch does more than I have tried to use.

reviews.title: Amazing device! Battery life is not an issue for me.
reviews.body: My five years old Galaxy Watch 4 was giving me signs. It was time to replace it. I bought the Watch 8 Classic because there is no Watch 9 Classic. I have it tweaked to my liking and I am blown away at what it can do. Battery life is an issue for some users, but not for me. I spend an hour on my PC flying my RC helicopter simulator every day. I charge the watch while I practice, and it is fully charged when I'm done. I have disabled the features that I don't need or use, and I have no issues or "charge anxiety". The rotating bezel is the bees knees. My Watch 4 had the software bezel, but the metal bezel is much much better. The build quality is excellent, and I have no problem with the size and weight. I am surprised at how lightweight it is despite the size. I got some strap adapters so that I can use my Watch 4 straps. Yes, it is a bit pricey, but you get what you pay for! It is a good investment in my opinion. The only time I take it off is when I shower. I have no trouble sleeping with it. The gestures feature is waaay cool. I'm very pleased with it; no buyer's remorse here. I watched several YT videos to help me to set it up. I highly recommend this watch.

reviews.title: This watch is an Amazing buy!
reviews.body: I am beyond happy with my new watch! You get the luxury without the cost. It has so many amazing features using the "Glory Fit App," which is very user-friendly. I'm able to take calls, make calls, and text from the watch. Listen to music by connecting via bluetooth. It allows you to customize countless features like temperature units, weight, and metrics. You can choose between multiple digital face diplays in your watch settings. You can also set the length of time display stays lit before it disappears. It features: training plans, goal setting and allows you to connect with friends. The watch straps are interchangeable so that you can attach different colors or styles. You can monitor your heart rate, blood oxygen levels, sleep, step count, weight, and more! It has a voice assistant and alarm clock as well. You can also sync most of your Apps on your paired device (I did my my phone), so that you can receive notifications and even use the same functions on your watch simultaneously. For example, I paired my youtube account so that whenever I receive a notification in the Youtube App of a new video, it shows that notification on my phone as well. I can even listen to YouTube using the play, pause, and stop buttons from my phone. I also synced our security camera device so that I can receive those notifications as well while away from home. I am able to select any number of applications I want to individually sync or not. This is great so that I can be selective and not have my watch going off every second of the day. It helps me to stay motivated as far as my fitness goes because I'm able to set goals - it sends you an achievement reward notification, which sounds once a goal has been reached. It has so many features that I haven't even begun to tap into. There is a slight learning curve, as with sny smart device, but it's very user-friendly after you patiently program and customize each feature to fit your needs and get the hang of it. I love the color selection options. I chose the black and light pink/rose gold color (for him & her), I also ordered (from another seller) face covers for protection. The covers were very easy to slip on (see in photos & video). It comes with a convenient USB, and the watch is packed in its own individual box. Note: THE BOX HAS (2) WATCHES PICTURED BUT ONLY COMES WITH ONE WATCH. I just want to mention it because my pictures & video show (2) watches, but it's only because I bought them separately in those exact colors pictured on their box. I took multiple pictures to help display some of the features and to demonstrate the ease at attaching a face cover (sold separately via another seller). This is an amazing buy, and it makes the perfect gift. Be sure to check out the video ~ hope this helps!

reviews.title: Surprisingly decent watch
reviews.body: Good watch for the money. You do have to download an app. It is not overly complicated to navigate. I struggled some getting it to connect with the app but I’m not tech savvy. Battery life was good. It would last for two days. It charged quickly. It didn’t track my sleep well, which was one of the reasons I bought it, but it does have to be in constant contact with your wrist and I don’t like my watches that tight. It did do a decent job on vitals and had charts to show weekly levels. The negatives were you had to change your settings to a certain exercise to get a more accurate result. Especially on steps. Since I’m up doing a lot of walking, lifting, bending and sometimes crawling when cleaning the house I found you get a better representation of steps if you changed the setting to indoor walking. 😁 The drawback on any of the exercise settings I would forget to switch back to normal. Which is a negative on me. The next one is a very personal preference. I really wanted to be able to change the bands. I like sparkles and my daughter likes blues. I couldn’t find any that would fit the watch. We ended up making a few cuts here and adjustments there to get them to fit but I don’t think most people would want to do that. My husband bought me an apple watch for my birthday and my daughter didn’t like having anything on her wrist so I gave them to the grandsons 10 & 9. They are obviously not gentle with them but they are still going. I would place that into the sturdy column.

reviews.title: Everyone thinks it’s an Apple Watch lol
reviews.body: I’m super happy with this purchase. I honestly wasn’t expecting to like this smartwatch as much as I do, but it surprised me in a good way. The screen is big, bright, and very clear, which makes it easy to read messages, check notifications, and track my workouts throughout the day. The fitness tracking also seems pretty accurate from what I’ve used so far. One thing I really like is being able to answer calls from the watch. The call quality sounds decent, and it’s convenient when my phone isn’t right next to me. It’s also very comfortable to wear all day and doesn’t feel heavy on my wrist. The battery life has been solid too. I usually get around two days before needing to recharge it. The funniest part is that almost everyone who sees me wearing it thinks I’m wearing an Apple Watch lol. It definitely has a premium look to it without the expensive Apple price tag. Overall, I’m really glad I bought it.

reviews.title: nice watch
reviews.body: I really like this smartwatch. The screen is clear, it’s easy to use, and the call feature works great. It has plenty of fitness options and is comfortable to wear. Great value for the price and definitely recommend it!

reviews.title: Don't buy this watch
reviews.body: I loved this watch for the price. But I purchased 2 watches on May 8th and received them on May 12th. The first watch literally died completely after 2 weeks of using it. Tried charging it, tried holding the button...nothing. I am deaf, and I rely on the vibrations on the watch when someone texts me. I never used the call function, so I can't tell you how well it works. Compatibility, it's great! Connectivity, it stays connected for the MOST part, but at times, it won't stay connected. I wish the battery lasted longer. It lasted less than 7 days! Not the kind of watch I wanted. There are other watches I've had in the past that lasted close to a month! This one sucked on battery life. The sleep monitoring sucked. It doesn't record it well at all—the heart rate and oxygen work just as they're supposed to do. I cannot contact seller to tell them their product sucks. So, on to a watch search that would last longer than what I have now.

reviews.title: Works ok for the price
reviews.body: Im at little on the fence about this watch. For the price it is great and when I first got it I was in love. Now that I've had it for a few weeks and have been able to use it I'm not sure how I feel about it all the time. It adds steps randomly, like even when I'm sleeping (I don't move in my sleep) I wake up and it'll say i took like 400 steps. The heart rate monitor and blood oxygen monitor seem to work just as intended. I got this watch to help track my sleep and this is where I keep having issues. Sometimes it won't register that I slept, or doesn't record it properly (and i have even started wearing the watch backwards so that the sensor is on my wrist so it can get a better read). Today it said I slept for 3 hours while I was out running errands. I also accidentallyet the watch die the other day (it lasted a few days without charging), but it seems like since then I've been having a lot of issues with the Bluetooth, the call features, tracking and notifications. The app is also pretty basic. Sometimes it's hard to find the settings your looking for and they don't give you many options to begin with. When I go in to look at my sleep it shows a graph which is nice, but if you want to try to see the times you have to press on this tiny sliver and most of the time it highlights the wrong thing and doesn't really break anything down for you. I know I got this watch at a great price, but I will be honest I have been looking for a different one similarly priced, considering sending this back. I guess if my opinion changes I'll update my review.

reviews.title: Solid Watch! Worth it if you're debating!
reviews.body: This is a solid watch! I didn't want to spend money on a fitness watch that I was mostly paying for a brand name.. This does everything a fitbit does and most everything the lower end Garmins do. I really like how lightweight it is! I haven't had it long enough to test out the two week battery life but so far it was a quick charge and has been at 100% all day even after wearing it all night and having the sleep and heart rate on, steps seem accurate maybe off one or two steps but nothing is going to measure perfectly even fitbits and Garmins aren't 100% accurate. I like all of the features! However, the Zepp app has too much going on but it's not as difficult to navigate as I was expecting from the other reviews. It's a fitness watch first so those features are great... Call and text is just okay. I gave it 5 stars but I almost just did 4 because it's geared towards men; the design, watch faces, the app etc.. Are all very Male "coded" Which is fine if you don't care I just happen to like a more feminine aesthetic and I think they could do better to have more feminine options or even more neutral options would be great but that is just a nitpicky personal preference. Overall this is a good watch! I did a lot of research and I would say if you're debating it just get it! It is far less expensive to try this and not like it and get something else then it is to try a $300-$800 watch that you hate but you already spent $$ so you feel stuck. UPDATE EXACTLY 1 WEEK LATER: Still a really solid fitness watch but not everything it promises I turned off most of the notifications and app features that don't make sense for my goals and the battery lasts a week. To be fair though I have only taken it off to shower and wash dishes I have worn it day and night for the entire week and currently it's at 10% A week is pretty solid still though. I also bought a screen protector that was pink and a new purple band and it did change the aesthetic for me.

reviews.title: All the features; a fraction of the cost
reviews.body: I am so pleasantly surprised by the quality and feature availability of this affordable off-brand watch. After switching to Android, i needed a watch to replace my Apple watch. I didnt want to get reinvested in an over-priced flagship like Samsung or Garmin, so I looked for something budget but feature rich. This was a SOLID choice and i am so happy with it. Pros: Price. Its hard to beat the low price of this watch. Battery. My apple had to be charged every day or so and it drained rapidly. The Amazfit lasts me at least 5 days with normal use. But here is the best part - its still doing pretty much everything my apple watch was! Im honestly shocked how long the Amazfit battery lasts while still giving me all the features i need. Notifications. The Amazfit integrates with the phone via the Zepp app. You will still recieve all your necessary phone, messages, email, socials, etc notifications to your watch. Integration with Android. This watch works great with Android via the Zepp app. Screen size. Another big surprise was how large the screen size is. I cant believe i paid a third the price of Apple but i got 3-4x battery life and huge screen. Cons: Cosmetic weakness. The metal edge around the screen is already getting some very small dings. I dont really care and it is purely superficial. Theres really not a lot bad i can say about this watch. Im so pleased with the value and capability at the very low price point relative to apple. Other features: Tracks sleep, heart rate, sends movement alerts, has routines, offers a daily biocharge tracker (think battery but its your body's remaining daily charge), tracks steps, movement, calories.

reviews.title: Decently solid value fitness band
reviews.body: Okay, I bought this for Christmas, so I've been using it for about 6 months now. I do believe that this is a good value for your money. It does most of the things I want it to do. It looks good, and I found compatible bands (the original band cooked my skin, and I had to remove it and put on a fabric band). I like its functionality, and the battery lasts a long while (not 14 days but still a good while). The only really negative thing I've found about it is that it will NOT keep notifications turned on from the Zepp app that goes with it. Because I forget to turn it on when it goes off, it's almost never sending me notifications, which is one of the things I bought it for. This is a big issue that I think Amazon needs to correct, or maybe more specifically, they need to correct on the connected Zepp app. No matter how many times I tell it to allow notifications, it'll work for a few days and revert back to none. Then, I go days without noticing it and have to turn it back on again. I've checked Reddit to see what others are saying, and it's definitely a known issue that needs to be addressed.

reviews.title: Great Upgrade from my S7
reviews.body: Bought to replace a previous Tozo S7 which I used 24x7 and enjoyed using and worked reliably for almost year. Tozo was great buy at $35 and still a great buy. HOWEVER, decided to look at upgrading features. Finally, selected Amazfit Bipp 6 and amazed at all the features. First, immediately liked the better watchband that does not stickout, second screen slightly better, third GPS not on S7, Fourth, App much better and worth price difference alone with so many features and frequent updates including being able to keep many watch bands right on the watch - S7 only allowed 1 and no updates. The permanent 4 on S7 ugly and not used. Now a few issues on the Bip 6: At little difficult pairing on startup and side buttons a little stiff until used a few days. It also is time consumig learning new operation & features. Otherwise, no complaints. A best buy and outstanding smart watch making my decision to spend more great.

reviews.title: Amazing Amazfit - Excellent so far.
reviews.body: Edit (06/10/25): Now about 8 days into the Bip 6. After a week of use, the watch was sitting at 50% charge. I charged it up to 96%+ in about an hour. I'm using a USBC charger which I think provides about 2A. Can't say for sure as it's a charger built into a lamp in my bedroom that has both USBC and USBA; the "C" charger shows my Pixel phone charges "rapidly" whereas the "A" plug charges normally (slower but fast enough for the phone to hit 100% sometime during the night). I did try the "A" port (with an A-to-C cable) but it is slower. Still totally happy with the Bip 6. More feedback in a few months. Early days but I thought it might be helpful for those trying to decide between a Fitbit and this Amazfit Bip 6 (a truly unfortunate name). I had been using a Fitbit Charge 5 for a couple of years. The first week I wore it, the Charge 5 detected Afib and that probably saved my life. So I wanted to really like the Charge 5 and continue using it. However, I discovered it was terribly inconsistent in providing a sleep score and HRV; perhaps 40% of the time it just failed. A month or so ago (after 2+ years of use), it would just go "black screen" if I did anything with the Charge 5 other than simply looking at the screen. The battery also didn't last very long and the charger "connection" (magnetic) was hit-or-miss so it was time for a new watch. After deciding against another Fitbit (reviews have gotten worse over the years and Google has already said Fitbit will soon no longer be supported properly), the choice was either an expensive Garmin (and they're all expensive), a Samsung Galaxy watch (also $$$), or one of these "cheap" Chinese brands. (Can't use an Apple watch as my phone is of the Android variety). This Amazfit seemed to have the best reviews of the cheap smartwatches so I bought it with the 3-yr warranty for under $100 total. Amazon delivered it the next morning. Followed the prompts and set it up in a few minutes so it syncs with my Pixel 6a with the Amazfit Zepp app. I charged it using the provided charger "puck" (you must provide your own USB-C cable, remember this!) and, once it reached 100% (a couple of hours maybe), I strapped it on and configured the watch both with the watch's preferences and the Zepp app. I have most of the integration with the phone switched off; why did I need to answer my phone with the watch when I have my phone on my hip all day? I just wanted the watch to keep track of my steps, heart health, and sleep (the latter the most important point). So here we are after three nights and the watch seems to be 100% accurate in sleep tracking and heart health reporting (and it keeps perfect time, of course). As I indicated above, these are still early days but I'm thrilled with this Bip 6. I even am dabbling in the watchface creation app on the web and even that works! Why would I want to use that? I hate tiny type on a large screen so why not make a watchface that really shows off how large all the information can be presented? Great stuff. I am not going to test how waterproof the watch might be; I remove it before showering or swimming and am careful otherwise. BTW: There's a function on the watch where you can "eject" any water that might have found its way into the speaker. (Yes; the watch can play music and you can speak through it to your phone but I'm not going down that patch.) The only downside I can see (and it's not for me) is the length of the band; I have a small wrist but the fourth hole in the strap makes the watch fit properly; I would have expected a longer strap for larger wrists. However, using that fourth hole leaves about 1.75" beyond the buckle (.75" of which tucks back inside the band and that's fine). I would recommend to Amazfit that they provide a longer strap for larger wrists (much like how Fitbit does it). Oh, yeah; one more thing. One of the included apps on the phone is a compass! I set it up so one of the buttons on the side of the watch launches it. You know when your GPS starts off by saying "head east"? Who knows where that is without a compass? Now I know. I'll report back in a few months with more info.

reviews.title: Here’s an honest review for ya!
reviews.body: I was honestly considering returning this, but now I’m a bit undecided. Maybe I’ll write this review and it’ll help me decide. For context, I’m a big watch person - especially for workouts - so I set a budget of $50 max and decided to give this one a try. It was right on the money. When it arrived, I’ll admit the packaging made me a little skeptical. Usually, presentation says a lot about the product, and this didn’t give the best first impression. AT ALL. After opening it, the watch itself did feel a bit flimsy at first (see photos), but surprisingly, the actual build quality turned out to be better than expected. It feels fairly sturdy, which was a nice surprise. I tested it at the gym this morning for the first timr, and it definitely held its own. The workout tracking exceeded my expectations - it offers a wide variety of activities you can easily select, which is a great feature! The battery life is exceptional! It lasts for a very long time which is ALWAYS a plus! I also liked that I could customize the watch face with a personal photo. However, there’s a downside: if you upload your own image instead of using one from the app’s store, you’re very limited in what data can be displayed. Instead of showing time, date, steps, calories, etc. all together, it only allows you to display one or two items. In my case, I could only show the time and date, which was disappointing. Cons: The app is probably the weakest part of this product. There’s a “Find My Phone” feature, but it disconnects every few minutes. You have to reopen the app to reconnect before using it again, which defeats the purpose - especially if you’re trying to locate your phone when it’s lost. Not sure how someone is supposed to find their lost phone but need their phone and watch need to be connected to the app before using this tool. Make it make sense??? You can’t lol. It also claims to support notifications from apps like Snapchat, Facebook, and Instagram, but despite enabling everything, I haven’t received any of those. Not a single one. I only get basic notifications like calls, texts, and a few random apps. I work in software, so I’m prettyyyy comfortable with tech. If I’m having trouble getting these features to work properly, that’s something to keep in mind if those functions are important to you. Please be aware of this if you’re searching for a watch solely for this reasoning. Another downside is that the wristbands aren’t interchangeable - there’s no easy way to swap them out, which is limiting. Which really sucks. Overall, for $50, it’s decent. But honestly, for an extra $20–$30, you could probably find something much better without all the disconnection issues this one constantly gives you. I’ll give it a few more days before deciding whether to keep it or return it. More than likely I’ll be returning to get something more reliable but I’m writing this review for those who wants to stay in a reasonable price range, while giving them the honest review they deserve before spending their hard earned money. Hope this helps!! EDIT 5/24/26: I ended up keeping the watch. The more I used it, the more features I was discovering both in-watch, and in-app. However, I’m still keeping it as 3 stars because of the Cons I’ve listed still being an issue. I’d say give it a try yourselves and see how you like it. You can read all the reviews but it’ll affect everyone differently.

reviews.title: This Review is the only one you need to read! This watch DOES IT ALL!!!!!
reviews.body: This will be the only review needed to know this is the Smart Watch to purchase!! I have at this point probably purchased and returned more than 50 smart watches because I wanted notifications to have an audible tone and not just vibrate. With Bluetooth 5.2 it was an automatic with most of the accompanying apps you had to partner the watch with but when 5.3 came out, it became vibrate only on all apps with the exception of ONE…VeryFit. Additionally, VeryFit is the ONLY one which will register notifications from LITERALLY EVERY SINGLE APP you have which sends banner notifications to your phone, not just the 10-15 options typically seen in the other apps like Gloryfit, DaFit, FitCloudPro, HBand, etc. In order to receive these Push Notifications on an iPhone, which is what I have, you need to go into Settings, Bluetooth, touch the “i” in the circle and check off “Show Message Notifications” and “Share System Notifications”. You must then go to the App List, find VeryFit, make sure Background App Refresh is checked and Notifications are mirroring the ones I’ve captured in my images. The other important piece of info is the watch volume is set low when it first arrives. Make a phone call from the watch and touch the speaker icon key to allow for raising the volume. In the VeryFit app itself, go to Device, click Notifications, be patient and wait a few seconds and the screen will expand - check off “Sync Phone Notifications” and this is where all the excitement is! As notifications come to your phone, they will also become listed here on this page (and your watch will get the alert for them at the same time) and this is where you can Allow or Turn Off the specific notification. I have also captured this in my images for reference. As you can see, I get notifications for everything I receive on my phone. If you need more assistance, do as it says and tap the “i” in the circle on that page and you will get the detailed instructions just as I have given you now. I have also captured those in my images for you to reference as well. This tracks sleep, stress, energy, blood oxygen level, heart rate, gives you weekly averages on all. It can track your cycle for females and ones weight. It has suggested programs to help with better sleep habits, managing weight, stress, breathing exercises etc. It has every possible physical exercise activity one could imagine. It’s waterproof, has excellent options for watch faces - many are free or you can opt to pay for some if you choose not to become a Community member and if you do, those become free then as well. You can share your progress within the community to help stay motivated if needed. You can contact customer service if you have additional questions at anytime by tapping the little blue operator floating on the page within the app as well. There are screen protectors available, watch cases are shown available but they are too big, so don’t bother, you can change out the bands - there’s nothing you can’t do with this watch and the battery life is also fantastic, lasting me a week so far, even with all the many notifications I receive!! Obviously, I highly recommend it!! You won’t regret the purchase! The only thing I am now in need of is finding its twin in rectangular form because I like to switch between that and round; should I find it, I will update this review with the information! I hope this review has helped!

reviews.title: Good watch if it lasts — You won’t regret this purchase
reviews.body: Update 6/3/26, company responded to my email and sent a new watch asap. I will report back in a couple months if it keeps working. Update 4/20/26, just short of 2 months. My watch has been acting up, the screen has not lighting up for me and the charge going from 100% to zero in just a couple minutes, and now the screen won’t turn on and Bluetooth will not connect to my phone. I have added a video of the issue that is causing me to update my review. Not the update I wanted to give as I loved this watch, but I felt compelled to come back and give an update to others so they were aware of what i experienced. I typically don’t write reviews, but I had to for this product. I used to be a Fitbit owner and very much enjoyed the fitness tracking. I was ready to move to a different style, I wanted one that looked more like a watch. I searched and reviewed garmin and nowatch. I didn’t love garmin due to the size of the watch face on my smaller wrist and the one I liked the best was around $500. The nowatch brand is beautiful but along with the expensive price, I didn’t love that you couldn’t look at the watch and see steps. So I landed on, why not give this product a try?? The watch face size was smaller which was better for my wrist size, the price was better than right and it had all the features I wanted, plus more. Once I got this watch I wore this watch and my Fitbit together to compare stats, believe it or not, this watch was closer to the miles walked measured on my treadmill compared to the Fitbit, the sleep stats were similar. Love the ability to answer calls and make calls in this watch. The weather tracking and all notifications come through well. And the screen is amazing. I did swap out my band (20mm), just for personal preference, the one that came with it was durable. Battery lasted 7 days, I used a decent amount and tracked fitness each day. 100% would recommend!!

Die Auswahl der kostenlosen Hintergründe/Uhrendisplays ist meines Erachtens völlig ausreichend und die kostenpflichtigen Displays sind auch nicht teuer, wenn man unbedingt noch etwas anderes brauchen sollte. Für Sport und andere Aktivitäten hat der Hersteller so ziemlich alles an „üblichen“ Sportarten in die Software gepackt. Nach vielen enttäuschenden Erfahrungen mit dieser Art von Uhr im günstigeren Preissegment, bin ich diesmal absolut begeistert. Es muss tatsächlich kein teures Produkt wie ein „angebissener Apfel“ sein um eine Menge Spaß mit einer Smartwatch zu haben. Spaß der auch noch einen klasse Preis hat. Beide Daumen 👍👍...

reviews.title: Getting the basics right
reviews.body: I have used the forerunner 55 watch for over a year now and I have been very pleased. It’s got most of the features that you would want and nothing too flashy or useless. The big selling point for me was the 2 week battery life and I’m happy to say that it has held up pretty well. I use this to track my sleep, mountain biking, gym workouts, and any other random I activity I get into. I went down the rabbit hole of all the fancier watches they have and realized I don’t need them. Sure it would be nice to have a touch screen, but do I really need it? Having a touch screen instead of 2 week battery life is not something I would swap out. And I prefer the buttons over a touchscreen because it just works better for me anyway. I like the size of it cause it’s on the smaller side and the buttons are placed well and useful. Overall, this watch has been great and I probably will stick to the forerunner series when I need a new watch in a couple more years. If you are getting a watch for a specific activity, maybe look at one of the more niche watches but if you just need a good all around watch for a moderately active lifestyle, this might be just what you need.

reviews.title: 3 years and counting!
reviews.body: *** I've been using this watch for 3-years (& 1-month) now. It still works great and I still have zero regrets! I even got one of my sons to buy the same model. *** ------------------------------- Original 11-month review: Thanks to this watch, I was able to drop the 20+ pounds I put on during my post-covid depression. It got me moving again and whereas the original daunting number of 10k steps in a day made me nervous, I now walk around 23k steps daily without even thinking about it. The challenges on the app have helped me move from my former weight loss goals to my present toning ones and suffice it to say, all of this has helped tremendously with my mental health as well. As for the watch features, I was looking at all sorts of brands and all kinds of models and settled on this one and never looked back. I needed a time teller, a pedometer and a heart rate monitor, in no specific order. I received all of those and more with this wrist decor. Not only does the watch look nice and feel weightless on my skin when adjusted correctly, but it works so well at everything it was made to. The heart rate monitor is very accurate when compared with other heart rate monitoring devices. The watch is simple to clean although I was afraid of damaging something whilst attempting to clear out the 'gunk' around the plug-in site. I didn't purchase the watch for the sleep related feature but it is an interesting bonus. After roughly 9-10 months of continuous 24-hour use, I finally started noticing it act up during my treadmill workouts. My heart rate would drop to 0 and at one point I saw it jump to 248. Since I wasn't dead or dying during any of these times, I thought I'd start turning it off at night and I haven't noticed the issue since. It could have just been an error that required an update but like I said, I didn't buy for the sleep feature anyhow. The battery life is pretty good I'd say. When I told my husband one day that I should 'charge my watch tonight because it's been a couple weeks' he was really surprised. I keep track on my exercise calendar whenever I feel the need to plug in, which I do during the night so it doesn't interrupt my steps during the day. I normally charge once it hits somewhere in the 10-19 percentile. This takes (me specifically) about two weeks to accomplish, with roughly an hour and a half, minimum, of recorded activities at least five days a week and the watch otherwise just being turned on consistently. Of course, there are extra outings that warrant using the start button once in a while and yet I still find my charge schedule to remain the same. You can choose from a variety of watch faces that come standard but I definitely have enjoyed looking through the Garmin store at other options. The background I've used for quite some time now shows the moon in its current phase and as a lifetime star gazer, this is a face I was more than happy to throw money at. I spent just a few dollars and received something around 10 different looks, several animated such as plants or flowers that grow or open as you complete your steps for the day- amazing, if you like that sort of thing, turns out I do. Overall, I love my watch and I hope it lasts me a good, long time but if and when it finally dies from time cancer, I'll be sure to replace it with another Garmin!

reviews.title: I love this watch!
reviews.body: I very much Enjoy this watch.. I use it to go on runs, walks, or bike rides to be able to track my performance, and record a map of where i did it Without A Phone and upload to Strava with that map later. Also great quality, not touchscreen, but buttons are memorizable, not like another "device" to mess around on, it can show your notifications, but it is not attaching or time wasting... Overall, it's a good size, not super bulky, and not so small it looks weird, it functions well a little slow but it works, GPS again is very useful for keeping track of things accurately, 10-15 minute setup/connect to phone and pretty easy through the garmin connect app. Would recommend! enjoy!

reviews.title: Fit for my purposes
reviews.body: Wanted a simple wrist device for heart rate monitoring at the gym and while walking, with or without a HRM strap but definitely without all of the current smart phone connectivity clutter. No, I don't care about texts, emails or other messaging when working out--I want to escape that noise. Struck out at REI. The days of simple HRM watches with straps seem to be over. But this device seems to fit the bill, albeit at a higher price point. I have tested the HR accuracy against my combination Polar HRM and Garmin high end cycling computers (1040/1030) and it tracks with remarkable accuracy --remarkable given its reliance on technology that does not include a chest strap. Variation to the Polar chest strap 1030 or 1040 combination did not exceed 3%, when it was not spot on. Quality seems good. As with any of these devices, operation becomes more "intuitive" with increased use. It may be that some of the cheaper knock-off smart watches available on Amazon perform well as well. IDK and am not going to speculate. All I know is that this one is fit for my purposes.

reviews.title: Excellent watch functionality but some tweaks recommended
reviews.body: I had a sports watch and polar chest strap monitor 25 years ago for Concept 2 rower training. Technology has improved enormously since then. I chose the Garmin Forerunner 55 because I wanted simplicity as well as multi-functionality. It fulfils both needs. Above all the Garmin sports watch is accurate. I am now 71 and have just started training prep for another C25K with my daughter - hence the need for an accurate heart rate monitor. The things I like about the watch and app follow plus some suggested tweaks. On the positive side customisable heart rate zones are useful, and it is easy to develop warm up, walk, run, repeat x8 workouts, which can then be modified in subsequent weeks. However, I had to use AI to pose a dozen or so technical questions about how to set up specific procedures and to analyse and interpret some of the performance data that the Garmin produces. The written Garmin instructions in multiple languages don’t touch the sides of what the app can do hence using Google Gemini to pose detailed questions. Another user tip - the Garmin app can be integrated with the Chronometer app which monitors food and exercise expenditure. This combination of apps is a really sophisticated tool to record data, if you are of a scientific disposition. For example, if your Adjusted Baseline Activity hits zero, it indicates that your Garmin has accounted for every metabolic "tick" above your resting BMR. The wider screen of an Apple Mac is much more accessible to see all the post exercise Garmin data. The IPAD version of the Garmin app is actually a scaled mobile app and it is difficult to escape from a page as the menus are obscured. A workaround is to reset your IPad display to ‘more space’, but I would recommend using a laptop and the Garmin website which have no technical issues.

reviews.title: Fantastic Smart Watch for the price, AMAZING battery life!
reviews.body: UPDATE after 2 weeks of owning this Smart Watch for Women: WOW! It's been a week and a half since I last charged this smart watch, and it is only down to 16%! The battery in this watch is AMAZING! SO much better than the Versa2 I had before! [Earlier] So far, I am very impressed with this smart watch! (I previously had a Versa 2 and after about a year the battery barely lasted 2 days, which became very annoying, and then it just stopped charging at all) This Smart Watch for Women is VERY user-friendly. Its time, date, timezone, heart rate, steps etc all work extremely well. And it does much more than my Versa 2 ever did. This smart watch also receives AND sends calls, and did it seamlessly! I haven't yet used the text function to send, however, it has received all my texts and alerted me. It works well with the app, which was easy to download and set up. The BluTooth works well also. I'm also happy that this watch is waterproof (up to a certain depth) because I will be paddleboarding this summer, and swimming. The watch came with two bands from which to choose, which is nice. And it came with its own charging cord, proprietary at one end, but USB on the other. It seems to charge quickly. I would definitely recommend the Smart Watch for Women, especially for those who want a lot of the functions of an Apple Watch, but don't want to pay that exorbitant price! This watch is SO much more reasonable, AND it looks very nice on.

reviews.title: Great googly-moogly the choices!
reviews.body: So realistically, I have gone through 4 (yes this is my 4th) smart watch this year (I think?! Might be 3 but anyways) and thos one by far has FINALLY given me everything I've been looking for. Well, almost everything. Still cant text out on it but, it is what it is. So, some interesting things about this watch compared to the others ive had are the accuracy of the biometrics taken, the screen quality, and overall battery life. Blood oxygen levels and stress monitoring? Excellent! I can even listen to music and make phone calls on this watch! reviews.title: Recommended, lots of pluses, a few caveats
reviews.body: I've come to really like this rose gold smartwatch that I bought as a replacement for a Fitbit Charge 4. I have narrow wrists so it's big in comparison but as said, I'm getting used to it. I love being able to read it at a glance without squinting. The screen is sharp, crisp, gorgeous color and easy to read. Set up was initially easy but when I started using the watch, customizing screens, layout of icons and grant it the permissions it needs, I had to turn to googling "IDW28" and found most of the answers i needed. I am fairly tech savvy and after a lot of frustration, I could only solve my issues this way. (The companion app was no help.) The biggest problem was the watch would compete with my ear buds, phone or bedside speaker to take over Bluetooth control, and attempt to direct the audio to the watch. Audio would cut in and out as it repeatedly tried to take control. I finally figured out what was wrong when I realized a phone call I received was switched to my watch. I had a Dick Tracy watch! 😂 Lol and the audio is not nearly loud enough to make calls on our listen to music. Overall the watch with its phone app is exceptional to monitor steps, heart rate, sleep patterns, exercise sessions, stress level, water intake, weather and control your phone's music app, camera and much more. It also alerts you to notifications of messages and emails. Essentially it's the same notification that your phone displays (not the whole email or text) and you cannot respond. It does not measure blood pressure as some reviews suggest. It will connect to your AI asst but I don't need that. I do wish for a way to enter water intake in the watch but for now that has to be done on the phone app. It charges fast and is easy to hook up. The battery lasts about a week but you're mileage may vary depending on your settings. I would definitely recommend buying if you are looking for an easy to read screen that is a giant step up from something like a Fitbit. If you want to send messages or emails, respond to them, see images attached in same then look to spend 5-10 times the price. Me? I'm happy with the purchase. I don't need to make calls on a watch or compose replies to texts and emails on my wrist. I really hope they solve the problem competing for Bluetooth as I'd like to turn on some of the features I had to give up to solve the problem.

reviews.title: Can't complain...much
reviews.body: Hello there, future watch owners. If you're like me, you've spent wayyy too much time agonizing over which knockoff smart watch to buy, and have probably read every review ever written. So, here is a list of every observed helpful and unfortunate aspect of this quality timepiece. I've been using it about a month. Pros: It looks nice. The screen is large enough to read and navigate easily, without feeling like you have a tablet on your wrist. The responsiveness is decent and the picture is clear. The swipe-right shortcut saves your most recent selections. There are lots of options for what it can do. Workouts, music, phone, calculator, stress, sleep, O2, heart rate, water intake, and something I found especially helpful as someone who leaves their phone lying around, Find My Phone. I've used most of these but have barely scratched the surface on the sports/workouts. Notifications show up with a red dot rather than a large icon, which I like and are easy to read and clear. I really like being able to adjust the brightness on the screen, and having a shortcut for the wake gesture; it's easy to turn off at night - because it's bright enough to burn your retnas - and back on during the day. The flashlight function is very helpful and almost absurdly bright. The alarm works well. The battery has been fantastic. I probably have less notifications set up for social media and email than some, but it easily lasts me a week+, which is way more than my poor, retired 4 year old Versa Lite ever did. Cons: The app sucks. It's like they tracked daily notifications with "app unpaired from device" and forgot to fix it. I am re-pairing every couple of days. It links up quickly but I wish it would stay linked. There are no screen protectors available that I've found and as a result, there is already a scratch on the face. There is also a chip off the wrist sensor already, which makes me wonder about the longevity, and my skins safety. I wish that when you pressed the side button from a selection, it would take you back to the menu, rather than back to the home screen, but that's minor. I also haven't found replacement bands. I don't care for the cloth band but I like the silicone. Eventually it will wear out and I would like to be able to replace it. I haven't braved the water with it yet because I'm afraid of drowning it, so I can't speak to that. I think that for the price-point, it is worth it. I threw the extended warranty on it, so I'm basically covered for three years if something messes up and then I just get a new one. Rant over, enjoy your day 🙂 hope it helps!

reviews.title: Great value smart watch with tons of features
reviews.body: This is a great budget smart watch for someone who is maybe interested in trying one and doesn't want to spend hundreds of pounds on a top branded one. This watch offers you a wide variety of apps and facilities that you would find on a top branded watch It has lots of health apps such as heart rate, sleep, blood oxygen levels and stress levels. It also has a wide variety of fitness apps included which can help you begin your fitness journey with things like walking plans and running plans, or to continue in a journey with more advanced features. The display is large and clear, colours of vibrant and it's a very sensitive screen allowing you to easily navigate your way through the various menus and settings. You will download an app indicated in the instructions, this will allow you to fully personalise your watch as well as store your data - obviously your watch has a limited memory and you will need to store data externally. It charges using a special magnetic USB cord which attaches to the back of the watch. Charging is fast. It's incredible how much you get in this watch for such a low price, it's fantastic for people on a budget or someone just wanting to test the water to see if a smart watch is for them.

reviews.title: Packed with Features and Surprisingly Polished
reviews.body: This smartwatch delivers far more than I expected at its price. It’s stylish and comfortable to wear, and the pink gold version looks particularly refined without feeling too flashy. The screen is clear and responsive, and basic navigation feels smooth. Bluetooth calling has worked well, and the battery life has easily lasted a full week with moderate use. I like the health features, especially the heart rate and sleep tracking, which seem reasonably accurate for general wellness. Notifications come through reliably, and I’ve found the hydration reminders and camera shutter function more useful than expected. The included extra strap is a nice touch, and the ability to swap bands with standard 22mm ones adds even more versatility. While I didn’t dive deep into the fitness modes, the range of options is impressive for anyone with an active routine. The app has room for improvement, especially in reducing clutter and simplifying customization, but it does what’s needed once set up. Overall, this is a very capable smartwatch that gets a lot right, especially for everyday tracking and light communication needs.
