reviews.title: Ottimo prodotto ricco di funzioni ed adatto ad ogni occasione!
reviews.body: Questo smartwatch della AEAC si è dimostrato un prodotto davvero valido e qualitativamente ben fatto. Arriva a casa in una scatolina carina bianca con l’immagine di un orologio e la scritta smartwatch. Aprendo il packing troviamo lo smartwatch con cassa quadrata di colore dorato con un cinturino in silicone di colore rosa già montato. In dotazione abbiamo poi il cavo di ricarica usb con attacco magnetico e il libretto di istruzioni con la lingua italiana. L’orologio, che è un articolo da donna, si presenta molto elegante e adatto ad ogni tipo di occasione. Presenta 1 pulsante al lato che serve per accenderlo/spegnerlo e per navigare nei vari menù e sottomenù, in alternativa al touch screen che risulta comunque preciso e sensibile. Una volta acceso compare la schermata iniziale ed effettuando swipe si scelgono le varie funzioni. Le cose che questo smartwatch può fare sono davvero tante: per le sportive ci sono tutte quelle funzioni relative al benessere del corpo dovute a più di 100 attività tra le quali nuoto, trekking, corsa etc.etc. Ci sono anche molte funzioni più o meno utili come contapassi, cardiofrequenzimetro, monitoraggio ossigeno, monitoraggio del sonno e misuratore di pressione. Poi ci sono le funzioni di un orologio classico come la sveglia e il datario e le funzioni smart che attraverso un collegamento bluetooth ad uno smartphone ci permettono di leggere messaggi da app social come instagram e facebook o da applicazioni come messanger o whatsapp. La connessione ci permette anche di utilizzare le varie play list presenti sul device o di utilizzare la fotocamera dello stesso senza bisogno di prenderlo. L’orologio ha un quadrante rettangolare LCD da 1,8 pollici con una ottima risoluzione di 240x280p in full HD e luminosità, che può essere ulteriormente modificata attraverso le impostazioni. La chiusura del cinturino risulta molto forte e resiste anche a strattoni abbastanza violenti. La connessione con il cellulare è immediata ed è stabile fino a 10 mt circa dal dispositivo (in presenza di ostacoli come porte o muri ovviamente è minore). L’orologio comparirà nella sezione del bluetooth del dispositivo con il nome IDW19 BT. Se tutto questo non bastasse Il costruttore ci mette a disposizione un app gratuita di nome “Very fit” anche in lingua italiana che completa ulteriormente questo smartwatch. Quest'app è davvero utile in quanto una volta scaricata e abbinato l’orologio ci permette di rispondere e chiamare senza prendere il cellulare con una qualità audio sufficientemente buona per conversare anche all’aperto in mezzo ai rumori del traffico. L’app fornisce ulteriori possibilità di settare lo smartwatch nelle sue funzioni e scaricare tanti quadranti diversi o utilizzare una foto personale come sfondo ed ovviamente scaricare eventuali aggiornamenti. Sempre con l’aiuto dell'app possiamo avere un data base dei nostri progressi nelle varie attività sportive e nel monitoraggio delle funzioni corporali ed è possibile anche importare vari contatti telefonici, quelli che magari si chiamano più frequentemente, cosi da non prendere affatto il cellulare. Il costruttore asserisce che questo orologio è impermeabile infatti ha la certificazione IP68 però io il bagno o la doccia con l’orologio eviterei di farlo in quanto il vapore potrebbe danneggiare la batteria. Può essere collegato a dispositivi che hanno android 6.0 o superiore o iOS 9.0 o superiore. Le mie impressioni su questo prodotto sono davvero ottime. Menu e sottomenu sono cosi facili ed intuitivi che non c’è alcun bisogno di vedere il libretto di istruzioni. La batteria al litio è di buona qualità con una durata superiore ai 6/7 giorni utilizzandolo in maniera normale con una ricarica che non dura più di 2 ore. Il cinturino in silicone sembra di buona qualità morbido e flessibile risulta molto comodo e anche dopo averlo indossato una intera giornata non porta prurito o rossore. Vedremo con il tempo anche la durabilità. La lunghezza totale di questo smartwatch è di 25 cm circa il che significa che può essere indossato da persone con una circonferenza del polso che va da 15 cm fino a 20 cm e oltre. Questo tipo di smartwatch non permette di installare applicazioni aggiuntive, non è fornito di GPS integrato per un eventuale navigatore e non da la possibilità di scrivere messaggi o vedere foto. Io l’ho regalato a mia moglie e devo dire che le è subito piaciuto. Lei non è particolarmente affine con la tecnologia ma ha subito imparato ad usarlo, almeno nelle sue funzioni principali. Lo indossa tutto il giorno anche quando lavora e mi ha detto che è cosi leggero che a volte dimentica di indossarlo. Il prezzo di questo al momento della recensione non è disponibile quindi non posso fare una comparazione ed una eventuale valutazione in merito. In conclusione questo è un prodotto di cui sicuramente ne consiglio l’acquisto anche per un eventuale idea regalo appena ritornerà disponibile alla vendita. Spero di essere stato utile nell'esporre tutte le caratteristiche di questo prodotto che mi è stato proposto tramite il programma Vine di Amazon, in cui cerco di dare sempre valutazioni oggettive ed obiettive dei prodotti offerti e testati. Resto comunque a disposizione per chiarire ulteriori dubbi sul prodotto.

title: SAMSUNG Galaxy FIT 3 [2025, 40MM] 1.6" AMOLED Display | IP68 Water Resistant | 14 Days Battery Life | 100+ Watchfaces | 100+ Exercise Modes | International Model (Fast Charger Bundle, Black)

reviews.title: So pleased with this Galaxy 3 fit. Great value for all that this does!!
reviews.body: This Galazy fit 3 is amazing with all the functions. I fell twice last year so I was thrilled that this has a fall detection on it and will call emergency help. Everything is really accurate. It was super easy to set up. It comes with a couple instruction booklets. Plus it has steep by step instructions to follow on the screen. The battery lasts a long time when I turn down the display light. Great value for all you get at an affordable price. I linked it to my health records. My Dr recommended me getting one of these a long time ago and I'm glad I finally did. It is compatable with amazon music so I can put on my headphones and control volume from my wrist. I still have to have my phone on me. But that's not a big deal. It's nice to know how I'm sleeping too. I have narcolepsy and it heals me show my sleep specialist how I'm sleeping at night.

reviews.title: Incredible value and the ultimate everyday companion!
reviews.body: I am honestly so impressed with this watch, especially for the price point. It does pretty much everything the more expensive "big name" smartwatches do, but without the high price tag. It has become an essential part of my daily routine. The activity tracking is spot on, and it’s been incredibly helpful for keeping me accountable and motivated to reach my goals. I love that it tracks my sleep and monitors my stress levels—that stress tracking is a huge plus for me. But my favorite part is how durable it is! It is completely waterproof—I wear it swimming in the pool, in the shower, while washing dishes, and even out in the rain, and it has never failed me once. Plus, it charges incredibly quickly, so I barely have any downtime with it. If you’re looking for a reliable, sleek feature-packed tracker that actually keeps up with your busy life, I highly recommend this one!

reviews.title: Highly recommend!
reviews.body: I'm replacing an old and now dead Fitbit that lasted far longer than most. It was always unreadable in sunlight. This Galaxy is perfect for me so 5 stars, but the heartrate is not accurate. Besides that, it's great! Light weight, comfortable wristband even playing golf or pickleball. Phone call and text notifications very handy and the phone finder has saved a lot of time searching. Large numerals, brightly lit and super easy to read in the brightest light. Claims to be water resistant but with some caveats so I remove it when water is involved. Sweat is no problem. Battery lasts about 5 days and recharges fast.

reviews.title: Good simple lightweight watch
reviews.body: This little watch does everything I need. I didn't want a "phone on my wrist" but wanted something light weight that tracked my steps, was a timer, was connected to my phone for messages. Thus does all this and more! It tracks my sleep better than my old Galaxy watch ever did. It's lightweight and comfortable to wear. I can see my messages, and control my audio on the watch. While I can't personalize the watch face, there are enough choices that I have the face I like. Perfect little watch for what I need. I do NOT need nor want AI on my watch (nor phone for that matter) and was happy to find one that does not offer it! I gave it four stars due to the faulty fall detection function. Twice it tried to call 911 just because I rolled over in bed. Then when I actually fell, it did nothing. I turned off the fall detection as it's useless. But other than that, it is a great little watch for those who want a simpler life!

reviews.title: AMAZING! ABOVE & BEYOND
reviews.body: This watch is 100% AMAZING! I recently left the Apple ecosystem and switched to the Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra, and I absolutely LOVE it. I am NEVER going back to Apple. I've owned several top-of-the-line Apple Watches over the years, but when I really thought about it, I only ever used them for the heart rate monitor, telling time, and tracking my runs. I couldn't justify spending hundreds of dollars on another smartwatch. So I decided to give the Galaxy Fit3 a try, and I'm honestly blown away. When I ordered it, I thought it would just track my steps, heart rate, and the time and I was perfectly fine with that. Instead, I found a fitness tracker packed with features I wasn't expecting. If you have a Samsung phone, this is an absolute no-brainer. It pairs perfectly, does way more than I ever imagined, and for around $50, the value is unbelievable. Save your money and get this you won't regret it!

reviews.title: Great!!!!
reviews.body: Wanted something simple to use, and this is just that. Set up was pretty easy. I couldn't get my notifications to work properly when I first set it up, but all I had to do was reboot it and had no issues after that. Stays charged for about 2 weeks. Had a generic watch prior to this I that I had to connect to the app everyday so it would stay linked.... I dont have to do that with thus one. I think its great and especially at this price!!!

reviews.title: Heart rate and Sleep tracking FTW
reviews.body: Great for heart rate and sleep tracking. If you don't want to get a full blown smart watch get this one. The other features are decent. For the 45ish bucks I am quite happy with it. Step counter seems to register +10% higher than actual. Battery life is 3-4 days. Charging is super fast and easy.

reviews.title: Samsung does it again.
reviews.body: The product works great. No subscription to use. The only issue I had was that Samsung takes 2 weeks to switch your phone number over for 2 step verification. So for about a week I was unable to even start using the device. I said screw it and made a new account. The band is to small for my large wrist, but it was easy to replace with a better band. Not sure why all watch manufacturers do that.. Anyway tech side, you get what you need. Stress, heart rate, sleep, step, food, calorie, period tracker all in one. You can also connect with your doctor on there, but I have not tried that function yet. It's worth the price and I even got my wife one.

reviews.title: A near full smartwatch for a fraction of the price.
reviews.body: At this price? This is 80% of a full smartwatch and a fraction of the cost. I'm extremely happy with it as a fitness tracker. Can control my music playback, works as general purpose HR tracker. Very light and comfortable with excellent battery life, goes for many days. (Since I don't sleep with it, I stretch it to weeks) What it lacks from a full smartwatch? Payments (I don't need), answering calls plus some fancier health tracking like ECG or VO2max. But for the price, who cares? I wear it and don't worry about it. I would prefer I could set the watch without phone and also use standard watch straps, but hey the price! The Samsung app is one of the best for general health tracking. Best by far for nutrition tracking. Serious fitness enthusiast may find it a bit lacking. Shame the watch doesn't work with iPhone. This is a highly recommended device unless you are CERTAIN you need all the fancy features of a Galaxy or Pixel.

reviews.title: Product quality
reviews.body: The products are 100% working and as same as it shows on amazone . So i am happy to buy .

reviews.title: It's a great watch
reviews.body: The battery of this lasted me 5 days with always on display on and without turning on the sleep mode at night. i also kept my phone connected all that time.. So maybe the 13days claim isn't right. but 5 days seems like a decent enough time. Connectivity is really great with the phone. I got notifications in real time. The band is of great quality. there is no itching or anything. Accurate workout calculator. Steps counter is 90 percent great i think. I would say there is an error of around 500 steps give or take during the day. That's not much of a problem according to me. Sleep tracking is really really good. Loving being able to track my sleep so accurately. I love this watch overall. Looks great on my wrist . The dial isn't too big. Doesn't feel heavy and clunky.

title: Samsung Galaxy Watch9, Graphite, 40mm Bluetooth Smartwatch

reviews.title: Battery lifte
reviews.body: I like the watch alot. I thought the battery would last longer. But overall it a good watch.

reviews.title: Daily charging is required for continuous health monitoring
reviews.body: Functionality is very good but it comes at a price in battery utilization. Watch must be charged daily: 1-2 hours. That is the only real complaint. It does take a while to figure out and configure the watch so you get the settings and health measurements you need, especially given battery considerations. You can get better life if you shut down all the auto measurements, wifi, and stick to a simple dark display. Lots of data on-line to help. The display is very good even is sun. Band is silicon so does not breath. It can be easily replaced with inexpensive, comfortable cloth ones.

reviews.title: Great Upgrade from Galaxy Watch 5
reviews.body: As someone who loved her Galaxy Watch 5, I was very excited to finally upgrade to the Watch 9. My old watch finally died this week, which seemed like perfect timing with the new coming out (though I wish I could have taken advantage of pre-order deals but alas). Luckily, I was able to get a replacement pretty quickly and in a color I liked as well. First, I have to say that while I love my watch, it was a bit of a panic attack at first, as the setup was way different from my first watch. As someone who mostly used her watch for productivity tasks, step tracking, and heart rate monitoring during workouts, I found all the new fitness-tracking features extremely overwhelming. I almost sent it back because I wasn't sure if I wanted all these options. Since I didn't want to put up with the lack of functionality and durability of the Fitbit, I decided to stick it out and just turn off some of the features. It was better to have them in case I wanted them later. Once I got my watch working, though, I was very impressed. The fit has been great and it seems more durable than my old watch. The only disappointing thing about it has been that it doesn't work with any of my old Galaxy Watch chargers, which is annoying since I will have to buy new ones. Fairly minor, but still disappointing. I also love that there are so many band options (I personally am not a fan of silicone bands). Overall though, I love the color of my watch and how it feels, and consider it a good value for the money.

reviews.title: Save your money
reviews.body: Watch looks good and was easy to setup. New to Samsung watches, always had fitbit. First, it does everything the other watches do but software is not as intuitive. Actually rather clumsy. Battery. I knew going into this purchase that I would get maybe 30 hours per charge, Fitbit Sense gave me 3 days. But what I wasn't expecting was that the watch takes 90 minutes to charge. Tried three different power blocks including a 43w fast charge. My fitbit charged for 3 days in 20 or so minutes. As others mentioned watch band was too small, had to order a larger band. I like many things about the watch but battery issues may be a deal breaker. May be returning it. Not happy.

reviews.title: Great Upgrade from an Old Galaxy Watch!
reviews.body: I upgraded to the 44mm Watch 9 from a Galaxy Watch 5 that served me well for many many years. The performance difference is night and day, opening apps and navigating swiftly instead of lagging. Gemini/Voice recognition is nearly instant too instead of waiting 10 seconds for it to process and query. The biggest jump though was definitely the battery life! I usually go for a workout first thing in the morning followed by a full day at work. With the watch 5 I was lucky to get to lunch before it was low on battery, often needing a recharge just to survive til I was back home. The watch 9 though is INSANE! I am wearing this thing from 6am til 10pm and when tossing it on the charger at the end of the day it's got 60%+ remaining life. I'm confident I could wear it to sleep track and then charge it while showering the next day to make it easily through 24 hrs no sweat. Definitely worthy if you're a few years back and want some future proofing. Will update as time goes on, I know this honeymoon period wears off quick.

reviews.title: what a piece of useless garbage
reviews.body: It's official, Samsung makes of piece of crap for a watch. Sat on charger all day and all night and it's at 1%. Amazing right. Originally phone charged, when booted and somewhat installed, I was now locked out with an Emergency Call passowrd required. Frustrating to me and BTW, I hate Google with a passion. The fact that Samsung is in bed with me makes me furious. I need and want a Google account less than I need a THIRD NOSTRIL. Sending this back before I have a stroke from frustration. Will try for a replacement but I really have no hope. Besides viewing anything from a 2 inch screen makes me BAT crazy. Yes, there is a whole of people out there that live on their phone and watch, BUT I DON"T and I am not duct taping an electronic device to my rear end - just not that insecure. Sorry folks, if you want to married to something electronic, but I don't.

reviews.title: Can't complain. Very nice :)
reviews.body: I have been wanting a Samsung Galaxy watch for quite some time now. I come to see the 9 was coming out, so I went ahead and pre-ordered. I set it up, and I absolutely have been loving it. I am able to track so many things health wise, which I was looking forward to especially with upcoming heart problems that began recently. I also love that when I am away from my phone I am able to see my notifications, especially if something urgent or important is happening. Very smooth, pretty Smart Watch. Really cannot complain. It has newer features than the previous watches, and it is fun to explore around. :)

reviews.title: It could have been 5 stars.
reviews.body: The Samsung Watch 9 is a good-looking watch. I find its thin design is much better looking than the new bulky/thick Samsung Ultra2. This watch looks gorgeous, feels well made, is easy to read and is bright enough at 3000 nits. The Watch 9 is also very comfortable to wear. The new silicone strap makes this possible. I am excited to see the previous strap is gone. The old strap was uncomfortable and always difficult to put on. I was never fond of the previous folding-in strap design. I have experienced battery life from 2 to 3 days which I find acceptable. The watch is turned off when not in use. The biggest problem with the watch is that its charging method is not backwards compatible. It will not charge on my existing wireless charger or charge from the puck of my previous Samsung watch. So, if you do not have a usb-c charger lying around for the included puck, you need to buy that as well. The charging puck included with the Watch 9 has a different charging configuration than what was used in Samsung's previous generations. While on the subject of charging, I noticed that even if the watch is turned off prior to charging, the Watch 9 will boot itself up again while charging. I find this very irritating. Due to this, I now have to remember to turn the watch off AFTER it is fully charged. Maybe it's me, but I do not want the watch to be constantly on when not in use. Charging time is about 2 hours (from 20% to 100% charge). I would have given this watch 5 stars, if it were not for the charging issues I have encountered.

title: Amazfit Active Max Smart Watch, 1.5" AMOLED Display, GPS, iOS/Android

reviews.title: Not just a sport watch
reviews.body: Excellent battery life paired with one of the brightest screens. OS is snappy and rich in useful features. 3000 nit screen is great for viewing in bright daylight. The flashlight function is one of the most used features on my watch. The light can be toggled to red as well. The sleep tracking is improved over the balance model. Find my phone is another feature that I use daily. I prefer this to apple or popular android brands. The watch itself has a nice sporty look but can also be dressed up just by changing the clock face. This is my 3rd amazfit and they just keep getting better. The price is a steal. This is a legitimate high end brand with some fantastic budget watches. Lastly, there are many accessories from 3rd party manufactures available.

reviews.title: This watch has big bang for your buck!
reviews.body: This watch is awesome! I’ve used Apple watch for years and the battery life on that is terrible. Very different story for the Amazfit Active Max! I’ve had it for a month now and haven’t fully exhausted the battery life on this one yet. I have charged it back to full a couple times, but I’m on my 9th day now, attempting to drain the charge completely to cycle the battery, still at 27%. The Zepp app syncs with IOS health and it has so many features! I was looking at $500-$600 Garmin watches before this, but this watch does everything they do. I’ve also inadvertently banged the bezel on the countertops in my home several times, no scratches! Went for a jog the other day and the watch started a workout and mapped my run! There’s a lot of free watch faces to load to it, and very simple and quick updates. I’ve also used the phone feature to receive a call and the voice and sound were crystal clear! This is a great watch, I absolutely recommend it!

reviews.title: Perfect size if you feel the Active 2 is too small
reviews.body: I previously had the Amazfit Active 2, but felt it was a bit small for my wrist. This however is perfect. Easier to see the heart rate info and whatnot with the larger screen. Plus the battery life is way longer than the 10 days claimed on the Active 2 and while it's not a huge deal to charge, it's still much more convenient to have extra battery life. One thing I was a little unsure of was the thickness. The photos kind of make it look like a beast. While it is thicker than the Active 2 it's not obnoxious and it's given me no pause whatsoever in terms of look and feel. Brightness is excellent, though I haven't had it long enough to test it on a sunny day outdoors. **Edit** Have been out in full sun with it and no problems seeing the screen The strap is very comfortable and is the same type of quick release strap with the pins that other smart watches have. Doing some googling it's a 22mm strap which shouldn't be a problem to find. One thing worth mentioning is some peoples skin is sensitive to silicone straps. My skin is not, but I've also had nylon with velcro and can recommend that if you want to use a different strap. Also there's no more tucking the tail of the strap down between your skin and under the strap, it's now routed the way most other straps are, on the outside. I'll update this review if I have any issues, but if you're up in the air between this and the Active 2 and you don't have tiny wrists I'd definitely go with this. Edit 1/22/26: Zero issues to report. One thing worth mentioning is that the face is not completely flat. The edges at the bezel curve down slightly. This means a flat 1.5 inch screen protector won't work; the edges would come off or there would be bubbles that you can't remove. I'm currently using the same screen protector I had for my Active 2. It doesn't cover everything but it does cover the flat part and vast majority of the screen completely and without any raised edges or bubbles. You can view my profile to see which I used. There seem to be some tempered glass screen protectors here on Amazon that curve down at the edges (with the bezel markings to match), but since this is so new I haven't bought one yet.

reviews.title: Solid smartwatch that punches above its price
reviews.body: Stunning 1.5" AMOLED display with sharp, vibrant colors even in direct sunlight, 25-day battery life is genuinely impressive and delivers as advertised, built-in GPS maps work reliably without needing your phone nearby, lightweight and comfortable for all-day wear. Cons: App ecosystem feels limited compared to Garmin or Apple Watch, some advanced health metrics lack accuracy during intense workouts. Overall a fantastic value smartwatch — the battery life and display alone justify the purchase.

reviews.title: Perfect in many ways
reviews.body: It’s been a week now since the purchase and I can honestly say this is an excellent smart watch! Build Quality: Excellent, well thought out and very good quality controls. Arrived well-packaged with good protective packaging. There is a very small font but well written manual. The screen is of very high definition and very bright. Functionality: Excellent and very responsive. Easy to pair with my IPhone and the alerts are instantaneous, both the phone and the watch receive, emails, alerts etc at exactly the same time and the watch doesn’t show any lag at all. I would say, it beats my Apple watch in receiving the same alerts from the phone! If you’re very active and do all kinds of sports, you’re in luck. The watch is loaded with functions for any sport imaginable. These functions can be turned on or off / customized to suit your life style. Zepp app: The Zepp app is used to set up / pair / customize the watch and it is an excellent app actually! Customization: Also excellent. The watch can be customized in dozens of ways. There are countless watch faces that are free as well as ones that one could purchase. But honestly, the free ones are truly good! Cons: Nothing serious. The band would be much better if the connections are like Apple’s (slide in and lock in place) instead of using pins. The instructions manual really requires a magnifying glass. But it is so intuitive that one may not need the manual and the magnifying glass! In summary: This is a terrific smart watch. I am wearing it more frequently than my Spple watch that cost 3x more! I highly recommend it , especially when on sale!

reviews.title: I really can't say enough.
reviews.body: Best smart watch I have used by far. Have been using it for over two weeks now and it has been great. It was bought to be a "work watch". One I used for my work phone so I didn't have to pull it out every time my coworkers or boss buzzed me. Very quickly I swapped it out for my main smart watch (new Google 3 that came with my phone). This watch is so easy to use, has a huge display, fits snuggly, looks great and holds up in my job, working with my hands. I really can't say enough, I have tried several other smart watches for long periods of time and this in two weeks is by far superior. This is my first review for any watch I own. I use my watch and phone for personal communication as well as fitness tracking and it uses maybe 5% battery life a day, max. It was an excellent purchase. Glad I did. Would buy again. Wish It was around sooner.

reviews.title: Best smart watch ever made !!!!
reviews.body: Amazing !!!!!!!!!!!! I’ve had the Apple Watch SE the Apple Watch Ultra 2 . The bip active max it’s beyond better I actually get all my notifications messages with sounds alert, massive days without charging truly a smart watch that everybody should have I could not stand charging my Apple Watch every day. The active Max does all the vitals track steps like a track dog. It’s really amazing. I’m so happy I got it really high-quality . 170 dollars is extremely good for all you get !!! It’s great and highly recommend . Big round interactive face makes it very resourceful with interactive icons and multi function ..

reviews.title: Not bad for the price.
reviews.body: Had it for about 3 weeks now. Set up was a little tricky but not too bad. The pulse reading seems pretty accurate but I'm not sure about the sleep yet. Sometimes it seems very accurate and sometimes not, so time will tell. The steps count differs quite a bit from that on my phone but I'm not sure which is the more accurate I'll test it when I get a chance. The standing time is totally off. If I stand for one hour and sit for seven it shows me standing for seven or eight hours. The worst part was the wristband. It was very uncomfortable and actually gave me a pretty bad rash so I replaced it with a flexible one.

reviews.title: Runners Watch
reviews.body: I used coros pace 3 for almost 2.5 years until there was hardware issue with crown and touchscreen. I had two amazfit watches previously, GTS and BIP. But I liked my coros pace 3 the most because of its accuracy, battery life and training modes. I didn’t expected it would end this way. It was an expensive watch so I decided to go with a budget watch this time and purchased crossbeats armour pro. I returned it the next day as it wasn’t able to sync with Strava. Next I decided to go with Amazfit watch because i had good experience with my GTS and BIP. Scrolling around I came to know about newly launched Active Max. I just ordered looking at the reviews and ratings on amazon although I didn’t expected much from this one. After using coros pace 3 i was not expecting much from this watch but to my surprise it surpassed my expectations. It did everything what my coros pace 3 did and at not so expensive price tag. It is pretty accurate in distance, heart rate, calories tracking. The calling feature is amazing and speaker and mic are crystal clear. So many good features like quick notifications, bt calling, offline and online music control, AI coaching, Always on display and not to forget it has a very strong gps connection. Gps locks up very fast, within few seconds and doesn’t loose signals throughout the run. 16K is Great value for money for this all in one accurate and precise, premium, feature rich bundled watch.

reviews.title: Surprisingly amazing for the price.
reviews.body: I am pleasantly impressed by this watch especially since it's replacing my Garmin Forerunner 945 which has lost its bezel seal. I'm going to start with the negative: The watch doesn't have built-in golf recognition. I believe that other models from Amazfit do. That's about it as far as negatives go. I track my sleep, my runs and my swims. For me, the watch provides the same type of metrics as the Garmin. If anything, this watch tracks my swimming way better than my garmin. I get the real distance from a swim at the lake. When the Garmin would have me finish in the middle if the lake. The battery last longer than the once impressive 945. I have my music via mp3 upload to the watch, but I can also make phone calls and answer them using the watch microphone and speaker. Really pleased with this Amazon Warehouse Deal!

reviews.title: المفترض متكامل
reviews.body: المنتج وصلني بدون سلك تايب سي افرض ماعندي ؟

reviews.title: AMAZ-ing!!!
reviews.body: I am sooo glad I came across this brand and this watch in particular before I went and bought a Garmin. This is a fraction of the price (extra cheaper coz I bought it on sale) and it is sooooo good and does everything a Garmin does, maybe even more. reviews.title: Returned this and upgraded to LTE version
reviews.body: I've had Garmins and Fitbits only in the past and this is just a huge, massive upgrade. Love the customizations that can be done with the watch too with the cool looking bands and faces that I bought separately on Amazon. I've had it for a year without any screen protectors and it's been durable enough that it's held up well with very little wear and tear on it, but I'm wise enough to use protectors for it now. My only complaint is the battery. It's a bit disappointing that the battery barely lasts a day. I've had to buy 3 chargers for it. One charger for my car, one for work, and one for home because this thing dies fast if you plan to work out with it and use it all day. Still, I love this watch.

reviews.title: Great for Water Sports!
reviews.body: I have had a Samsung Galaxy watch since they first came out. My first one is still going strong, but I needed one that would track my activity in the water, since the majority of my activity is water related. This watch is great for that! It has been in the water with me now almost daily for weeks and works like a charm! I have an app that will automatically set the watch to the water mode, or I can set it myself. It counts each step, stroke and workout moment - and seems to do so accurately. The size is a nice upgrade from the earlier versions, being slightly easier to read. All my apps and information were easily transferred to this new watch, making the transition seamless. It doesn't vibrate quite as strongly as my last one did, so I miss a notification here and there, but since my phone is never more than a few feet away from me, that really isn't an issue. Time will tell if it lasts as long as my first watch did, but I am really so impressed with this watch. To me, it is worth spending the cash to have the added assurance of counting my water activities.

I love the size , the appearance, battery life is good. I literally have no complaints. I love how sleek and elegant it looks regardless what band you have. I also love all the features it has. Calling, GPS, wifi ,accuracy , notifications and more. Super happy

reviews.title: Great smart watch
reviews.body: I ordered this watch because my fitbit suddenly stopped working. I honestly was just going to get another fitbit but decided to look around at other options for smart watches. I primarily used my previous watch for tracking my steps, sleep, and golf play time, but the selling point to this watch was the additional apps that I get access to. I use 18 Birdies when I golf and this watch is compatible with that app. I haven't used it yet since I just got it last week, plus it's been raining every day, but I can't wait to test it out. I also go to the gym and listen to Spotify when I'm working out. I can connect my headphones to my watch and listen to music. I'm still learning so much about this watch but so far I love it. I did have to turn off the AOD after I got it because it was draining my battery faster than I wanted it to. The reason I dropped a star is because the battery life is decent but not great. I have to charge it daily, but I do like that when it's fully charged I get an alert on my Samsung phone to prevent overcharging. I'm a very petite woman and ordered the 40mm. I was afraid this might be too big for my tiny wrist but it really isn't. I honestly like the size and don't think it's too big at all. Overall, I'm really liking the watch and would highly recommend it to anyone who may be on the fence about getting one.

reviews.title: DO NOT Buy! Failed within 15 days; Support SUCKS! Overpriced, Go Watch 7
reviews.body: BOTTOM LINE: if you don't need the 3 Labs - Advanced Glycation End (AGE) product index, the Antioxidant index (does not work anyway), or the Vascular Load, ***Go With the WATCH 7!*** If you do get a watch 8, return it to Amazon as soon as it screws up! Watch 8 #2 is now "inching up" on its O2 measurements. At first, it was 2% points over my Innovo FDA-Approved O2 device. That's okay, because as long as it was consistent, I could deal with it. Now, it is 3% over my Innovo -- My Watch 8 #1 and Watch 7 did the same. I hope this is not a harbinger of failure. It also must be tightened down painfully snug at night. Oct 14, 2025. Bought new watch 8, now Watch 8 #2 I am riddled with inflammation, so pursue antioxidants. I take 3 supplements twice a day. Yet the Antioxidant index stays low. Farce. ****************************** Below is the Watch 8 #1 Oct 10, 2025 - Samsung refunded cost Sent it in a second time. Kept checking (two weeks) and nothing. Finally, Samsung offered a refund. Not for the tax, of course. Awaiting refund. Sep 26, 2025 Already Failing with Same Errors Was on the phone forever with Samsung, being fobbed off on every department imaginable. I bought a Brand-New Watch for $350, and they "repaired it" only to have the same problems! I am so mad I could chew a horseshoe and spit nails. I wish I'd never bought this thing! If you are stupid enough to buy it, return it to Amazon at the first fail! It is not YOU! The sensor array is P-poor and it fails. I miss my Watch 4. Sep 25, 2025 Samsung repaired the watch under warranty. It wiped out all trending in the app. "New" watch still has "blanks" in its monitoring (picture). Samsung says, "wear snugly". It is already so snug it hurts (picture). Furthermore, the "O2" monitoring is 5% MORE than my commercial O2 monitor. I guess I have to go back to wearing five different monitors that are correct. Sep 15, 2025. The watch has become worse. I will contact Samsung under the warranty. Anytime I get sweaty, the watch stops tracking on the wrist! I'm skinny - BMI 20.2. It's a fitness watch, for God's Sake! One expects it to work when you are sweaty! But no - it stops tracking the heart rate and the oxygen level. This is not at all what one wants in a Fitness tracker! Aug 31, 2025. The watch has developed issues with tracking heart rate. I was walking - spanking pace - and the watch stopped tracking my heart rate. I stopped for a directed measure. It said "put your watch on". I took the watch off and cleaned it, and had same result. I finally rebooted the watch and it worked again. I DID NOT have this problem with the Watch 4. Aug 5th, 2025. Anti-oxidant scan doesn't work right. The scan kept saying low - eat a carrot. Three days of carrots and it is still low. Also, I tried to take another scan and the software kept saying "Put your watch back on." - but the watch WAS on. Too many bugs. Aug 2nd, 2025 My initial review wasn't accepted; I am unsure why. I hemmed and hawed about Watch7 and Watch8. I went for this Watch 8 due to features. I am very disappointed. First, I have many Samsung-branded chargers. I was very disappointed that the Watch8 band would not allow the Watch 8 to work on the flat chargers. I guess you could put a weight on the watch, like 2 lbs (!) to press it down, but I believe Samsung should have designed their Watch8 to be compatible with its supporting chargers. See first pic. Second, this is a 40mm watch. I compare it to the Watch4 and the Watch 7, the only others with which I have familiarity. The Watch8 face measures 40mm, but the display is smaller by 2mm, making it a 38mm display. I cannot at this time comment on durability as I have had it three days. Color is personal choice. EDIT - Watch began failing before 30 days! I thought it was me. Functions. The Watch8 is extraordinarily bloated by location-tracking bloatware. I do not do use email, bixby, wallet, etc. from the watch, but it will not allow me to uninstall these apps. Furthermore, every app tracks your location with precision! I have no idea why outlook would need location, for example. The Watch8 has the same processor as the Watch7. Comparing it with the Watch4, I do not see any difference in performance. I would have expected better. The new Health features are AGE - Advanced Glycation End products. Not sure what the low - adequate - high means, and there isn't a lot of information on the web. It also does the antioxidant index - very low - low - adequate. I tried the recommendation --- eat carrots. My value did not change. Lastly, is vascular load. It is supposed to an indication of lifestyle factors affect on your health. Basically, get sleep, exercise, and good diet. Shrug. The Watch8 is supposed to have a better battery. However, I do not see the Watch8 lasting any longer than my Watch4. I still charge the Watch8 at my noon-ish nap time, and see the Watch 8 is down to 66% at noon, and again down to 66% at night, after having been charged at noon. If I could uninstall some of the not-used apps, it may be better, and maybe not. All in all, after seeing all the additional tracking and inability to turn it off, the questionable value of the new "features", the failure to be compatible with industry and brand standard equipment, I wish I'd gone with the Watch7.

reviews.title: The absolute best value-for-money fitness tracker on the market!
reviews.body: After testing several wearables, the Samsung Galaxy Fit3 has completely blown me away. If you are looking for a device that delivers premium health tracking without the bulk or price tag of a full-scale smartwatch, this tracker is an absolute home run. ​Here is my breakdown after putting it through its paces daily: ​Superior Sleep Analytics: The sleep tracking feature on this device is incredibly sophisticated for its price point. It doesn't just log when you fall asleep and wake up; it breaks down your sleep stages (REM, light, deep) and gives you a legitimate, actionable sleep score. It’s light and slim enough that it doesn't bother my wrist at night at all. ​Flawless Menstrual Cycle Tracking: The health tracking integration is seamless. Logging and predicting periods is straightforward, reliable, and integrates perfectly with the Samsung Health app dashboard, keeping all my data in one clean, easy-to-read spot. ​Accurate Step Counting & Daily Metrics: The pedometer is highly accurate and doesn't pick up phantom steps from just moving your arms around. The beautiful, crisp 1.6-inch AMOLED display makes checking your step goals mid-stride incredibly satisfying, even in direct sunlight. Unbeatable Battery & Value: Because it runs on a streamlined operating system rather than a heavy smartwatch OS, the battery life is spectacular. You can easily go days and days without even thinking about a charger, which completely outperforms premium smartwatches that require daily charging. Final Verdict: At this price tier, the build quality and premium aluminum frame feel luxurious, and the feature set rivals trackers double its price. It provides total reliability for daily health monitoring. If you want top-tier metrics on a budget, this is the one to get!

reviews.title: Fits comfortably on my wrist, easy to read bright colored perfect size screen
reviews.body: Arrived quicker than scheduled so that was a nice surprise. I love the soft pink color and I also like the larger screen. My last fitness tracker was smaller screen. This looks similar to a well known expensive brand watch. I just got it today and got right to programming it so I could start wearing it. I can't rate it on durability or accuracy yet but I sure hope it will be more reliable than my last fitness tracker which I won't mention the brand. I like the brightness of the screen which I find easier to read outdoors. UPDATE: Samsung Galaxy Fit 3 (2024) review continued: I'm quite pleased with this item as it seems to actually work each day! Imagine a fitness tracker that actually works and doesn't randomly stop mid day!! Another plus that I discovered by accident is my watch reminds me when I'm out of range of my phone. This helps me to remember to not leave my phone behind if I'm working outside or over at my son's house. I have gotten home and realized an hour later that my phone isn't in my bag. This watch vibrates right away when the phone isn't in range. As an older person this is a help for me. I want to have my phone nearby in case I have a medical issue. I also love the bigger screen and the watch is very responsive which was another frustration with my last fitness tracker. I love the long charge battery life. I doubt I'll ever go back to my prior fitness tracker as it was so maddening to NOT be able to figure out the issues and sometimes it would "wake up" and start working again. This Samsung Galaxy Fit 3 is easy to wear and provides the health tracking numbers that matter to me. Thumbs up.

reviews.title: Love at first sight
reviews.body: This watch is honestly almost perfect. Literally like a 9/10. The design is sleek, the watch face is not too big for my tiny wrist, has a vibrant and attractive display, and the watch band is really nice and soft! I had a fit bit charge 4 before this one and it finally quit on me. I wanted a low budget option because I haven't been consistent and don't have 300 dollars to waste for it to sit around if I end up not staying consistent. For 50 dollars this beauty fits nearly all my needs. Paired to my samsung phone immediately when I pulled it out of the box. Super easy to set up, and tons of different ways to customize the watch face. Have I mentioned its so pretty?? I don't typically wear a watch but I wanted the health metrics to track my heart rate and steps. This is one of two mild caveats. It doesn't actively track your heart rate. Every couple minutes or so it pings your heart rate to get more of a time line than a live feed. No worries, it pings often enough you get a good idea. Only mildly sucks because I use the live feed heart rate monitor to help clue me in to if I might have a panic attack or if I'm overreacting. Another thing. I have been using google health to track my calories and set specific goals for some of my macros I'm trying to hit. Unfortunately, the samsung health app doesn't get this specific and just gives you the suggested daily intake as a metric rather than letting you set your own. What sucks more is that these two apps don't sync with each other. So now I have 2 seperate apps to track my health. All in all. Its really a fantastic little gadget. For $50 I would 10000% buy it again if they came out with a newer version. Will update again after I've had it a few weeks.

reviews.title: Cool Watch - UPDATE 2/17/26
reviews.body: I just received my watch today 2/15 it came fast as promised. I can already say that I like the watch. The color, it was easy to setup and pair to my S24 Ultra with no problems. It's slim, sleek, and cute on my wrist. When I got the watch it was already at 76% I used my phone to charge it to 100% I love the different functions the watch offers. You can adjust the brightness to your liking. In will update on the battery life after a week. It has many different options face changes for the watch and it's easy to read. And for the price it's really affordable. I'm not disappointed at all about purchasing this watch. I'm a HUGE FAN of Samsung products. Update 2/17 - I wanted to vive an update after me having the watch since Sunday afternoon 2/15. The battery life does not live up to as it is advertised for 13 days. You'll probably get about 4 or maybe 5 days at best. Right now as I'm updating my review on this watch I'm at 39% and it's Tuesday evening 2/17 so I know maybe tomorrow I'll have to charge it. The accuracy of the sleep tracker is good. In the Samsung Health App it gives a breakdown of how many hours you slept, if you snoring it records your snoring and you can hear yourself snore. On "smart thing" samsung app it shows you where your watch is or you can go under the wear app and click on "find my band" and it'll take you right to the "smart things" app and it'll show you where your watch is located. Overall I'm satisfied with the watch. So many features. I changed my 5 star to 4 due to the misinformation on the battery life. Would I recommend it to someone that's looking for just a "fitness" app I definitely would. I how the review helps the next purchaser. 3/07/26 UPDATE: The charge on the battery last 6 days. I tracked how long the battery would last without notifications. I charged it last Sunday (afternoon) & this morning 3/07 it was at 3%. Another cool feature that I came across. The walking feature has a voice commentary that tells you how far you been walking, the length of time it comes on when you reach your 1st mile in thought that was cool that it actually talks to you.

reviews.title: The fitbit killer
reviews.body: My wife and I have been fitbit fans since the Charge 2 (2016).  Before the google purchase, fitbit was a strong leader in lower cost fitness trackers.  It did concern us that our fitbits would die frequently (nearly each one we had died within a year from the Charge 2, 3, 4). However after talking with customer service they would send us replacement.  So, ok, we can deal with that.  (Even though in the past few years you had to provide a ton of documentation including, IIRC, your drivers license.) I had a fitbit 6 that I got for Christmas 2024.  Wow, a color screen.  LOL.  I needed a replacement as the screen on my Charge 5 kept getting dimmer, and dimmer, to the point when I could not read it outdoors and barely indoors.  So I was gifted the Charge 6 and it was big step up.  But it took me a few months until I realized that the floors option was gone, not just not working, but removed, to make space for other features I could care less about. So I looked around in late June and discovered the Fit 3.  So I bought one.  I am SO GLAD I did.  What do I need?  Step counter, heart rate, floors, distance, calories.  Oh, and the kicker for me was AIRPLANE MODE.  I study various energetic sciences including BioGeometry and the EMF coming from our devices is not benign.  I don't wear a tracker to sleep, don't want anything live, and keep my blue tooth turned off unless I am actively syncing. This is what I see comparing Fit 3 to Fitbit Charge 6.   What the Fit 3 has as an advantage:  Larger screen, airplane mode, beautiful faces, much cleaner UI on the watch and in the android app(s) (I am using this with a Pixel 7 phone).  The ability to sync only turning on bluetooth.  A few years ago fitbit/google basically said we aren't syncing your fitbit unless you have both location/GPS and bluetooth turned on.  Sometimes you could get the fitbit to sync with location off but this was tricky/spotty. What advantages did the Charge 6 have for me, personally.   None really.  It cost about 3x the amount for the Charge 6 compared to the Fit 3.  That's ridiculous. In a head to head comparsion of measurements this is what I see.   Fitbit Charge is often slower to start your step counts and the Fit 3 is quicker on that.  So you steps counts are going to go up and perhaps the Fit 3 does count some arm motions as steps when it should not.  But the Fit 3 is still very close (within 1-3%) with the Charge 6.  The Fit 3 tends to undercount calories compared to the Charge 6, I can't tell which is more accurate.  On the Charge 6 bluetooth syncing was always a laborious pain taking sometimes minutes to get the past few days of data and often having to turn bluetooth off/on and/or restarts to get it to sync.  The Fit 3 is very fast *most* of the time.  I did have one instance where the Fit 3 was not syncing in the Health App and I had to open the Wearable app and trigger a sync from there, which worked. The big thing is battery life.  I have automatic activity tracking turned on and except when syncing in the evening I keep it on airplane mode.  I charged it overnight last Thursday/Friday before I first put it on.  It's now Wednesday evening, nearing 6 complete days of use and my battery level is at 55%.  That frugal energy use is really good and is on par with the earlier monochrome fitbits. I am very pleased with my Fit 3 purchase.  Back in the early to mid 2000's I was very excited about Timex was doing just in digital watches (Iron Man, etc).  The Fit 3 harkens back to those kind of days for me when you could get a very full functionality wrist device that looked good, worked great, and was a good deal.  This is definitely worth a close look if you don't need an higher priced fitness/communication device that is emitting EMFs into your pericardium meridian 24x7.  Well done.

reviews.title: Nice fitness tracker
reviews.body: I've had a long line of Fit Bits and when I found out Samsung has a non-smart watch tracker, I decided to give it a chance. (I don't want to pay smart watch prices.) Out of the box, the Fit 3 was in Spanish, but when I put it on the charger, it reverted to English. It stayed English until I got a new phone and had to reset the tracker in order to pair it with the new phone. The tracker reverted to Spanish and putting it on the charger did not change that this time. I pressed the top option on the device's screen and got to choose from a whole list of languages. I chose English, but this is where someone who wants another language will find it. The charge on this item is supposed to last up to 13 days. I've had this device for 3 months, and I got 6 days out of each charge (7 if I let the device die) for the first 2 months or so. Now, it last 4-5 days. I don't have the display always on and I don't consider my use of this device heavy by any means. 6 days is what I got out of my most recent Fitbit. My Fit 3 charges from 20% to 70% in about 20 minutes and to 100% in about an hour. The trick is to get the charger properly seated, because the first couple of times, I don't think it was on correctly, as I got the main display, not the charging percentage display, and it took about 2 hours to reach 100%. I wore the new Fit 3 side by side with my old Fitbit Charge 6 for 24+ hours to compare - 2 nights and one active day. The first night, the Fit 3 recorded 20 more minutes of sleep and the second night, the Fitbit recorded 20 more minutes. I don't know how either determines when I am asleep and not quietly reading, so I figure the results are comparable. The Fit 3, while behind on step count early in the day, ended the day with almost 1,500 more steps than the Fitbit. Both counted activity (cleaning, for instance), not just pure steps. I'm OK with this - I figure any movement is better than no movement. There are many more features that I don't use. I may in the future, but I'm happy with what I do use. I tried taking photos on my phone (also a Samsung) with my Fit 3 as a remote shutter button. I like that feature! Text notifications come to my Fit 3, but not all of them. When I am using my phone, notifications do not go to the tracker (I have found that this is the default and I can change it if desired). Group texts never do (they will go to my car, so I don’t know why they won't go to my Fit 3), and random regular texts don't. I found in the Health app where I can pick and choose which apps will send notifications. All told, I like this device. It’s not perfect, though. I miss the feature that Fitbit has that reminds me to move each hour. I'm now forced to choose between step count, floor count (I assume that means how many stairs I climb), or active hours. I like counting steps, so that's my main goal. I like seeing the hearts light up throughout the day as I get closer to my goals. I also have active minutes and active calories burned as goals, but I don’t care as much about those.

For day-to-day tracking it covers everything I need — steps, heart rate, sleep, calories, stress monitoring. The band is comfortable enough to sleep in and the clasp is secure so I never worry about it coming loose during workouts. It handles sweat well too and I've worn it through some pretty intense sessions with no issues. For the price, this thing punches way above its weight. It's not trying to be a full smartwatch and it doesn't need to be — it does its job brilliantly. The pink colour just makes it even better. Highly recommend, especially if you want something stylish, lightweight and reliable without breaking the bank.

reviews.title: The Ultimate Triathlon Watch
reviews.body: I use the Garmin Forerunner 970 every single day, and buying it has been one of the best investments I've made. As a triathlete, it has everything I need for swimming, cycling, and running—and much more. The training and performance metrics are outstanding, and the sleep tracking has been incredibly useful. Coming from the Apple ecosystem, I was especially impressed by the battery life. It lasts so much longer than I expected, making it easy to wear 24/7 without worrying about charging. Despite all of its features, the watch is incredibly lightweight and very comfortable to wear all day and night. I barely notice it's on my wrist. Paired with the Garmin HRM-Pro Plus, it becomes an exceptional combination for running and swimming metrics, and overall training analysis. I highly recommend it to anyone who is serious about running or triathlon.

reviews.title: The Best Sports Smartwatch I’ve Ever Owned
reviews.body: Absolutely phenomenal. The Garmin Forerunner 970 exceeded all of my expectations. The AMOLED display is stunning, incredibly sharp, and easy to read in any lighting condition. GPS accuracy is outstanding, the training metrics are extremely detailed, and the battery life is impressive even with heavy daily use. I use it for workouts, walking, and everyday health tracking, and it performs flawlessly. The build quality feels premium, it's comfortable to wear all day, and every feature works smoothly and reliably. If you're looking for a high-end sports smartwatch with advanced performance metrics, excellent battery life, and top-tier quality, this is worth every penny. Without a doubt, one of the best tech purchases I've ever made. Highly recommended! ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

reviews.title: One of the best smartwatches as a Triathlete
reviews.body: One of the best smartwatches I’ve used as a triathlete. Comes with a built in triathlon function that can track all 3 sports + transition times. Battery life lasts pretty much 2 weeks and recharges while I’m in the shower. Garmin also syncs all data from the Forerunner 970 with the Edge bike computers and connects with their heart rate straps and if you use a Wahoo/Zwift trainer everything syncs together as well. Display is super bright and comes with an always on display now + built in flashlight at the top which is probably one of the best things about the watch. I’ve also seen zero scratches on the display so I can attest the sapphire display they use is definitely more durable than my last Apple Watch’s display glass. It takes some getting used to compared to how easy Apple Watches are to pick up immediately but everything just makes sense once you figure it out.

reviews.title: The gadget that i always want to have.
reviews.body: As a recreational runner, the Garmin Forerunner 970 has proven to be a tremendous gadget that has truly transformed my training. The amount of data it collects is impressive, allowing me to monitor my progress with professional-grade accuracy. The device stores and translates complex metrics into a simple format, making it easier to make decisions to improve my fitness. I must admit that, at first, it is complicated to understand so much information and navigate through all the features it offers. However, once you get past the learning curve, it becomes indispensable. It is a powerful tool that, while offering elite-level functions, perfectly adapts to those of us who run for passion and health. A high-quality investment that keeps me motivated to keep clocking in miles!

reviews.title: Amazing watch!!
reviews.body: This is one of the best Garmin watches I've ever had. The bright AMOLED screen is awesome, and the features are second to none. I love the color scheme with the gold bezel and buttons. I also love the color of the watch band, but found it too long as it wraps around my wrist almost twice, and also don't like that the band is not a QuickFit band. I like to switch out colors occasionally, so I replaced the band with similar 22mm QuickFit bands. I just wish Garmin would make this original band with a QuickFit connector. The battery life on this watch is amazing!! It lasted through a 5-hour race while playing music on it, and normally only needs to be charged every couple weeks. It's also really cold you can download and customize your watch faces. If you buy this watch you won't be sorry!

reviews.title: This watch is worth every penny!
reviews.body: This is the absolute best "smart watch" that has all the performance features I want even though, realistically, I won't use as many of them as I talked myself into believing when I made the decision to buy it. The Venu 4 was the other contender but I really wanted the on wrist color maps of the 970 even though the price was nearly $200 more. Another positive note on the new Garmin watches in general is the marked improvement in the UI and how customizable it is. My old Venu 2 Plus was very clunky and everything was buried deep in a chaotic menu structure. That watch, however, is still running strong. Other than theses points and the basic high quality of Garmin devices, the biggest advantage is the phenomenal battery life! I am getting 10-15 days depending g on how I use it. I have a Galaxy Ultra which I absolutely love but it needed to be charged everyday, even when not using workout features, which is why I was looking for replacement in the first place. If you can take the price hit, this is the beast to get.

reviews.title: Beautiful Watch!

reviews.title: Worth every penny.
reviews.body: I was concerned about making a switch from Fitbit to Garmin and in price shock, but it has been 2 months with my 970 and I LOVE it! The options are many and I am still learning to use more each week, but I like it. I love stats. This watch provides me with LOTS of stats and tracking from health to fitness for me. The battery life is a what caught my eye on this model, but the stats are beyond what I imagined. Garmin has challenges available. Each month I have been joining quite a few of thier challenges and that is very motivating for me. If you are on the fence about purchasing this, I truly don't think you will be disappointed once you pull the plug. This will last me for years to come.

reviews.title: Excellent product, best sports watch available.
reviews.body: Fantastic item, worth the expense. Lots of running data (probably more than I need, would be enough for an elite runner). Upgraded from a Forerunner 165 mainly for the maps (which are excellent, almost OS map quality) and the ability to plot courses on the watch. Music and lap times through bluetooth headphones. The watch also has a speaker to give times and warnings about pace (too slow/fast) which are useful during races when I don't wear headphones. Also has inbuilt torch which is good enough to assist when running after dark, and suprisingly useful at other times (think searching in dark cupboards, examining fuse box, etc). Battery normally lasts me about five days, with running everyday and on a fairly bright setting. Would be less if you used the "always on" setting. Screen bright and easy to read, even when racing (without my reading glasses!), and the screens are all customisable whether you are interested in pace, distance, heart rate, time in heart zones, ascent/descent, etc. The watch has metrics for loads of other sports, including cycling, swimming, snowboarding, etc, which I cannot comment on, but for a distance runner this is probably the best sports watch available today.

title: Smart Watch, Real Time Smart Translation Watch, Two-way Instant Voice Translation, Online & Offline Language Translator Device for Men Women, AI Translator Smartwatch with Health Fitness Tracker

reviews.title: The Ultimate Travel Companion on Your Wrist
reviews.body: ​The first thing you notice is the presence this watch has. Unlike slim, minimalist trackers, this device leans into its "mini-smartphone" identity. The build quality is substantial, featuring a vibrant display that makes navigating the Google Play Store surprisingly intuitive. Having full access to an app ecosystem means you aren't stuck with "lite" versions of tools; you can run the actual apps you rely on. ​Communication & Translation: A Game Changer ​The standout feature is undoubtedly the Two-way Instant Voice Translation. ​International Meetings: In a professional setting, the real-time smart translation acts like a digital interpreter. It reduces the "awkward silence" of typing into a phone. ​Connectivity: While it supports offline mode for basic phrases, it truly shines when connected to Wi-Fi. The cloud-based processing ensures the translation captures nuances and technical jargon often missed by offline engines. ​Independence: Because it functions as a standalone device, you can keep your primary phone tucked away in your bag while navigating a foreign city. ​Health and Activity Tracking ​Despite its focus on communication, it doesn't skimp on the vitals. It provides a comprehensive suite of sensors: ​Vitals: Consistent monitoring of Heart Rate and SpO2 (Blood Oxygen), which is particularly useful for adjusting to jet lag or high-altitude travel. ​Sleep Quality: The software breaks down REM, light, and deep sleep cycles. ​Fitness: It tracks the staples—steps and movement—but also differentiates between indoor and outdoor activities, using built-in GPS to map your treks accurately. ​Camera and Remote Control ​The integrated camera is a "secret weapon" for travelers. ​Direct Capture: Great for quick snaps of signs or documents for instant translation. ​Remote Shutter: It doubles as a cell phone camera controller. This is perfect for solo travelers or group shots where you want to prop up your main phone and trigger the shutter from your wrist. ​Battery Life ​For a device running a full OS and a bright screen, the battery performance is impressive. You can expect at least 3 days of regular use. This is a significant step up from many high-end smartwatches that require a nightly charge, giving you peace of mind during long transit days. ​The Verdict ​Pros: ​Standalone capability with Google Play Store. ​Superior real-time translation (best results via Wi-Fi). ​Multifunctional camera and remote control. ​Robust 3-day battery life. ​Cons: ​Requires Wi-Fi for the most accurate, nuanced translations. ​Larger form factor than standard fitness bands (to accommodate the "mini-phone" hardware).

reviews.title: Very Helpful for My Job as a Taxi Driver

After using it for a while, it's been really helpful for communicating with passengers. The watch looks stylish and lightweight, and the large screen is easy to read. The best part is the built-in translation. I can translate directly on the watch without using my phone or installing other apps. The translation shows in full screen and can also read the result aloud, which makes conversations easier. It supports 127 languages online and 20+ offline languages. I mainly tested English and Spanish, and for simple daily conversations the translation is fast and accurate. Other languages I haven't tried yet. Besides translation, it also has health tracking, sports modes, weather, and other smartwatch features, and the battery lasts about 2–3 days. Pros Translate directly on the watch Fast translation for daily conversations 127 online languages + 20+ offline languages Large screen and comfortable to wear Cons No SIM card (needs Wi-Fi or hotspot) Built-in speaker volume is a little low The seller also included a mini Bluetooth speaker, which makes the translation voice louder. Overall, it feels like one of the world first watches that can translate directly, and it's been very useful for my work and daily communication. There are more features I'm still exploring, and I may update this review later.

reviews.title: Great MagSafe Hold & Premium Look without the Premium Price Tag
reviews.body: Finding a solid case for an iPhone SE that actually includes strong, reliable MagSafe compatibility can be a bit of a hunt. I picked this up looking for an everyday protective cover that wouldn't break the bank, and straight out of the box, it delivered exactly what was advertised. It offers an incredible value compared to high-end name-brand cases that cost three to four times as much. Real-World Details & Performance The fit on the phone is absolute perfection—it snaps on snugly and feels almost like a factory-custom cover with no loose edges or awkward alignment. The translucent matte finish gives the phone a very clean, high-class aesthetic that looks much better in person than standard clear TPU cases. Functionally, the MagSafe magnets are surprisingly strong. Magnetic chargers and accessories lock into place firmly with zero slipping. It has already survived a few accidental drops around the house without a scratch to the phone or the case itself. While I've only had it for a short time—so long-term durability over months of heavy use remains to be seen—the initial build quality feels remarkably sturdy. Pros & Cons Pros: Strong MagSafe Hold: Magnets align perfectly and grip chargers securely. Custom Fit: Wraps precisely around the phone without bulk or gaps. Classy Aesthetic: Translucent back gives it a sleek, high-end look. Unbeatable Value: Delivers the protection and features of expensive cases at a fraction of the cost. Proven Drop Defense: Handled initial drops smoothly with great corner protection. Cons: Unproven Long-Term Wear: Too early to tell how the TPU border and translucent back will hold up against daily friction and yellowing over time. Final Verdict If you need a reliable, attractive daily case and aren't putting your phone through extreme hazard environments (like heavy construction or intense outdoor sports), this is an absolute winner. I would easily buy this again or pick one up for my kids' phones. Highly recommended for anyone wanting full MagSafe functionality and sleek style on a budget!

reviews.body: This case has been a great match for my Pixel 11 Pro. Drop protection has held up in real use, I have had a couple of accidental drops from pocket height with zero damage to the phone, the raised edges around the screen and camera plateau do their job keeping both off flat surfaces. Despite offering real protection, the case stays impressively slim and does not feel bulky in a pocket or bag. Overall this is a well designed case that strikes a great balance between showing off the phone's design and offering genuine everyday protection. The trusted OtterBox durability combined with a minimalist look makes this an easy recommendation for anyone who does not want to sacrifice style for protection.

reviews.title: Good value
reviews.body: This case looks much better in front of you than a picture can render. I have the Product Red iPhone XR and this is the red case. The color comes very close to the color of the aluminum frame and looks like part of the phone. At first glance it doesn't look like there is any case at all! The red color is a shiny, metallic red as opposed to the matte red color of the iPhone frame. It does not clash where the phone's color can be seen in the cutouts and it nicely compliments the color on the back of the phone! Contrary to what another reviewer said, this case does indeed have a lip for basic screen protection. If you lay your phone face down on a perfectly flat surface with this case on, the screen will not contact anything. That being said, it is minimal by design. If you think you may be tossing your expensive phone around in places where the screen could be impacted perhaps you would be better served with a more robust case. This case is a great value for what it is! It complements the phone's styling. It will protect your phone from scratches on the back and sides. I had an iPhone 6 Plus with no screen protector installed on the glass for four years. The only protection was the lip provided by the various cases I used. The glass never got more than the most superficial, barely visible marks in that length of time. Totally worth it to me for the arguably better user experience of the naked glass screen. Even the most pricey tempered glass screen protectors do not match the buttery smooth touchscreen experience in my opinion. My fingers do not slide the same way. Anyway, the glass on the iPhone XR is significantly tougher than previous phones and I don't anticipate a problem. I offer that information only to illustrate that, with proper care in handling, you can rock an inexpensive, minimalist case with no issues. It should be noted, as another reviewer has said, that the back of this case is NOT perfectly clear. The phone can be seen but there is a pattern or texture which is noticeable if you hold it to the light just right. Not a deal breaker at all for me. You can still showcase the beauty of your XR with this case but it could be an issue if you require a perfectly clear back. I think this pattern may have something to do with durability and I doubt it will be an issue to most users. There is a color coordinated lip to protect the camera lens and I love the custom color coordinated cutout for the flash and mic modules in the back. So many XR cases simply have a huge opening that looks like it was designed for a dual camera setup. I like the extra attention to detail. One caveat: The fit is snug. If you are like me and frequently take you case off for thorough cleaning or want to rock a different case for that day, care should be taken when removing this case. The iPhone's aluminum frame is slippery and you could launch your phone out of your hands! I bought several cases together to compare. The Ranvoo case is nearly identical to this one. That one is much easier to remove because it is ever so slightly thinner. It has the same attention to detail in the cutouts and the same pattern in the "clear" back. The tradeoff is there is virtually no raised lip to protect the screen which is why it's easier to remove. Both products are good for what they are. This Torras case is a remarkably nice product for the money. With proper care it could be the only case you need but at this price, it will be a nice option in your iPhone's wardrobe.

reviews.body: Snug fit with my iPhone 17 Pro so it protects my phone quite well and I’m quite happy with it. Seems to be durable as I have dropped my phone a couple of times I’m very surfaces and so far, I haven’t seen a crack anywhere. Quality seems to be solid so far but only time will tell. Feels very slick and smooth, but maybe too smooth as it has been known to slide quite easily. There is a protector for the front screen (which I did not purchase), but I decided against it as I have discovered front screens reduce the phone‘s ability to detect commands with my finger after time has progressed and dirt/detritus builds up behind the screen after a certain length of time. I was concerned at first that the edge of the case on the back where the lenses are located would raise the phone too high and not allow charging when the phone was laying down on a charge mat, but that was not the case. Although, I did discover that exact positioning is important as just laying it down doesn’t always mean the phone is charging. So, I had to make sure to watch the screen when I wanna charge to make sure the mat and the phone aren’t position to charge when needed. All in all, this is a pretty solid product and I haven’t seen any yellowing in the plastic case as of yet, but it’s only been a couple months since I’ve been using it so maybe after a year I’ll reassess again. If there was one thing that would bug me about this case, is the raised lip of the back of the case surrounding the lenses. There was already a raised area on the phone for those lenses and this case just makes it that much more pronounced. I can only guess that the raised lip area on the back of the case is to further protect the lenses, but that also makes it harder for easy positioning for charging, and makes the phone bulkier when being placed into a pocket or bag. Still, this protects my phone and does what I want it to do so the raised area on the back is a minor issue that I can live with for now. Would I get another one? Hmmmm, maybe. Too early to tell at this point. But I won’t say no if something better comes out on the market.

reviews.title: Great MagSafe Hold & Premium Look without the Premium Price Tag
reviews.body: Finding a solid case for an iPhone SE that actually includes strong, reliable MagSafe compatibility can be a bit of a hunt. I picked this up looking for an everyday protective cover that wouldn't break the bank, and straight out of the box, it delivered exactly what was advertised. It offers an incredible value compared to high-end name-brand cases that cost three to four times as much. Real-World Details & Performance The fit on the phone is absolute perfection—it snaps on snugly and feels almost like a factory-custom cover with no loose edges or awkward alignment. The translucent matte finish gives the phone a very clean, high-class aesthetic that looks much better in person than standard clear TPU cases. Functionally, the MagSafe magnets are surprisingly strong. Magnetic chargers and accessories lock into place firmly with zero slipping. It has already survived a few accidental drops around the house without a scratch to the phone or the case itself. While I've only had it for a short time—so long-term durability over months of heavy use remains to be seen—the initial build quality feels remarkably sturdy. Pros & Cons Pros: Strong MagSafe Hold: Magnets align perfectly and grip chargers securely. Custom Fit: Wraps precisely around the phone without bulk or gaps. Classy Aesthetic: Translucent back gives it a sleek, high-end look. Unbeatable Value: Delivers the protection and features of expensive cases at a fraction of the cost. Proven Drop Defense: Handled initial drops smoothly with great corner protection. Cons: Unproven Long-Term Wear: Too early to tell how the TPU border and translucent back will hold up against daily friction and yellowing over time. Final Verdict If you need a reliable, attractive daily case and aren't putting your phone through extreme hazard environments (like heavy construction or intense outdoor sports), this is an absolute winner. I would easily buy this again or pick one up for my kids' phones. Highly recommended for anyone wanting full MagSafe functionality and sleek style on a budget!
