reviews.title: Great reliable case for the price. (2024 update)
reviews.body: Bought this back in August of 2021 and just recently bought a new one after 1 1/2 years. I have a iPhone 12 and suppose to fit the 12 and 12 pro. Went with this case cause i wanted something reliable but not bulky. The case is a nice size, easy to slide in and out my pocket. I’d say it’s a Good size for most people that the phone still feels comfortable in your hand. I was very hesitant about how bulky it would be and wasn’t disappointed. The rubber layer, on the buttons it’s pretty thick and i personally struggled a bit sometimes to get it to work that i was patient enough to wait for it break in that i started to using my nail and ended up digging into the rubber of all buttons and even the socket to switch to vibrate had to dig in there to switch it. Overtime the rubber does start wearing out so dust/dirt will tend to get in between the case and the phone and will potentially scratch the phone as it did to mine. It’s only two small a scratched at the edge of the top of the phone. Also the port protection probably ripped off after about 4-6 months? But that’s due to me using my phone so much and having to charge it and still using it which made it wear out faster so i think for someone who’s not always on there phone it’ll definitely last longer than it did for me. The plastic is good but could be better. If you drop it in the bottom the plastic is the first to take the impact which will probably crack as it did for me on two spot. Can’t recall when the crack by the camera happen as i only recently noticed it when buy this for the second time. The first crack in the bottom corner happened around the 1 year mark but if you look at my photos i can easily pop it back in place and keep using it without issue. There’s also a small thin plastic that goes in front of the port protection that broke off around 6 months of having it. The plastic is pretty durable, you’d really have to put some force on it to dig into the plastic so small scratches are not really a thing to worry about. If your responsible with not dropping your phone, almost any line of work that’s not construction, i definitely suggest this case if you don’t want a bulky case. For those who work in a more active line of work like huge construction job sites, i recommend upgrading to “DEFENDER” series case. Those are the cases my job has on our work phones and they’re pretty bulky. If you’re someone who’s slightly clumsy, i suggest this case. Overall a great case if you want something reliable, looks great and isn’t bulky. This was based off my experience and other will have their own that probably won’t align with mine. I looked at the reviews before buying it the first time and some people broke it within 3 months from what i recall. it still depends how active your are and what environment your in. If your a office worker, this case will most likely last you a few years compares to someone who’s in a environment that can get pretty filthy and is fast pace. It also depends on how you take care of you things. It’s going to happen to everyone at some point so if you really want more protection with sacrifice of it’s look and size, i suggest upgrade to the defender series or get two cases and swap them for work and off work. Silly but it’s an investment on saving your self the hassle of having to fix a phone or a get a new phone. Update May 2024: Recently had to replace my case again this time it was pretty beat up. Same broken spots as before. Lasted me a good year and honestly could’ve gone longer but looked too messy to be carrying around. I still give this case 5/5 stars. I drive for work and visited construction sites and move heavy equipment and often have my phone on me and risk dropping it a lot. Luckily I’m not clumsy but have dropped it from inside the truck on to the floor outside a couple of times. Maybe like a 4ft drop? Takes the impact no problem, i don’t drop my phone to often and even so i don’t walk around carelessly thinking this case is going to protect it. Even with a bulkier case, it’s important to remember phones still can have internal damage so don’t expect it to completely protect your phone. At the end of the day you are your phones best protection. As i mentioned i recently upgraded cases and did not purchase this case again. Reason being that I’m pretty good with not dropping my phone and this is a bit too bulky to support wireless battery back charging. As i bought a wireless battery pack and could only use it if i remove the case which then I’d have to carry separately in my pocket. It works with a wireless desk charger, just have to position it right. Not sure about other types of wireless desk chargers but the one i have at home definitely needs to be positioned correctly to pick it up. I still recommend this case for anyone looking for extra protection but something not to bulky. I have changed to the “jetech” magnetic case. its a very thin case and will eventually make a review on that.

reviews.title: Slim and reliable iPhone case with good protection
reviews.body: I’m very happy with the ESR iPhone 14 Pro Case. It has a clean design, feels durable, and provides good protection while keeping the phone slim. I like that it supports MagSafe, making it easy to use with my MagSafe accessories and chargers. The clear black design also looks great because it lets the original iPhone design show while still adding protection. The case feels sturdy without adding too much bulk. Pros: Slim and lightweight design Good protection for everyday use MagSafe compatibility works well Clear design looks great Durable build quality Comfortable grip Cons: No major issues so far Overall, this is a great iPhone case for anyone looking for a balance between protection and a slim design. It feels high quality, works well with MagSafe accessories, and keeps my phone protected without making it bulky.

reviews.title: Legit Military-Grade protection without the "Brick" feel!
reviews.body: If you’re tired of cases that claim to be "tough" but feel like cheap plastic, or "rugged" cases that make your phone too big to fit in a pocket, the ESR Military-Grade Shockproof Case is the upgrade you’ve been looking for. I’ve tested a lot of MagSafe cases, and this one feels like it was engineered, not just manufactured. Protection That Isn’t Just Marketing The first thing you notice is the Air-Guard corners. They aren’t just decorative; they create a visible cushion that actually absorbs impact. I’ve already had one "heart-stop" moment where my phone slid off a high counter onto a tile floor, and it literally bounced. Not a scratch on the phone or the case. The "Military-Grade" label actually feels earned here. The MagSafe Connection (HaloLock) ESR’s magnets (they call it HaloLock) are notoriously strong—often stronger than the official Apple cases. • The "Snap": When you bring it near a charger or car mount, it grabs hold with a very secure click. • Reliability: I use a heavy MagSafe power bank and a wallet attachment; neither budge even when I’m walking or the car hits a bump. It’s rated for 1,500g of holding force, and you can definitely feel that extra "tug." Design & Utility Depending on the model you get, many of these come with the Stash Stand around the camera. This is a game-changer: • It protects the lenses when closed. • It’s made of a high-quality zinc alloy that doesn't feel flimsy. • It works in both portrait (for scrolling/FaceTime) and landscape (for videos) without blocking the MagSafe ring. The Build Quality The back is a hard, scratch-resistant polycarbonate that stays clear much longer than cheap TPU. The sides have a nice matte grip that prevents that "slippery soap" feeling. It adds just enough "heft" to make the phone feel protected without doubling its thickness. Pros: • Superior Magnets: Best-in-class MagSafe strength. • Corner Protection: Air-Guard tech is legit for drop safety. • Tactile Buttons: They remain clicky and responsive, not mushy. • Raised Edges: Significant lip around the screen and camera for "table-top" protection. Cons: • Tight Fit: It’s a very snug fit, so it takes a little effort to get the phone out if you swap cases often (but that’s also why it’s so protective!). Final Verdict: This is the "Goldilocks" of cases—it’s tougher than a standard clear case but way sleeker than a traditional bulky rugged case. If you value your phone's trade-in value and use MagSafe accessories daily, this is an absolute no-brainer. 5/5 Stars.

title: OtterBox iPhone 8/7 & SE (3rd/2nd Gen) Commuter Series Case - Black

reviews.title: Amazing (typical) Otterbox performance
reviews.body: I work in trades so I wanted something that would protect my phone but not make it feel like I have a scrap 2x8 in my pocket. Also being in trades it has gone through its fair share of abuse and after having this for a little over a year now the only damage I can report is some cosmetic scratches, dings, a small non important piece of plastic as well as the rubber flap that goes over the charging port ripped off (though I'm to blame on most of that...). Long story short I told myself I would get a new phone when my current iPhone 8 dies. In desperate attempts to speed that up without being too blatant (as I've now had this phone for easily 6-7 years now and I'm ready for a new one) I've thrown this thing across rooms, out of second story windows, off roofs and ladders, etc. I think you get the point... Fortunately (or unfortunately) it has protected my phone through it all. The only things I have against it though is that the opening for the charger does give some trouble to the thicker aftermarket chargers (e.g. I have a Ryobi lightning charger that's thicker to supposedly protect it but it still charges with some "convincing"). In an attempt to handle that I ripped off that rubber flap that I mentioned before (no, that solved nothing but I felt better in the end). NOTE: It actually was starting to rip off slowly through use about 6 months in but I just expedited that process. The other point is that after a year of use (and abuse) its texture has gone pretty smooth so the grip isn't anything to marvel at but it does its job. I somewhat handled this by cutting a bunch of grooves with a utility knife but I can understand others not wanting to follow suit. TL;DR - Doesn't impede in screen or button usage. Great protection in a smaller and sleek design. May have some problems with charger clearance if you have really bulky aftermarket chargers. Notes for the picture: Mostly here to show the missing rubber flap that would usually cover the charging port. There was a think plastic piece that would go right below it and create a hole that the flap would fit into but that broke off as well. Most damage is through my abuse (for example the bottom left corner) but for the most part it's still in working condition. You can also see my "custom texturing job" I did on the back lol. Does it look pretty? No. Is that my fault? Absolutely.

reviews.title: Great, not too bulky, yet very protective case - Just avoid Amazon shipping!!
reviews.body: For the money especially, this is a great case. Unlike the defender series or others like it this doesn’t have the P.I.T.A. two-sided case that locks together and is difficult to remove. Some reviews say it’s hard to put on, they’re clearly doing it wrong as it’s VERY easy. It’s a 2 part design, so while it comes together, it’s key to put the rubber part on the phone before snapping the hard plastic cover in place. No doubt people saying it’s a tight fit tried both at once. That’s more difficult and puts strain on the plastic. I’m the worst about dropping my phone. ai must have dropped it (iphone 8) at least 75-100 times minimum, and I don’t even worry about breaking anything anymore. The lip of it sticks out just enough to protect the screen, and the dual layering is ultra shock absorbent. It’s also pretty thin considering the amount of protection. I gave a 4 for durability and sturdiness as over time the outer plastic snapped on me and the inner rubber cover has a few worn areas, but at $20, replacing wasn’t particularly bothersome and it certainly lasted a good 6-9 months of hard use - better the case than my screen! Still a 5 in total as sometimes something has to break, and so perhaps it’s better being a little less sturdy. To anyone asking, of course it fits a 7, there is no big difference in the shape of 8 and 7. Idk if the lip would protect the plus as well since the screen is bigger, but that’s an overall risk the Plus phones have. Finally, I wish I could rate Amazon delivery separately. If you live in a city apartment building or even a house and won’t be home, they don’t bother reading delivery instructions (which always has info to access my mail room / lobby). It’s probably Amazon’s fault for having impossible schedules, but the drivers will *sometimes* try to buzz once (not always), then ignore the delivery instructions and leave the box outside if you’re not home or can’t answer. When I wondered where my replacement case was, a quick review showed some lady walking by, noticing the pile of boxes left, and took a couple small packages on top before walking quickly off, one of course was mine. Almost more infuriatingly, customer service put it down to “delivery error” and said they’d blame the shipper.. yet Amazon is the shipper. So they blame themselves and do nothing to fix it, and outsourced customer service means people that can only answer a few basic questions before they get confused and off script. This time they promised me they were working with delivery drivers to fix the problem, yet it’s been happening for at least 2 years. If my neighbors didn’t look out for each other and bring in anything left outside, much more would have been stolen by now. And still they have my sensitive door access info, which I don’t give out lightly.. and never use it. How it’s cheaper to replace these items than just fix the problem is beyond me. My advice, if 1-day delivery is an option, is to buy it alone so as not to make the $35 minimum and let UPS handle it, since their drivers would never leave packages out on a city street (they also take note of info like door codes, how crazy). It’s to the point where if I see Amazon shipping I dread it and have to try to stay home. At the very least a notification saying the package is outside for anyone to take would be a start. That’s enough about Amazon shipping, just on my mind since the first order got stolen. UPS safely brought the replacement though

reviews.title: Just what I wanted!

reviews.title: Great case, but watch your charging cable.
reviews.body: I see the case has undergone a slight re-design since my original one. It come with in soft inner rubber shell with an outer hard rubber shell. I guess that's to better absorb impact. The original one they were molded together. Now the inner shell appears to be removeable. That said, it seems to be well made. It's a tight fit to get the phone in. The buttons line-up where they should, so they are functional. Someone mentioned in another review that they liked the dust cover for the charging port. For me, it's a a love/hate relationship. I love the idea of keeping it closed when not charging, but since the "hinge" part of the flap has a strong reflex to close, I have to keep my phone motionless while charging or the pressure the lid has will cause the cord to pop-out just enough to stop charging without visual queue to know it happened. I actually get better results on a cheaper and thinner cord, but then it wears out the cord faster. So, for sturdiness, I give this 5 stars. But overall, due the the aforementioned charging issue, I give it 4 stars. Also, the outer case is a bit slippery, I wish it had better hand grip material, but workable if you know that.

reviews.title: Amazing protection for the price! Only replacing to upgrade to MagSafe.
reviews.body: If you are looking for a good case that completely surrounds your device, look no further! I bought this as an Otterbox style (thought not fully waterproof) protective case for my iPhone 14. It’s lasted me quite well, but wasn’t a MagSafe version. (That is literally my only complaint.) It meets my needs and is far more capable than the price would indicate. So much so that I am upgrading to a MagSafe version in a slightly different color without hesitation or regret! The glass screen protector has maintained superb clarity despite’s bumps, drops, spills, and even flinging my phone down a hill (on accident). I think the hilly road surface would have caused more harm, but just 2 1/4” scratches resulted. The clarity and usefulness were not affected, and I have to shine a light across the screen to even spot where the damage happened. Because of the double layered edges, this gives really good shock and impact protection. Drops only concrete, asphalt, and tile have cause zero damage to the case or phone. The thicker edges help my grip and make this easier to hold onto, but I have large hands. Despite that this still fits neatly into a belt holster without issue. The case seals well enough, but at the same time it’s not hard to open to clear a speck of dust or drop of moisture off the screen before resealing it. I have dropped my phone into a running shower for almost zero moisture getting into the case. I highly recommend this case as someone who isn’t gentle and often a klutz while handling my electronics.

reviews.body: I really like this phone case! It fits my phone perfectly and feels sturdy and well-made. The design is simple and stylish, and it provides good protection without being too bulky. reviews.body: 📦 Mon premier coup d’œil : Au déballage, je suis agréablement surpris par le packaging très classe. Et une fois installées, ces 2 parties tiennent bien et ne se désolidarisent pas. Le verre trempé qui se met sur les lentilles de la caméra arrière tient bien aussi et il est suffisamment protecteur. Je suis satisfait par la robustesse de ce modèle et par le fait qu'il laisse bien entrevoir le téléphone. 📊 Mon verdict : ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ 5 étoiles pour ce kit qui protège intégralement l'Iphone 15 Pro Max.

title: OtterBox iPhone 13 (ONLY) Commuter Series Case - Black, Slim & Tough, Pocket-Friendly, with Port Protection

reviews.title: Slim but tough OtterBox case that balances protection and pocket comfort
reviews.body: The OtterBox Commuter Series for the iPhone 13 is a great option if you want reliable protection without the bulk of heavier rugged cases. The two-piece design combines a shock-absorbing inner layer with a tougher outer shell, which helps protect the phone from drops and everyday bumps while still keeping the case relatively slim. It slides easily into pockets and feels comfortable to hold. The raised edges around the screen and camera provide extra protection when placing the phone on flat surfaces. The port covers are also a nice feature since they help keep dust and debris out of the charging port. Buttons remain responsive and easy to press, and the case fits the phone snugly without shifting. The texture along the sides adds a bit of grip, which makes the phone feel more secure in hand compared to smoother cases. One helpful tip is to press around all edges of the case after installation to make sure both layers snap together securely. It’s also useful to occasionally open the port cover and clean out any lint buildup to keep charging connections clear. Overall, this is a durable and well-designed case that offers strong everyday protection while staying slim enough for comfortable daily use.

reviews.title: Fits great!

The buttons are still easy to press, the grip feels secure, and I appreciate the port covers that help keep lint out. I’ve already dropped my phone a couple of times, and not even a scratch. Great material, color and appearance! Sometimes paying a little more upfront saves you from replacing a phone later.

title: ESR for iPhone 15 Pro Case for MagSafe, Anti-Yellowing, Clear

reviews.title: Slim and reliable iPhone case with good protection
reviews.body: I’m very happy with the ESR iPhone 14 Pro Case. It has a clean design, feels durable, and provides good protection while keeping the phone slim. I like that it supports MagSafe, making it easy to use with my MagSafe accessories and chargers. The clear black design also looks great because it lets the original iPhone design show while still adding protection. The case feels sturdy without adding too much bulk. Pros: Slim and lightweight design Good protection for everyday use MagSafe compatibility works well Clear design looks great Durable build quality Comfortable grip Cons: No major issues so far Overall, this is a great iPhone case for anyone looking for a balance between protection and a slim design. It feels high quality, works well with MagSafe accessories, and keeps my phone protected without making it bulky.

reviews.title: Legit Military-Grade protection without the "Brick" feel!
reviews.body: If you’re tired of cases that claim to be "tough" but feel like cheap plastic, or "rugged" cases that make your phone too big to fit in a pocket, the ESR Military-Grade Shockproof Case is the upgrade you’ve been looking for. I’ve tested a lot of MagSafe cases, and this one feels like it was engineered, not just manufactured. Protection That Isn’t Just Marketing The first thing you notice is the Air-Guard corners. They aren’t just decorative; they create a visible cushion that actually absorbs impact. I’ve already had one "heart-stop" moment where my phone slid off a high counter onto a tile floor, and it literally bounced. Not a scratch on the phone or the case. The "Military-Grade" label actually feels earned here. The MagSafe Connection (HaloLock) ESR’s magnets (they call it HaloLock) are notoriously strong—often stronger than the official Apple cases. • The "Snap": When you bring it near a charger or car mount, it grabs hold with a very secure click. • Reliability: I use a heavy MagSafe power bank and a wallet attachment; neither budge even when I’m walking or the car hits a bump. It’s rated for 1,500g of holding force, and you can definitely feel that extra "tug." Design & Utility Depending on the model you get, many of these come with the Stash Stand around the camera. This is a game-changer: • It protects the lenses when closed. • It’s made of a high-quality zinc alloy that doesn't feel flimsy. • It works in both portrait (for scrolling/FaceTime) and landscape (for videos) without blocking the MagSafe ring. The Build Quality The back is a hard, scratch-resistant polycarbonate that stays clear much longer than cheap TPU. The sides have a nice matte grip that prevents that "slippery soap" feeling. It adds just enough "heft" to make the phone feel protected without doubling its thickness. Pros: • Superior Magnets: Best-in-class MagSafe strength. • Corner Protection: Air-Guard tech is legit for drop safety. • Tactile Buttons: They remain clicky and responsive, not mushy. • Raised Edges: Significant lip around the screen and camera for "table-top" protection. Cons: • Tight Fit: It’s a very snug fit, so it takes a little effort to get the phone out if you swap cases often (but that’s also why it’s so protective!). Final Verdict: This is the "Goldilocks" of cases—it’s tougher than a standard clear case but way sleeker than a traditional bulky rugged case. If you value your phone's trade-in value and use MagSafe accessories daily, this is an absolute no-brainer. 5/5 Stars.

reviews.title: Lasted two years before it started falling apart
reviews.body: I’m a happy camper when it comes to this case. I had my old one for two years before the plastic started to fall apart. Initially, I got a different case for five dollars that even came with a screen protector and I thought to myself this is such a great deal, when I tried it the magnetic component of the case failed miserably so I returned it and got this case again for about $13 which is the same price I paid for this case two years ago. You get what you pay for. This is a great case that served me for two years and the magnetic component of it is very strong. In the pictures you can see the two years old case next to the brand new one.

reviews.title: Great phone case option, just keep in mind that it does yellow over time.
reviews.body: Firstly, I love the feel of this case, it's honestly a case I continue to buy and buy again. Since it perfectly fits my iPhone 15 plus, the installation is easy. This particular model doesn't have a kickstand, but I'm okay with that since I have a MagSafe pop socket. Did I mention MagSafe? I LOVE MagSafe compatible phone cases, it makes accessories easier to use, especially since I don't have to take the case off and on again. My phones fallen a multitude of times, and hasn't had any damage to the body of the phone. In terms of overall protection, screen protection is sound, especially from someone like me who doesn't use a phone screen! My only flaw with this however, is that the case does yellow, as I've mentioned this is the case I continue to "buy and buy" over again and again...

reviews.title: Quality case that saves phone every time
reviews.body: Amazing quality case at a great price! Super easy to install, and it helps protect the screen and body of the phone very well. Sleek design and it’s been dropped numerous times and always saved the phone! The clear plastic does eventually turn yellow, but that’s only because I rarely clean it/use it all the time, and even then, it takes a long time to show wear. Happy with quality and material!

reviews.title: Handy dandy charger!
reviews.body: This thing is compact, charges quickly, and manages all three devices well. Easy to use, great for traveling. Love it.

reviews.title: Sleek, great looking wireless charger.
reviews.body: Super sleek and compact, love that it folds to make it even less noticeable. Charges my watch, airpods and iphone Pro max at a good speed. Magnet is strong for the phone. Cannot be knocked off the charger easily. Would highly recommend this for anyone who is looking to consolidate chargers.

reviews.title: One Charger, Three Devices — Love It!
reviews.body: I really like this charger. I can charge my iPhone 17 Pro Max, Apple Watch, and AirPods all at the same time without having three different chargers taking up space. It’s compact and doesn’t take up much room on my nightstand, which is a big plus for me. I also love that it folds up so small. It’s easy to throw in my bag when I travel and I only need to bring one charger for all three devices. So far, I’m very happy with it.

reviews.title: Great charger, but weak MagSafe magnets hold it back
reviews.body: This Belkin charger is a great product overall, but it has one significant drawback that I don’t think should be overlooked. First, the positives: my Apple Watch Ultra 3 fast charges as advertised, and so does my iPhone. The charger itself is lightweight and compact, and it comes with a 45W charging brick and a nice rubber-overmolded cable that feels high quality. From a charging and build-quality standpoint, I’m very happy with it. Unfortunately, there’s one issue I can’t get past: the magnetic strength of the MagSafe phone mount. The magnets simply don’t feel strong enough. It doesn’t take much of a bump to knock the phone off the charger, and that’s something I think potential buyers should be aware of. I believe the weaker magnets may actually be an intentional design decision. Because the charger itself is so lightweight, stronger magnets could cause you to lift the entire charger when trying to remove your phone. I can understand the reasoning behind that tradeoff, but I still think the magnetic hold is too weak in practice. Belkin appears to have tried to compensate for this by adding a silicone surface to the charging area to provide additional grip against the back of the phone. Unfortunately, it doesn’t provide enough friction to make up for the weaker magnets. Personally, I would have preferred a heavier base combined with stronger magnets, even if it added some weight to the product. If Belkin had addressed this, I genuinely think this would be a 10/10 charger. As it stands, I’d give it a 7/10. The charging performance is excellent, the included 45W power adapter and cable are nice, and the overall design is very good. The weak magnetic hold is really the only thing keeping me from loving it. You may think this won’t bother you, but I would seriously consider it before buying. A surprisingly light bump can cause the phone to fall off the charger, and for something you may use every day for years, that matters. If you’re comparing this with the Anker Prime, which costs roughly $30–$40 more, the additional cost may be worth considering if it provides a more secure magnetic connection. Over several years of daily use, $30–$40 isn’t much of a premium to avoid an annoyance you’ll potentially deal with every day.

reviews.title: Compact in Size, Fast Charging, Saves Space and Great for Travel
reviews.body: I love this 3 in 1 charger! Say goodbye to all of the charging cords! It is small and compact. I bought the white one to match my furniture. My Apple Watch, AirPods Pro and iPhone charge quickly. The iPhone phone will fast charge to 50% in about 1/2 hour. The watch will fully charge in a similar amount of time. I love that the charger is compact and folds up for travel. The other Belkin 3 in 1 charger that I have is a side by side and takes up a lot of space. With this new design the old charger has been relegated to the guest bedroom.

reviews.title: Works well with iPhone 17 and Apple Watch 11
reviews.body: Quickly charges both my iPhone 17 and Apple Watch 11 simultaneously. Have not tried Apply EarPods charging so I cannot comment on that feature. The small charger footprint and single charge cable have significantly reduced the clutter associated with multiple charge cables on the table. Completely satisfied with this purchase!

reviews.title: Belkin Magsafe Charger
reviews.body: Great charging, sleek profile, strong magnetic, quick charging, easy to use, and it’s been durable the past year so far. Definitely would try it before knocking it.

reviews.title: Nice looking charger with very annoying quirks/bugs
reviews.body: It's cool that this is the "official" charging dock that Apple endorses. When it works, it works well and it feels quality, with all hinges feeling sturdy. Time will tell after folding it hundreds of times whether the hinges will hold up, but I feel optimistic. This is one of the few options you have unfortunately for 25W charging if you have a newer iPhone, as they tend to be really expensive. Watch charging works fine and reasonably well, but it seems like the pad doesn't shut off and the watch continues to get warmer as it sits fully charged. Phone charging doesn't seem to have this issue, but it might be whatever cooling tech they have keeping it room temp-ish. The part I hate the most about it is the airpod charging area. It has an annoyingly bright white LED that lights up when you put it on the charger, and it takes forever to start charging, if it even does that. I've woken up contless times to my airpods not having charged at all, even though I put it down as correctly as possible. Even when I move it back and forth on the charger it takes forever to finally register the airpods are on there and frankly it's a really poorly functioning charger that tarnishes an otherwise decent dock. Even when it does successfully charge, it does the same thing where the charger doesn't shut off after fully charging and the airpods are really warm when I pick the case up. All in all, a decent charger but don't expect the airpods charger pad to work well. Frankly, I expected better for almost $100 and I'm pretty disappointing overall.

title: Belkin Qi2 15W Wireless Fast Charging Station, 3 in 1 iPhone Charger

reviews.title: Great Charging Stand
reviews.body: I literally cannot complain. It does everything it advertises. The magnet holds up with a MagSafe case on my phone, allowing me to finally use nightstand mode which is awesome. Let’s my charge my AirPods and Apple Watch at the same time as my phone, so everything is ready to go in the morning. Have not experienced any overheating of any device, I find my watch is actually cooler than when I used the regular wired charger for it. It folds up for easy travel carry, easy to set up and use, and it looks good too. Charging seems like good speed, honestly usually only charge at night and even a 5 hour rest gets everything at full charge. Great charger, highly recommend, and it looks pretty good too, folded or unfurled.

reviews.title: Amazing Travel Charger for Apple Products
reviews.body: The Belkin MagSafe Charger 3-in-1 is the perfect travel charger. It is able to charge your iPhone, Air Pods, and Apple Watch simultaneously. The magnet strength is great. You don't have to worry that your phone will fall off the charger, unless you give it a good knock. It folds down nicely which makes it super easy to pack, and the base is nice and sturdy. I own two of these, both for over 6 months, and they work flawlessly with the range of Apple products. I think this is a really good value for the money, and certainly beats bringing multiple chargers and/or cables for your devices. Highly recommended if you are part of the Apple ecosystem.

reviews.title: Broke within 2 months
reviews.body: I was happy with this charger at first, but it completely stopped working after just two months. I gave it the benefit of the doubt and replaced the cord, assuming that was the culprit—but nope, all three charging platforms are dead. For what this costs, I expected it to last a lot longer than that.

reviews.title: Great Materials, Strong Magnetic connection. Quick Charge
reviews.body: Great Charger, Strong Magnetic connection, Sleek appearance, takes up little space, great value.

reviews.title: Three in One
reviews.body: This charger is just what I was looking for. The size is perfect for my desk and doesn’t take up too much space. I can charge my phone, watch and earbuds all at once, eliminating the need for extra cables. It is sturdy and in my opinion reasonably priced for what it does. I am very pleased with this purchase.

reviews.title: More power
reviews.body: This was able to charge my iPhone and my Apple Watch without it taking forever. Had purchased another charger, had to send it back. Wasn’t enough power to charge watch this works.

reviews.title: Great Until It Wasn’t
reviews.body: Update 2: This charger failed again and again it was during an international trip. The same story. Before travelling I had a chat session with Belkin to confirm (or not) that this will work out of the US. I was assured it would. It didn't. That was in March. reviews.title: Good charger - Gets a bit warm at Max Output - Extremely Flexible All in One Travel Brick
reviews.body: This is a handy charger to have around for traveling as it can power up a pretty decent laptop and or your cellphone and or your Bluetooth earbuds all at once. It gets a little warm when you start asking it to output max power for sustained times but that's sort of to be expected. I'm still working on getting a better test setup to measure power from the wall but my current gear has this pulling 108w from the wall to deliver 93w to the device, this means there's about 15w of heat being generated and that helps explain the 120f temps this will reach when pushed hard. I let me load test run for a good long time and there were no thermal events that caused it to throttle power or just cut off so while it gets warm it seems well equipped to deal with the heat. Most laptops aren't going to need a full 100w and this thing would barely break a sweat providing the 20-30w all my laptops need under even heavy load. The real selling point for this though is the ability to charge a laptop while at the same time having two more ports available for charging the other stuff we all have with us now. Most chargers that can do laptops can only do a single thing so this does help justify the cost, but it is still cheaper to just buy three different USB-C chargers vs this single one. Hopefully this drops down from the current $40 price tag into a more reasonable $30ish range soon. It's a good charger at an okay price right now and for a lot of people that's going to be good enough.

reviews.title: My favorite WeGear charger design so far—three front-facing ports and genuinely fast charging
reviews.body: I now own several WeGear fast chargers in different sizes and configurations, including compact 45W single-port chargers, this 100W three-port model and a larger 140W multi-port charger with an illuminated wattage display. All of them have worked extremely well, but this may be my favorite overall form factor. It has two USB-C ports and one USB-A port, all positioned conveniently on the front. On this model, either USB-C port can deliver up to 100W when used alone, while the USB-A port supports up to 22.5W. When several devices are connected simultaneously, the available 100W is intelligently divided among them. I particularly appreciate the front-facing ports. My 140W WeGear charger has a display that briefly shows the exact wattage being drawn through each port, which is useful and interesting. However, its charging ports are underneath. Because most wall outlets are too low for me to see the bottom of the charger, connecting a cable after it is already plugged in becomes an exercise in playing Braille. I generally have to attach the cables first and then plug the entire charger into the wall. Consequently, I use that model as a stationary charging station with USB-A and USB-C cables permanently attached. With this one, I can leave the cables elsewhere and easily plug in whichever one I need while the charger remains in the outlet. That sounds like a small distinction, but in daily use it makes this design considerably more convenient. I tested this 100W charger directly against my 45W and 140W WeGear chargers using the same high-speed cable and the same Samsung smartphones. The estimated charging time was identical with all three. That is exactly what should happen: a higher-capacity charger cannot force a phone to accept more wattage than the phone is designed to draw. My smartphones are already receiving their maximum supported charging rate from each of these chargers, so moving from 45W to 100W or 140W does not make an individual phone charge any faster. The higher total capacity becomes useful when charging several devices at once or when powering something more demanding, such as a compatible laptop. For my everyday needs, the three ports provide an excellent balance between capacity and convenience. I use USB-C rechargeable devices constantly, including two smartphones, dog e-collars, flashlights and countless other household items. It seems that nearly everything now comes with a rechargeable battery, which is convenient until half the house simultaneously announces that it is running out of power. I now keep WeGear chargers distributed throughout my home so I can quickly recharge something wherever I happen to be. The sleek black housing is attractive, and the slim GaN design and folding electrical prongs make this charger compact enough to carry in a purse, backpack or laptop bag. The listing also specifies protection against overheating, overvoltage, overcurrent and short circuits. Mine has remained reliable without excessive heat, overcharging or any other problems. A suitably rated high-speed cable is essential. A charger can only perform as well as the cable connecting it to the device, and the listing notes that reaching the full 100W requires a compatible 5A cable. I already own several high-speed WeGear cables, and they have consistently delivered true fast charging. After years of owning chargers that claimed to be “fast” but were anything but, I’m now thoroughly spoiled. These WeGear chargers reduce charging time dramatically compared with my older equipment, and every model I’ve tested has performed reliably. This 100W three-port version combines the best features for my purposes: multiple ports, true fast charging, easy front access, a compact profile and enough total capacity for several devices. Five stars.

reviews.title: A compact 100W charger that actually charges my MacBook Pro fast
reviews.body: I have been testing this Wegear 100W charger for a couple of weeks, mostly with my MacBook Pro and a few other USB PD devices like cameras. Here are my thoughts. The first thing I noticed is how small this charger is. It is smaller than the 140W charger that came with my MacBook Pro, which made it an easy swap for travel and for keeping on my desk without taking up much space. When I plug in my MacBook Pro, it charges quickly, close to how fast the original 140W charger does. The battery went from low to full in a short amount of time, right around what I expect from the stock charger. One thing to note is that this unit runs hotter than the Apple charger while it is powering the laptop. That makes sense since the MacBook Pro normally uses a 140W supply, so this 100W unit is likely working near its top capacity to keep up. There is no display or indicator on the charger to show exact wattage, so I could not confirm the exact output, but the charging speed and battery results told me it was doing its job well. Beyond the laptop, I tried this charger with a few other devices that use USB PD, including a camera. USB PD is not a simple on and off power flow. The charger and the device go through a negotiation process to figure out a voltage and current level that works safely for that device. I have used other chargers in the past that could not complete this negotiation with certain devices and simply would not power them. This charger has not had that problem with anything I connected so far, which says something about how well it handles different device types. For anyone wondering about the heat, this seems to be normal behavior for GaN chargers running near their max output rather than a sign of a problem. Since it is not sending a constant fixed wattage but adjusting based on what the connected device needs, some warmth during heavier charging sessions like a laptop is expected. If you need a compact charger that can genuinely keep up with a power hungry laptop while also handling phones, tablets, and other PD devices, this one has worked well for me so far. Just keep in mind it will get warm during heavier use, so give it some airflow rather than tucking it under a pillow or blanket while it works.

reviews.title: Awesome
reviews.body: The Good True High-Speed: Powers a dead smartphone to 50% in under fifteen minutes.Smart Power Sharing: Intelligently splits wattage across multiple devices without dropping connections.Ultra-Compact: Uses GaN technology to pack massive power into a tiny, travel-friendly footprint.Secure Fit: Rigid folding prongs snap firmly into place and do not sag out of loose wall outlets. The Bad Blocks Adjacent Plugs: The wider body shape can slightly overlap tight power strips.LED Is Too Bright: The blue indicator light glows vividly in a pitch-black bedroom at night. Full Breakdown I have gone through dozens of cheap wall bricks over the years, most of which claim to feature "fast charging" but fail miserably the moment you plug in a second device. I bought this premium GaN charger to streamline my travel kit and act as a reliable daily hub for my power-hungry gear. After a month of heavy use, it has proven to be an absolute powerhouse that lives up to every bit of its marketing. The charging speed is nothing short of incredible. When using a single port, it effortlessly juices up my laptop at maximum speed, matching the performance of the bulky OEM brick it replaced. The internal chip is exceptionally smart; when I add my phone and tablet into the other ports, it doesn't constantly reset the connection or cut the power like cheaper alternatives do. It smoothly reallocates the wattage so that every plugged-in device gets the optimal charge safely and quickly. The build quality also justifies the premium price tag. Thanks to the Gallium Nitride design, the charger is remarkably small—roughly half the size of standard laptop bricks. It easily slides into a pocket or a small tech pouch. It also runs incredibly cool, staying barely warm even when working under a full load for hours. The folding prongs feel robust and don't collapse when you try to push the brick into a stiff outlet. If you are tired of carrying a tangled mess of slow chargers and want one definitive upgrade to rule them all, this is it.

reviews.title: Fast charging, Big Power, multi device
reviews.body: Wegear 100 W GaN USB C charger block powers up my devices faster than I've ever seen! I can have multiple devices plugged in and all charging at the same time! I have tried power blocks that say they are higher power and faster charging but they always seem to give me trouble. That has not always been the case with other chargers. I carefully tried new cords and older cords with my newest smartphones and some that were older and having trouble receiving a charge, and continuing to charge. The newest cords worked instantly, my phone lit up with super fast charging or turbocharging with greatly reduced times showing for full charge. I carefully date and label my cords so I don't get them mixed up with older chords that just don't seem to work unless plugged into a much older lower power charging device. Some of my oldest smartphones that were difficult to charge are now useful again as backup cameras, audio players, streaming devices at home so my newest devices can be fully charged when I leave for the day. The charger block does get noticeably warm when charging three devices at the same time, so I am careful to unplug it when not in use. Two USB C connection s are color coded red which indicates high power and the USB a connection is color coded black. I notice when I plug in a 2nd or 3rd device to charge, the other items charging will flash and ring as if the power was interrupted briefly then restored. This Wegear charger keeps charging all three devices--most other chargers seem to fail or only allow one item to charge at a time. If I could give this item Six Stars, I would! Exceeding my expectations!! ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

reviews.title: Great charger that can be brought along for the trip.
reviews.body: I was skeptical that something this slim could pack 100 watts, but the wegear charger proved me wrong within the first use. It charges my devices noticeably faster than the stock brick that came with my laptop, and it does so without turning into a hand warmer in the process. Even after an hour of charging my laptop and phone simultaneously, the block stays cool to the touch, which says a lot about the GaN tech doing its job properly. The three ports have been a genuine convenience upgrade for my daily routine. I can charge my laptop, phone, and a set of earbuds all at once without hunting for an outlet or unplugging one device to power another. It has enough output to actually run my laptop during use, not just trickle charge it, which is not something I can say about every "laptop compatible" charger I have tried in the past. What really sold me, though, is the folding plug design. I travel often for work, and chargers with rigid prongs are notorious for either stabbing through the lining of my bag or snapping off entirely. This one folds flat and slides into a laptop sleeve or side pocket without any fuss. Between the speed, the multi device support, and the travel friendly build, this has quickly become the only charger I bother packing.

It easily doubles my gaming time, turning the Ally into a truly portable handheld instead of something that constantly needs to be plugged in. The 100W output is no joke — it keeps up with demanding devices without throttling, and fast charging works exactly as advertised. I can game while charging without noticeable slowdown or excessive heat. The TFT smart display is also a great touch, giving clear info on power usage and remaining battery, which is very helpful. Build quality feels premium, it’s compact for its power capacity, and having multiple USB-C ports makes it versatile for charging other devices like phones, tablets, or even a laptop. If you own a ROG Ally or any high-power handheld, this power bank is absolutely worth it. Reliable, powerful, and well-designed.

reviews.title: Power bank that actually has power!

reviews.title: Heavy, but powerful charger
reviews.body: This is a somewhat heavy (weighs about a pound), but powerful battery. I don't mind the weight, I expect that from a 20k battery. It feels solid and well built. I like the display and how it shows the negotiated voltage and amps so you can see what it is doing. I also like that it has a trickle charge mode for lower power devices like my watch and earbuds. Most batteries will shut off because there isn't enough of a power draw, in trickle charge mode the battery will not shut off for 3 1/2 hours. Please note that they recommend that you use a minimum 65 watt charger to charge the battery. You can use less power, but the battery will take longer to charge. With the more powerful charger it takes a little over an hour to fully charge. One day my M4 MacBook Air was down to around 25% and my phone was around 40%. I plugged both into the battery at the same time. I charged my phone to 80% and computer to 100% and the battery was down to about 10% remaining charge. The computer was drawing around 60 watts the majority of the time. One thing that has left me curious is that I have yet to see it either receive or draw more than 3 volts @ 20 amps since it says it is capable of 5 volts. Both my charger and computer should be capable of 100 watts, but I also know that devices negotiate with the charger so it doesn't bother me that it is less.

reviews.title: No more fluff in the port excuses
reviews.body: I’ve always found charging my phone overnight a bit annoying – constantly trying to get the cable in the right position, and still waking up with a low battery more often than I should. This MagSafe-style charger has completely removed that hassle. Now it’s just a case of placing the phone down and letting it attach magnetically, which feels a lot more reliable than fiddling with cables in the dark. Since using it, I’ve stopped waking up to a nearly dead phone, which is exactly what I wanted from it. It comes as a simple package with the charger itself, a USB-C cable and a USB-A converter, so you’ve got a bit of flexibility depending on what plug or setup you’re using. The magnetic alignment is strong enough that the phone stays in place easily, even if you move it slightly on the bedside table. What stands out with this set is having two chargers. It makes it easy to keep one at the bedside and the other in another room or take it for travel, so you’re not constantly unplugging and moving things around. It also supports faster wireless charging, so it doesn’t feel slow compared to wired charging overnight, especially when paired with the right adapter. It’s more than enough for overnight use and day-to-day top ups. Case compatibility is decent too. It works through most standard slim cases without issue, but for the best magnetic hold you’ll want a MagSafe-compatible case or one with built-in magnets. Thicker cases do weaken the snap-in feel a bit. Price wise seems to be normal for the price of 2. Overall, it’s a small change that makes a big difference in day-to-day use. No more cable faff, no more guessing angles – just put it down and it charges. Exactly the kind of simple upgrade that makes life easier.

reviews.title: Carga rápida, tamaño mínimo y magnífico precio. Totalmente recomendado
reviews.body: Si estás buscando jubilar los dichosos cables de una vez por todas y te llama la atención el nuevo estándar de carga inalámbrica Qi2 y tienes dispositivos que aceptan la carga inalámbrica, quédate por aquí porque te voy a contar detalladamente mi experiencia real con este pack de 2 cargadores magnéticos. Después de estar trasteando con ellos a diario, usándolos tanto en el escritorio de casa como llevándomelos de viaje, aquí te dejo mi análisis a fondo, sin rodeos, con lo bueno, lo genial y también con esos pequeños detalles que conviene saber antes de lanzarse a por ellos. 📦 ¿Qué nos encontramos en la caja? De primeras, lo mejor de este producto es que es un pack doble. Te vienen dos bases de carga inalámbrica magnética de color violeta oscuro (tampoco es demasiado oscuro). Visualmente llaman la atención ya que tienen un perfil ultra delgado (apenas unos 5 milímetros de grosor) y pesan poquísimo (unos 54 gramos). El chasis es metálico, lo que le da un toque premium muy limpio, y el cable viene integrado con conector USB-C y un acabado trenzado que se nota bastante resistente al trote diario (dobleces, tirones en la mochila, etc.). ⚠️ Un detalle crucial de inicio: El pack no incluye los adaptadores de pared (los enchufes). En la caja solo vienen las dos bases con sus cables. ⚡ Rendimiento y Velocidad: ¿De verdad carga a 25W? Aquí hay que ponerse un poco técnicos, pero de forma sencilla. Estos cargadores cuentan con la nueva certificación Qi2 / Qi2.2, que es básicamente la evolución universal del sistema MagSafe de Apple. Promete hasta 25W de potencia máxima. En el día a día, con los teléfonos compatibles más recientes, la velocidad se nota un montón. En apenas 30 minutos te puede plantar la batería en torno al 50%, siendo notablemente más rápido que las típicas bases inalámbricas antiguas de 15W. Pero ojo, que aquí viene el "truco" de la potencia: 1. El enchufe importa: Para exprimir esos 25W de punta, necesitas conectar la base a un adaptador de pared de 30W o superior con salida de 12V (el típico cargador rápido potente que uses para la tablet o el portátil). Si lo conectas a un enchufe antiguo de menos de 20W, la velocidad caerá en picado. 2. Carga desde el portátil: Si eres de los que, como yo, viaja mucho y conecta la base directamente al puerto USB-C de tu ordenador portátil en una reunión o cafetería, la potencia real se verá limitada por la del ordenador (suele dar entre 10W y 15W). Sigue siendo comodísimo para mantener el móvil con energía mientras trabajas, pero no irá a su velocidad punta. 🧲 El imán y el ajuste magnético: El cargador lleva internamente imanes de neodimio N52. En dispositivos de la manzana o teléfonos preparados nativamente para alineación magnética, la experiencia es súper cómoda: acercas el teléfono por la parte trasera, se "pega" solo en la posición exacta milimétrica y empieza a cargar. Es ideal para la mesita de noche porque no tienes que andar tanteando a oscuras a ver si ha encajado en la bobina. Dado que es mucho más pequeño (aproximadamente la mitad) que las bases de carga inalámbrica, si tu dispositivo no tiene la alineación magnética has de asegurarte que realmente está bien colocado, ya que además no tiene ningún led que indique que está cargando, sólo puedes saberlo por lo que te indica tu dispositivo. A tener muy en cuenta con Android y fundas: • Si usas dispositivos como los últimos Samsung Galaxy o Google Pixel, o incluso si llevas el iPhone con una funda convencional, necesitas obligatoriamente que la funda sea compatible con MagSafe/Qi2 (las que llevan el anillo magnético integrado). • Si intentas usarlo con una funda de plástico normal o de piel gruesa sin imanes, el agarre se debilita muchísimo y el teléfono se soltará con cualquier movimiento. En algunos terminales Android sin funda o con carcasas inadecuadas, el imán puede sentirse algo flojo, así que el secreto para que no se mueva nada es una buena funda magnética. 🥶 Gestión de temperatura y seguridad. Al ser tan sumamente compacto y delgado, la disipación del calor es puramente pasiva a través de su carcasa metálica. Durante las cargas rápidas intensas, vas a notar que el cargador y la trasera del teléfono se calientan bastante. Es un comportamiento normal en la carga inalámbrica de alta potencia, aunque en ciertos modelos de teléfonos más pequeños o compactos (como ediciones SE o similares) esa sensación de calor puede ser un poco más acusada de lo esperado. Por suerte, incluye chip inteligente con protección contra sobrecalentamiento y detección de objetos extraños, por lo que corta el flujo si detecta anomalías. 🔍 Lo que se echa en falta (puntos a mejorar) Para ser totalmente honestos, hay un par de detalles de diseño que podrían haber redondeado el producto: • Sin indicador LED: El disco no tiene ninguna lucecita que te confirme visualmente que está pasando energía. Tienes que fiarte del pantallazo o la vibración de tu propio móvil al colocarlo. • Tamaño reducido: Como el disco es tan minimalista y delgado si no usas una funda que guíe el imán de forma automática, al principio te puede costar un par de intentos centrarlo perfectamente sobre la zona de carga trasera a la primera. ⭐ Conclusión: ¿Vale la pena? Rotundamente sí, sobre todo por la versatilidad del pack de dos unidades. Por el magnífico precio que tiene, es ideal para dejar uno fijo en tu zona de trabajo habitual (el escritorio de casa o la oficina) y meter el otro directamente en la mochila o el neceser de viaje. El color violeta oscuro es super original y elegante, rompiendo con el aburrido monopolio de las bases habituales de siempre. Si tienes claro que necesitas un adaptador potente en casa para sacarle los 25W y usas fundas magnéticas adecuadas (o tu dispositivo tiene alineación magnética), este kit te va a dar una comodidad muy importante en tu rutina diaria, ahorrándote el engorro de andar buscando y rompiendo cables físicos a cada momento. Una compra de lo más práctica y recomendada.

reviews.title: Great if your charge port has commitment issues
reviews.body: I use this with my iPhone 8 because sometimes the charge port is finicky so I have to use wireless charging, and I gave the second one in the 2 pack to my cousin who has an iPhone 14 Pro Max. The magnet connection is strong, it snaps on tight and doesn't shift. The slim design is great for when it's stuck to the back of your phone and you're using it so it's not bulky in your hand. For my iPhone 8, there's no magnets in the phone, so it doesn't attach, but it works fine as a normal Qi pad if I centre it and it doesn't make my phone hot. It charges my phone at 7.5W. That's an iPhone 8 limit, not the charger's fault. My cousin's 14 Pro Max gets 15W, since 25W Qi2.2 only works on iPhone 15 and newer. No wall adapters are included so you need a 25W+ USB-C PD brick to get fast charging on phones that support it. With my iPhone 8, a basic 10W brick is enough. If you use a weak adapter with a newer phone, charging will be slow. For the price of a 2 pack, it's good if you need a backup for port issues or want Qi2.2 speeds on a newer phone. The strong magnet is great for MagSafe phones, and it still functions as a standard wireless charger for older models.

reviews.title: Deciding between the Belkin and Anker Charger? Get the Belkin!
reviews.body: Over the past few months, companies like Anker and Belkin have introduced new charging stations that support Qi2.2 charging at 25 watts. Unfortunately, these products come with an extremely high price tag, as is common when they are first introduced. When spending such an exorbitant amount of money on a 3-in-1 charger, you want to make certain you carefully research all the available products to make the most informed choice. I bought both the Belkin MagSafe charger and the Anker Prime 25-watt charging station. In the end, I returned the Anker and kept the Belkin. The Anker was the most tempting purchase, given its unique design that included a display screen built into the stand that provided data on the exact charging wattage of each device. The screen also includes a clock and information on the current cooling level. I must admit, Anker's unique overall design and incorporating a screen make for a highly innovative product. The problem is, the Anker did not perform as expected. While charging my Apple Watch Ultra, it would only charge between 0.5-1.0 watts. My AirPods would only charge at about 3.4 watts max. Both these devices should be charging at 5 watts, but they never reached that level. Anker claims that "For watch models that support fast charging, the power can reach 3W - 5W when the battery is low. However, the power fluctuates during the charging process and does not remain at a high level continuously." However, even when my Apple Ultra Watch was near empty, it never reached 5W charging while on its stand. Despite the absence of a built-in screen, I noticed that the Belkin MagSafe Station charged my watch at a faster rate. My iPhone 16 Pro Max charged at a variable rate, which is normal for these chargers. You should only expect 25-watt charging when the phone is below 50%. Any charge above that will be slower. Another thing that I like about the Belkin over the Anker is its elegant design and small footprint. The stand looks very classy, has a padded charging base, and doesn't move when quickly grabbing and removing my phone. Anker also remained in place under the same circumstances. A win for both products. At the time of this review, the Anker costs $40-$100 more than the Belkin. I wouldn't mind paying more for the Anker if it performed as well as the Belkin, which, for me, did not. Furthermore, I had several frustrating issues dealing with Anker support when returning my unit and obtaining a refund. What I learned here is that just because a company puts out what appears to be a high-tech product with a pretty screen doesn't make it the better choice. If it doesn't perform as advertised, the consumer loses. I am having a much better experience with the Belkin. It's a solid charger that works as promised.

reviews.title: Worth the price!
reviews.body: I had 3 less expensive generic 3-in-1 chargers for just over a year... they worked okay, but I was never completely happy... then about a month ago the weak magnets started to cause my Apple watch to start off charging but then lose the connection and let the watch die overnight. So I started looking for better solutions and found this one. First, I generally believe that "brand name" vs. "generic" is often just an excuse to charge more. I really balked at $129 for a charger. In the end however, I decided to take a chance and took the plunge. WOW! What a difference! First, the magnets are much, much stronger... dropping connectivity will likely not be something I ever worry about again. And because the connection is so much better, and coupled with the huge (power wise) 45 watt adapter... all 3 of my devices (iPhone, Apple watch and AirPods) all charge much faster and reliably, even with all 3 on the charger at once. Second, the information I found regarding the cooling fan and a "hum" appears to be overblown... I can't hear a thing! (But I also have other devices nearby that I can hear so it could just be drowned out; except, even with my ear right next to this charger I could not hear anything. So, don't let the fear of a fan scare you off. The only negative thing I can think of is that the arm for the phone is adjustable, you can lay the phone completely back to 90 degrees so that the screen points up (or very close to 90 degrees) if you want. It seems to be a friction kind of adjustment, I do not see any way to tighten or loosen it... it holds position pretty well so far, but I could see this becoming an issue later. And the folding arm for the phone will be useful if I ever travel with it... fold it down for compactness and through it in a suitcase... perfect. Overall, not the least expensive by far... but so far, the quality is the best I've found. I'll wind up with one or two more over time most likely (unless something even better comes along).

reviews.title: Gorgeous sand color - great quality and aesthetically pleasing
reviews.body: I am absolutely thrilled with this Belkin 3-in-1 charging station. My favorite thing about it is the aesthetics. I chose the Sand color, and it looks beautiful on my nightstand. It blends perfectly with my home decor. Beyond its looks, it functions perfectly. It keeps my bedside table clutter-free by charging my phone, watch, and earbuds all in one central place with just a single power cord and with a small footprint. There is a built in fan to keep from overheating that makes the faintest sound, but you can turn it off if it bothers you. The build quality feels premium and heavy. If you want a multi-device charger that actually looks elegant and complements your room, I highly recommend this one! It’s so easy to set up and use. It would take little space in luggage for travel.

reviews.title: Great Charger for Apple Users, Just a Few Minor Drawbacks
reviews.body: Overall, this is a great charger and I’m very happy with it. It looks clean on my desk, charges all of my Apple devices in one place, and seems to charge faster than most chargers I’ve owned. The only charger I still reach for when I need the absolute fastest charge is Apple’s 45W charger. It’s excellent for an office setup and helps keep everything organized. Setup was simple and the build quality feels durable and well made. A couple of downsides: the magnetic connection can feel a little loose at times, and you have to get your phone centered just right or it may slide off. It also makes a bit of noise, which can be distracting when you’re trying to focus and get work done in a quiet office. It’s definitely on the expensive side, but for the convenience of charging three Apple devices at once, I think it’s worth the price. If you’re invested in the Apple ecosystem and want a clean, all-in-one charging station, this is a solid choice.

reviews.title: Best Charger I've Ever Owned
reviews.body: I absolutely love this Belkin 3-in-1 Charging Station. The build quality feels premium right out of the box, and it looks incredibly clean and modern on my desk and nightstand. The Qi2 25W charging is noticeably faster than my older MagSafe charger, and the built-in cooling fan is a fantastic feature because my phone stays much cooler while charging. The fan is also surprisingly quiet. I really appreciate being able to charge my iPhone, Apple Watch, and AirPods all in one place without dealing with multiple cables everywhere. The magnetic alignment is strong and secure, and the adjustable viewing angle makes it great for StandBy mode and FaceTime calls while charging. Belkin did an excellent job with the design, performance, and overall convenience. If you want a high-end wireless charging station that actually feels worth the money, this one delivers. Highly recommended.

reviews.title: Sleek, fast, and actually charges at the speed it promises
reviews.body: Been through a few multi-device charging stations and this is the first one that looks as good on the nightstand as it performs. The design is clean and minimal — nothing about it looks cheap or cluttered, which matters when it's sitting on your desk or bedside table every day. The Qi2.2 25W fast charging is the real headline and it delivers. iPhone charges noticeably faster than standard MagSafe setups, and the cooling fan keeps things from throttling down during long charging sessions — a detail most competing stations skip entirely. The on/off control for the fan is a thoughtful touch for anyone who wants silence at night. Having all three devices — iPhone, AirPods, and Apple Watch — charged simultaneously from one cable in one spot is the kind of quality-of-life upgrade that's hard to go back from once you have it. Everything snaps and seats exactly where it should with no fiddling. Belkin has been the reliable answer in this category for a while and the MagSafe lineup continues that. Fast, well-built, and genuinely stylish. Exactly what it promises.

reviews.title: Works as intended
reviews.body: So I just bought a brand new one two years, but it’s because I never registered the warranty for our first one. This is basically a one piece kit that is a great starter for battery charging for most kinds of automotive and marine batteries. It’s very simple to use, and the one reason our last one stopped functioning is because of built in fail safes. In this case: my wife and I were washing our camper and this got wet and then got some dirt on it, it got through the water resistant seal and the charger could detect this. The great news is the charger will literally cease to function if it has become damaged. It will give a flashing red light, and you cannot put it into Force Charge mode. The only downside is unless you have a multimeter, you may not know that it has become damaged internally. I figured it out because of the mode not working, and it wouldn’t charge any batteries. The fuse was fine. So make sure you register this when you get it. It does the job and the only way you know it’s working is because of the status light, as it is beyond quiet. It’s basically a plug with the clamps for the battery terminals, so it is easy to store and carry around. I highly recommend this charger if you need something simple without a lot of functionality, just don’t leave it exposed to the elements.

reviews.title: Perfect for bringing batteries back to life
reviews.body: Great little charger that’s perfect for maintaining and bringing batteries back to life. It’s compact, easy to use, and works with both 6V and 12V batteries. The smart charging features take the guesswork out and help prevent overcharging, which is a big plus. It’s not the fastest charger since it’s only 1A, but it’s ideal for trickle charging and keeping batteries in good shape. Overall, very reliable and worth it.

reviews.title: Little Miracle
reviews.body: Okay, I did NOT expect this little thing to work, but it did and might for you IF you have patience. My Grandfather who was MoAT (Mechanic of All Things) owned back in the day what I thought were REAL chargers, they were so big and heavy they had to be put on wheels and rolled around, they had giant switches that'd illuminate and while I'm probably purely imagining this they were plugged into 220-volt outlets. This thing fits in the palm of my hand, just as pictured, smaller than most mobile phones. "Huh," I said, "this should be comical." I hooked it up and, as others have said, figuring this thing out is NOT straight forward, the instruction manual is weak to say the least, the good news is, as I found, there are many intrepid experimenters who, like me, bought it on a whim and did some trial and error which it'd seem 99% of them got the thing to work to their needs, just like me hence, I'm taking the time to write this review. What this lacks in coherent features or instructions it makes up for it in the end by eventually (boy I mean eventually) getting the job done, for that honestly I'm giving it a generous five stars, because it did what I wanted it do against all odds, just like the Phil Collins song. ("Just take a look at my car now, 'cause it's finally starting here.") To get the to point, this took TWO WEEKS to charge a completely dead battery in a completely dead system. If it'll help anyone I own a 2000 Lexus RX300 that is, in fact, drinking age, if I could find a small ute-friendly bar to have a couple with me of which, in terms of trusty old friends, this boring beige over beige has been one of my best now with over 270,000 miles with no reason, per the Lexus dealer, to give up the ghost before 300,000. Toyota quality and then some with only wearables and maintenance needed BTW, the car has only had one issue, eating car batteries every four or so years. Being a cheap bastard and Lexus parts are pricy I've chosen battery over a slightly-off generator which brings us to the recent hullabaloo and the need to be the Noco Genius, though it'd prove not straightforward as I hoped. Hooking up the Noco Genius you get a slowly blinking light, like a heartbeat, that will tell you nothing really. Also there's a force-charge setting where you hold the button (there's only one button on the whole thing, this thing is basic) it supposedly will force a charge into a battery... this doesn't work, at all. After some digging it supposedly only does this if a battery is below some arbitrary limit which, my battery was completely dead, kaput, nada, force charge only made the 6V light go on which, apparently, is what others experienced. Point being, don't hold you breathe. I kept trying to charge the battery but it didn't budge, didn't budge, didn't budge, then I had a thought and said to myself "self, what if I unhook the battery, THEN charge it?" As in, is it because it's also hooked to my car hence current is going other places? Mind you, this thing is only one (1) amp, that's very little, if you're looking for a quick charger or something to charge and jump your car, this ain't it, have you seen the size of this thing? Ha no, no, but it will trickle, very slowly, a charge into your battery... if it's not hooked to the car. Listen, some people this may work when the battery is not hooked up and, in fact, I hooked my battery back up AFTER this thing actually worked and then hooked up the Noco to it and it did, in fact, go from red blinking to green, sooo, yeah, that happened. But I'm burying the lede here: The Noco charger worked for me but ONLY after it was hooked to the battery without being connected to the car. Total time to charge the battery not hooked to the car? About 36 hours. Great? Eh, there's a pandemic, I'm not really going out much so had time on my hands, not to mention my wife's car. In summation, IF you have even a completely dead battery or run down battery and IF you don't have to go anywhere in the next two days and IF you're comfortable unhooking the leads from your car to your battery so that it'll only be charging the battery itself this Noco Genius is, er, uh, genius! It really works! It works and for the cheap cheap cheap money its worth every penny. If this thing cost even 50% more I'd be taking down stars but this thing cost less than a steak dinner (back when I ate steak) so suffice to say it got my battery charged all the way up, hooked up to my car and after the computer was all "what the... ??? Was I in a coma" my car fired right up and ran, I even drove it around a bit. This would be a good thing to own for just-in-case as its just in case money. If you have any situation close to mine, get this trickle charger, if you need the big guns, well, open up your wallet and say ah. Luckily most of us, probably 99% of us, if your battery is run down, this will do the trick. Best of luck!

reviews.title: Seems pretty good so far
reviews.body: I have two of these. They are not exactly the same model (I think one of them is an older version of this model). The older one, I have had in the garage for several years to keep the batteries in the cars up when they are not driven very often. Some people say these are not for car batteries and I won't argue with them but the one I have out there definitely keeps the battery in my 2001 Corolla charged. And in fact, we had an incident where someone left a dome light on in that car and drained the battery to the point to where there was absolutely no response from anything electrical in the car. We started the car with a jumper pack, pulled it in the garage and connected it to the Noco and let it do it's thing. That's been at least a year and that battery is still going strong in that car. I purchased this one off Amazon to use on various SLA batteries I have around. I have two jumper packs with 18 AH SLA batteries in them. One of them had been sitting in the garage for several years due to the fact last time I tried to charge it, it wouldn't charge. I was going to order a new battery for it from Amazon but I figured I kind of needed an extra charger for SLA batteries anyway and this Noco unit was less than the price of a new battery for the old jumper pack. I figured it would be a long shot to try and charge that old battery and get any more life out of it but I thought it would be interesting to see what would happen. Can't be a tougher challenge for a SLA battery that's been sitting in a garage dead for years. Well, that jumper pack doesn't exactly have easy access to the battery but after some fighting with it, I got it open and popped the clamps on the terminals. The charging light began to pulse and after about a day, went green (was still pulsing but was pulsing green). It finally went solid green. I left it plugged in a few days. I have one of those miniature inverters that plugs into a cigarette lighter (that particular jumper pack doesn't have a built-in inverter but does have a cigarette lighter plug). So I plugged it in and tested it with a clamp light. So far, seems to be working about as well as you'd expect for a jumper pack battery that is probably approaching ten years old now. Or maybe better than you'd expect. It's only a 12 watt LED in the clamp light but my main goal was to get every last bit of value from any SLA batteries that I can. I'd definitely have a use for a small inverter like that in a power outage and if you have an extra battery that you can plug it into, so much the better. I believe the built-in charger on that jumper pack just may have died or was not up to charging it's battery for whatever reason. Remains to be seen how much more life I can get out of such batteries but it's definitely worth the price paid.

reviews.title: Reliable. Battery was ready when needed
reviews.body: In January 2026, the temperature dropped to -25°, without wind-chill, over 3 days. The electricity went out. I needed to start my emergency generator, and the battery was dead. I start the generator every month and run it for 1 hour to maintain the battery. This battery was only 7 months old. I was lucky. I had a battery for the sump pump in case of emergency, and I was able to use it. Here it is the end of August 2026, and we've been experiencing thunderstorms daily. Last night the electricity went out. I've had the battery on the NOCO Genius 1 since January. I installed it and the generator started right up. The battery has been on the charger for 7 months, so if there was a problem with the charger, I'd know by now. The charger is reliable and it protects the battery. Choose the right one by amperage of your battery.
