reviews.title: Works with a REALLY low battery
reviews.body: My wife has a 1995 Mercedes SL320 that she did not drive all winter and well into the new year... when she opened the garage door and tried to start it the battery was dead, drained by MANY months of the old style mechanical clock running without the car being started so the battery could charge My (brand name withheld) several year old 10 amp 'smart' charger would not work because the battery was too low to be detected So, I looked for a different charger with a FORCE mode to get a dead battery to start charging... I connected this one at about 7PM at night (it never would go into force mode, since the battery had 'just enough' charge to be detected) and when I get in the car at 7AM the next morning the battery had enough of a charge for the dash lights to come on, but not enough to run the starter The PDF I downloaded shows that this 1 amp charger will take 'about' 23 hours to charge a 30 AH battery... the battery in her SL320 is a 100 AH model, so I will let the charger run for another full day before I try to start the car again (or maybe 2 days to get the charger enough time to work) So far, this charger is doing exactly what I need (I thought about a larger model to charge quicker, but decided that slow charging was good enough... she hasn't driven her car since last Fall, so she can now wait a day or two)

reviews.title: Very easy to use, but it should include printed instructions
reviews.body: Very easy to use, but it should include printed instructions I bought this because my car battery had gone dead after the car had been sitting for a while. I wanted something I could connect and leave charging rather than just jump-starting the battery again. So far, I’ve been impressed with how simple it is to use. I connected it to the battery, selected the appropriate mode, and it began charging without any fuss. The indicators make it easy to see what it’s doing, and at the moment it seems to be working exactly as intended. My one criticism is that there is no conventional instruction manual included. Instead, you scan a QR code and go online for the instructions. That worked fine for me, but I don’t think it’s a particularly good choice for a product like this. Not everyone has a smartphone readily available, and battery chargers may be used in garages or emergency situations where having basic printed instructions in the box would be useful. Other than that, my first experience with it has been very positive. It’s compact, straightforward to connect, and remarkably easy to operate.

reviews.title: Will not buy any other charger
reviews.body: The Belkin MagSafe 3-in-1 charger is hands-down one of the best charging stations I’ve ever used. It charges my iPhone, Apple Watch, and AirPods all at once without any clutter—just one sleek, solid base that looks great on a nightstand or desk. The MagSafe connection is strong and perfectly aligned every time, so I don’t have to fumble around getting the phone positioned. The Apple Watch charger is built-in and angled perfectly for Nightstand Mode, and the AirPods sit snugly on their charging pad. Everything stays in place, and all three devices charge efficiently and simultaneously. Build quality is top-notch—premium materials, sturdy feel, and a clean modern design. It’s not cheap, but you get what you pay for here: performance, style, and convenience. If you’re invested in the Apple ecosystem and tired of tangled cords or multiple chargers, this is absolutely worth the investment.

The magnet wireless charging for the phone wasn’t working anymore, but the wireless charger on the base and the watch charging were still working. Now I’m being told I might not even get a refund if I don’t still have the manuals and original packaging for a product that stopped working after two weeks. reviews.title: One of those products that just quietly works
reviews.body: I bought this charging station for my wife as she is deep in the Apple ecosystem (I'm on the Android side), and she’s been using it for about 6 months now. She's happy with it. It’s one of those products that just quietly does its job every single day without any issues. The design is clean and modern, and it looks great on her nightstand. The MagSafe thingy holds the iPhone securely in place, even with a case on, and the Qi2 charging is surprisingly fast and reliable. She usually puts her phone on at night, and it’s fully charged by morning without fail. It also charges her Apple Watch and AirPods at the same time. It’s so nice to have one sleek unit instead of three separate chargers and a mess of cables. The non-slip base is a nice touch too, though I wish it stuck to the surface a bit more, sometimes it doesn’t keep the whole thing as steady as I’d like. Maybe the whole stand is a bit too lightweight... Just for fun, I tried putting my Samsung Buds on the bottom charger, and it actually worked! So it's not limited to Apple devices, which is a nice bonus. If you’re deep in the Apple ecosystem (or live with someone who is), this is a fantastic addition to your/their setup. Highly recommend it.

reviews.title: Great Charger for those with an iphone & apple watch
reviews.body: Bought this for my wife to charge her watch and phone at the same time on her night stand. She loves it. Charges very well, the magnet is strong and works. I recommend getting the magsafe case. Super easy to connect your watch and phone to to get them to charge overnight. Doesn't take up a lot of space and works exactly as anticipated.

reviews.title: Excellent charging stand
reviews.body: This 3 in 1 MagSafe charger is the best investment I could have made for my phone and accessories. I have an iPhone 14 pro max and I have zero issues with it charging with my MagSafe case on it. I’m not sure if the other reviewers understand that they still need to line up the magnet-it’s not just going to “catch” without taking an extra second to line it up. Once aligned, the magnet is extremely strong and my phone has never once fallen off of this charger This charger charges my phone, apple watch and airpods simultaneously and quickly. It was a little pricey however having 3 chargers in 1 that I am not constantly having to search for or replace due to broken chords is worth every penny. Do not believe the reviews that say it broke after 2 months or 2 years-this charger had only been on the market since November 2022 (2 months total) and it’s the first and only MagSafe charger apple endorses, which is why I purchased it. Well worth the money. This is an excellent charging system that is aesthetically pleasing.

reviews.title: Easy to use, great product!
reviews.body: When you move into the apple ecosystem, it is usually done first with an iphone, then with airpods and finally with an apple watch. Before buying the product I was a little unsure, as it is an expensive product. But it was totally worth it, just for the ease of being able to charge the three products, which I mentioned above, quickly and easily, without having to be handling two and three cables (even without the need to handle multiple outlets) which greatly simplifies the cable management for those who seek visual simplicity. The only thing not convenient is the material of the base with which the product is made, as it tends to "absorb" dust, dirt, grease etc etc in a very easy way, it is not an easy product to clean but with a little patience can be left as new. If I had to improve something it would be the above mentioned and additionally in the black version I would also try to leave the Magsafe Pads in black color, for those who have a dark palette of colors on their setup. In my case I used the product with an Iphone 13 (normal), Airpods 3 and a watch series 8 and it charges these three devices without problems. The convenience here is that since it is a product that allows you to charge these gadgets so easily, this allows me to rarely run out of battery or forget to charge any of them.

reviews.title: Perfect for a second car that doesn't get driven often
reviews.body: I was hesitant to buy one of these because of the reviews about fires. Don't pay attention to those reviews. This little trickle charger keeps your car battery at full and in brand new condition. I read somewhere online that if you put a brand new AGM battery in your car like I did and keep this NOCO Genius10 hooked up, the battery can theoretically last up to 10 years because the NOCO will continuously keep it charged and repaired. It seems that my battery was not the problem with my car as the starter relay on the clutch needed replacing so now my car starts again. But I put in a new AGM battery anyways and won't have to worry about replacing it for another 7-10 years as long as I keep the NOCO attached when not driving the car for long periods of time. As for the NOCO functionality itself it has a couple buttons, one to choose what kind of battery you are using, regular 12V, AGM, or Lithium Ion. The other button I believe is for what kind of charge you want(trickle, decharge, repair) but since I have a brand new battery I simply keep it on trickle charge. The cord length is not very long so in order for my NOCO to reach my car battery and the wall socket in my garage I used a decent gauge extension cord. The instructions say not to use an extension cord but there is no other way since my wall outlet in my garage is too far away from the car battery. I keep a smoke detector next to the NOCO and battery just to be safe. I got the NOCO on sale during Prime Day so it is definitely a good value for the money. So far so good.

reviews.title: Solid!
reviews.body: Purchased the NOCO Genius charger in hopes it would resurrect my battery. Un fortunately, it did not save my battery, but I cannot blame that on the charger. The only complaint I have is the lack of instructions. They were not minimal, there were none at all provided with the unit. Luckily, able to look on line and find plenty of videos, however, this does not negate the need for an instruction and care pamphlet. The unit feels solidly built and works as expected. While it did not resurrect my battery as it claims it can do (not in all situations), mine was 5 years old, lead acid and probably just to far gone for help. However, it is doing a great job charging my marine battery and using it to keep it charged until used again. I like it. Much more compact than the older styles and easily able to mount to a wall or post as a charging station. I would definitely buy again.

reviews.title: Pretty neat device, very capable as well
reviews.body: I have a battery charger made in the 1970s, inherited from dad that passed away in 2011. It was time for another one, and I was going to buy another Schumacher that weights about 15 Lbs. Was ready to pull the trigger and decided to see if something better was out there, thus buying a Genius 10 instead based on YouTube reviews. The Genius 10 was much larger and heavier than how it looks in the picture. The build quality is really good in my eyes, looks like tough ABS polymer, very nice cords with that good feeling wire jacket insulation. The new clamps are nice looking and very practical to me. It's heavy and awkward to store, so I bought the Noco case as well; I thought the other case was too small in size. I ran some test with it, on a 12V Honda Lead Acid and Group H8 AGM battery and was happy the results. It was more intuitive than the 1970s version I have with 30 amp boost that is scary to use. What I like with Noco or Genius, it's several tools in one unit, so every 3 or 4 months, I can use the Genius to check the status of all my batteries, well that is the plan at least. One neat thing, using the 12V output to keep a battery online while changing a battery, so the cars computer keeps running and doesn't reboot from removing the battery causing weird things to happen. I have no regrets in my purchase and bought the case to enhance it more. I think the price is reasonable as well considering what a $100 buys today.

reviews.title: Saved me from buying a new battery!
reviews.body: EDIT 2/26/24: I am now the blocks "AAA". Been helping people start their cars when jump starts with cables have not worked. Definitely handy to get other people out of an otherwise expensive pinch. I have a car battery that I purchased around 2016 (date of review 1/3/24). The car itself does not get driven much, at most 2-3 times a week no longer than 15 minutes one way. Throughout the years I've drained it by leaving the car lights on. Its always required a jump start after that to get going again. Recently I've been an idiot and been leaving my lights on more frequently. Eventually it required me to jump start everytime I wanted to turn on the car. It was becoming a hassle and I was about to call it quits and purchase a new battery until I came across Project Farm's review on battery chargers. This was at the top of the list so I figured to give it a shot. I was not disappointed! I charged it for 4 days straight, put it in my car, and it started right up. Not surprised considering it was just charged but the real test laid ahead. I was going to be out of town for two weeks and leave the car sitting. I came back two weeks later and the car started up, no hesitation whatsoever, as if it was a different battery! The NOCO Genius 10 saved me about $150-200 at least in a brand new battery. On top of that, I can now use it for other batteries in the event of any similar issues. The instructions on the other hand are a bit confusing and had to rely on YouTube comments to piece it together. For those who are confused at what to do, I did not do a 12V repair (function which this unit has) as it requires the battery to be completely charged first. All I did was charge it straight for 4 days uninterrupted. When first put on battery to the charger it will be in standby mode. You push (or hold depending on what you need) the MODE button to select your desired option. I was charging a lead acid battery so I selected 12V. The meter at the top slowly advanceD from each of the four bars until the final bar was pulsing green which indicates its charging to full (over 80% I believe). The green charging light continued to slowly pulse even on the 4th day but I took a gamble and disconnected it from the battery. For the battery to be 100% charged, the green light should stay solid. That means my battery worked 2 weeks later after sitting and it wasn't even at 100%. The unit can also force a charge on batteries that are extremely under voltage. Thats a separate setting that I haven't had to use yet. It can also charge AGM and Lithium but I believe the 12V repair function is only for lead acid. Unfortunately I had to go through 3 separate orders because the first two were from Amazon Warehouse and I encountered issues with both, consecutively. I ended up getting frustrated and just purchased a brand new charger. Pros: Solid build quality Excellent cable connections with weather covers Compatible with a wide variety of batteries Repair and Force charge batteries Cons: Poor instructions Charge is slow BUT I think thats how these chargers work TL;DR Try this first before rushing to get a new battery it is a good investment that can save you a lot of money

reviews.title: Riptide pool vacuum owners, look no further!
reviews.body: I just bought this after researching what is the best battery charger or maintainer for owning a Riptide pool vacuum system. This is for personal use and not running a business. Advice for new pool owners or even existing ones, do not buy a junky 500-1500 dollar pool robot, but a hammerhead or Riptide vacuum. Long story short I bought this maintainer to charge the vacuum battery and maintain it between uses. Charged it in no time and I also use this for my Yamaha 700 ATV. Fantastic unit. Only regret is before I opened this, I didn't test it on an ATV battery that died on me to test it's recovery mode. Chance are that I gave the kid at Advanced Auto parts a free ATV/motorcycle battery because if he had one of these NOCO 10s, chances are he saved the battery and got new life into it. Cant go wrong with this especially for the fast charging, force recharge mode, and versatility to charge, maintain, and breathe batteries back to life. Just one more thing, First time charging the battery after sitting idle for 3 weeks and 2 uses in my case and charged it to full literally in 5 min. I like the unit for keeping the battery at full between uses and not overcharging costing me $300 for a new battery. Well worth the money for less worry and hassle. Hope this helped someone with whatever they were looking to use this for. Also cable length is more than sufficient. Im sure there's an extension option if needed too.

title: NOCO GENIUS5 5A 6/12V Smart Battery Charger, Trickle Charger & Maintainer

reviews.title: Reliable Smart Charger That Brought a Neglected Battery Back to Life
reviews.body: I purchased the NOCO GENIUS5 to maintain the batteries in vehicles that don't get driven regularly, and it has been one of those tools that quickly proves its value. Setup was straightforward. The included connectors are easy to use, and the charger automatically detects the battery and selects the appropriate charging mode. I especially appreciate that it can be left connected for maintenance without worrying about overcharging, which gives me peace of mind when storing a vehicle for extended periods. One of the batteries I used it on had been sitting for quite a while and was struggling to hold a charge. After connecting the GENIUS5 and allowing it to complete its charging cycle, the battery recovered enough to reliably start the vehicle again. While no charger can fix a battery that's physically damaged or completely worn out, this unit did a good job recovering a battery that I initially thought might need replacement. The charger itself feels well-built and the display indicators are easy to understand. I also like that it supports both lead-acid and lithium batteries, making it useful for multiple vehicles and equipment around the house. A few things prospective buyers should know: The 5A charging rate is ideal for maintenance and general charging, but it isn't the fastest option if you're trying to charge a large, deeply discharged battery in a hurry. The indicator lights are simple and functional, though some users may prefer a charger with a more detailed digital display showing voltage and charging status. Overall, this is a dependable smart charger that is easy to use, versatile, and well-built. Whether you're maintaining a seasonal vehicle, motorcycle, lawn equipment, or simply want a charger that can safely stay connected long-term, the GENIUS5 is a worthwhile investment. Helpful tip: If you're using it for battery maintenance, consider installing the included quick-connect lead permanently on the battery. It makes future charging sessions much faster and more convenient.

reviews.title: NOCO Genius5
reviews.body: I bought the Genius5 after neglecting a relatively new battery in my motorcycle. Due to weather and travel, I often have long gaps between rides. Unfortunately, one of these gaps was long enough to damage the battery. I didn’t realize that batteries need a minimal charge to avoid sulfation, and mine had become severely discharged. Although my NOCO GB40 starter worked fine, the battery wasn’t holding a charge even after a day of riding. Instead of immediately replacing the battery, I decided to try saving it with the Genius5. After charging the battery with the Genius5, I tested it with a battery analyzer, which reported it as damaged. I then ran the desulfation process, and afterward, the analyzer showed the battery was in good condition. I repeated the tests several days later to be sure, and the battery still appeared to be in good health. Now, I keep the Genius5 connected to my motorcycle whenever I’m not riding for more than a week, and I haven’t had any battery issues since. I still carry the GB40 in my panniers, just in case, but I haven’t needed to use it lately. Some notes on the desulfation process: The desulfation process seems to send voltage peaks, and you may hear some bubbling inside the battery. This happened to me, and from what I’ve read, it’s normal as long as there’s not too much bubbling and no vapors, heating, or swelling of the battery. The entire process takes a while, so it’s unrealistic to monitor it the whole time. However, I recommend watching it for the first 20 minutes to ensure the battery noises aren’t increasing. After that, you can leave it running while staying nearby, just in case something goes wrong. A final note on this process: because of the voltage peaks, I didn’t run it with the battery connected to the motorcycle to avoid any potential damage to the circuits. For regular maintenance charging, I do keep the battery connected. The Genius5 is designed to work with standard batteries, gel, and even lithium ones. The one I used was a Gel Yuasa, and I’m pleased with the results. I also purchased the NOCO cables (GC002 X-Connect M6) to make it easier to connect the charger without removing the seat. The cables were a bit expensive but seem well-constructed and are quite convenient. Final thoughts: If you have a vehicle that sits unused for extended periods, and this happens frequently, then this charger is ideal for you. However, if you only need it once a year or less, it might be easier and cheaper to disconnect the battery from the vehicle while you’re away to prevent discharging. For my use case, the Genius5 has been worth it, and I’d definitely buy it again.

reviews.title: Resurrected a dead battery overnight
reviews.body: My interstate battery went completely when I went returned from a 6 week trip. Tried jump starting by using my other car but failed. Noco is one of the few chargers that can charge a completely dead battery. Watched a project farm youtube video on car battery chargers ( see chart at 18m29s of the video) before buying. I purchased the 5A one due to time constraint ( charged 75% in 8 hours ). You can buy the 2A version or 1A version if you have all the time and just want to keep batteries fully charged. I let it charge overnight and had a fully functional battery in the morning. This happens to me whenever I go on long trips ( 4 weeks + ). With a rechargeable jump starter, you are limited by the battery life of the starter which is only 3-4 years after which most batteries fail. The wall charger hopefully will last a long longer. Saved me a lot of time - No need to drive the car around after jump starting to get some charge into the battery. Just charge overnight and done. Love it.

reviews.title: Good Quality, Great Value
reviews.body: Easy to use and well built. I used it to charge the AGM battery on my Ducati and it worked great. The indicator lights are clear, and the connector makes it easy to plug in whenever needed. Great for keeping the battery maintained, especially if you don’t ride every day. Overall, I’m very happy with it.

reviews.title: Yeah so don't mix up your fused alligator cables if you buy different models
reviews.body: I bought a Genius1 and Genius5. The latter failed on first use due to my mistake mixing up the alligator clips during unboxing. I didn't look closely enough to notice that the 1 and 5 aren't just feature levels but are current ratings in Amps. The proprietary connectors are identical but the 1A unit has a 2A fuse and the 5A unit has a 10A fuse, and they're on the battery side of the connectors not the device side, so obviously the 2A fuse correctly blew when I tried using the 5A unit. They work fine after fixing my careless mix-up, but I'd like these better if the device or fuse holder were marked with a recommended fuse rating, or the connectors couldn't mate with the wrong device, or the fuse holder were on the device side of the proprietary connector, or the unit came with spare fuses, or the fuse ratings were included in the online user guide, or the user guide were included in the box, or the safety guide were printed in a typeface legible to adult human eyes. Anyway, keep your cables together with the devices and don't mix em up.

reviews.title: High quality at a reasonable cost
reviews.body: This charger/tender worked well to "revive" a ~80Ah lead acid battery that sat in a low state of charge for nearly a year. After an initial 2.5 hour cycle in repair mode, followed by a higher amp charge from an older/larger charger, a noticeable improvement in battery performance was observed. A shorter repair cycle, about 30 minutes total, restored some capacity on another lead acid battery still in use. There are cheaper desulfator-only options, of questionable reliability/longevity, so the additional features offered on this model were cost-effective for my intended usage. While I have not yet used this as a tender/maintainer for any length of time, the cabling to and from the charger are long enough to reach from one side of a car to the other. This unit did not seem to produce much heat in repair mode with ~75F ambient temp. In auto charge mode between 25% and 75%, it was warm to the touch. I'll have to try a longer charge period to see if it heats up further. UPDATE: after using repair & charge mode on a flat battery for a few hours, this unit can get fairly hot. Using this on a flat surface so air can get underneath is a good idea. This product did not come with a manual in the box, just the warranty booklet. Tracking down a user manual on the manufacturer's site did not require much effort. The 6V and repair mode are not activated by quick presses of the single button. Pressing & holding for a few seconds activates these extra modes from standby. Some form of documentation in the box would have been more convenient than going to the website, but I digress.

reviews.title: Revived my battery
reviews.body: I bought a used 2022 Honda Ridgeline with ~7,000 miles on it some months back. It was a "dealer demo car" and was well-maintained as a result. Now, it's got around 12,000 miles on it. One day, I left the lights on too long with the ignition off, and had the radio playing. Stupid on my part, but my battery didn't have enough charge to deliver the amps needed to turn the engine over. I bought a Noco GB40, and it worked well - it'd start my truck when needed. Yesterday, it didn't. I guess the battery had degraded too much, so I was shopping for new batteries when the sticker shock hit me. Given the age of my truck, I thought it would be silly to replace the battery. Someone recommended the Noco Genius5, so I gave it a shot. Amazon's same-day delivery got it to me quickly, and I basically hooked it up to the battery, plugged it in, set it to AGM mode, and let it go to work. I waited several hours for the charger light to show "solid green", indicating it was fully charged. I started up my truck; it sounded better than the day I bought it. However, on the dash, it had a note about an "emissions problem". My scan tool showed a permanent code with the Transmission Control Module and a bunch of other temporary codes. Since I didn't have any codes before, I figured I may have freaked out the electronics by charging the battery while the battery was hooked up to the truck, or maybe by touching the terminals out of sequence when removing the cables. Either way, I removed the battery from my truck, hooked up the Genius5, and set it to "repair mode". My truck had low mileage when I bought it, at about a year old, which likely meant that it say for a while when not in use. Maybe that could have led to sulfation or stratification, which could have meant it wouldn't charge as effectively from the alternator. I also wanted to remove the battery to allow the computers to reset in the truck. If it was still throwing codes after that, I'd bring it into the dealer. This morning, when I woke up, I noticed the Genius5 was in standby mode, meaning the repair mode had finished. I started the Genius5 back up, and set it to AGM mode again -- it took about a minute, but it said the battery was good to go with a solid green light. I Installed the battery back in my truck, fired it up, and I kid you not, it sounded better than ever -- less strained, more powerful, and all of the codes were gone. My truck had a freakout -- not due to this device, I'm sure, but likely due to me doing something stupid. It's rare for me to review a product so quickly. This thing is amazing, has lots of neat accessories available for it, and saved me money. I'll continue using it to prolong my batteries and save me money in the long-run. If you're on the fence, this little device is absolutely legit. 10/10 would recommend.

reviews.body: I bought one of these for my wife after using one myself for several years. I teach online so my camera gets constant use. The image quality is terrific, especially after using the setup software to increase the camera resolution. The camera is plug-and-play, requiring no setup in either Windows or Ubuntu Linux. The only minor complaints I have are that images are dim in low light (make sure your face is well-lit from the front!) and that it occasionally re-focuses spontaneously and causes a few seconds of blurred video. But 99 percent of the time the image is excellent. Audio quality is very good too, but the microphone can be overdriven, causing distorted sound. This is seldom a problem for voice calls but if you're using it for something louder like an acoustic instrument you should turn down the microphone gain in either the camera setup or the application itself, and make sure from the person on the other end that they're not hearing distortion. With the mic properly set you get decent audio fidelity, no matter what your sound source is. My biggest complaint about this webcam has nothing to do with the device itself. It's too popular. It's almost always sold out at the Logitech store, and when they do make some available, they are snapped up by resellers who scalp them at a $15-$30 premium. It would be helpful if Logitech would limit the number people could buy to give more people a chance to get this great camera at a more reasonable price.

reviews.title: RightSight feature may not work on SurfacePro with Snapdragon (ARM64) processor
reviews.body: FYI: I purchased this camera after seeing someone else who presented using it. Everyone was curious what camera they were using because it was such good lighting and great video. However, I'm not sure this camera is working with full functionality on my hardware. I went through a bunch of troubleshooting, and here's the conclusion per ChatGPT... Good morning ☀️ — thank you for the detailed info. That explains everything. You’re on: Surface Pro 11th Edition (ARM64) Snapdragon X (ARM) processor That is the root cause. ________________________________________ 🎯 The Real Issue Logitech RightSight is currently not supported on Windows ARM (Snapdragon X / ARM64). Here’s why: RightSight depends on: • Logitech’s middleware service • x64 camera processing components • AI framing pipeline extensions On ARM Surface devices: • Logi Tune runs under emulation • The Logitech camera extension layer does not fully attach to the Windows Modern Camera Stack • AI features (RightSight) fail to initialize • Video works (because UVC driver works) • 4K works (hardware OK) • But AI framing = unavailable That’s exactly your symptom set. ________________________________________ ✅ Why Everything Else Works ✔ Camera app works ✔ 4K works ✔ Windows Hello works ✔ Device shows correctly ✔ No USB issue ✔ No driver corruption Only vendor AI features fail — classic ARM compatibility limitation. ________________________________________ 🚫 This Is Not Fixable Via Settings Disabling: • Frame Server • Basic camera • Studio effects • Multiple apps setting Will not fix it on ARM. This is architectural, not a configuration problem. ________________________________________ 🔎 Confirmation Test (Optional) In Logi Tune: Go to Crop. If: • Field of View options work (65°, 78°) • Zoom works • But Auto-Framing is disabled That confirms it’s just the AI layer. ________________________________________ 🧠 Why This Happens Surface Pro 11 (Snapdragon X) uses: • Windows on ARM • Modern Camera Driver (MCD) • NPU-based camera pipeline Logitech RightSight expects: • x64 processing environment • Vendor extension hooks not fully exposed in ARM64 camera stack Until Logitech releases a native ARM64 version of the RightSight service, it won’t enable. ________________________________________ 📌 Current Status (Early 2026) As of now: • Logitech supports Intel/AMD Windows • ARM64 support is partial • AI features are inconsistent or unavailable ________________________________________ 💡 Your Options Option 1 — Wait for Logitech ARM-native update This will likely come, since Snapdragon X PCs are new. Option 2 — Use Windows Studio Effects (if available) Surface Pro 11 has NPU-based auto framing built in. Check: Settings → Bluetooth & devices → Cameras → Built-in camera If Studio Effects exists there, you can use Windows auto-framing instead. Option 3 — Use Software Framing (Zoom / Teams) Both now have built-in auto framing. ________________________________________ ✅ Final Conclusion Your hardware is fine. Your configuration is fine. Your issue is ARM platform compatibility.

reviews.title: Logitech MX Brio: A Stunning Leap Forward
reviews.body: ## **Logitech MX Brio Ultra HD 4K: The New Gold Standard for Video** If you haven’t upgraded your webcam in a few years, the **Logitech MX Brio** is a startling reminder of just how far imaging technology has come. Gone are the days of grainy, "good enough" video calls. We are officially in the era of ultra-crisp, professional-grade production sitting right on top of your monitor. ### **Crystal Clarity & Visual Fidelity** The jump to **Ultra HD 4K** is immediately noticeable. The clarity is staggering—it picks up textures and details that older 1080p sensors simply smudge away. Whether you’re in a high-stakes board meeting or recording content, the image looks expensive. It handles difficult lighting with ease, ensuring you don't look washed out when the sun hits your desk or like a shadow when the lights are low. ### **Pro-Grade Audio** Usually, webcam microphones are an afterthought, but the audio here is surprisingly **clear and crisp**. It manages to isolate your voice while minimizing that hollow, "bathroom" echo common in cheaper units. While dedicated mics still have their place, for 95% of users, this audio quality is more than enough to sound professional and authoritative. ### **Total Software Control** Where this camera really shines is the **Logitech G HUB or Logi Options+** integration. The level of control is deep: * **Fine-tuned adjustments:** You can tweak ISO, shutter speed, white balance, and exposure. * **Field of View:** Crop in for a tight headshot or widen it out to show your workspace. * **Show Mode:** A clever bit of tech that lets you tilt the camera down to show your desk, automatically flipping the image so your viewers can see your sketches or notes correctly. ### **The Verdict** It’s incredible to see how much technology has shifted in just the last few years. We’ve moved from "webcams" to "miniature cinema cameras." The **Logitech MX Brio** isn't just a tool for Zoom calls; it’s a high-performance piece of hardware that brings professional studio quality to a plug-and-play format. reviews.title: The best “professional work” webcam I’ve personally used, especially for virtual backgrounds
reviews.body: I bought the Logitech MX Brio after spending years using a mirrorless camera setup (Lumix GH3 + prime lens) as my desk webcam. I work remotely full-time and spend most of my day in video calls (99% in Microsoft Teams), so my priorities are a little different from the average streaming-focused review. What I wanted was: • excellent image quality at normal desktop distances • reliable performance in Teams • strong virtual background segmentation • stable autofocus/exposure • easy to set up For my use case, the MX Brio has honestly been excellent. The biggest surprise was how good the image looks in real-world meetings. Yes, my GH3 (and other mirrorless cameras) can still produce a more cinematic image in ideal conditions, but in Teams specifically (where video is heavily compressed and usually capped at 1080p), the practical gap is much smaller than people think. As far as the camera is concerned, what matters most is consistency and signal quality, and this camera delivers both. The MX Brio handles exposure transitions smoothly, autofocus has been reliable, and image sharpness is very good without looking overly processed. Logitech also seems to have improved color handling compared to some older Brio models that could occasionally look harsh or over-sharpened. Where this webcam REALLY shines is virtual background and portrait segmentation. I use a virtual background almost 100% of the time, and this camera consistently gives cleaner edge separation than several other webcams I’ve tested. Good lighting absolutely helps, but the MX Brio seems to provide a very clean image feed that works well with Teams’ background processing. A few other things I appreciated: • solid low-light recovery without becoming a smeary mess • flexible field of view options • sturdy physical build • built-in microphone • easy mounting and positioning There are a couple tradeoffs worth mentioning: • Logitech’s software ecosystem is still a little fragmented (Logi Tune, G Hub, etc.) • if you are primarily a streamer/content creator, there may be better options depending on your workflow • this camera, like any, benefits significantly from proper lighting and good positioning. It's worth it to invest in a couple lights and proper mounting system But for a professional desk setup focused on video meetings, presentations, collaboration, and hybrid work, I think Logitech understood the assignment here surprisingly well. This is the first dedicated webcam I’ve used where I no longer feel tempted to drag a mirrorless camera back onto my desk.

reviews.title: It actually works for Windows 10!
reviews.body: I was super excited to purchase this 4K webcam to help myself have crisper, clearer video chats when teaching online. Since changing from an established workplace to freelance, I had to return my previous company computer, and that left me with my old 2012 HP running Windows 10. The built-in webcam on my laptop is terrbile! At my brother's recommendation, since I needed something better (and since simply using my cell phone wouldn't work for the long-term), I began looking into external webcams. I asked Google's AI to help me find something suitable for my laptop in particular, and somehow this 4K camera came up. However, when it came in the mail and I plugged it in, my computer didn't seem to recognize it at all. No blue light! Anyway, I was beginning to wonder if I'd have to return it, but I had already attached the "privacy" adhesive over the lens and was concerned that this might mean I couldn't send it back. Also, I really wanted it to work! So I did a ton of troubleshooting, updating things on my computer here and there, installing drivers, etc. Nothing worked. I then bought an external USB 3.0 hub since my laptop's hubs aren't powerful enough for a 4K webcam evidently. Plugged everything in. Still, nothing! Then finally, I asked AI for recommendations regarding that particular webcam and my specific laptop, once again. The final recommendation it gave me was to "install Native EMEET Software." I had read earlier that everything would be supplied automatically as soon as you plug it in, but it turns out that's not always the case. I went onto the website, and there's a place listing "downloads" where you can get the needed software for either Windows PC or Mac. So, I downloaded the Windows one ... and voila! At long last, after installing that software, the camera worked! Apparently it's still not perfectly displaying in 4K, but no matter! The quality is is a step down from that, since my computer cannot quite support 4K. What it can display though is still a MASSIVE upgrade from what I had before! The low-light performance is excellent, and you can adjust the camera settings (contrast, saturation, etc.). I've never used an external webcam before so to me this is pretty cool. Plus, I can always use this camera on a newer laptop whenever I'm able to purchase one, and then I can have perfect 4K. But for now, attached to the laptop that I have, this camera quality is still beyond "good enough"; it's great. I'm glad I didn't give up and send this back. So it's completely worth it -- just know that if you have an old computer running Windows 10, you might have to jump through multiple hoops first before getting it to work. ;)

reviews.title: Video streaming is your job = PASS ... Casual video for mtgs/life = BUY IT -- checks all the boxes
reviews.body: If video streaming is a way you make money, do NOT buy this. This webcam + microphone is not for professional level video streaming. If you need a webcam + mic device that is good enough, and performs better than most/all laptop integration webcams, then just buy this and call it a day. There are a lot of options, but I promise that unless you are a really particular human, you will be happy with this product. a) WfH business person taking video calls for work = YES b) private individual streaming to connect with friends/family = YES c) a recreational streamer = YES Detailed review notes below.... **MOST IMPORTANT THING TO KNOW** The camera can only go so far, but a lot of what determines the final video quality is what YOU do to create a good video streaming environment. Read: If you are in a windowless cave 50' below Earth's surface with no artificial lighting, poor video quality is on you, not the device. Lighting and distance of the camera from your face are THE MOST IMPORTANT VARIABLES in determining whether this camera performs well or not. I posted a photo of my specific camera placement and lighting and desk situation, and have tested out four different lighting scenarios (listed below) to show the impact of lighting on the video quality. **REVIEW NOTES** Each number 1-4 below has a matching image that I have attached to this review: 1. Only natural light from my office windows (indirect sunlight) 2. #1 + clip-on desk lamp with warm colored LED *MY FAVORITE SETUP* 3. #2 + recessed ceiling lights (3" white colored LEDs with 8' ceilings) 4. Natural light from windows + recessed ceiling lights (NO desk lamp) *NOTE*: Each image was taken via Windows Snipit tool while waiting to join a Google Meeting BOTTOM LINE, you have to mess around with your lighting and camera distance to get the sweet spot for your specific environment, and may require additional lighting sources (e.g. lamp) to get it right. The EMEET app is super easy to install and provides decent enough picture settings to tweak the image quality without being overkill. No login/account/signup required. I recommend keeping the "white balance" on AUTO at all times.

reviews.title: A great 4K cam with Sony sensor
reviews.body: The box for this is quite sturdy although not very visually impressive. Acer should put more effort into their packaging, particularly on a premium product like this. These are my main likes and dislikes for this product: Like: Sony 1/2 “ sensor 4K HDR Premium lenses Full metal body Compact and portable Good overall build quality Fully Plug & Play Dislike: Expensive at £79.99 rrp Lens cover falls off too easily As you can see there is a lot I like about this webcam. The image it produces look very natural, being not too colourful or contrasty, with just the right balance. The sharpness at 4K is a noticeable improvement over 1080p or even 1440p, as long as you have a monitor good enough to see the difference of course. The Sony CMOS sensor is good at controlling signal noise, so the fuzziness is kept to a minimum in low light, and is far better than a standard webcam with a generic cheap sensor. The autofocus is surprisingly good, again this is due to the sensor and chip combination. Tracking actually works in most instances, which I have not seen on a webcam before. The dual mics work very well and remove background noise almost completely. Voices are clear, even multiple voices can be heard perfectly within about six feet of the camera. Installation was a few seconds, as it is plug and play. This is being used on Windows 11 but it should also work on Apple Macintosh computers. The lens cap is a bit of a disappointment, it is not strong enough and is easy to knock off when handling the camera. A more powerful magnet is needed. The current price for this is £66 which I think is reasonable, and at that price it’s going to get a solid five stars.

reviews.body: What can i say other than I love the LED desk lamp and that it is dimmable, easy to adjust, and operate. It does not take up much space on the back of my desk and is easy to setup. You can plug it into a USB-A port or plug it into the USB-A block it comes with. We are considering buying another one for my son's desk. reviews.title: Recommended. Could be improved but good as is.
reviews.body: TL;DR: Recommended but could be improved. I'm using this lamp in my living room to illuminate a bluetooth keyboard in the evening. The gooseneck keeps the lamp where I put it and feels like it's well made and will last. The lamp has 3 color settings - white, amber and off-white(?). I'm not sure why they choose off-white rather than red, which is useful when you don't want to compromise your night vision any more than you have to. The lamp seems to be quite efficient; I've been running it on an old no-name (and over-rated IMHO) 30,000 mA USB power bank for about 12 hours, and I've got 87% of the battery left. It's wide enough to illuminate a full-size keyboard, but the LED strip is designed so it's easy to keep glare off the screen. I've got two power banks, neither of which start when the lamp is plugged in; you must push the button on the power bank to turn on the output. This is because the lamp (and other devices) don't draw enough current when the lamp is off for the power bank to notice it's connected! As a result, if I turn the lamp off (such that the lamp's blue standby light comes on) the power bank thinks nothing is connected and shuts down after a few seconds (and thus losing my dimmer adjustments). The lamp has a wide illumination range; it gets quite bright, and dims to a very low level, such that I can keep it on when I'm not using it and it isn't distracting. This is important because WHEN HE LAMP LOSES POWER IT FORGETS HOW MUCH I've DIMMED IT (for which I have deducted a star). To compensate for this, when I turn the light on for the evening I set the default (white) light to the level I need to view my keyboard; I set the other two colors to the lowest level. When I want to take a break and watch TV for a bit, I select the amber color and I can dim the light is enough that I don't notice it. Then when I want to type some more I switch to the white color and I'm in business. I have one other nit: The lamp's gooseneck threads onto the top of a stiff upright tube, which screws into the desk mount. This tube is long enough that I can barely position the lamp perfectly (due in part to my setup - others may not find it too long). This could be solved by shipping a 2nd tube about half the length of the current tube. This way I could use the short tube and it would give the gooseneck more 'reach'. Some may find it useful to use both tubes for added height.

reviews.title: Versatile light source for home office, workshop, or craft area.
reviews.body: TL;DR: A really great desk lamp and even better customer support. I’m really enjoying this desk lamp. I appreciate that you can adjust the color and brightness of the light and the gooseneck such that you can adjust the position. It clamps right onto the edge of my adjustable stand-sit desk. It’s been the perfect addition to my home office. I also had an exceptional experience with the support team this past week. Oddly, when I turned my lamp on to start the week, the light was not bright and it was kind of flashing a bit. I thought maybe there was something wrong with the USB port it was plugged into, so I tried another. It was on the same multi-plug though. Same problem. I emailed the support email from their seller page with an explanation and a video and within 24 hours I had a response - one that suggested I try another power source but that also stated if the issue persisted they would certainly make it right. So this time I actually moved it to a different multi-plug (a step I should have done myself before the email) and the lamp was working fine. Clearly an issue with my power source. Sheepishly I responded and acknowledged my mistake. Their response? To offer me a partial refund so that I could purchase a new power adapter - something they obviously did not have to do. All this to say - if you’re thinking about buying this lamp, do it. I can assure you that the company stands by their product. And I will always recommend a company that goes above and beyond with their service, which this one absolutely did.

reviews.title: Great for big monitors, but overpriced for what you get
reviews.body: Solid monitor light, but probably not worth the price unless you have a huge screen This has been a nice addition to my desk setup. I chose it because, as you can probably tell, my monitor is massive (49 inches), and I needed something that would actually cover a decent portion of the screen. Pros: Brightness: This light really helped brighten up my space. My office tends to be pretty dark, so it’s been great for overall visibility and eye comfort. Size & Flexibility: I love how large it is and that I can move it around to get the angle I want. Quality: It feels well-made and doesn’t look cheap at all. (To be fair, this is the only monitor light I’ve tried, so I don’t have a ton to compare it to.) Cons: Price: Even though the build quality is solid, I still don’t get how this costs over $50. It’s just white and warm light with brightness adjustments. No RGB, no standout features. If you don’t have a large curved monitor like mine, I’d say go with a cheaper one that offers more features. Remote only: This part is wild to me. There are zero controls on the light itself. Everything depends on the remote. So if you misplace it, you’re basically out of luck. Final thoughts: Overall, the light works well, and the size is perfect for my ultra-wide monitor. I just think it’s overpriced for what it is. If you specifically need the large size and basic lighting, it’s a good pick. But if not, there are more affordable options out there with better features.

reviews.title: The best
reviews.body: Excellent. One of the best deck lamps in this segment that I’ve ever used. Not a single cent wasted. The weight, mounting system, and especially the quality of the long flexible arm (it’s light but holds its shape confidently) are impressive after trying many other cheap (and not-so-cheap) mounts. The brightness and light quality are finally sufficient for painting — I’m an artist, and this one lamp alone is enough. I no longer need to turn on additional light sources to work comfortably on smaller formats. It seems the manufacturer, unlike most others, uses powerful new-generation LEDs here. The lighting is well-designed, with high build quality and adjustable color temperature. The wireless remote is excellent — very convenient, high-quality, and you definitely won’t lose it or spend time searching for it. Fantastic ergonomics. I’ve been using the lamp for six weeks now and just decided to write this review because I can confidently recommend it to anyone who values high-quality workspace lighting — at a price four times cheaper than professional equivalents. The only thing worth noting is that the working part of the lamp gets warmer than similar models with cheaper LEDs, but it’s not a problem — it’s just warm, not hot, and the plastic housing is also of very high quality.

reviews.title: Great lighting solution for dual monitor setup

The brightness levels are great and make it easy to switch from screen work to writing or handling small parts on the desk without needing extra light. The gooseneck holds its position well once adjusted, and the remote is surprisingly responsive and handy. The build feels solid and I haven’t had any issues with it drifting or sagging. The various color temperature settings also help a lot depending on the time of day. If you're not looking for something that eliminates every shadow like a photography setup, this light does the job for 99% of daily work needs. Definitely a solid buy for any home office or study space.

reviews.title: Great quality, worth the price
reviews.body: I think this is a great product. I needed something for work that helped ease my eye strain due to light sensitivity. When searching for a monitor light I saw that there were many less expensive options available, however I went with this one because of the reviews and multiple settings (4-5 brightness levels, yellow lighting or bright lighting, timer, etc.). It is working great so far and I am really impressed. I really appreciate the very easy and functional touch settings pad that is battery operated and not attached to the light fixture itself. This allows me to keep it close by and adjust the settings when necessary. I also really like that the lights tilt so I can have them directly projecting onto my screen or I can turn them around to bounce off my cubicle wall, allowing for a more soft overhead light. I recently purchased a different model from a computer store that was on sale for $17 (single light, not double like this one) for my home computer, and it just does not compare. It feels cheaper and does not come with the same settings as this one. I have learned to buy quality items that I will only have to buy once versus less expensive items that require replacing more often. This light feels heavy duty and does an amazing job.

reviews.title: A decent desk lamp
reviews.body: I like that this desk lamp has a small footprint and can be placed off to the side, out of the way, but then using the gooseneck the light can be brought in where it is needed. I also like that it is quite bright and can be dimmed from low light to full output. The light color itself can be adjusted between 3 levels, warm, cool or a mix of warm and cool. I personally prefer the white cool light as it seems like a better color for a work light. I don’t use the ambient sensor function so can’t comment. The base is heavy and holds the lamp without tipping even when the gooseneck is cantilevered far out. There is a light diffuser on the end of the lamp shade which can be removed if you want the full blast harsh light, which may be more useful in some situations. There is a usb charger port. The dimming control is a little funky and the click stops were not expected. I would rather have a smooth silent dimmer than one with detents. Also the range of lowest light to highest light is not very wide. Nevertheless, at this price point there isn’t much to complain about. This is a nice bright lamp with more functionality than one would expect at such a low price and seems well made. It is recommended.

reviews.title: Iluminación inteligente y versátil para cuidar la vista en cualquier espacio de estudio o trabajo
reviews.body: Disponer de una fuente de iluminación adaptable, respetuosa con la salud visual y capaz de ofrecer múltiples opciones de configuración resulta fundamental para optimizar las horas de lectura, trabajo o estudio en casa. Esta lámpara de escritorio avanzada ofrece una solución sumamente práctica y versátil para iluminar cualquier superficie con total comodidad y precisión. Análisis de calidad El artículo destaca por una sólida construcción que integra setenta y ocho diodos emisores de luz de alta eficiencia con una potencia de quince vatios, diseñada para proporcionar un rendimiento lumínico uniforme y duradero. Su estructura cuenta con un cuello de cisne flexible de cuarenta centímetros con giro completo, una base equipada con puertos de carga USB tipo A y tipo C, y un sistema de control dual que incluye botones táctiles y un práctico mando a distancia. Experiencia de uso Gracias al cuello de cisne de 360 grados, el cono de luz se puede ajustar exactamente a la posición que se desee, y la combinación de diferentes temperaturas de color y niveles de brillo garantiza un trabajo extremadamente agradable y agradable a la vista, tanto si se concentra en la pantalla por la noche como si está leyendo. Los puertos USB integrados para cargar dispositivos, así como el práctico mando a distancia y el modo nocturno, también son puntos a favor en el uso diario. reviews.title: Needs a heavier base for maximum positioning. Good desk light.
reviews.body: This is a lightweight desk lamp. The base of the lamp is covered in a felt material. The head of the light can be easily rotated so it can swivel left and right and the flexible arm is coated in a soft silicone material and bends easily. It also maintains the position you bend it into and doesn't sag since the head of the light is relatively light. The button controls are not individual buttons, they're plastic bubble buttons. Once the flexible arm is connected, it cannot be removed. The back of the lamp is just a plastic housing, no metal there to help dissipate heat, but even so I found that the back of the light only got slightly warm even at maximum brightness. Not even warm enough to be used as a hand warmer. The light has 5 brightness levels and the light is a very even diffuse light pattern and a wide cast area. The light output at maximum is quite bright, but not bright enough to over saturate printed material which would make it unreadable. The night light mode provides a much dimmer light output than is achievable with the brightness controls. It works very well as a night light. By default when pressing the night light button, the color temperature is warm. You can cycle through the other color temperatures after selecting night light mode. In order to get out of night light mode, you need to increase the brightness. When you turn the light off and turn it back on, it will remember which mode it was in last and use the same mode as it was in when it was turned off, this also applies to the night light mode, not just the brightness and color temperature. The brightness of the light isn't controlled via PWM, so it is flicker free. The 4 LEDs on the base illuminate to tell you which timer setting you're on. Due to the fact that the base is very lightweight and doesn't have any heft to it, you cannot move the head of the light too far away from the base. If you do, the imbalance of the weight will just cause the light to fall over. Also accidental bumps can knock it over easily. A heavier weighted base would help a lot here to allow for maximum range of positioning. I have another old fashioned halogen bulb desk lamp and it has a very heavily weighted base even though the head is lighter than this unit's head and it has very good stability as a result. The remote is a wireless remote and not an IR remote so there's no need to point it at the lamp to use it. I tested it, and it has very good range, going through 3 walls with ease. The base has a felt layer on the bottom providing some grip to keep it from easily sliding around. Although there is a USB-A and USB-C ports on the back, you need to provide your own cables. Included is a 12V/2A barrel connector power adapter, however it isn't UL or ETL certified, but then again neither is the lamp.

reviews.title: Just what I was looking for!
reviews.body: I'll be honest. I was looking for something in my local brick and mortar stores. Target, Walmart, Home Depot, Lowes... every place let me down because they all had the same unimaginative junk. And certainly not in store so I can just go get it. I have a pretty deep computer desk with dual 27" monitors on moving arms. I also have a separate soldering table. I wanted good, shadow free illumination on both and nobody had anything that would work. Lo and behold, I stumble across this on Amazon. I love when someone has a good idea and turns it into a great product. Unboxing is just ridiculously easy. There is no building. All you have to do is screw clamp it to your surface and plug it in. It seems it'll fit a pretty thick surface too. 1 1/8" (almost 3cm) thick shelf stock for a desk and it has enough space for another inch or so. No flickering that I can see. It's clean smooth light. The color temperature options are plentiful and you can cycle through presets of both temp and brightness or do a smooth transition to what you want. The side panels are separately turned on and off (together) and can fold down 90° (if you really wanted to) or all the way up to upside down on top of the main lamp. It's all folded together in the box, so just unfold and use. Only real issue is there's no telescoping function. So if you have a small desk and want it mounted at the back AND close to your surface, you might have to get creative. The auto brightness is interesting... it gets brighter when the ambient light goes down. I expected the opposite. But maybe this makes sense. I prefer manual control anyway. Overall, very great product for anyone working at a desk, writing, making, what have you. I love this thing already. There's a really good video review that will show you all you need to know. I bought two right then and there (for both tables) and I do not regret my decision at all.

reviews.title: It's Mostly Wonderful

You can control the brightness or illumination of each type of element, so that the arms that are pointed up can have light, while the ones pointed down can be dimmed or turned off altogether to prevent glare. The brightness starts as very dim and goes all of the way up to very bright (with some glare), and many steps in between. Nice! All in all, I've had this lamp for over a month now, and haven't noticed any defects or bad design, except for the slight wobble. It's great if you like to have a room for computer use while having the ability to light the whole room without glare. That's why I give it a '5'.

reviews.title: Simple lamp with a great selection of colors.
reviews.body: I see a lot of confusion about this product. The directions aren’t very descriptive, . 1. This product does have different color lights . 2. You can turn the color cycling off so that it stays on whatever color you desire. 3. You are able to adjust the brightness, there are three levels The thing to keep in mind is you navigate this one button device with the timing of your button presses. A long 3 second tap will turn it on and off. The default when you turn it on is the white color. The white is not too cool, nor too warm. You can adjust the brightness and at the highest level it is plenty bright if you need to find something in the room. I don’t think it will adequately light a large dark room on its own. But you can read using this light if you are within a few feet of the lamp (for most people). . If you want to change to the color setting, then a quick one second tap after the device is turned on. At this point, you will be on the color cycling mode. if you do nothing, the device will cycle through various shades of green, blue, red, yellow, etc. For example, you will see a turquoise blue, a cornflower blue, a hot pink, a pale green, etc. If you want to select a particular color, wait until it cycles to the color you like, and use a one second tap to select. This will pause it on the color that was lit when you tapped the button. If you want to turn the device off, just press the button for three seconds. You will have to repeat the process every time you turn the device on, It isn’t very resource-intensive so I wouldn’t let that deter you unless you are picky and this is a dealbreaker. I’m sure more expensive units have more robust memories, settings, and remote controls with more than one button to navigate. Only two items come in the box, the lamp (which is roughly 7” tall, and 4” wide at the base) and the power cord (which is not infuriatingly short) so setup is easy.. There’s no charging or batteries required. So far I like it and plan to keep it. I have insomnia, and read about light therapy. When I’m ready to sleep, I plan to change the color to an Amber/orangey/pink color to mimic the sunset to tell my body it’s time to get tired and go to sleep. I just received it, so cannot speak to longevity. I always come back and edit reviews if anything changes. If it stops working, I’ll update with a date so you’ll know how long mine lasted. Hope this helps! Edit : 6/1/24 I wanted to amend this review to specify that the color portion of this lamp is not dimmable. This may present an issue if someone is trying to use a color To fall asleep as I mentioned I was using this for. I agree that the lamp is very bright for colors. To fix this, I use a Small canvas bag I received with another product over it. I can still see the color and the lamp but it is much less less bright. If I didn’t have that bag I would use a scarf or some other type of lightweight fabric over it to use it for nighttime.

reviews.title: This lamp has a secret feature (a glowing review)
reviews.body: This lamp was purchased on 12/6/2025 for $18.99. The quality is more than adequate, but the lamp is very lightweight and definitely not what I would consider a premium product, however it looks good and functions well for the price that I paid. On the lamp that I received which is the model with a cord (not rechargeable) I can touch and hold the top control panel when the lamp is off, and it will come on in an ultra low mode which I absolutely love! Other than that if you were just to tap the top when the lamp is off there there are 3 brightness levels to cycle through with each tap: Low, Medium and High. The light that emits from this lamp is soft, the color temperature is pleasant and leans warm which for me is a great thing. To get to the colored mode you must press and hold on the top of the lamp while the white light is on and then tap the top to start/stop it from slowly cycling through the spectrum of colors, ie once it lands on your favorite color give the top panel a tap and it will freeze there on that color. The lamp also remembers that color too so the next time you enter color mode by holding down on the top panel it will come on directly to that last color which was used. I wish the brightness could be controlled when in the color mode but it cannot. I would guess that the brightness when in color mode is factory set to be somewhere around Medium and is not dimmable or adjustable in any way when in color mode which could obviously appear brighter to your eye depending on which color you have landed on or that the lamp is currently cycling through (if you just leave it continually and slowly flowing from one color to the next in a mostly smooth and seamless fashion). So far this is a nice, cheap and attractive bedside lamp.

title: Govee RGBIC Smart Table Lamp 2, Touch Bedside Small Table Lamp (Corded)

reviews.title: Perfect Desk Lamp for My Home Office
reviews.body: The Govee RGBIC Smart Table Lamp 2 has been another great addition to my growing Govee ecosystem. I bought it for my home office desk, and it fits the space perfectly. The lighting is bright, vibrant, and easy to customize. I like being able to switch between clean white light while I’m working and colorful lighting when I’m gaming or just relaxing. The RGBIC effects look fantastic, and the app makes it simple to create different scenes and automations. Since I already have several Govee products throughout my home, this lamp integrated seamlessly into my existing setup. Everything works together flawlessly through the Govee app, making it easy to control all of my lighting from one place. The build quality feels premium, and the modern design looks great on my desk without taking up much space. If you’re already invested in the Govee ecosystem—or you’re looking for a high-quality smart desk lamp—this is an easy recommendation. It’s been one of my favorite additions to my home office.

reviews.title: Fun lamp with great preset modes
reviews.body: This is such a fun little lamp. The colors are bright, it looks great, and I really like having all the different preprogrammed lighting modes to choose from. It makes it easy to change the mood of the room without having to spend time adjusting everything manually. My favorite feature is definitely the music sync. It reacts to the music really well and makes the whole setup feel a lot more lively, especially if you have people over or just want some ambient lighting while listening to music. The app is easy enough to use, and there are plenty of options if you want to customize things beyond the presets. Overall, it looks good, works well, and is just a genuinely fun addition to the room.

reviews.title: Love it, love it, love it...!
reviews.body: What can I say. It's a govee, and has all the variety and quality that name possesses. Excellent ease of programming. Bright colors. Touch control and app running device, has a great fit on my TV stand, and seems made of a superior material, doesn't appear flimsy, at all.

reviews.title: Bought 2
reviews.body: I already own a few Govee products, so I decided to give this smart bedside lamp a try. I really needed a new bedside lamp, so I figured I’d test it out—and I’m so glad I did. I ended up loving it. The brightness is excellent. It can get very bright at 100%, but you can also dim it down as much as you want, which is perfect for nighttime use. I was pleasantly surprised by how many different settings it has. I’ve used the Govee app before with my monitor backlight, but the features on this lamp feel completely different and much more immersive. There are so many fun modes—like fire-like flames, fireflies floating around, night sky effects, and soothing ambient lights. One of my favorite features is that you can actually draw in the app and have your drawing show up on the lamp. It feels creative and playful, not just functional. I was so satisfied with this lamp that I bought one for my sister, and I’m planning to get one for my parents as well. Great quality, great features, and amazing value for the price. Highly recommend.

reviews.title: I'm 35 or 36 and I love this lamp ☺️🥰😅
reviews.body: 😃🥰 This thing honestly cheers me up every day☺️ its only been 1 week and im still gushing over how cute and fun this lamp is😃 PROS: • Clean, modern, smooth curves. I love that the branding logo is at least blended in nicely and not tacky.. pretty minimal. Not tacky. • I LOVE the DIY functions. Choosing your own colors from the color wheel is awesome. There are many colors to choose from ! #1 reason for buying this lamp was the DIY functions 🥰 • Price was okay, but still a bit steep. I bought 2 for a total of 162$ ... (you got a deal if you bought 2) 80 bucks is a bit steep still... even with all this lamp does. I would not pay more than 80 for this lamp... especially because it's not cordless like the updated one. • I love that they update the app with new options for preset scenes! I didn't even expect that and then I saw new ones appear one day. • I love that you can dim the background color in the DIY Sketch section. Helps a lot with night time chill time... plus looks great paired with bright colors in contrast to the dimmed background. I'm an adult female and I have so much fun playing with this lamp. All in all I LOVE this lamp. The cons/improvements I list below, are just me being very critical of the color limitation. CONS / Improvements • I wish you could get deeper colors.. like a deep striking red, a basic 'green crayon' green, a forest green... etc but it's just not possible. The greens are lime green to aqua. The reds aren't red, they are hot pink to coral pink even on the reddest setting. • The lamp is very bright, even on its lowest 1% setting. I can't have these on at night when I'm sleeping... which is kind of a bummer. Sometimes we have to turn them off when we're watching tv at night too, because theyre just so bright. Even the various sleep preset scenes that do have darker dimmed colors.. it's still quite bright. *** Correction though ... I found in the DIY Sketch that you can actually dim the main background color. Huge plus ! Now night time wont be so bright and I can really make other colors pop against the dimmed background. • Wish it were cordless of course, but I am sure they will make a cordless version since they already did with the Table Lamp Pro JBL speaker one. Hopefully they keep these ones smaller like they are but make them cordless. • For the preset 'scene settings' ..... you can't actually change the colors to anything you want. For the ones you CAN customize (there are a few you 100% can not) There is a list of 8 different color "combos" to choose from. If you don't like a color used in any of those 8 color combos, you cant do anything about it. So for my favorite scene settings, I can only use that scene if I use one of the 8 pre set options provided for that scene. This is shown on one of my review photos. However, I have recreated some of the "preset scenes" using the DIY/Sketch function. That enables me to use whatever colors I choose.. but still there are limitations around this. For example, the "Fire" Preset Scene, you can't choose other colors for that fire movement scene at all. Which sucks. It would look very cool in other colors. *** EDIT --- I stand corrected after exploring some more. In the DIY section, you do have "fire" as an effect and you can change the color of it... including various colors it will morph into. It just doesnt show on the actual 'fire' preset scene. Very happy to have realized this ☺️ • The Ai function is super cool.. and I know it works awesome on their other products such as their light panel or curtain lights... this one has limitations only because of the inability to use darker or duller color. For example in my last photo you can see I asked for a moody greyish blue sky... slate grey/slate dull blue would have been awesome with white clouds... but it can't do those colors (slate greyish blue). HOWEVER now that I know I can dim the background significantly in the DIY section, I can maybe pull this off. Finding a way to realllyy have "millions" of colors to choose from would be great. I'm being really picky here lol I do love the color options it does have. 😍🥰 With most variations of any color on the DIY color wheel, outside of the most obvious variations, the difference is barely barely noticeable, even if on the app they show as very different shades or tints of blue, there is barely a difference once on the lamp...... Though there often IS a difference. You can see the slight change when you switch back and forth, for the most part. You get a lot of pink, since the entirety of the red are variations of pink.. plus the actual entire pink section. Much of the "purples" are actually fuschia pink. You have to go very blue to get a regular "purple". There are way less variations of green, purple, yellow. Green for example, there is only lime green and quickly goes to aqua, or yellow on the other side. Basic green crayon color would be awesome. Purple usually looks more blue or fuschia.. depending what colors you pair it with it or whether purple is totally by itself. Or if you dim the background color, your 'purple'(fuschia) will probably turn more towards actual purple. When I use a red background, (which shows hot hot reddish pink to orangey red.. never real red).... i can get a purple heart on it by making the heart blue. It then shows up purple. So there are tricks. ☺️ I am really happy with the custom colors though despite these few limitations haha I'm making it sound worse than it is. It's an awesome lamp. 🥰 I wish I could draw/sketch white and grey mountains... like light grey with contrasting dark grey and slate grey, with white tips mountains. I will play around with it some more though, because in the DIY "Fire" effect, I see some 'slate' greys possible be used. So it seems possible? Another example of this limitation: 🎅🎄Christmas colors.. there are none. ... Since red is hot pink and green is lime green. So the preset christmas scenes do not give christmas vibes at all. Same with the Halloween... purple is never purple enough unless you have zero colors near it... or place enough blue next to fuschia to turn the fuschia a nice purple. The halloween presets that have orange and purple next to eachother, the purple never shows well enough to look Halloweeny. In my opinion. St Patricks Day Preset Scenes are capable of lime green only... Other than that, These lamps are so awesome. 😁 I'm totally buying more Govee products 😏😛 I ordered the Uplighter off their website just days after I bought these lamps😛 One small annoyance is I ordered from the Govee website 5 days ago and my uplighter still isnt here. I went through the website bc it was on sale for 170 + an extra 8$ off coupon code....... 5 days later today the lamp is here on Amazon on sale for 160..... So I could have got the lamp within 24hrs had I been able to use Amazon but they lagged 5 days on matching their amazon store sale to their website sale. Hopefully it arrives today.
