A partir de ese día, la Instant Porridge se ha convertido en el desayuno estrella de la casa. Prueba 6: Caldo de pollo (Opción: Soup/Broth). Intente hacer un caldo de pollo a presión, y un éxito mas. En esta época trabajando en casa, la IP ha sido una gran aliada pues no tengo la preocupación de que la comida se va a quemar mientras estoy en alguna junta. He hecho platos que nunca me había animado a cocinar (p. ej. mole de olla con costilla cargada y suadero), y he optimizado mi tiempo en la cocina con platos con los que normalmente tendría que estar pendiente como frijoles, lentejas o arroz. Todo lo que me decían mis amigas era cierto. Vale completamente la pena y recomiendo encarecidamente a toda persona que busque cocinar de manera eficiente en espacios y tiempos optimizados.

reviews.title: Gran inversión para la cocina
reviews.body: Gran inversión para la cocina, soy una persona muy ocupada y me gusta cuidar de mi salud me cocino, pero en los guisos y cocciones de frijoles se consume mucho gas , opté por esta olla que vi, ya hice mi primer caldo de res con verduras quedó la carne muy suave en poco tiempo ⏱️ me encantó, tiene muy buena seguridad para la presión. Lo que me encanta: ✔️ Cocina mucho más rápido que una olla convencional. ✔️ Tiene varias funciones, desde cocción a presión hasta salteado. ✔️ Es segura y fácil de limpiar. Lo que podría mejorar: 🔹 La curva de aprendizaje puede ser un poco alta al inicio, pero una vez que entiendes los tiempos y funciones, todo es sencillo. En general, es una excelente compra si quieres ahorrar tiempo en la cocina y hacer recetas deliciosas sin complicaciones. ¡La recomiendo totalmente!

reviews.title: Me encantó !!!
reviews.body: Llevo más de 1 año con esta olla y consideró que ha sido la mejor compra !!! La olla es de acero por lo q no se raya ni desprende como entes tóxico, los tiempos de cocción están bien establecidos en cada botón. Hagi desde ensaladas al vapor hasta carnes asadas y frijoles !! Muy buena

title: Instant Pot Pro 6 Qt 10-in-1 Electric Pressure Cooker, Black

reviews.title: Large stainless steel pot with handles is awesome!
reviews.body: My previous insta pot was a 6qt non-stick pot. I really enjoyed that pot. But many times I wished it was a little bigger. And getting the pot out of the unit was a bit dicy, you have to use pot holders for the heat and it could slip out of your hands. However I also became concerned about the non-stick coating on the pot. I had put a couple of scratches on the bottom so I was concerned about the coating. Enter this new pot. Very nice 8 qt size. I actually thought 8 qt might be too big but on my first use I almost filled it up, so it's not too big. The stainless steal pot is awesome and the handles make it very easy to lift out(without pot holders) and I dont feel like it's going to slip out of my hands. First use was a stew and it came out great. I did wash it in the dishwasher before use. I found the silicon seal to be hard to put back onto the lid, I had to use a little water as a 'lubricant' to get it to slip back into place. There are LOTS of options on this thing.....it took me a couple minutes just to pick one for the stew and I finally picked the 'slow cook' option which took six hours....but it was worth the wait....the meat was very tender and the potatoes and carrots were just right, not too soft and not too hard......by the way, if you shop Walmart, the organic carrots taste way better than the regular carrots......I just buy a bag of organic petite and dump them in....this time I also added a bag of frozen mushrooms and that was great.....too many times I buy fresh mushrooms and forget to use them within a day or two and have to chuck them. 10/17/25 update Still loving this pot....the only issue I have is the silicone pressure ring can be difficult to put back in place. To show how large it is, just now I put in a whole 3 lb bag of potatoes, a whole chopped up celery bunch, a large onion, 8 oz of fresh mushrooms, bag of carrots, 64oz of chicken stock and about 2 lbs of chicken......I put it on an option for 6 hours of 'slow cook'......the slow cook option is pretty cool.....

reviews.title: Worth the extra money over the less expensive Instant Pots
reviews.body: My first IP started having some display issues after about 5 years, so I decided to replace it since I use it just about every weekend. The replacement arrived with a dent in the side, and I worked with Amazon and received a partial refund, but it never seemed to cook well. I was constantly getting a burn notice, and I was never comfortable with the dented outer casing, so I decided to replace it again after about 1 year. I decided to not buy a less expensive model this time and spent the extra money on the Instant Pot Pro. So glad I did! The differences are very noticeable and appreciated. The slots to hold the lids are positioned at 10 and 2, which makes it much easier to work with than on the lower cost models where it is at 9 and 3. The display is much more informative, and I really love having more control over the heat when sauteing. The handles on the inner pot are a great addition. The inner pot stays level and doesn’t move around when you’re stirring so it keeps the heat even while sauteing. Also, it is easier to take in and out of the outer shell. Don’t get me wrong, the lower cost models like the DUO or the Rio are good machines. The Instant Pot Pro is just a much better device. I cooked with it last night for the first time and couldn’t believe it was possible to be MORE impressed with the Instant Pot. If you’re shopping for one and not sure which one to choose, the lower cost models are good, but the Pro is significantly better imo.

reviews.title: Wider is better
reviews.body: I recently upgraded my old pressure cooker to the Instant Pot, and I’m thrilled with the improvements. The most noticeable difference is the wider cooking area, which makes sauteing, stirring, and lifting the pot out much easier compared to my previous model. In terms of cooking efficiency, the Instant Pot has been a game-changer. The display clearly shows the current stage of the cooking process (preheating, cooking, releasing), eliminating any guesswork. Additionally, the pressure release is significantly quieter and less messy than the older units I’ve used, which is a major upgrade that I didn’t anticipate. Cleaning up is also a breeze. The stainless steel exterior makes it easy to wash, and I appreciate not having to keep extra pans around since most tasks can be completed in one pot. However, there’s a minor downside: the Instant Pot takes up some counter or cabinet space, and there’s a slight learning curve if you’re new to the Instant Pot menus. But after a few uses, it becomes intuitive, and the time and effort saved are well worth it. Overall, I’m incredibly happy with my purchase and highly recommend the Instant Pot to anyone looking for faster and easier home-cooked meals.

reviews.title: Why Don't You Have One Already?!
reviews.body: I upgraded from Instapot Duo to the Pro. The fact the Instapot Pro has handles makes a world of different. On the Duo it is was a pain pulling the pot out and straining it while hot. On top of that it inner-pot of this "Pro" has a heavy bottom making a great is steel pot, so it just work like a normal pot on the stove top giving me the options in using either the electrical device or on the stove top. When in doubt get the 6 qt, is fits most things for a 1-4 person household (I'd argue even 6). Might not hold a Large whole chicken, but I manage by being able to breakdown a whole chicken (it isn't hard, just watch a video) I cook professionally. But at home the Instapot is the best appliance I've gotten. I make Bean from dried at a fraction of the time, amazing quality fresh stock that doesn't require me to to wait 8 hours on a stove top, it takes the place of crockpot, rice cooker (*), and a normal pot. Stews, Gumbo, Chili, and Braises are done greatly when you are pinch for time making what would normally for 5 hour is only an hour or two and near same quality. Which has saved me during a dinner party where my sous dropped braised short ribs 2 hours before plating. It is an investment but if you eat (or plan to eat) legumes/beans, and you use stock/broth occasionally or consistently in your diet. This will save you some money and time while giving you a better product than store-bought stock/broth and canned beans. Both the beans and stock you make freeze well, and cooked frozen bean reheat/thaw fast. And if you freeze veggie scrap (like onion skin, carrot/parsnip peel, celery tops and bottoms) as well and save bones from you chicken (rotisserie, chicken thigns, or whole chicken) you can make stock with all the stuff you were going to throw way anyway. Better than store bought while also being basically free. Lastly it is great for meal prep and you can set it to have your ingredients in it before leaving to work and being done by the time you get home from work. If you cook consistently for yourself and/or for loved ones, or want to cook more at home. An Instapot makes thing easy at a press of a button, and the Pro has very convent features (like HANDLES I cant praise enough!) that make life much more easy. When you get one you will ask also ask "Why didn't I get one sooner?". I work late nights and early morning, this gives me more time and saves me from eating out. ~*I've mentioned "rice cooker" and I want to expand on this.~ The Instapot works great as a rice cooker but compared to an actual rice cooker, it is a little slower to cook (20min vs 30-35min) and the rice (especially short-grain/sushi rice) builds starch and stick to the stainless steel pot, requiring a slight bit more finesse to clean. I personally eat rice (and grains) consistently and i like saving 10-15min of what little time I have at home, so i have both a cheap rice cooker and instapot. However if you want to minimize your appliances (i.e. have less "appliance clutter") and need to conserve space in your kitchen, then having just an Instapot will work well enough and do every thing a rice cooker can, plus much MUCH more.

reviews.title: Excellent Multi-Cooker – A Must-Have!
reviews.body: I absolutely love this Instant Pot! It’s incredibly easy to use and has made cooking so much faster and more convenient. The food comes out delicious every time, whether I’m making rice, soups, chicken, or even yogurt. It heats evenly, saves time, and the quality is excellent. The large capacity is perfect for meal prep or family dinners. Highly recommended for anyone looking for a reliable and versatile kitchen appliance!

reviews.title: If you wish your IP was wider and spits less on pressure release - this is for you!
reviews.body: I’m a long time Instant Pot user and have bought many upgrades over the years. I was attracted to this new RIO Wide because, you guessed it, it’s wide. I do a lot of sautéing as well as cooking larger bone in chicken breasts, which aren’t as convenient in the standard narrow tall 6 qt IP. I also wanted to steam larger vegetables like 5-8 ears of corn on the cob. For the functional bits - it surpassed my expectations. I cook 5 ears of corn on the cob regularly now in this guy. They are very easy to get out with tongs with the lower height of the device. The settings are a perfect variety and the controls are easy to read and configure. I’ve cooked a half chicken in there after browning it first with the wide cooking surface. It turned out tender and delicious. The chimes at ends of cycles are melodious and make me smile - not the harsh beeping of older models. Steam release is exceptional - both super quiet and without wet spitting that you can get with older IPs. That alone has made it my go to IP. It is larger, so if you want to store it, you will need some space for that. I just leave mine on the kitchen island because I use it all the time. The lid is wide, so you can’t slot it into those IP slots that hold the lid on smaller models. This just means you need to be careful to drain any liquid caught in the lid into the pot when you remove it so you don’t drip it across your counter/electronics. Because of the width, the steam trivet is very easy to remove when it is hot. That’s something I struggled with a bit on my older, narrow IP. Stir fries are a dream to cook in this cooker. It feels very safe from steam burns due to the backward facing steam vent and the steam release buttons location far in front of that vent. I’ve put the lid in the dishwasher, which held up well. But mostly I clean stuck on food bits with some Lemi Shine citric acid on high pressure for 3 minutes and a soak in that overnight. That leaves the pan looking brand new as you can see in the photo. If you were debating whether you needed this IP in your collection, I can assure you that you do.

reviews.title: BUYER BEWARE..SLOW COOK DOESN'T WORK...ZERO CUSTOMER SERVICE
reviews.body: I we'll start this by saying if I could give this product zero stars or negative stars, I would. Absolutely. I have tried to order this product FOUR times. Amazon will not let me individually review this item for each one of those purchases, although they are different experiences. The first time Amazon sent me a defective product with a broken lid and a damaged body (I knew that I was purchasing it from the Amazon sell, but I had no idea it was gonna be unusable) My second order was with a Christmas gift card for a brand new product. I purchased the 8 qt "pro" as an upgrade from my current duo nova instant pot. I have enjoyed that product, although I do get an error code fairly frequently stating that the pot is the wrong size for the base… Instant pot told me that there is no fix for this I just need to order a brand new pot which I refuse to do so I fidget with it and it will work. Anyway, the brand new 8 quart would not come up to temperature on the slow cook function. I let it sit for four hours and it was still preheating and the food inside was raw. I had to take the food out and cook it in the oven. I sent the pot back The third time I ordered a 6 quart instant pot pro which looked beautiful, but had the exact same problem. There was also a problem getting the lid to come off the pot I had to take a butter knife and push down the steam release so that the lid would release and allow me to remove it even when I was not using the pressure cook mode. The slow Cook function absolutely would not preheat I did an experiment by putting water in the pot and turning it on for eight hours in the morning with no food in it and it never came up to temperature. Seven hours later it was still blinking preheat and the water inside was like 150°F. I contacted instant pot and they wanted me to do this almost tremendous task of taking a video showing the problem taking several photographs explaining the context of the problem blah blah blah blah. I said no I am just going to send it back until I can get one that actually works. That brings me to my fourth and final order of the instant pot Pro 6 qt. I know that it will shock you, but I had the exact same problem. I could not believe it. I looked it up online (as I should have done in the first place)and found that this is a common problem with this product. It just will not come up to heat on slow cook. One YouTube video said that it takes hours for this particular model to come up to temperature and you will need to have an instant thermometer handy so that you can check your food every few hours to ensure that it's actually cooking appropriately. I don't know about you, but when I slow cook food it is my expectation that that food is going to cook, even if I am out working in my garden or running a quick errand to the store. Why would I be on standby for eight hours when I can probably cook it in the oven in one or two and have a somewhat consistent result? Well, I did contact instant pot (again) and they required me to send photographs, and an explanation, and the whole rigmarole, which I did this time only to get a reply just a couple hours later where I was told the same thing : if you were going to cook something on slow cook it can take up to four hours to preheat on a longer cook. My reply back to instant pot was that several sites on the Internet know that there is a problem with the instant pot pro in that the slow Cook function does not work correctly. The Internet knows that this is a flaw. Amazon is becoming aware that this is a flaw. And I believe that instant pot knows that this is a flaw yet they refuse to either correct the problem or honor their warranty. I am sad to say that I will never buy another instant pot product after the runaround that I was given by this company, who refused to assist me, will not honor the warranty, made excuses for a faulty product, and ultimately just basically said if you don't like it go return it (literally). So I am. GOOD NEWS-- UPS will pick it up for free.

reviews.title: No PRO but good enough
reviews.body: I think Instant Pot are going backwards. I bought the original (or an early model) back when they became the 'thing' a few years ago. It worked great for many years. Eventually though the pressure seal wouldn't hold so it was time to 'upgrade'. I got this version thinking it would be better, it is labelled 'PRO' after all. The reality is it's a step backwards in many ways. The good: I like the look, it certainly looks PRO and the steam release guard (aka a cap) and the switch to release the steam are welcomed additions. The handles are great and definitely help when you're wanting to lift out a pot full of boiling hot chicken stock. The display works well and there are other features like a beep reminder incase you missed the original beep when the cooking finished. I also love the ability to save favourites, extremely useful especially when considering one of the Pro's flaws. The bad: The interface of this is a big step back from the previous generation Instant Pot that this replaced. It feels like the mini computer inside this struggles to keep up with what you're asking it to do, especially when it comes to setting a time. The lag of the timer as you turn the dial is awful. And as you're adjusting the timer there is a constant beeping sound which is just really annoying. You can actually turn off the sound but that also stops all the useful notifications like when your food is cooked so there's not really a good solutions here (besides being able to set a common time / pressure combo as a favourite which helps). They also changed the Yoghurt setting so my previous sweet spot of 9 1/2 hours like the older model no loner worked. With this Pro model it was taking 16+ hours to make a quite awful yoghurt. After a little research I found out the temperature of its default setting is 42° which is too low. I bumped it up to around 45° and now I get my great yoghurt in 9 1/2 hours again. I have no idea why they changed this but fortunately I have saved this setting as another favourite and no longer use their setting. Overall, besides those quirks, the Instant Pot Pro does all the things you would expect from an Instant Pot. The handles are very useful and I can't imagine going back to the handle-less pots. The interface is tolerable but should be better at this price point. And the changed cooking programs can be avoided by saving your preferred versions (though there are only 5 favourite slots).

reviews.title: Eficacia, Sabor, Tranquilidad sin mucho esfuerzo!
reviews.body: Compré la Instant Pot y genuinamente fue una de las mejores decisiones para mi cocina. La uso varias veces por semana y me ha resuelto cosas que antes eran un dolor, sobre todo cuando la carne o el pollo están congelados. Literal: de congelador a plato servido, sin drama. Uno de los momentos donde más la amé fue en Navidad. Pude hacer la cena completa en aproximadamente 2 horas, cuando normalmente habría pasado toda la noche cocinando. Carnes suaves, bien cocidas, con sabor, sin estar pegada a la estufa ni estresada por tiempos. La presión funciona excelente, los resultados son consistentes y te da mucha tranquilidad saber que puedes cocinar incluso cuando no planeaste nada con anticipación. Es ideal para: pollo o carne congelada, guisos, caldos, arroz, comidas “de diario” y también para ocasiones especiales. Al principio intimidan un poco los botones, pero es cuestión de usarla un par de veces. Después se vuelve automática en tu rutina. Además, la olla interior es fácil de limpiar y el sistema de seguridad se siente muy confiable. No exagero cuando digo que me ahorra tiempo, energía y estrés. Si cocinas en casa y quieres resultados buenos sin pasar horas, vale totalmente la pena. La recomiendo sin dudar y definitivamente la volvería a comprar y de hecho estoy pensando comprar más tamaños :D.

reviews.title: Muito mais que uma panela de pressão
reviews.body: Produto ótimo. Panela interna de inox que pode ser retirada e usada no fogão. Facilita limpeza e vai durar para sempre. Faço iogurte em potes em banho Maria toda a semana. Pasteurizei ovos inteiros com a função sous vide. Silenciosa quando usa pressão, que funciona maravilhosamente.

reviews.title: A SOLID PURCHASE
reviews.body: After my previous Instantpot stopped working one day. It was time for a new one. This one I chose as it had sous vide function. I have used this function twice now. I am quite impressed with it I must say. This Instantpot has ten functions. It is bigger than my precious one at 8qt. While I don’t cook for many I do not regret choosing the bigger version. What I enjoy about this particular Instantpot is the following: -The steam release is so much more easy to use. Just slide down to open and slide up to close. -The stainless steel liner with handles is the best update to this device ever. Silicone handles make it so easy to remove a scorching hot pot. -As with my previous pot this one has the dial to adjust time, temp and such. So easy and handy. -the cord is attached rather than having to plug it in the pot each time. As of yet I haven’t use this Instantpot for anything else. I can’t imagine it be any less than my other Pot. One thing I can think of that I’m not so impressed with: -There is a small slot to slide one thickness of your cord in the back, to hold it. It is fairly useless as being able to hold more cord would have been so much more useful. Even a nice Velcro strap to fold the cord up would have been so much better. Is this InstantPot worth buying? It is in my opinion a solid buy. It has more than one use and is a well built product.

reviews.title: Great service by reseller
reviews.body: Product was working fine till unexpected malfunction happened. The Tokion team was then extremely helpful. Provided me multiple options for repair through warranty and when all solutions were exhausted, full refund was issued upon shipping back the item

reviews.title: Very convenient
reviews.body: The product demo was given by Mr. Zafar Khan. The demo was really good and detailed. Made things so much easier. And the product is really convenient and amazing to use. Must buy.

title: Instant Pot Duo Plus 6 Qt 9-in-1 Electric Pressure Cooker, Stainless Steel

reviews.title: good
reviews.body: This is a game changer! I use it almost every day. It makes cooking soups, stews, and rice incredibly fast and easy. The meat comes out so tender. The stainless steel inner pot is high quality and super easy to clean. Worth every penny!

reviews.title: Indispensable upgrade to the classic slow cooker
reviews.body: When my old slow cooker committed suicide (our neighbor's construction work caused the inner stoneware liner to leap off of the drying rack and shatter on the floor), I took advantage of the opportunity to upgrade to an Instant Pot. I'd been hearing so much about how fast and easy they make cooking. The first week I had it, I made a different recipe in it every night. Lasagna, macaroni and cheese, hearty mushroom and barley stew, and many others. We quickly realized that the Instant Pot cooks pasta completely differently from the regular method of boiling it. And it tastes amazing. The pasta cooks through completely, yet remains substantial to the bite. We cook all of our pasta in the Instant Pot now, even if it's just spaghetti, not a full meal. We've sautéed in it, steamed, pressure cooked, and even made rice. Everything came out perfectly. I think I'd prefer to sauté things on the stovetop, simply because I don't like reaching down into a hot pot to stir things. But if you're a college student with no stove, it gives you a great option for more styles of cooking. One helpful tip I'd add is when releasing the pressure valve, make sure your Instant Pot is well away from walls and windows. Otherwise, you'll have to clean starchy water stains off of them. Now, I make sure it's got plenty of clearance, and that there's nothing on the counter that I don't want getting wet, and it's fine. I just wipe up the moisture that condenses as part of kitchen cleanup. We love the instant pot so much, we haven't put it away since we got it! We use it a couple of times a week at least.

reviews.title: Makes Cooking Easier and Fun!
reviews.body: First time pressure cooking user and I was nervous. That being said, I’ve used this a dozen times now and I love it! Easy to use, and a great addition to a busy life. This instant pot makes the process of cooking so much better. Rice isn’t sticking to the bottom of the pot, the short ribs I cooked were tender, and the chicken breast I JUST cooked were juicy and cooked through! The size is big enough to cook 4x4 short ribs standing up, 2x big chicken breasts laying down (you can squeeze a 3rd). I also made stir fry rice in it easily. Easy to clean as well. I love it!

reviews.title: Why I bought the Instant Pot IP-DUO Plus60 9-in-1 Multi-Functional Pressure Cooker, 6 Qt
reviews.body: Instant Pot IP-DUO Plus60 9-in-1 Multi-Functional Pressure Cooker, 6 Qt - I've wanted a PC for a long time and have done a lot of research. I was originally leaning towards the PPCXL because that's what my cousin has, but I did some more research and ended with this one, waiting until the Duo Plus came out. So, since I'm the 4th reviewer, here's some of the thought process I went through in deciding to get the DUO Plus and also some thoughts on the IP vs the PPCXL and also other considerations on accessories, size, etc. So far, I've only had it a few days, but overall satisfied and plenty of online support for recipes and helping you decide the post PC for your needs. **Why I went with the Instant Pot (IP) duo60 Plus - Three new preset buttons - cake, egg, sterilize. It also had the yogurt function which other IP do, but not some of the other makes. Large LCD Screen with Digital Display Mute button for those beeps in the night when cooking yogurt etc. Plus / Minus button for both time and pressure Keep Warm Selector can be selected to on or off at anytime. Delay start of 24 hours and keep warm for 10 hours. Lid rest (right or left side) **Why I went with IP vs PPCXL - Food Grade 304 (15/8) stainless steel pot vs stainless steel with teflon coating. I felt I could scrub and treat the pot however I wanted and not worry about scratching and what utensils to not use. Yes, you can buy a replacement inner pot for a Teflon pot, but after I spend $100+ I really don't think I should have to buy a replacement inner pot. Some of the FB group users are fine with the Teflon pot, but there are also a lot of complaints, so it might be in the handling, but every Teflon pan I ever had eventually got tossed out because of the coating coming off. IP came with some of the accessories you pay for on the PPCXL. It had the trivet with handles, condensation collector, Rice Paddle & spoon and a couple intro guides/cookbooks. Free shipping for IP. PPCXL site wanted $29.99 Buttons weren't quite clear on PPCXL site so it made me think they were hiding lack of selection on preset buttons. Also, confusing on what you were buying - regular PPC or PPCXL. A lot of their verbiage refers to PPCXL, but not necessarily when you go select your items for your shopping cart. Yogurt Button - The IP has this and the PPCXL doesn't. The IP allows you to bring the milk to 185 in the IP, cool to 120 (I will be using the quick cool method in the sink) and then put in yogurt mode for incubation (8-12 hours). The PPCXL doesn't have this and you wrap it and put it in the oven. Warranty on IP is 1 year and I went with the Square Trade Warranty for 4 years for an additional $14.37. No deductible, no hidden fees, no shipping, transferable. PPC has 60 day money back/replacement. After that up to one year you have to pay $24.99 for shipping. Their extended warranty if $15 for 3 years. Slow Cooker Mode had a low, medium and high heat button. IP has a + and - sign to increase or decrease the time. Others you have to select a preset and keep pressing to increase, you can't decrease time. Overall ratings - IP 4.7 and PPCXL 4.1. I read through a lot of comments by verified buyers and the PPC owners seemed a lot more upset with customer service. I looked through a lot of Reviewers who do this for a living or at least blog and they leaned towards the IP. I messaged with the PPCXL people online and you can tell they've been coached for answers knowing what their down faults are and not really answering the question or referencing what you know is a negative. There are more IPs on the market and most recipes are geared towards it from a "preset button" perspective. IP has a left and right handle that will hold your lid tilted. I belong to a Pressure Cooker group - there are a lot of complaints about other manufacturer's instructions, quick start guide, etc. Lots of issues with lids locking, not pressurizing etc and I really don't see this for the Instant Pot family of PCs. **Sizing - I measured my crock pot which was 6 quart, so that's what I ordered. It's an OK size for 2 people, but since you can only fill it 2/3 full when cooking under pressure you should take that into consideration. I figure on a roast, I will do the meat first, then veggies. The 6 quart will hold four pint canning jars for sterilization. **Accessories - What else to buy? I got the OXO Good Grips steamer with extendable handle and a pack of 3-IP Rings color coded (dark for savory meats, orange for desserts and I will use the clear for yogurt). I had read they were dishwasher safe, but not 100% as they might keep flavors. On my next order I'm looking at 2 cookbooks (IP Electric Pressure Cooker Cookbook for $9 and IP Obsession for $12). There are plenty of Facebook Group pages you can join for recipes too and online reviewers. Just type in what you are making followed by "in a pressure cooker" or "in an IP". I'm also buying IP Silicone Mitts for easy removal of a hot pot since I will be making yogurt ($10). The only negative of the Instant Pot is you can't get a 10 quart and if I had a REALLY big family that would be the only reason, but based on the above, I would probably just buy a 2nd Instant Pot. I hope this is helpful. I did a lot of research and felt the need to share it. I will update this as I use it and get additional questions. 8/9/2017 update - I've been using my IP for a few months now. I use my steamer basket and trivet a lot. I make a "bowl" out of heavy duty foil and put on the trivet when making a whole chicken and it makes trivet clean-up easier. I bought an IP plain glass lid for slow cooker & yogurt mode. I don't use my extra rings cause I use my plain lid for yogurt, so no use to swap rings. I didn't get the silicone mitts. I realized I didn't need them. My inner pot doesn't get that hot on yogurt mode. I like the 2 cookbooks. I use Bar Keeper Friend to clean the pot. Still really happy with my IP-DUO Plus 60. I'm part of a FB PC group and I don't see complaints on the IP. Very happy with my purchase. 12/29/2017 update - So on Black Friday I bought the 3 qt Instant Pot because I felt like I need to have twins. It's a great size and great for sides and especially my 2 quart of yogurt I make at least weekly, so it doesn't tie up my 6 qt IP. We winter in FL and I was able to "sneak" the 6 qt into the truck and now I have the 3 qt here too. I made an entire Thanksgiving dinner for Christmas (Irma got in our way last month repairing) in the 2 pots. In future years, I'll prob just bring the 3 qt cause it fits better in my cabinets in the mobile home.

reviews.title: Pretty good, but saute stew meat on the stove or in small batches.
reviews.body: Am pleased overall with functionality and ease of use. Couple things to consider if you're on the fence: This relates to the saute feature only: if you're sauteing anything more than a medium onion or trying to brown a decent amount of cubed stew meat you should probably fire up a pan instead (or brown in smaller batches). It gets hot enough but seems to struggle STAYING hot enough and you'll risk overcooking whatever you're trying to brown. After you pressure cook a savory meal the lid gasket retains the smell so strongly that you'll think you forgot to wash the lid. Consider swapping the spare gasket (included) for sweet/rice type dishes. I've only had my instapot for a couple weeks so there might be a better way to deal with this. Otherwise it's a pretty solid purchase!

reviews.title: Instant Pot Duo Plus: Multifunctional Electric Pressure Cooker for Fast and Easy Cooking
reviews.body: The Instant Pot Duo Plus is one of those appliances that truly makes life easier in the kitchen. It combines several functions in one appliance: pressure cooker, slow cooker, rice cooker, steamer, yogurt maker, sauté function, sterilizer, and even sous vide cooking. This allows you to prepare a wide variety of recipes without needing multiple utensils.

reviews.title: Easy to use and secure
reviews.body: This Instant pot is great. The size is perfect for cooking for 6 people. I love the stainless steel pot and it has all the functions I need. Very secure and easy to use. Love it!

reviews.title: The Ultimate Kitchen Time-Saver!
reviews.body: The Instant Pot Duo Plus has completely transformed the way I cook! Having nine appliances in one saves so much counter space, and it makes preparing meals faster and more convenient than ever. Whether I'm pressure cooking soups and stews, slow cooking, steaming vegetables, making rice, or even preparing yogurt, it consistently delivers excellent results. The controls are intuitive, and the preset programs make it easy to cook a wide variety of meals with minimal effort. I especially appreciate how quickly it cooks while still producing tender, flavorful dishes. The stainless steel inner pot is durable, easy to clean, and holds up well with regular use. The build quality is excellent, and the safety features provide extra peace of mind while pressure cooking. Overall, this multicooker is a fantastic investment for busy households or anyone who enjoys cooking with less time and effort. It's versatile, reliable, and one of the most useful appliances in my kitchen. Highly recommended!

reviews.title: Outstanding and Informative Instant Pot Demo by Suman from hyderbad
reviews.body: I recently had the pleasure of attending an incredible Instant Pot demo by Suman, and I must say, it was an exceptional experience! Even though it was conducted through a video call, Suman's professionalism and expertise shone through, leaving me thoroughly informed and eager to start cooking with my Instant Pot. From the very beginning, Suman exuded enthusiasm and passion for the subject matter. His friendly demeanor and clear communication style made it easy to follow along and grasp the essential concepts. He began by introducing himself and setting the agenda for the session, ensuring that we knew exactly what to expect. Throughout the demonstration, Suman showcased an impressive depth of knowledge about the Instant Pot. He not only explained its various features and functions but also provided practical tips and tricks to make the most out of this versatile kitchen appliance. His step-by-step instructions were easy to understand, and he patiently answered all our questions, never rushing or making us feel hesitant to ask. One aspect that truly stood out during the session was Suman's attention to detail. He paid careful attention to every aspect of the Instant Pot, from proper handling to recommended cooking times for different dishes. He also emphasized safety precautions, ensuring that we understood how to use the Instant Pot responsibly and avoid any potential hazards. By the end of the demo, I felt confident and inspired to explore the vast array of recipes and possibilities with my Instant Pot. Suman's expertise and professional approach left a lasting impression, and I am grateful for the invaluable knowledge he shared during the session. Thank you, Suman, for the outstanding demonstration – you've made me an Instant Pot enthusiast! Overall, I rate Suman's Instant Pot demo with a resounding five stars!

reviews.title: Maravillosa, amo mi Instant Pot!
reviews.body: Estaba por comprar una olla de cocción lenta cuando la instant pot se cruzó por mi búsqueda y después de leer bastante sobre ella en internet, decidí gastar un poco más de lo que tenía planeado y la compré. Y no me arrepiento! La olla es simplemente maravillosa, especialmente para alguien como yo, que trabajo fuera de casa y tengo marido y dos niños qué alimentar. No es que la instant pot sea más rápida que una olla de presión convencional, dado que como cualquier olla de presión, hay que esperar que alcance la presión adecuada, luego está el tiempo de cocción y después la despresurización para poder abrirla, pero la GRAN diferencia es que al poderse programar simplemente te olvidas de ella y no tienes que estar vigilando nada, lo cual para alguien con muchas actividades es una magnífica ayuda. Tiene muchas funciones (cocción a presión, cocción lenta, arroz, granos, vapor, salteado, yogurt, esterilizar, etc) y el instructivo viene en inglés, francés y español. Es muy sencilla de usar y de limpiar, además de ser increíblemente silenciosa. El recetario que contiene es muy pero muy básico, pero en internet encuentras un montón de recetas súper sencillas además de que en Amazon puedes encontrar recetas en libros y Ebooks a precios muy razonables. A un mes de haberla comprado ya cociné en ella arroz, pollo, vegetales, carne, avena, arroz con leche con resultados muy satisfactorios y muy fácil. Denle una oportunidad, de verdad la van a amar. Update: Después de usar la olla por 3 meses, sigo muy satisfecha con mi compra, se cocina super fácil en ella y sobretodo sin estar cuidando nada. Lo único en contra que le encuentro, es que el aro de empaque que trae la tapa guarda el olor de lo que cocinaste. No importa con qué los laves, va a guardar el olor. Aunque eso no es un problema para cocinar, pues no vas a querer preparar una avena o unas verduras si el empaque huele a pollo o carne. La solución que le veo es comprar uno o dos empaques de repuesto y usarlos para diferentes tipos de comida, tal vez uno para cosas dulces, otra para saladas y otro para lácteos.

reviews.title: Excelente, una maravilla
reviews.body: Es uno de esas cosas como los celulares, microondas, el internet que uno se pregunta, “como pude existir tanto tiempo sin ello?” Hace la vida mucho más sencilla en la cocina y es muy fácil de entender y usar. Soy persona de edad y no me gusta tener que aprender nuevas técnicas pero es muy fácil su uso. Yo compré el mini 3 quart Duo Pot Que es más que suficiente para mi marido y yo. TLa verdad, no duden en adquirir uno. Estoy tan feliz y contenta con esta compra.

reviews.title: Tamaño adecuado para cocinar para dos personas.
reviews.body: Tengo otra igual grande y me gusta mucho. Compre la version mas pequeña para un trailer chico y con esta me siento preparada para cocinar yna amplia variedad de alimentos.

reviews.title: I've used these for well over 15 years and have loved every minute.
reviews.body: If you have never used these before and are looking for a pot that cooks just about anything in less than it would normally on the stovetop, take the leap. I did so many years ago. My reason for getting this in the first place way back when was because I used to make rice everyday. After several expensive rice makers, they all had the same thing in common after a year or so. The non stick pot inside would start to peel away and to replace these was almost the price of what the Instant Pot was at the time. So the NUMBER ONE REASON I bought Instant pot in the first place was for the Stainless Steel pot on the inside. Amazing, and I pray that they don't turn to the non stick pots ever. I know that some of the other products they have do have the non stick pots, like in the air fryers. I do have an air fryer with the non stick and I am not happy about that, but I love the fryer aspect of it. There you have it folks, as a general rule of thumb, I tend to replace electronic cookware after about 10-15 years. I use these almost every single day, so I am very pleased with the company. Customer Service is also very responsive, so all in all a good choice. Real bang for your buck!

title: Instant Pot Pro 8 Qt 10-in-1 Electric Pressure Cooker, Black

reviews.title: Large stainless steel pot with handles is awesome!
reviews.body: My previous insta pot was a 6qt non-stick pot. I really enjoyed that pot. But many times I wished it was a little bigger. And getting the pot out of the unit was a bit dicy, you have to use pot holders for the heat and it could slip out of your hands. However I also became concerned about the non-stick coating on the pot. I had put a couple of scratches on the bottom so I was concerned about the coating. Enter this new pot. Very nice 8 qt size. I actually thought 8 qt might be too big but on my first use I almost filled it up, so it's not too big. The stainless steal pot is awesome and the handles make it very easy to lift out(without pot holders) and I dont feel like it's going to slip out of my hands. First use was a stew and it came out great. I did wash it in the dishwasher before use. I found the silicon seal to be hard to put back onto the lid, I had to use a little water as a 'lubricant' to get it to slip back into place. There are LOTS of options on this thing.....it took me a couple minutes just to pick one for the stew and I finally picked the 'slow cook' option which took six hours....but it was worth the wait....the meat was very tender and the potatoes and carrots were just right, not too soft and not too hard......by the way, if you shop Walmart, the organic carrots taste way better than the regular carrots......I just buy a bag of organic petite and dump them in....this time I also added a bag of frozen mushrooms and that was great.....too many times I buy fresh mushrooms and forget to use them within a day or two and have to chuck them. 10/17/25 update Still loving this pot....the only issue I have is the silicone pressure ring can be difficult to put back in place. To show how large it is, just now I put in a whole 3 lb bag of potatoes, a whole chopped up celery bunch, a large onion, 8 oz of fresh mushrooms, bag of carrots, 64oz of chicken stock and about 2 lbs of chicken......I put it on an option for 6 hours of 'slow cook'......the slow cook option is pretty cool.....

reviews.title: Worth the extra money over the less expensive Instant Pots
reviews.body: My first IP started having some display issues after about 5 years, so I decided to replace it since I use it just about every weekend. The replacement arrived with a dent in the side, and I worked with Amazon and received a partial refund, but it never seemed to cook well. I was constantly getting a burn notice, and I was never comfortable with the dented outer casing, so I decided to replace it again after about 1 year. I decided to not buy a less expensive model this time and spent the extra money on the Instant Pot Pro. So glad I did! The differences are very noticeable and appreciated. The slots to hold the lids are positioned at 10 and 2, which makes it much easier to work with than on the lower cost models where it is at 9 and 3. The display is much more informative, and I really love having more control over the heat when sauteing. The handles on the inner pot are a great addition. The inner pot stays level and doesn’t move around when you’re stirring so it keeps the heat even while sauteing. Also, it is easier to take in and out of the outer shell. Don’t get me wrong, the lower cost models like the DUO or the Rio are good machines. The Instant Pot Pro is just a much better device. I cooked with it last night for the first time and couldn’t believe it was possible to be MORE impressed with the Instant Pot. If you’re shopping for one and not sure which one to choose, the lower cost models are good, but the Pro is significantly better imo.

reviews.title: Wider is better
reviews.body: I recently upgraded my old pressure cooker to the Instant Pot, and I’m thrilled with the improvements. The most noticeable difference is the wider cooking area, which makes sauteing, stirring, and lifting the pot out much easier compared to my previous model. In terms of cooking efficiency, the Instant Pot has been a game-changer. The display clearly shows the current stage of the cooking process (preheating, cooking, releasing), eliminating any guesswork. Additionally, the pressure release is significantly quieter and less messy than the older units I’ve used, which is a major upgrade that I didn’t anticipate. Cleaning up is also a breeze. The stainless steel exterior makes it easy to wash, and I appreciate not having to keep extra pans around since most tasks can be completed in one pot. However, there’s a minor downside: the Instant Pot takes up some counter or cabinet space, and there’s a slight learning curve if you’re new to the Instant Pot menus. But after a few uses, it becomes intuitive, and the time and effort saved are well worth it. Overall, I’m incredibly happy with my purchase and highly recommend the Instant Pot to anyone looking for faster and easier home-cooked meals.

reviews.title: Why Don't You Have One Already?!
reviews.body: I upgraded from Instapot Duo to the Pro. The fact the Instapot Pro has handles makes a world of different. On the Duo it is was a pain pulling the pot out and straining it while hot. On top of that it inner-pot of this "Pro" has a heavy bottom making a great is steel pot, so it just work like a normal pot on the stove top giving me the options in using either the electrical device or on the stove top. When in doubt get the 6 qt, is fits most things for a 1-4 person household (I'd argue even 6). Might not hold a Large whole chicken, but I manage by being able to breakdown a whole chicken (it isn't hard, just watch a video) I cook professionally. But at home the Instapot is the best appliance I've gotten. I make Bean from dried at a fraction of the time, amazing quality fresh stock that doesn't require me to to wait 8 hours on a stove top, it takes the place of crockpot, rice cooker (*), and a normal pot. Stews, Gumbo, Chili, and Braises are done greatly when you are pinch for time making what would normally for 5 hour is only an hour or two and near same quality. Which has saved me during a dinner party where my sous dropped braised short ribs 2 hours before plating. It is an investment but if you eat (or plan to eat) legumes/beans, and you use stock/broth occasionally or consistently in your diet. This will save you some money and time while giving you a better product than store-bought stock/broth and canned beans. Both the beans and stock you make freeze well, and cooked frozen bean reheat/thaw fast. And if you freeze veggie scrap (like onion skin, carrot/parsnip peel, celery tops and bottoms) as well and save bones from you chicken (rotisserie, chicken thigns, or whole chicken) you can make stock with all the stuff you were going to throw way anyway. Better than store bought while also being basically free. Lastly it is great for meal prep and you can set it to have your ingredients in it before leaving to work and being done by the time you get home from work. If you cook consistently for yourself and/or for loved ones, or want to cook more at home. An Instapot makes thing easy at a press of a button, and the Pro has very convent features (like HANDLES I cant praise enough!) that make life much more easy. When you get one you will ask also ask "Why didn't I get one sooner?". I work late nights and early morning, this gives me more time and saves me from eating out. ~*I've mentioned "rice cooker" and I want to expand on this.~ The Instapot works great as a rice cooker but compared to an actual rice cooker, it is a little slower to cook (20min vs 30-35min) and the rice (especially short-grain/sushi rice) builds starch and stick to the stainless steel pot, requiring a slight bit more finesse to clean. I personally eat rice (and grains) consistently and i like saving 10-15min of what little time I have at home, so i have both a cheap rice cooker and instapot. However if you want to minimize your appliances (i.e. have less "appliance clutter") and need to conserve space in your kitchen, then having just an Instapot will work well enough and do every thing a rice cooker can, plus much MUCH more.

reviews.title: Excellent Multi-Cooker – A Must-Have!
reviews.body: I absolutely love this Instant Pot! It’s incredibly easy to use and has made cooking so much faster and more convenient. The food comes out delicious every time, whether I’m making rice, soups, chicken, or even yogurt. It heats evenly, saves time, and the quality is excellent. The large capacity is perfect for meal prep or family dinners. Highly recommended for anyone looking for a reliable and versatile kitchen appliance!

reviews.title: If you wish your IP was wider and spits less on pressure release - this is for you!
reviews.body: I’m a long time Instant Pot user and have bought many upgrades over the years. I was attracted to this new RIO Wide because, you guessed it, it’s wide. I do a lot of sautéing as well as cooking larger bone in chicken breasts, which aren’t as convenient in the standard narrow tall 6 qt IP. I also wanted to steam larger vegetables like 5-8 ears of corn on the cob. For the functional bits - it surpassed my expectations. I cook 5 ears of corn on the cob regularly now in this guy. They are very easy to get out with tongs with the lower height of the device. The settings are a perfect variety and the controls are easy to read and configure. I’ve cooked a half chicken in there after browning it first with the wide cooking surface. It turned out tender and delicious. The chimes at ends of cycles are melodious and make me smile - not the harsh beeping of older models. Steam release is exceptional - both super quiet and without wet spitting that you can get with older IPs. That alone has made it my go to IP. It is larger, so if you want to store it, you will need some space for that. I just leave mine on the kitchen island because I use it all the time. The lid is wide, so you can’t slot it into those IP slots that hold the lid on smaller models. This just means you need to be careful to drain any liquid caught in the lid into the pot when you remove it so you don’t drip it across your counter/electronics. Because of the width, the steam trivet is very easy to remove when it is hot. That’s something I struggled with a bit on my older, narrow IP. Stir fries are a dream to cook in this cooker. It feels very safe from steam burns due to the backward facing steam vent and the steam release buttons location far in front of that vent. I’ve put the lid in the dishwasher, which held up well. But mostly I clean stuck on food bits with some Lemi Shine citric acid on high pressure for 3 minutes and a soak in that overnight. That leaves the pan looking brand new as you can see in the photo. If you were debating whether you needed this IP in your collection, I can assure you that you do.

reviews.title: BUYER BEWARE..SLOW COOK DOESN'T WORK...ZERO CUSTOMER SERVICE
reviews.body: I we'll start this by saying if I could give this product zero stars or negative stars, I would. Absolutely. I have tried to order this product FOUR times. Amazon will not let me individually review this item for each one of those purchases, although they are different experiences. The first time Amazon sent me a defective product with a broken lid and a damaged body (I knew that I was purchasing it from the Amazon sell, but I had no idea it was gonna be unusable) My second order was with a Christmas gift card for a brand new product. I purchased the 8 qt "pro" as an upgrade from my current duo nova instant pot. I have enjoyed that product, although I do get an error code fairly frequently stating that the pot is the wrong size for the base… Instant pot told me that there is no fix for this I just need to order a brand new pot which I refuse to do so I fidget with it and it will work. Anyway, the brand new 8 quart would not come up to temperature on the slow cook function. I let it sit for four hours and it was still preheating and the food inside was raw. I had to take the food out and cook it in the oven. I sent the pot back The third time I ordered a 6 quart instant pot pro which looked beautiful, but had the exact same problem. There was also a problem getting the lid to come off the pot I had to take a butter knife and push down the steam release so that the lid would release and allow me to remove it even when I was not using the pressure cook mode. The slow Cook function absolutely would not preheat I did an experiment by putting water in the pot and turning it on for eight hours in the morning with no food in it and it never came up to temperature. Seven hours later it was still blinking preheat and the water inside was like 150°F. I contacted instant pot and they wanted me to do this almost tremendous task of taking a video showing the problem taking several photographs explaining the context of the problem blah blah blah blah. I said no I am just going to send it back until I can get one that actually works. That brings me to my fourth and final order of the instant pot Pro 6 qt. I know that it will shock you, but I had the exact same problem. I could not believe it. I looked it up online (as I should have done in the first place)and found that this is a common problem with this product. It just will not come up to heat on slow cook. One YouTube video said that it takes hours for this particular model to come up to temperature and you will need to have an instant thermometer handy so that you can check your food every few hours to ensure that it's actually cooking appropriately. I don't know about you, but when I slow cook food it is my expectation that that food is going to cook, even if I am out working in my garden or running a quick errand to the store. Why would I be on standby for eight hours when I can probably cook it in the oven in one or two and have a somewhat consistent result? Well, I did contact instant pot (again) and they required me to send photographs, and an explanation, and the whole rigmarole, which I did this time only to get a reply just a couple hours later where I was told the same thing : if you were going to cook something on slow cook it can take up to four hours to preheat on a longer cook. My reply back to instant pot was that several sites on the Internet know that there is a problem with the instant pot pro in that the slow Cook function does not work correctly. The Internet knows that this is a flaw. Amazon is becoming aware that this is a flaw. And I believe that instant pot knows that this is a flaw yet they refuse to either correct the problem or honor their warranty. I am sad to say that I will never buy another instant pot product after the runaround that I was given by this company, who refused to assist me, will not honor the warranty, made excuses for a faulty product, and ultimately just basically said if you don't like it go return it (literally). So I am. GOOD NEWS-- UPS will pick it up for free.

reviews.title: No PRO but good enough
reviews.body: I think Instant Pot are going backwards. I bought the original (or an early model) back when they became the 'thing' a few years ago. It worked great for many years. Eventually though the pressure seal wouldn't hold so it was time to 'upgrade'. I got this version thinking it would be better, it is labelled 'PRO' after all. The reality is it's a step backwards in many ways. The good: I like the look, it certainly looks PRO and the steam release guard (aka a cap) and the switch to release the steam are welcomed additions. The handles are great and definitely help when you're wanting to lift out a pot full of boiling hot chicken stock. The display works well and there are other features like a beep reminder incase you missed the original beep when the cooking finished. I also love the ability to save favourites, extremely useful especially when considering one of the Pro's flaws. The bad: The interface of this is a big step back from the previous generation Instant Pot that this replaced. It feels like the mini computer inside this struggles to keep up with what you're asking it to do, especially when it comes to setting a time. The lag of the timer as you turn the dial is awful. And as you're adjusting the timer there is a constant beeping sound which is just really annoying. You can actually turn off the sound but that also stops all the useful notifications like when your food is cooked so there's not really a good solutions here (besides being able to set a common time / pressure combo as a favourite which helps). They also changed the Yoghurt setting so my previous sweet spot of 9 1/2 hours like the older model no loner worked. With this Pro model it was taking 16+ hours to make a quite awful yoghurt. After a little research I found out the temperature of its default setting is 42° which is too low. I bumped it up to around 45° and now I get my great yoghurt in 9 1/2 hours again. I have no idea why they changed this but fortunately I have saved this setting as another favourite and no longer use their setting. Overall, besides those quirks, the Instant Pot Pro does all the things you would expect from an Instant Pot. The handles are very useful and I can't imagine going back to the handle-less pots. The interface is tolerable but should be better at this price point. And the changed cooking programs can be avoided by saving your preferred versions (though there are only 5 favourite slots).

reviews.title: Eficacia, Sabor, Tranquilidad sin mucho esfuerzo!
reviews.body: Compré la Instant Pot y genuinamente fue una de las mejores decisiones para mi cocina. La uso varias veces por semana y me ha resuelto cosas que antes eran un dolor, sobre todo cuando la carne o el pollo están congelados. Literal: de congelador a plato servido, sin drama. Uno de los momentos donde más la amé fue en Navidad. Pude hacer la cena completa en aproximadamente 2 horas, cuando normalmente habría pasado toda la noche cocinando. Carnes suaves, bien cocidas, con sabor, sin estar pegada a la estufa ni estresada por tiempos. La presión funciona excelente, los resultados son consistentes y te da mucha tranquilidad saber que puedes cocinar incluso cuando no planeaste nada con anticipación. Es ideal para: pollo o carne congelada, guisos, caldos, arroz, comidas “de diario” y también para ocasiones especiales. Al principio intimidan un poco los botones, pero es cuestión de usarla un par de veces. Después se vuelve automática en tu rutina. Además, la olla interior es fácil de limpiar y el sistema de seguridad se siente muy confiable. No exagero cuando digo que me ahorra tiempo, energía y estrés. Si cocinas en casa y quieres resultados buenos sin pasar horas, vale totalmente la pena. La recomiendo sin dudar y definitivamente la volvería a comprar y de hecho estoy pensando comprar más tamaños :D.

reviews.title: Muito mais que uma panela de pressão
reviews.body: Produto ótimo. Panela interna de inox que pode ser retirada e usada no fogão. Facilita limpeza e vai durar para sempre. Faço iogurte em potes em banho Maria toda a semana. Pasteurizei ovos inteiros com a função sous vide. Silenciosa quando usa pressão, que funciona maravilhosamente.

reviews.title: A SOLID PURCHASE
reviews.body: After my previous Instantpot stopped working one day. It was time for a new one. This one I chose as it had sous vide function. I have used this function twice now. I am quite impressed with it I must say. This Instantpot has ten functions. It is bigger than my precious one at 8qt. While I don’t cook for many I do not regret choosing the bigger version. What I enjoy about this particular Instantpot is the following: -The steam release is so much more easy to use. Just slide down to open and slide up to close. -The stainless steel liner with handles is the best update to this device ever. Silicone handles make it so easy to remove a scorching hot pot. -As with my previous pot this one has the dial to adjust time, temp and such. So easy and handy. -the cord is attached rather than having to plug it in the pot each time. As of yet I haven’t use this Instantpot for anything else. I can’t imagine it be any less than my other Pot. One thing I can think of that I’m not so impressed with: -There is a small slot to slide one thickness of your cord in the back, to hold it. It is fairly useless as being able to hold more cord would have been so much more useful. Even a nice Velcro strap to fold the cord up would have been so much better. Is this InstantPot worth buying? It is in my opinion a solid buy. It has more than one use and is a well built product.

reviews.title: Great service by reseller
reviews.body: Product was working fine till unexpected malfunction happened. The Tokion team was then extremely helpful. Provided me multiple options for repair through warranty and when all solutions were exhausted, full refund was issued upon shipping back the item

reviews.title: Very convenient
reviews.body: The product demo was given by Mr. Zafar Khan. The demo was really good and detailed. Made things so much easier. And the product is really convenient and amazing to use. Must buy.

title: Instant Pot Rio Mini 4 Qt 7-in-1 Electric Pressure Cooker, Black

reviews.title: Perfect Mini Multi-Cooker for Everyday Meals
reviews.body: I absolutely love this Instant Pot! The 4-quart size is perfect for small families or meal prep, and it doesn’t take up much counter space. It heats up quickly, cooks food evenly, and the 7-in-1 functions make it incredibly versatile. The controls are simple to use, and cleanup is fast thanks to the nonstick inner pot. It’s a stylish, reliable appliance that has made cooking much easier. Highly recommended!

reviews.title: Very happy with purchase.
reviews.body: I like the shape of this one and the death of this one much better than my old 3 quart instant pot let me explain. The old 3 quart mini instant pot was taller and smaller around. So if you’re a person that had a six or an 8 quart instant pot you had to re-buy all of your accessories. And I am in process of downsizing. I gave away my big six and my eight cord instant pots in favor of just having one smaller one and I chose the Rio. It’s is big around as the six and 8 quarts, but it’s not nearly as deep so it’s not as deep as the other instant pot mini design which I don’t think is available anymore I’m not sure this one is bigger around so it’s easier to get a chicken in there a whole chicken And maybe a little bit of carrot and vegetables. Every little beep or noise was frightening! I almost peed my pants when I released the pressure valve and loud hot greasy steam erupted from its behind angrily! That was not a fun clean up job! So after St patties was over it sat for months till I eventually pulled it out again to try making rice (yeah no I can’t seem to cook it on the stove). The rice cooked great in about the same time it took my old rice cooker. I now love my pot because of what happened last week. We got home late and I grudgingly wandered into the kitchen late one night wondering what I was going to make for dinner. reviews.title: Review from a confirmed foodaholic
reviews.body: Over the years, I have purchased hundreds of items from Amazon, and for the most part, got what I expected. I never reviewed any of them. But from the moment I received my Instant Pot, I felt that I had purchased something that not only exceeded my expectations, but will make my life easier (and more delicious)! I am a holistic nutritionist and a follower of a lower carb/paleo/primal lifestyle (and yes, it is not only a food regimen, but a lifestyle). Many of the meals I prepare require advance planning and preparation, and I am OK with that, realizing that it is an investment in my family's health and wellbeing. I was looking for something that would support my food choices and perhaps make it a little less time-consuming. I have used a crockpot extensively over the past years and while I appreciate the ease of use and the ability to put a meal on the table soon after I got home in the evening, there is that "everything tastes the same" factor I was running into with my family. So I began thinking about ways to cook my meals faster and realized that a pressure cooker may be the answer. But, I am scared of pressure cookers. Even though my head tells me that people have been using them for many years with no problems, my heart said there was a strong chance I could blow up the entire kitchen, myself included. I had no idea there were electric, programmable pressure cookers out there that would virtually eliminate that worry until I began researching them, first on Amazon, and then on other websites. I eventually purchased the Instant Pot over the others because of the stainless steel insert (no aluminum), the size of the pot (I wanted a larger capacity), and the ease of use. The day it arrived, I plugged it in and began reading the manual. The manual was very helpful, even included a suggested trial run to familiarize one with the basics. My first meal was potato soup (I know potatoes are not low carb or paleo, but once in a while you gotta have potato soup). I was amazed at how easy and delicious it was to make this soup that would normally take a couple of hours. I just coarsely chopped the vegetables, threw those in the pot, added the seasonings and the liquid, started the pressure cooker option, and in 20 minutes all I had to do was use my immersion blender to puree the soup, add some cheese, stir and it was ready to eat. AND the soup was every bit as good as my slower version that keeps me tied to the kitchen to stir and monitor until it's done. That is the hidden beauty of this appliance, that while it's cooking your food, you are free to do other things such as harass your kids to get their homework done. No more watching over a pot! My second recipe was lemon pepper chicken wings. There is a searing option, so first I browned the wings in a bit of butter, then added lemon pepper, salt, and 2 more tablespoons of butter. Put on the lid, set the pressure cooker for 25 minutes, and out came the most delicious, fall-of-the-bone wings just loaded with flavor. The family went wild! I also made mushroom gravy (no flour) pork chops in 30 minutes in the pressure cooker - the gravy was so good my son ate in on top of some gluten free noodles the next day for lunch - and a breakfast meat loaf in the slow cooker, also a winner. I am also using this to reheat food since we don't use the microwave anymore and I'm finding that it seems easier and makes less of a mess than going stovetop. That's a pretty long review for a first-timer but I am so enthusiastic about this product that I just had to share.
