reviews.title: A Nice Upgrade From My Oral-B Pro 100
reviews.body: I recently upgraded from my old Oral-B Pro 100 to the Oral-B iO Series 3, and I can definitely tell the difference. The brushing experience feels much smoother and quieter, and my teeth feel noticeably cleaner after each use. One of my favorite improvements is the pressure sensor. It helps me avoid brushing too hard, which is something my old toothbrush didn't have. I also like the different cleaning modes they're simple to switch between and let me choose what feels best. The brush head glides comfortably over my teeth, and the handle feels solid and well-made. Battery life has also been great so far, lasting several days before needing a recharge. If you're still using an older Oral-B model like the Pro 100 and have been thinking about upgrading, I think the iO Series 3 is well worth it. It feels like a much more refined brushing experience, and I'm really happy with the purchase.

reviews.title: Very nice looking, powerful and inexpensive. A great purchase!!
reviews.body: What a bargain!! This is replacing our old power toothbrush and upgrading to something much better. The cleaning modes are delightful, and the recharge time is efficient. Keeping the brush assembly in the holder and protected from the elements with the plastic case is such a great idea. The quality of this Oral-B toothbrush is second to none, as expected. The power and vibration of the brush is something we'll have to get used to, but that's a given considering our old one is well over 10 years old. 2 thumbs up on this product.

reviews.title: Clean teeth are a must!
reviews.body: Really like this toothbrush. Holds a charge well and I really like the brush heads they seem to clean very well. Has a 2 minute timer and lights that help you to know if you are applying the correct amount of pressure. I'm pleased with it and happy I bought it.

reviews.title: Its a good toothbrush would recommend if your in the market
reviews.body: I’ve been using the Oral-B iO Series 3 for a few weeks now, and the difference compared to a standard electric or manual toothbrush is night and day. It leaves your teeth feeling amazingly smooth, like you just stepped out of a dental cleaning. ​What makes it great: ​Unreal Cleaning Power: The round micro-vibrating brush head gets into every spot with zero effort. My teeth have never felt cleaner or fresher. ​Smart Pressure Sensor: This is probably the best feature. The light indicator shows green when you're using the right amount of pressure, red if you're pressing too hard, and white if you're too soft. It takes all the guesswork out of brushing and protects your gums. ​Built-in Timer & Modes: The built-in 2-minute timer pulses every 30 seconds to let you know when to switch quadrants, making it super easy to ensure a complete clean every single time. ​Solid Battery Life: Holds a charge really well for daily morning and night use, and the charging base takes up very little counter space. ​If you’re thinking about upgrading your oral care routine, this toothbrush is worth every penny. Highly recommended!

reviews.title: I love this toothbrush!
reviews.body: I always forget to write reviews after I buy stuff on Amazon. I should try to do it more because it is helpful when you find a review that is real. So, I bought this toothbrush to replace another brand that I bought about a year and a half ago. The old toothbrush just wasn't doing a good job at cleaning my teeth. I have always had problems with cavities and plaque build-up. The only sure-fire way of getting all of the plaque for me was to use Plax prior to brushing. Still, I find myself in the dentist's office every six months with a hygienist jack-hammering my mouth with water pick to get my teeth clean. It's embarrassing and it makes me feel anxious about my gum health. I saw the Oral-B iO Series 3 here on Amazon and it was discounted. According to Oral-B it is really good at getting rid of plaque. I took the manufacturer at their word, and bought it. Holy crap, ya'll! This thing is amazing! The iO3 has a round brush head similar to the polishing tool your dental hygienist uses. I've used cheaper Oral-B electric toothbrushes that also have round heads, but they weren't as robust as the brush head on the iO3. The bristles aren't hard, but they are dense and arranged in a way that they can hug your teeth while brushing. You can get that brush on every surface of each tooth (except directly between the teeth, of course). The motorized handle has a pressure sensor that changes color based on how hard or soft you are pressing. If you get it just right, it lights up green. The iO3 also helps you time your brushing so that you the recommended two minutes. It pulses when it's time to change to a different quadrant. It doesn't automatically shut off when the two minutes are up, however. That's fine with me as I will just continue brushing other parts of my mouth like my tongue and the roof of my palette when I'm done with my teeth. There are supposedly three types of brushing settings to choose from, but I have only used the default cleaning setting. The other two setting are supposed to be for sensitive teeth and whitening. The default works just fine for me. The build is solid and feels good in my hands. I like that the handle comes with two brush heads, a travel case, and case for the brush heads. I like to take my brush head off and put it in the case after I'm finished just because I'm paranoid about having a toothbrush exposed in the bathroom. It's nice to have the option to shield it from germs. So, TLDR, this is a great electric toothbrush. My teeth haven't felt this clean since the last time I went to the dentist. Oral-B did a fantastic job of designing a product that makes brushing easy and will almost certainly result in you having a positive visit at the dentist, and may help reverse gum issues and prevent cavities. I definitely recommend you buy this product if you are in the market for an electric toothbrush.

reviews.title: A noticeable upgrade from the Pro 1000!
reviews.body: I previously owned the Oral-B Pro 1000, and while it did a good job cleaning my teeth, this model is definitely an upgrade. The pressure sensor is one of my favorite features. When I press too hard, the light changes color, making it easy to know when to ease up. It's a simple feature, but very useful. It's also noticeably quieter and smoother than the Pro 1000, and the battery life is much better. Overall, brushing just feels more comfortable and enjoyable with this model. I'm very happy with this upgrade and would definitely recommend it.

reviews.title: Best toothbrush I've ever owned
reviews.body: This is by far the best toothbrush I have ever used! The dentist told me several years ago to buy an electric toothbrush so I bought the cheap oral B ones from walmart and forced myself to use that several times a week. Thinking that was better then just using my regular manual one. My husband bought this in black about a month ago and liked it and it was on sale so I decided to jump and get it as well. I've been using it for a week now and my mouth still feels as clean as it did the day I came home from the dentist with a cleaning. It was a little strong on the vibrations at first but after the week of using it consistently it no longer bothers me. Its not loud at all and I love the 30 second interval vibrations it gives you so you know to move on to the next quadrant in your mouth. Over all the best thing I've bought all year. Would recommend it to everyone.

Trying to get product support without much success, they close support via chat and phone call at 3:00. I’m still at work till 5:00. Bought replacement heads I hope I can still return. reviews.title: La meilleure brosse-à-dents électrique
reviews.body: Après deux mois d'utilisation, je peux le dire, il s'agit de la meilleure brosse-à-dents électrique que j'ai utilisé. En voyant ce nouveau type de brosse pourtant, je me demandais au départ s'il ne s'agissait pas d'une autre façon d'attirer le consommateur, mais non. Le système de nettoyage me paraît bien différent de ce que j'utilisais auparavant, y compris chez Oral B. POURS : - Le système de vibration / rotation de la brosse est tout simplement très bien pensé. C'est très doux à l'usage, cela paraît également très précis et le résultat est vraiment bon. - Le voyant qui permet de savoir si l'on appuie trop sur la brosse est très visible, c'est assez simple d'adapter la pression exercée. - J'aime également la vitesse de vibration. CONTRES : - Un peu dispendieux. Sur du long terme, si la brosse-à-dents reste toujours aussi fiable, cela pourrait compenser son prix. Conclusion : C'est un coup de cœur pour la brosse Oral B iO ! En espérant que cela dure plusieurs années.

title: Philips Sonicare 7300 Rechargeable Electric Toothbrush, 3 Brush Head, White

reviews.reviewer_name: It's a great deal in this price. It working nice and worth buying it. Battery capacity is excellent. I suggest to get this one if you are looking for a smart watch in lower budget.
reviews.title: ★★★★★ Great upgrade from a manual toothbrush
reviews.body: I’ve been using the Sonicare 7300 for a few weeks now and it’s made a noticeable difference in how clean my teeth feel. The pressure sensor is genuinely useful — it lights up if I’m brushing too hard, which I didn’t realize I was doing with my old brush. The SmarTimer keeps me honest about brushing the full two minutes, and it pulses every 30 seconds to remind you to switch quadrants. Having 12 different brushing settings might sound like overkill, but I actually use a few of them — the gum care mode is gentler on my gums, and the whitening setting feels more thorough for the odd coffee stain. Battery life is excellent — I’m easily getting close to the advertised 21 days on a single charge, so I’m not scrambling to find the charger during travel. The included travel case is a nice touch and keeps everything protected in my bag. Only minor gripe: it’s a bit pricier than a standard electric toothbrush, and replacement brush heads add up over time. But for the overall brushing experience and results, it’s worth it. Bottom line: A solid, feature-packed electric toothbrush that’s easy to recommend if you want something better than a basic model without going full premium.

reviews.title: Very happy with this purchase
reviews.body: 5 Stars I like this Sonicare much better than the older model I bought at Costco. It feels more powerful, cleans my teeth better, and I really like the pressure sensor and different brushing settings. The battery lasts a long time, and the rechargeable travel case is a great feature for trips. Overall, it’s a great upgrade and I’m very happy with it.

reviews.title: Highly recommend!
reviews.body: My Sonicaire Diamond became wobbly and loose. It was no longer taking care of tartar buildup. So happy I replaced it with this one. (The Diamond reviews at the time of my purchase were not good especially for the price point so I chose this one.) Love the travel charger, effectiveness I once had of tartar removal & overall cleanliness. To me, the value is good and it’s sleek and easy to travel with. The initial charge has lasted so far 2 weeks. Bristles are firm but will soften.

reviews.title: Top quality
reviews.body: This puppy is miles beyond my ten year old Sonicare, and also various newer models from other brands. Faster vibrations, stronger cleaning, more settings, much longer battery life. Definitely the best electric toothbrush I've used. Use it with a good tooth powder, activated charcoal, baking soda, clay, or better still alternate between a few of these, and your dental bills will quickly shrink. At fifty during prime week, this was a steal. Even at double that, it's definitely worth it. PS Use generic heads, they're 10% the price of Phillips heads and almost as good.

reviews.title: I SWEAR by the brand -- reliable, sturdy yet delicate enough for my hand and small mouth.
reviews.body: This is my THIRD Philips Sonicare in my lifetime. I'm old. I have good teeth and I take care of them. My dental hygienist tells me I'm one of her favorite patients. It's the toothbrush my dentist from years ago recommended and I absolutely love the brand. It's great for my gums as well as my teeth. It is GREAT value for the money and the fact that in my lifetime, I'm on my third (I'm 76), I think that's a very good brand recommendation. And it's very lightweight and easily transported. I like the white because I feel like I can see that it's pristine and clean. Nice design that lets me twist the bristles up and down along each tooth. Love it and highly recommend it. The whitening depends more on dentifrice being used, I believe, and the fact that one brushes multiple times a day. Check with your dentist on details for whitening.

reviews.title: A new level in toothbrush performance, but no wall plug and an intrusive app
reviews.body: This toothbrush appears to live up to the extravagant claim on the box. I have no way of knowing if the amount of plaque removed is actually 2000% more than what my previous Sonicare could do, but it is a huge improvement. I used to believe the job of an electric toothbrush was to pound my gums into submission, but this model is far more gentle and does a better job of reaching the tricky trouble spots my dentist never tires of pointing out. So I do recommend this product with almost no reservations. But before you open the box you should know that the power cord is a USB-A plug, wall unit not included. Phillips says this is to cut down on electronic waste, which is such an obvious euphemism for "it saves us money" that you wonder why they even bothered. Also, the Sonicare 7300 has Bluetooth connectivity, and you can download an app and connect to, um, your toothbrush. I said what the heck I'll give it a try. The app says it values your privacy but then it doesn't let you complete setup unless you agree to send all data to Phillips so they can help you with suggestions for improving your dental hygiene. Then the home screen comes up and it's a dental chart, at which point I killed the app and uninstalled it. Perhaps you might find such detailed help useful, but I'm not interested in being an unpaid beta tester or belonging to a floating focus group for future products. I've been using a Sonicare for years and will continue to do so. But the way this product is packaged and presented seems to make it just another way that big business is trying to carve off a big slice of my conscious awareness. And I’m getting tired of that. reviews.title: A good value for the uses you'll get out it.
reviews.body: this toothbrush is a good value for the money, since it is packaged with a charging base, travel case, and 3 replacement toothbrush heads. You can also set it up to auto deliver the heads when they get worn out. The auto delivery is easy to do, just follow the instructions that will be on the Amazon website. The appearance is black, with other colors available. The size is right for the use by family members of all ages that are capable of using it. The handle is durable and sturdy. The handle is light weight and not too heavy to use. The vibration will take some getting used to, as it tickles the gums, for first time users. It will clear up in about a week or so. It has green LEDs that show the current charge, then turn amber when you need to change the brush head. I recommend it to anybody that needs a reliable toothbrush, that isn't a hard-to-find item.

reviews.title: The Toothbrush That Thinks It’s Better Than Me… and Honestly Is
reviews.body: The Philips Sonicare 7300 doesn’t just clean your teeth — it judges your entire dental existence. In the best way. The first time I turned it on, I swear it sounded like it was saying, “Move aside, amateur, I’ve got this.” And it did. This thing blasts plaque off your teeth like it’s clearing a runway. My mouth hasn’t felt this clean since the day I grew my first tooth. The pressure sensor lights up like a tattletale every time you brush too hard. The timer keeps you honest. The brush heads feel like they were engineered by NASA for enamel. And the clean afterward? Unreal. My teeth are so smooth I’m convinced I could butter toast with them. It’s powerful, it’s smart, it’s slightly condescending — and it’s absolutely fantastic. Five stars. My dentist is going to weep with joy.

reviews.title: Works well.

So you have 9 months of brush usage before you’d buy a replacement.

reviews.body: I’ve been using this Oral-B Pro 100 CrossAction battery toothbrush for a while now and I’m really happy with it. reviews.title: A vibrating, "you-get-what-you-pay-for" electric toothbrush.
reviews.body: I've never bought into the hype of "electric toothbrushes," but I thought I would give this relatively-cheap one I saw discounted on Amazon a shot. Mainly because it came with 10 replacement heads and if the batteries ever went kaput, I could just use it as a normal, albeit bulky, toothbrush. After using it every day over the last month, I have to say that I have rather mixed feelings about this rechargeable toothbrush (words I thought I would never say). First, the positives, and there are some to be found here. The battery life, in my experience, has actually been fairly good. Though, that could likely be attributed to how low-tech this tech toothbrush actually is (we'll get to that later.) The brush is lightweight as well, allowing you to maneuver it easily. The three vibrating modes do work and offer some variation for you to test and see which you like best. The brush also has an internal timer that briefly stops the vibration every 30 seconds, ultimately shutting off after 2 minutes. I personally found this to be annoying at first, but now kind of like knowing how long I've been targeting a specific area for. And finally, yes, you could use this as a "manual" toothbrush if your forgot to charge the battery. Keep in mind that the bristles are incredibly soft, so if you like your normal toothbrushes with some tensile strength, this one might not be for you. Now for the "bad," or mediocre I guess I should say. The Teetheory toothbrush is little more than a vibrating wand with a brush attachment affixed to it. The bristles don't move, sweep, rotate, or oscillate like a more premium electric toothbrush would, so leave that fantasy behind now. Yes, the bristles do technically move, but that's just because of the vibrating motor that your brush head is on. The bristle movements are incredibly fine and gentle, to the point that you question if it's really doing any good at all. In terms of cleaning power, this is probably far from dentist-recommended. Also, if you have sensitive teeth, I wouldn't recommend this toothbrush. The vibration is all along the top portion of the brush, so if you even graze your teeth, you'll get a rather uncomfortable sensation. I personally don't have very sensitive teeth, but every time I've used this brush, I make the mistake of touching my teeth with the plastic, non-brush portion and it doesn't feel pleasant. Now, with a product like this, you have to take into account the price you're paying, which is significantly less than that of a premium electric toothbrush. I'm aware of and totally understand that. But judging this product on merit alone, I can't really say that I would wholeheartedly recommend it. Does it clean your teeth well enough? Yeah. Does it do it so well that I'll never use a normal toothbrush again? Not really. If you're truly gung-ho about dental care, would suggest spending the extra cash for a premium electric toothbrush. Specifically, one of the electric toothbrushes that actually spins. If you absolutely must have an electric toothbrush for cheap and you don't really mind it being low-tech, this will do you just fine, I suppose. As for myself, I will continue to use this brush for the foreseeable future, and hope to see if the reviews others have posted about the brush not working after a few charges are anomalies or something everyone should expect.

reviews.title: I love this toothbrush!
reviews.body: I always forget to write reviews after I buy stuff on Amazon. I should try to do it more because it is helpful when you find a review that is real. So, I bought this toothbrush to replace another brand that I bought about a year and a half ago. The old toothbrush just wasn't doing a good job at cleaning my teeth. I have always had problems with cavities and plaque build-up. The only sure-fire way of getting all of the plaque for me was to use Plax prior to brushing. Still, I find myself in the dentist's office every six months with a hygienist jack-hammering my mouth with water pick to get my teeth clean. It's embarrassing and it makes me feel anxious about my gum health. I saw the Oral-B iO Series 3 here on Amazon and it was discounted. According to Oral-B it is really good at getting rid of plaque. I took the manufacturer at their word, and bought it. Holy crap, ya'll! This thing is amazing! The iO3 has a round brush head similar to the polishing tool your dental hygienist uses. I've used cheaper Oral-B electric toothbrushes that also have round heads, but they weren't as robust as the brush head on the iO3. The bristles aren't hard, but they are dense and arranged in a way that they can hug your teeth while brushing. You can get that brush on every surface of each tooth (except directly between the teeth, of course). The motorized handle has a pressure sensor that changes color based on how hard or soft you are pressing. If you get it just right, it lights up green. The iO3 also helps you time your brushing so that you the recommended two minutes. It pulses when it's time to change to a different quadrant. It doesn't automatically shut off when the two minutes are up, however. That's fine with me as I will just continue brushing other parts of my mouth like my tongue and the roof of my palette when I'm done with my teeth. There are supposedly three types of brushing settings to choose from, but I have only used the default cleaning setting. The other two setting are supposed to be for sensitive teeth and whitening. The default works just fine for me. The build is solid and feels good in my hands. I like that the handle comes with two brush heads, a travel case, and case for the brush heads. I like to take my brush head off and put it in the case after I'm finished just because I'm paranoid about having a toothbrush exposed in the bathroom. It's nice to have the option to shield it from germs. So, TLDR, this is a great electric toothbrush. My teeth haven't felt this clean since the last time I went to the dentist. Oral-B did a fantastic job of designing a product that makes brushing easy and will almost certainly result in you having a positive visit at the dentist, and may help reverse gum issues and prevent cavities. I definitely recommend you buy this product if you are in the market for an electric toothbrush.

reviews.title: Each of these lasts about three to four months! Planned obsolescence.
reviews.body: I thought I'd come by and warn folks about these electric toothbrushes. See, Sonicare is a very famous brand of dental hygiene products, and the technology used here is proven to be very effective. Rapid gentle motion of a set of soft fibers-- you know. We all get it. So I've been using Philips Sonicare for many years, and I'm certain that my oral health has benefitted from that. The trouble is, Philips can't build one of these that lasts more than half a year. I keep having to replace the units because the power switch fails. One after another. The last purchase was 10 April. That's right-- just over three months ago. The rubbery membrane covering the power switch has cracked open and water has leaked into the switch, and the switch has failed. It either won't come on, or if it does finally come on, I can't then turn it off. Can you imagine? In the year 2024? Philips can't design and manufacture a power switch on a toothbrush that lasts more than a few months? Well, of course I know the answer. It's supposed to fail, and I know it. It's planned obsolescence, and I know it. I wanted to let you all know. These are very worthwhile products from the perspective of one's oral health. But the company is ripping you off intentionally. I'm at this moment going to another brand and I will not buy a Philips product of any kind again. It's a matter of principle to me. I won't. I refuse to bow down to these greedy and wasteful and arrogant corporations who try to manipulate me into more sales by intentionally manufacturing failure into their products. They are intentionally trying to arrange for us to develop habitual purchasing of their products, in repetitive cycles, again and again, and they're attempting to teach us to accept miserable quality as inevitable and only customary. I realize that this has become par for the course, and to many people it doesn't matter-- they're not bothered by constantly buying a new item, over and over and over again. I really don't care. I'm a discriminating and conscientious and logical person, and I refuse to participate in this kind of idiocy.

reviews.title: Mostly Love
reviews.body: I had an old waterpik which had seen better days. I had a sonic toothbrush which made my teeth feel wonderful but gave me repetitive stress issues. I finally decided to spend the money on this combo unit and it really is better than the the sum of its parts. It finds all the little hidden bits of leaves and such that distress one's teeth while efficiently cleaning that all important gumline. That is, it does exactly what it's supposed to do. And there's no spitting! Bonus! So, only *mostly* love, because it's just a little too smart for its own good. The brush pulses to make four time divisions then turns off. The only way to have enough water to make it to the end is to have it overflow while filling. Filled up to what looks like the same point is not sufficient. I'm big on saving water, but just a tad more generosity in the tank would actually save water. The old hunch is necessary while doing the combination, or else water will run down one's forearm. I'm not sure if there could be any design solution to that, but it's the brushing part that takes that long. Those who can't hunch can use the brushing part and waterpik part separately. It was hard at first to set the toothbrush in the receptacle, but I learned that holding the hose coil in place, against the unit, it's much easier to seat the brush. The only really bad thing about this is the price--and I paid up not to have black. :)

reviews.title: Takes a bit to figure out and adjust to...
reviews.body: One thing to know is that although its advertised that you can brush and floss at the same time, the actual application of this concept leaves something to be desired. When you activate the floss and bruch together feature, the flossing rinses all the toothpaste from you mouth before it can be used. So, I brush, then floss. The deep clean is amazing and this has enough power. The brush is set for two minutes and the it will stop automatically. FLAW: if you pause it briefly while brushing, the two minutes restarts. Unlike my phillips sonic care, which you could pause and restart without resetting the two minute time limit. This comes with two heads, one normal size and one for travel, i found they work equally well until one literally broke off in my mouth. I ordered more from Amazon and they have lasted well, so maybe a fluke. Bottom line: This thing does what it does well, but one must be patient and brush first, then floor. Also, don't forget to fill the water reservoir with warm water prior to using flosser. The flosser is super powerful and will clean the heck out of your teeth. Which, as I think about it, is the entire purpose of this thing: clean teeth. This doesn't disappoint.

reviews.title: Great Customer Service & Tips on Reconnecting the Flosser
reviews.body: TLDR: If somehow the flosser doesn't respond to the toothbrush's signals and the radio and toothbrush resets don’t work, drain the toothbrush's battery completely by setting it idle for a week or so and reconnect the set to power. Make sure you place the toothbrush in the base before reconnecting the set to power. Waterpik offers great customer service and the device works great and does what it's supposed to do most of the time. ----------------------------------------- I bought one 2.5 years ago, and after less than 2 months of using it, the flosser stopped responding to the toothbrush's command. I don't know how it happened but I knew it was a housekeeper who unplugged the device as he had to clean the counter. After a few days of testing the flossing function and trying the troubleshooting techniques without success, I gave up and contacted Waterpik's customer service. They asked for anything, you know, that would allow them to honor the warranty. The process was a bit annoying (just a bit, and is absolutely nothing compared to arguing with insurance about coverage) but Waterpik in the end sent me another set for free which I'm still using today. Being the environmentally conscious and lazy person I am, I kept the first set because it'd be a chore to dispose of it properly, so I just put it into the original packaging and stored it in the vanity cabinet. Last year, I had to move to another state and while I was packing stuff up, I saw the set and decided to give it another try before completely throwing it away. And it xxxxing worked!!!!!! Now that I commute in between cities, I've placed one at the residence close to my workplace!!! Also I've been periodontitis free for the past 2 years! Thanks Waterpik!!

reviews.title: It was just meh, and then the flosser feature broke
reviews.body: Unfortunately, I don't recommend this product for the following reasons: 1) The button to turn on/off the water flosser is directly below the button to turn on/off the toothbrush. I can't count the number of times that I've inadvertently pressed the flosser button and water sprays everywhere. It's easy to press this button because of its location on the toothbrush, and also because the handle for the toothbrush is small in diameter and slippery when wet...and of course it's going to get wet...so it's tough to avoid pressing buttons while trying to hold onto it. I can disconnect the water flosser to avoid this problem, but that defeats the purpose imho and is a hassle. 2) I seem to spend an inordinate amount of time keeping this unit clean. The toothbrush and base have lots of crevices. 3) At this price, I expected a better product, especially from Waterpik. It’s just meh. Not great, not terrible. I can work around the above annoyances, but wish I hadn’t spent so much money on it. I gave it 3 stars because the water flosser does a good job, and the reservoir holds a sufficient amount of water compared to the "all-in-one" models, where the water reservoir is in the handle. If you have a dental implant, you need a water flosser. Once this toothbrush/flosser needs replacing, I'll look for a different design. Hopefully Waterpik will come up with something better. UPDATE: Not long after giving this product 3 stars and a "Meh" review, the flosser stopped working. Actually, it won't STOP working, and wants to run continuously when the unit is plugged in. Now all I have is an expensive electric toothbrush. It gets one star.

reviews.title: Mismatched items cost time and money!
reviews.body: I had one of these and loved it. I even rave about the product to my friends and bought one for Christmas as a gift for one of my best friends. It ended up being a mistake with plenty of consequences. The unit didn’t work, and after several attempts of investigating it once she turned it over to me, I found that the base unit and the toothbrush don’t match IDs, so the highly touted wireless connection didn’t work and would never work since they are tied to the unit’s ID. This careless mistake on the manufacturer’s side meant I was forced to take back the present and return it. I had to then personally repack it and bring it to the post office and pay $66.60 to ship it back. Amazon is only going to reimburse me for half of that, and only weeks from now. Terrible service on both Amazon’s part (I’ve always been able to get returns picked up but they don’t offer it anymore) as well as Waterpik for screwing up in the first place!

reviews.body: I ordered this Philips Sonicare 3300 rechargable electric toothbrush to compare with my current electric toothbrush. What I like: -2 different intensity modes -Quadpacer timer at 30 second intervals (4 quads, 2 minutes) -it's rechargeable and battery lasts about 2 weeks brushing 2x per day and has an easy to read battery indicator -good price point for a trusted brand -sturdy and still worked after I dropped it in the sink What I did not like: - As a long time electric toothbrush user, the initial "ramp up" mode was irritating, even if it was short lived. I can see where a new user may appreciate that. -of the 2 brush heads included in the box, one was black like the base and the other was a different style, but was white (which looks odd). -the bristles on the Sonicare are more firm than the very soft bristles I am used to. -there is a usb charging cord only, so you need a USB outlet or a block to use a regular plug Overall, I feel this electric toothbrush is a good value for an entry level electric toothbrush. It's simple and does a good job of removing plaque, and is easy to maneuver in the mouth. I just wish it came with softer brush heads.

reviews.title: Good Laptop At A Fair Price
reviews.body: For the price, this laptop gets a 5 star rating. Well, more like 4.5 but I couldn't give it that. It's a good sized laptop with a clear screen. It's pretty darn fast and it looks pretty sharp. Speakers are decent but not mind-blowing and for what it's worth, it has a camera, which is, again, passable, not mind-blowing. The keyboard on the one I got is more of a darker grey (it's advertised as ash grey, which I believe is a lighter color) but I actually like the darker keyboard better. Typing on the keyboard is pretty smooth too. It could use one or two more outlets on the sides though. You only get one USB Type-A port, one USB Type-C port and a headphone jack. Fine if you're more of a minimalist, but not ideal for multi-tasking work. Also, a little tip; When powering on, all you need to do is press the power button, NOT press and hold. I didn't realize that at first and thought initially that their was a problem. Just a piece of advice. Overall, it's a good laptop, at a fair price and should work well for the "Average Joe". I just got it, so the only question I have is, how long will it last? Hopefully it lasts me quite a while. But we'll see. I also got one of the recommended carrying cases for it, but that's another review for another time. Overall Rating: 4.5/5 stars.

title: HP 14" Laptop 2026 Edition, Intel Processor, 4GB RAM, 128GB Storage

reviews.title: Great Buy, was what i expected it to be
reviews.body: Keep in mind that this is more of a rant, and I'm half asleep, but this is what I've gone through so far with the product. Originally came from an hp g62 2010 - 2018, was able to make the laptop last. Finally wanted to upgrade and saw this on sale, so I went for it and it was what I wanted in a laptop for what I do: Music, School, Youtube, Slaughtering Demons. The rant and rave of an individual: The screen is very nice, I can confirm it is an In-plane Switching Monitor or (IPS) as I do not have to center the screen or move my body to get a great view of it, unlike a lot of TN panels that I've used back in the day. The disassembly of the device is very very simple, remove the screws from the bottom of the case and the case pops off, might need a thin tool to pry the case off a bit (only con here) and you'll see the ram and the hard drive and the nvme along with the fans which make it easy for upgrades and cleaning. Also the battery is not soldered into the board and easily comes out for replacement after you remove some screws. All screws I noticed were Phillip's head. (I like to watch disassembly videos in case something happened, that way I can tear into it and hopefully fix the issue.) The ram is decent for 12 gigs, a 4 gig stick and an 8 gig stick, but I plan on upgrading the ram soon. Now after uninstalling a few things and setting windows to use less resources, I idle at about 18-19% which isn't bad at all, depends on what you do though. I do believe the manufacturer specifications have tested up to 16 gigs of 2666 on the board, however; there are cases with other omen laptops, where you can plop in 16 gigs in each dimm slot for a total of 32 gigs, wouldn't recommend it because it's not officially supported, but I will go ahead and try it (making sure i'm at the latest bios update from hp), and will provide an additional review/update. (I like to run a lot of things at once.) The processor is very nice, windows shows that i have 4 physical cpus and 8 logical processors, and I idle at 0% after turning the thing on (which mine booted into windows less than 3 seconds with the nvme 128 gig harddrive). I plan on upgrading the nvme from 128 gigs to 1 terabyte, might clone the drive or just grab a fresh install of windows 10 and slap it on a usb drive and fresh install, go from there. From what I read on the specification sheet for the dc0010nr, I think a cap of 512 Gigs nvme was officially tested and supported, but I'm going another 512 and see how the machine fairs. The 1 terabyte hard drive isn't slow at all, but I have nothing on it but a few games and some music, I constantly keep it defragged. The sound on the laptop is definitely an upgrade from my old hp g62 via software and hardware, but i use headphones into the 3.5mm jacks for mic and playback anyways. when it comes to gaming: Doom 2016 gives about 100 to 130fps on 1080p, ultra + open glide settings.... battlefield 1 on 1080p ultra gives about 45+ on mp and 60+ sp, drop it to high and it gives about 60+ but it depends on what map and what all is going on via gameplay. The heat on the laptop isn't bad, the machine will get warm and the fans will kick into high gear almost like a delay, but there is absolutely no throttling and when i'm finished with my gaming, the fans kick off to silent almost immediately. Also with the gpu, this is a verified gtx 1050 ti with 4096MB of vram in it. Final note: I think it's worth what I payed for: 799.99. If my desktop crashes and burns, it's a great replacement for it. It absolutely destroys solitaire and minesweeper along with other office products like excel spread-sheeting and you're in need for a couple of Pareto diagrams or 3 point beta distributions to resolve employee padding with P.M.O affairs making sure the stakeholders are happy. Alas I digress... I unboxed it, i pressed the power button and it immediately shot into windows and was ready to go. :)

reviews.title: Computer great, refurbish quality missed a major issue.
reviews.body: This review is mostly about the refurbish service, the computer itself is absolutely fantastic. My expectations for a refurbished computer was that I would get something that would show very modest wear, but work perfectly. I was delighted when I first opened my new Lenovo computer. The screen, keyboard, and touchpad appeared like it was brand new had never been touched. I was initially delighted with my purchase and started loading software and restoring my data. On the second day however, I noticed some unusual indentations around the power button. As I explored it further, I found that the computer had probably been dropped on its side. It actually bent the case enough to make the SD card slot unusable. It also makes the USB connectors quite tight (which may not actually be a bad thing in and of itself - but it's not right). The bottom of the case shows a physical crack and I am moderately concerned about whether there's some hairline fractures or other damage that isn't immediately obvious. The bottom line is, I've decided to keep the computer since it seems to be working fine and I really appreciate the pristine screen and keyboard that I received. I don't use the SD card slot so it's not a big deal to me for that. But I guess I'm just a little disappointed to have received a laptop that was clearly dropped hard enough to bend the case. I know this happed before shipping as the box it was delivered in showed no signs of any drop. It is a bit of a testament to the high-quality build that Lenovo puts into their computers but not a great example of careful oversight on the Amazon reconditioning service. I think they should have been more descriptive about this kind of damage on this particular item (maybe offered it with a bit more discount?)

I didn't want selfies, I wanted pictures. I spent nearly 1 1/2 hours online with support, with no resolution. As it turns out, my Issue falls under the category of SOFTWARE, NOT HARDWARE, which conveniently is NOT covered by WARRANTY or INSURANCE. I am sorry, but I am having difficulty accepting that rationale due to the fact that item purchased and described ( camera) was not 100% operational, but was, rather, defective due to the fact that it did accommodate all of my required parameters for choosing this device. But ultimately, and herein lies the real kicker: I can have this issue addressed and possibly fixed by "purchasing" a "service upgrade" entitling me to 1(one) 30 day Single Incident - Lenova Live Assistant - Set-up. Part #5WS1J63373. Oh, but that's not all, I get this for a mere $69.00, with an ISSUE DATE of June11 and an EXPIRATION DATE of June 25th. What does this even mean? I either have to accept or decline (or just let it go). Will this option be availabe later? Will it cost me more? Welcome to the life of a consumer. It’s a small detail that makes a big difference for outdoor use. The speaker is also very lightweight and easy to pack. It fit perfectly in my beach bag without taking up much space, so it’s a great travel companion for vacations, camping, or weekends by the water. Pairing with my phone was quick and easy, the controls are straightforward, and the battery lasted long enough that I never had to worry about it during the day. The optional light effects are a fun bonus, especially for evening gatherings, and you can turn them off if you want to save battery. Overall, this is one of those products that delivers more than you expect for the price. It combines good sound quality, portability, durability, and useful features into a very affordable package. title: Pillow Speaker for Sleeping, Bluetooth Speaker Under Pillow with Built-in Sleep Sounds + TF/microSD Offline, Auto-Off Timer, Side Sleeper Friendly

reviews.title: Not ideal for under the pillow
reviews.body: I tested this speaker specifically for its intended use as an under-pillow sleep speaker. It does function as described in the included instructions which mentioned putting it on top of the empty packaging box, and the Bluetooth connection, built-in sounds, and timer features all worked properly during my testing. However, the product title and listing heavily emphasize using it under a pillow for sleeping, and that's where I found some limitations. To hear the audio clearly, the speaker needs to be placed in a very precise position relative to your ear. If you move during the night, even slightly, the sound quality and volume can change significantly, which takes away from the convenience I was hoping for. Another consideration is that the sound is not as isolated as I expected. While it is quieter than using a phone speaker, someone sleeping next to you may still be able to hear what you're listening to, especially in a quiet room. Because of that, I don't think it's the ideal solution for sharing a bed with a partner unless they don't mind hearing some of your audio. The device itself is lightweight, compact, and comfortable enough to place under a pillow without creating a noticeable lump. Battery life also seemed adequate for several nights of use between charges, and the timer feature is useful if you don't want audio playing all night. Overall, the speaker works as advertised, but I wouldn't personally recommend it as a primary sleep-listening solution. For bedtime audio, especially if you sleep with a partner or move around during the night, I think low-profile sleep earbuds provide a more consistent and private listening experience. This may still work well for some users, but it didn't fully meet my expectations for under-pillow sleeping use.

reviews.title: Tiny pillow speaker with Bluetooth, offline playback AND a sleep timer
reviews.body: This is a clever little speaker for anyone who likes listening to something while falling asleep without filling the whole room with sound. The best part is that it's noticeably louder when it's under your pillow than when it's sitting out in the open, which is exactly what you want from a pillow speaker. There's a small gray speaker on top. You're obviously not getting booming bass out of something this tiny, but that's hardly what I want vibrating under my head while I'm trying to sleep anyway. It's tiny too, easily fitting in the palm of my hand, so I don't notice it under the pillow. Bluetooth was easy to connect. The controls are all along the side: volume +/-, plus a power button that's a long hold for on/off and a short click for play/pause. Even better, there's a sleep timer! Long-hold the + button to choose 1, 2, or 3 hours, so you don't have to leave it playing all night. It also has a microSD/TF card slot so you can load audio directly onto a card and listen without having your phone connected. I haven't tested the battery long enough to judge battery life yet, but I'll update if it's particularly short.

reviews.title: Thin and Sleek Under Pillow Speaker
reviews.body: I ordered this pillow speaker for my son who loves falling asleep to music. The speaker is thin and sleek at 15 mm. The speaker connects to Bluetooth very easily and the volume easily adjusts through the phone or the speaker. The speaker did work best off to the side of the ear rather than directly under it which we found sort of interesting. We do have other Bluetooth speakers, just not ones specifically designed for under the pillow, and we found that this speaker is a little low on volume with the tiny speaker.

reviews.title: Simple fun design
reviews.body: There is a lot to like about this product, but it has some serious flaws as well. First it is small and has a low profile, so if it does not disturb me under my pillow. However, my pillow is dense and the sound doesn't work well through it. It has to be so loud for me to hear and then it disturbs my husband. It does work pretty well as a speaker next to my ear. The bluetooth is easy to set up, and the sound is surprisingly clear. It is a little high pitched, but nothing that bothers me. The buttons work as expected, but it really needs a tactile difference between volume up and volume down. I would like to feel the buttons and know which is which by touch. The sleep sounds is a nice addition. I also appreciate the timer function. Ultimately it doesn't work as well as I wanted it to. That is in part because I move too much while going to sleep. Even moving an inch away from the speaker greatly reduces the volume. That is good if you don't want someone else to hear it, but bad if you shift around.

reviews.title: Tin can
reviews.body: Poor sound quality and volume. Nearly impossible to hear and when you can it sounds like it’s transmitting through a tin can.

reviews.title: Great Little Pillow Speaker
reviews.body: This is a nice little device that works exactly as I hoped. It connected to Bluetooth easily, and I had no trouble getting it set up and playing audio. I was pleasantly surprised by how well I could hear it when it was tucked underneath my pillow. The sound was clear enough for comfortable listening without needing to turn the volume way up. I also tested the 3-hour timer, and it turned off when it was supposed to. That's a nice feature if you like listening to something as you fall asleep without having it play all night. I think this would be especially useful for travel. Hotel rooms can be noisy, and having a small speaker that can be placed under your pillow is a convenient way to listen privately without disturbing someone else. It also charged quickly, which is always a plus when you're getting ready to head out. Overall, this is a simple, convenient device that works well and is easy to use. I would recommend it.

reviews.title: Great Sound Alternative, but Not Ideal for Sharing a Bed
reviews.body: I usually sleep with a speaker eye mask because I listen to guided meditations to help me fall asleep. The problem is that the speakers sit right next to your ears, so they can still feel quite loud even at the lowest volume. I thought this device might be a good alternative, but it didn't quite work out the way I had hoped. This type of speaker needs a surface to vibrate against in order to amplify the sound. Unfortunately, when I placed it on the mattress, the sound traveled through it—and now my husband can hear all of the guided meditations I listen to! I definitely would not recommend this if you share a bed with someone who doesn't want to listen along with you. Otherwise, it is easy to use, and I love that it includes a Chinese language setting. Each charge lasts through the entire night, which is great. However, unlike my speaker eye mask, this device needs to be charged daily. Overall, it works as intended, but if you sleep next to someone, be aware that the sound can travel through the mattress and become a shared listening experience!

reviews.title: Convenient Form Factor with Mixed Audio Features: A Middle-of-the-Road Sleep Speaker
reviews.body: The sleek, low-profile design of this under-pillow speaker makes nighttime listening far more comfortable than wearing earbuds or bulky headphones. It slips easily under standard or memory foam pillows, providing clear, direct sound without disturbing a partner sleeping nearby. Side sleepers will appreciate that it remains virtually unnoticeable beneath the pillow surface, eliminating awkward pressure against the ear. While the physical design works well, the preloaded sleep sounds leave something to be desired. The built-in ambient tracks and white noise options sound somewhat repetitive and cheesy, lacking the rich, organic depth you would want for a truly relaxing bedtime routine. Fortunately, the inclusion of Bluetooth connectivity and a TF/microSD card slot allows you to bypass the internal tracks and play your own curated playlists, podcasts, or audiobooks instead. The practical hardware features, such as the auto-off timer, add solid utility for managing nighttime battery drain. Setting the timer ensures the device powers down on its own once you drift off, making it reliable for overnight routines. The offline playback via memory card is also handy for anyone who prefers keeping their smartphone away from the bedside table while sleeping. Overall, the unit functions well enough as a dedicated sleep aid, but the value proposition is slightly underwhelming. Given the lackluster built-in audio tracks, the current price tag feels a bit steep for what is essentially a basic specialized speaker. It is a decent, usable option if you plan to stream your own content, but expectations should remain modest.

title: Ortizan X10 Portable Bluetooth Speaker (1st Gen), IPX7 Waterproof, Wireless

reviews.title: A real powerhouse of a speaker.
reviews.body: I originally got this speaker to play in the shower. I have since moved to playing it in my garage, outside when doing yard work, and in my car when I want to connect to my songs without having to connect to my car audio. It is very loud, the battery last for yours, and it is very easy to carry around. I love this thing. Pros - Sound Quality – is excellent. It is a lot loader than I thought it would be. Can play in your car and it matches the best sound system I have ever heard in a car. Sound is crisp with voice, thumping with bass, treble, tones, and other variables. The lights are neat, but I got if and kept it for the sound output. - Quality – nicely built. Heavy material which adds to the bass. I use it in the shower, so I know condensation is not an issue. Have not taken it in water, you will have to let me know how that goes. - Value for the money – you get a lot of sound for your buck. If all speakers this size plays like this, then you can only get the same, not better. - Connectivity – connected easily to my phone on the first attempt. Now I only have to turn it on and it connects every time. - Portability – Love the cord that comes with it. I am able to hang it in the shower or on a hook in the garage. I also take it outside in the yard and dust and bugs don’t affect it. - Battery life – the battery last a very, very, very, very...did I mention “very” long time? Well it does! I also like that it lets you know when the battery is going low. - Reliability – has been working perfectly since I got it. Never had an issue with it turning on or connecting. - Volume – it is very loud. Cons - None

reviews.title: Was a workhorse, bought another.
reviews.body: I have one I got from someone else. Have been using it for nearly three years. The other day it was turning itself off every few songs even when plugged in like it was powering down and the lights quit working. I looked it up to see if buying a new one was an option. I can’t believe these are only $30. From what I got out of the other one, and how it sounds, I figured it’d be $70-80 for a new one. New purple one came today. Highly recommend at this price point for sure. Always connects right to my phone, always had a long battery life unplugged, great sound for the size, and versatile due to compactness and alleged waterproofing. I dropped it prolly a hundred times, threw it at the wall once or twice. Lasted me three years and wasn’t brand new when I got it. I rarely leave reviews… this one I had to. If you have read this far, I recommend using the eq button on the speaker as well as an eq on whatever app you’re playing music through. No a 30 dollar speaker isn’t going to play standard eq well. You have to cut mids out a few decibels to get clear bass and highs. Simple way to make this speaker sound great instead of good.

reviews.title: Love it!!!!
reviews.body: It’s small, easy to carry, has an amazing long-lasting battery, and GREAT sound! I lost my first one at the beach and had to get another one, and honestly, it was a great investment. I take it to the beach, the park, and even use it in my room when I don’t want to bother anyone in the house with super-loud music from the living room. 😂 The functionality is great, and the fact that there are no cables needed is definitely a plus. It’s convenient, portable, and looks good too, just as mentioned. Definitely a great little speaker and worth the investment!

reviews.title: Bought it twice because apparently it’s that good
reviews.body: I originally picked up this BolaButty Bluetooth speaker for my wife to use at work during in house meetings so she could easily connect and play audio. The installation was basically nonexistent, just pair it and go, which made setup super quick. For its size, this thing puts out some serious power. The sound quality is surprisingly strong and clear, easily filling a room without sounding tinny. It handled presentations really well and made everything more professional. The controls are simple and easy to use, which is great when you don’t want to fumble around mid meeting. Overall functionality is exactly what you’d want from a portable speaker, reliable and straightforward. Now here’s the part that says it all. Someone liked it so much they decided to permanently “borrow” it from her desk. So I ended up buying a second one. That alone should tell you everything you need to know. Definitely worth the money and apparently worth guarding closely too.

reviews.title: Rival JBL
reviews.body: Based on the reviews I opted to pick up a pair of these speakers. The comparison JBLs are over $100 each...so took the gamble. I am very impressed with the pair, for the size the have great sound, rival the competition absolutely. I bought them for camping trip but had to test them out before obviously. Easy to pair them to play together. I cant speak on the 30 hr battery yet but for the price these are great, have good volume and pretty good bass too, and they light up. The come with cords to charge and another dual to plug in to a head phone style jack. I used w my Alexa for better sound with no problems. For the size I feel like they exceeded expectations. Says waterproof thats a bonus, but again cant speak on that yet

reviews.title: Perfect on your golf cart, deck, boat, or anywhere!
reviews.body: We bought one of these Bluetooth speakers for the golf cart and people have said it works better than their installed speakers. The price is fantastic too! So when we needed a blueprint speaker for our deck, we knew exactly what to buy! Really great sound, rechargeable, perfect size and good price. Have sent the link to several people for this great product!

reviews.title: Great Sound
reviews.body: So far it has worked great! The sound quality is very good and clear. It’s perfect size, It’s heavier than I thought, for me that’s a good thing. The wind picks up and it stays steady on the patio table. No issues connecting to my iPhone Apps. Haven’t tried to hook to the TV. Not sure if it’s capable. I wish it had USB, I have a lot of music on them.

reviews.title: Sound not as good (lacks bass even on Bass mode) as I'd hope, and some tech issues
reviews.body: Update 3: I am not doing "never ending updates" but just typing this to say that the issue STILL hasn't come back. The one thing I have noticed is that i am getting NO WHERE NEAR the "30 hour playtime" ... even 20 maybe pushing it. I am disappointed in that but overall ... I dont mind the speaker. Something in my reviews I thought of mentioning is that while this speaker doesn't sound as dynamic as others ... a "more even sound ... even if that means it lacks a 'thump' in the bass"... IS NOT always a bad thing ... say my Tribit XSound Surf ... listening to smooth jazz at night at low volumes ... it has "too much" of a thump ... this speaker not having that in my view ... makes this one better in some cases .... same way with my DOSS Soundbox Touch having a similar sound (but better mids/highs i think) Update 2: been a few days and "constant use" since the last update. The issue with no sound has NOT come up again yet ... and while i forgot what i have rated the Oontz Angle 3 Ultra (3.5?) i may have to bump that up to 3.75 (not to get crazy with decimals) when i say this ... but i'd give this a 3.5... yeah with certain genres it seems "flat" and lacking bass i'd like (I like a clean bass at best ... not overly done, so i am no "bass head") but other times my new favorites the Tribit XSound Gos have a "subwoofer like sound" (WHICH IS WHY it is my favorite ... at times) but late at night at low volumes i wish i could turn that extra bass off ... I BRING THAT UP due to the fact that THIS SPEAKER sort of has THAT type of sound. So with say easy listening, instrumental, and some jazz stuff in that exact situation ... i DONT DISLIKE the Tribit ... I just like the "lack of bass" (so to speak) more. I cant remember if i recommended or didn't recommend this in my original review.. to me now i'd say this is "ok" (even if that sound issue comes up where i have to play sound in a different app to get it back again, issue comes up) ... you can do better "bang for buck" but ... this is not terrible either. Update 1: Ok after trying what another reviewer said and trying to reset the speaker (pressing power button and holding for at least 8 seconds) I got things to work again. I also couldn’t get any sound in Kodi with my local media but after opening up another app and playing audio fine in that, (same device), then going back to Kodi sound in there worked again. I cant explain what happened but as I said others are having this issue too, but someone mentioned this and it worked for me. Now I plan on sort of doing part of what I planned to in the original review, I have a few other BT speaker, which include an Oontz Angle 3 Ultra, two Tribit Xsound Surfs, two Tribit Xsound Gos, a DOSS Soundbox Touch and a Braven BRV1BCB BRV-1. Versus the Tribits: - to me while I wish the Xsound Surf had better battery life (ONLY ADVERTISED at 10hr) … I would still say either the Xsound Surf or the XSound GO are the better option. They are my favorites and just overall in the same price range … they are just a better value and MUCH better sound. Versus the DOSS Soundbox Touch: - This is where it is interesting. I have not done an “A-vs-B” comparision head to head but out of all my speakers, this speaker sounds closest to this one. If I remember, the bass on the DOSS seems lower at lower volumes but while not like other speakers I have or a “Sub woofer” type sound. It gets more “present” as the volume goes up. It sounds clear and balanced but not for “bass heads”. I think the DOSS may sound better than this one, however its close … I think this speaker’s tuning in the mids are a little off but like the DOSS I’d say both of these speakers are a more “balanced” sound without a subwoofer like “thump”. Versus the Oontz Angle 3 Ultra: - note: I can only compare this to the Ultra model … I hear that if you go down in Oontz models they don’t sound as good. - This is where I wish I could take the extra bass in the Ultra and put it in the X10. The bass is there in the Ultra but while not muddy in MY VIEW. It CAN “linger” a bit. Where it slightly effects the low mids and mid-mids depending on the track. This I feel is exactly what the X10 here is MISSING, EVEN ON Bass Boost mode in the built in EQ. - Build quality – even if the Ultra is NOT my favorite speaker, I still totally recommend it and like it… the build quality alone (not the only thing) blew me away, for the sub $40 price I paid for it. Versus the Braven: - I admit that I do not use this as much as I should. This was gifted to me by someone who had no use for it and .. .well I love this one. It has a decent thump in the bass but not overdone. From what I remember this sort of reminds me of a Tribit tuning … a Good V-shaped sound but clean and not “forced” or overdone. (sound wise) “Everything is where it should be” Summary: I still cant say I recommend this due to the problems I had BUT if its a “ok this is a dumb fix to a problem that shouldn’t exist in the first place” (almost a James May quote) thing if I have the no sound issue again… Ok … I am ok with keeping this and I am not as “upset” (I don’t want to ham that up) about it. The bottom line is (say the “360 sound” that is just fake marketing … If it was “this looks like a JBL Flip but this is not 360 sound .. it just LOOKS the same” … ok then) … I just cant “trust” this speaker… not until I have more time with it and it behaves fine … I will be GLAD to do a second update to report the good news, if that happens. ---------------------------------------- Original Review I was going to write a more in detail review, comparing this speaker to various others I have but unfortunately things are not looking great. I am not 100% saying I am returning this already, but it looks like it may go in that direction. I will list some Cons but .. .things are not all bad when it was working correctly… Hopefully I can not some things as I go. Cons: - Sound quality – ok this is not all bad … but I knew this would lack bass … I get it but even with a V shaped EQ on top of the speaker (same I have set in the same app for ALL others I have) ..and even in this speaker’s third EQ setting “Bass Boost” there is a lack of bass in most genres, people would typically listen to. HOWEVER one of my use cases is late at night listening to say intrumental, Jazz, or Classical music. The lack of a big “Thump” in the bass (which CAN be overdone in other speakers I have heard) … wasn’t too bad and with those genres at lower volumes … the sound quality wasn’t bad. Really I’d never call it “muddy” but even bass boost (built in EQ) sounded like there was a lack of “average bass”. ALSO THIS IS NOT 360 sound. Sure you hear sounds from all sides but the two speakers are only facing one way (the exact opposite side of where the buttons are) … that is the direction things sound “clearest” … the sound is different on any other side and with the lack of bass … including the “bass” radiators on the side as part of the “360” is laughable in itself. - Voice pompt – this wouldn’t be too bad if it wasn’t SO LOUD … late at night it a bit loud compared to say where the volume is set … “BLUETOOTH MODE” “BLUETOOTH CONNECTED” … again I’d like just a beep or something like a ton but even the voice wouldn’t be that bad IF it was a “few clicks” lower in volume. Unsure (Pro? Con?) - Build quality – I WILL SAY this doesn’t feel super cheap, but others like my Oontz Angle 3 Ultra, or any of my Tribit speakers, just feel better. I also have to say I have never had a JBL Flip or any other speakers with an “all over” grill … and I knew I was getting this so maybe versus other speakers, this “style” makes it feel less solid … I could get a JBL Flip and think “oh … they ‘feel’ the same” build quality wise. ------------------------- My main issue – I was thinking of MAYBE returning this, having my sights on a Tribit speaker I have not experienced yet, but with the other Tribit speakers I DO have, blowing me away overall, I have kept my eye on a sale for that one. Not even a week into owning this speaker, while all devices connect to the speaker, the speaker outputs ZERO audio from any COMFIRMED CONNECTED device in bluetooth mode. I do admit PART (but just half at best) use-case is the microsd card slot and one reason I wanted this speaker. In addition to Rain and Ocean waves (“sound machine style”) I wanted to load a microsd card up with that sort of stuff and say maybe smooth jazz and sort of use it as a “custom” sound machine. Right now the microsd card slot function STILL outputs audio and it doesn’t sound bad … but with no sound no matter what I do (including a speaker reset) working … in under 7 days of having this…. I cant even trust this will last. I do note that many of the negative reviews also mention this exact problem. I can live with the sound quality being “meh” at best for typical genres and this only being a good speaker in specific use-cases but now there is no audio for any bluetooth … that is a deal breaker. I just CANT recommend this speaker. While my Tribit speakers are my favorite, I will say I have an Oontz Angle 3 Ultra and sound wise it has the opposite problem (bass tends to … not make things muddy… but it’s bass “lingers a bit too long” at times) … I still LOVE and recommend that speaker.

reviews.title: Incredible Sound, Long Battery Life & Perfect for Anywhere! 🔊
reviews.body: I’m extremely impressed with this Bluetooth speaker! The sound is loud, clear, and well-balanced, with rich bass that makes music sound amazing indoors and outdoors. Despite its compact size, the audio quality exceeded my expectations. The IPX7 waterproof rating is perfect for using it in the shower, by the pool, at the beach, or while camping without worrying about water. The battery lasts a long time, and Bluetooth 5.3 provides a fast, stable connection with excellent range. I also love the dual pairing feature, which creates an even more immersive listening experience. It’s lightweight, portable, and easy to take anywhere. Overall, this speaker offers outstanding performance and excellent value for the price. Highly recommended!

reviews.title: fonctionne tres bien😁
reviews.body: il fonctionne très bien. il est très doux au toucher sonne assez fort au maximum moi j'aime beaucoup mon produit 🙂

reviews.title: Un altavoz bueno, bonito y barato.

reviews.title: Son parfait et autonomie
reviews.body: Très bon son et grande autonomie

reviews.title: Honest review after 7 months
reviews.body: I didn't want to write a review straight away and waited till I use it for several months. I gotta say, I'm very happy about those speakers. It does the job efficiently and it's very practical. The sound quality is very decent for that category. Crisp and clear sound however the bass is not the deepest of course. Charging time is quite quick I'd say. Battery life is very very good. Connectivity is seamless and easy with all of my devices. I use it a lot outdoors while on the beach or when I'm cycling. title: Soundcore Boom 2 by Anker, 80W Outdoor Bluetooth Speaker, 24H Playtime

reviews.title: Ultimate Outdoor Powerhouse – Incredible Bass and Battery Life!
reviews.body: I am absolutely blown away by the Soundcore Boom 2. If you are looking for the perfect outdoor speaker, this is it. ​Sound Quality & Bass: The sound profile is incredibly crisp, but the star of the show is the "BassUp" feature. For a speaker this size, the bass hits remarkably deep without distorting the mids or highs. It easily fills a large backyard or noisy beach area. ​Design & Portability: The built-in handle makes it super easy to grab and go. It feels rugged, well-built, and durable enough to handle drops or outdoor elements. The synced LED lights on the side are a fun touch for evening hangouts. ​Battery Life & Waterproofing: The battery life is phenomenal—it easily lasts through a full weekend trip on a single charge. Plus, the IPX7 waterproof rating gives me total peace of mind by the pool. It even floats if it accidentally drops in the water! ​App Integration: I highly recommend downloading the Soundcore app. The customizable EQ lets you fine-tune the sound exactly to your liking, which elevates the experience even further. ​Bottom Line: Anker has outdone themselves. It offers premium, booming sound at a fraction of the price of its competitors. Highly recommended!

reviews.title: Good sound with deep bass, lightweight and many more awesome features
reviews.body: The Anker Soundcore Boom 2 is a serious contender in the portable speaker game. It’s super well-built with premium materials and packs a punch with loud, crisp sound and surprisingly deep bass. Bluetooth pairing is seamless and instant, and despite all that power, it’s remarkably lightweight and easy to carry around. Since it’s waterproof, you can take it anywhere without stressing whether you're by the pool, beach or at a party with friends. Plus, the battery life holds up for hours even with the extra bass button cranked, and the Soundcore app is a huge bonus in my opinion, letting you tune your audio with a customizable EQ, tweak the LED light show, and keep the speaker running smoothly with firmware updates. Love it and recommended to y'all.

reviews.title: It’s not Bose..but it’s REALLY close.
reviews.body: This portable bluetooth speaker is AMAZING!! It fit in my carryon backpack and was perfect for a trip to the beach! So easy to use and it a a cool LED light show on each end of the speaker. Held a charge for my whole vacation! Plenty of powerful bass and strong mids and highs! I want to get another one as you can link tgem up in party mode!! Its not Bose, but it’s REALLY close!!

reviews.title: Love it
reviews.body: Makes hanging in the backyard so much more fun. Bass definitely hits rights and the way it pairs with my galaxy s25 ultra is lovely. A match made in heaven. Its easy the operate, if you can't figure it out return it and buy some paper cups and strings. Batteries last long and the build quality is a1.

reviews.title: Amazing sound quality and portability!
reviews.body: Wow! I just ordered this for $85 and I’m blown away. This sounds better than any of the smaller Bose speakers I’ve had over the years. It has plenty of base and I can’t imagine most people ever needing anything louder. I think it looks nice, and the lights are sort of cool, although I don’t imagine I’ll use them much. The fact it’s fairly small and waterproof only adds to the value. I also just saw you can pair two speakers together to get stereo sound with separate right and left channels! Most people may not care about this but for me having portable stereo sound would be amazing. l just ordered a second one and I’ll update after I try it. No matter what happens, this is a steal at $85 and probably still a bargain at regular price.

reviews.title: Nice for the price
reviews.body: Bought this as audio and some lights for my golf cart. Its pretty nice. Not as loud as I wanted, but thats just me. Its plenty loud though. Bass boost works well. Lights are cool. Battery is definitely good. Sat outside overnight in a light rain and it wasnt an issue. Well built.

reviews.title: Impressive Speaker
reviews.body: I work as a grill cook, which means I’m in a very noisy environment. So I need a speaker that is very loud. And I can say this speaker gets very loud for its size, but is never harsh on the ears, like some other speakers which leave an almost ringing in your ears after a high note. And it does not distort at max volume which is a plus for me. I used to have a 50w Rave Neo from soundcore, until recently when I sold it to a coworker who was in need of a good speaker. I had it for nearly 5 years. When I had it, I was constantly getting compliments on how impressive that speaker sounded. So I decided to buy another speaker from Anker since it’s quality I can trust. Comparing to the 50w Rave Neo, both with bass boost, and boom 2 out of box sound profile. The boom 2 gets louder than the rave Neo, however gets a little “muddier” at high volumes, while the rave Neo keeps a fuller sound. Probably due to the fact the boom 2 is missing a full range driver, and only has tweeters and a racetrack “subwoofer”. However does not matter in my use case. The battery life seems the same, after 3 hours of use at high volumes with bass on, I only used 40% of the battery on the boom 2, while I also used 40% of the rave Neo. Portability goes to the Boom 2. It is only the length of a ruler, height of 3/4 of a ruler, and is fairly slim. so it fits on any standard sized table easily, it also weighs less than half what the rave Neo weighs. The rave Neo felt like a workout carrying it work, while the boom 2 is easily carried by one finger. I also give appearances to the boom 2. The metal grill on the boom 2 feels very rugged and is much superior to the metal grill on the rave Neo. Both plastics feel the same as well, however it does seem the boom 2 is more vulnerable to scuffs and marks as I already have a scuff on the boom 2 with only 3 hours of use, while I have never gotten a scuff on the rave Neo. The LIGHTSHOW. The boom 2 is amazing to watch as it lights up and moves the radiators to the music. Very nice touch since I never really enjoyed the lights on the rave Neo. The rave Neo was also impressive, but the diffusion on the boom 2 looks very premium. Charging. Both charge with an input of usb type c. However, with the rave Neo, you had to use a usb type A charging block, which was super annoying because I have been trying to get away from usb type a, and micro usb. Type c charging blocks and cords are worlds superior. And the boom 2 can charge from any type c charging block. Sound. The boom 2 is loud. It is not audiophile quality. But if you plan on sticking it in the corner of the room or on the outside of a basketball court, you might not feel or hear every instrument or every vocal chord in a singers throat, but I guarantee you will be satisfied with the volume of music you are receiving from this speaker, which does sound very pleasant at least, which is what this speaker is meant to do. Get loud, so you can listen to music while you are doing other activities. I highly recommend higher end soundcore speakers, can’t go wrong.

reviews.title: Big sound from a small box
reviews.body: I’m very happy with the volume and fullness of the sound coming from this little box. I bought this for outside on the patio and around the pool. I had been using a Bose Flex, which was great for indoor near-field listening, but a little weak for outside. This Boom 2 gets plenty loud enough to reach the pool half way across the yard at a comfortable listening level, and it can easily get loud enough to annoy the neighbors. Music is full and clear - the bass won’t rattle the furniture, which I never expected from a box this size, but there’s plenty of it for casual listening and small outdoor gatherings, for which this guy is perfect. Bluetooth connection to my iPhone is flawless; once it’s paired, you just need to turn it on and it automatically connects. The Soundcore app is easy enough to use if you need it, which I usually don’t. I just turn it on and start the music on my phone, and the party is on. USB-C charging is convenient, because almost every gadget I have uses it now, so there are plenty of charging points around the house.

La batterie dure très longtemps, surtout lorsque vous éteignez les lumières, gadget pour faire joli sympa mais pas très utile. Dans l'ensemble : excellent produit, à tel point que je n'ai commandé une deuxième, en jumelant les deux enceintes on atteint une puissance max de 160 w pour une valeur max de 200€ (2 fois 99€) très rentable. Excellent pour regarder un film sur tablette. Enceinte polyvalente qui se prête à tous les usages et à tous les espaces.
