title: JBL Grip Portable Bluetooth Speaker, Waterproof, Ambient Light - Black

reviews.title: Phenomenal mini portable speaker!!
reviews.body: I didn't expect much for this price point but I was pleasantly surprised! The audio quality on this JBL speaker is top notch. It was very easy to setup and it also has an app that allows you to change the colors on the speaker, adjust the equalizer, and connect to other JBL speakers so you can really have a party. Battery life is very solid - I didn't even charge it fully when I first opened it and that hour of charge gave me several hours of music. It doesn't come with a charging cord for the USB-c but I had plenty lying around so it wasn't a big deal to me. It is small and compact, perfect for pool days or bringing along to enjoy music on the go. I also adore the pink color - perfect for me! It's so good that I might buy a second one for my husband. Definitely don't hesitate to make this purchase!

reviews.title: The BEST Speaker I've ever owned!
reviews.body: I LOVE this speaker. I typically don't purchase higher-end products (because I'm quite the cheapskate) but I am SO glad I chose to indulge in this JBL Grip. It is totally worth the extra money spent. I got the red design, and it has a very sleek and clean design. The buttons on it are straightforward and responsive. Also, this thing is LOUD. I had it on about half volume, and it had my music loud enough to fill my entire bedroom, and even loud enough to make my family hear it from outside my room. Not only is it loud, but the sound quality is super rich and incredibly clear. This speaker is the perfect weight and is small enough to fit in a cup-holder, but still has such a strong enough speaker to pack a big punch! Also, it has about 4 different light-settings for the back of the speaker, which I love! This speaker is perfect for me, and totally worth it. The only downside is that it does NOT come with its own USB-c charger which is a little unfortunate since this speaker only has around a 12-hour battery life, but for how good of a speaker this is, I honestly can't complain that much.

reviews.title: Impressive
reviews.body: The JBL Grip is an impressive little Bluetooth speaker that delivers much bigger sound than its compact size suggests. The JBL Pro Sound is clear, crisp, and has surprisingly deep bass, making it perfect for listening to music at home, outdoors, or on the go. The ambient light feature is a nice touch and adds a fun atmosphere without being distracting. Pairing with my phone was quick and easy, and the Bluetooth connection has been reliable. The orange color also stands out and gives the speaker a unique, stylish look. Overall, this is a well-built, portable speaker with excellent sound quality, easy connectivity, and a fun design. If you're looking for a compact Bluetooth speaker that's easy to carry and sounds great, the JBL Grip is definitely worth considering.

reviews.title: Great sound, and for a reasonable price.
reviews.body: This is a terrific little bluetooth speaker that paired easily with my iphone 16. I'm no audio expert but this speaker has great quality, no tinny sound, and good base level. Read the details as this speaker does not come with a USB-C charger, which is no problem as I have plenty at home for charging other devices. I've had the speaker for less than a week, have used it twice, and so far I'm loving it.

reviews.title: Incredible Speaker! Sounds Great! But….
reviews.body: Prior to this purchase, I had owned three other Bluetooth speakers. The first was Anker. A cheap speaker that sounded meh and became tinny. And, TWO PulseSound speakers that tore after a bit of base. This JBL speaker sounds AMAZING but the battery life SUCKS. While I was waiting for this to arrive, I was using my Anker speaker, which I didn’t have a charger for, and it played for about three days straight with no charge. The JBL barely lasts 12 hours before it needs a charge. It’s a small price to pay for a quality Bluetooth speaker that sounds as good as this one does.

title: Oraolo S320 Bluetooth Speaker, Portable Bluetooth Speaker, 40W True Wireless Speaker,360° Stereo Sound Effect,IPX7 Waterproof Speaker, 32 Hour Playing Time,Suitable for Outdoor Speakers, Black
Outdoor Bluetooth Speaker, IPX7 Waterproof, 90W Peak, 32H, Black

reviews.title: Does not disappoint
reviews.body: The IPX7 Waterproof Outdoor Bluetooth Speaker has honestly impressed me more than I expected. It was recommended by my brother, and for the price, it performs better than a lot of bigger-name brands I’ve tried. The sound quality is crisp and clear, with no noticeable degradation so far even after regular use. It delivers enough volume and fullness to work well indoors or outdoors without sounding muddy or overly distorted. Connection has also been straightforward. Devices pair quickly, and the USB-C support is a welcome feature compared to older connection types. Having both USB and Type-C compatibility adds a bit of convenience and flexibility depending on your setup. Battery life is another strong point. It holds a charge for a long time, which makes it reliable for extended use or outdoor settings. The tradeoff is that it’s not a particularly fast recharge, so you’ll want to plan ahead rather than expect a quick top-off before heading out. The waterproofing is another plus, especially for outdoor use or keeping around a work area where accidents happen. Combined with the long battery life, it feels like a speaker designed more for actual use than just shelf appeal. Now comes the real test: durability. In this era of planned obsolescence, the question is how well it will hold up after a year or more of regular use. That’s ultimately what separates decent electronics from genuinely reliable gear. Still, first impressions are strong. The overall design feels practical and time-tested, with a bit of an old-school sensibility that focuses more on utility than gimmicks. Overall, this speaker punches above its price point. It’s practical, sounds good, connects quickly, and avoids a lot of the overhyped branding that bigger companies rely on. For the money, it’s been a solid buy.

reviews.title: Great value. Great sound.
reviews.body: I've had this speaker for over a year, and its still going strong. It sits on my covered front porch most of the year, and occasional rain mist/humidity doesn't seem to affect it at all. It seems very solid and well-built. The sound is great, with impressive bass and overall volume level. The battery life is good too, but I can't say for sure exactly how long because I keep it plugged to a charger most of the time.

I am upset I have to replace it already however I do feel like I got what I paid for 👍 the speaker is super loud it's got good bass

reviews.title: Unbelievably good at the price point.
reviews.body: This is one very impressive Bluetooth Speaker. So good in fact that within a hour of the delivery of the first one I bought another one. I can't wait to hear how 2 sound connected with the way the first one sounds. Im not easily impressed when it comes to music and sounds being a bit of a audiophile. But I am completely and totally impressed with this speaker. It's just that good. The bass is even better than I expected. The clarity and volume are equally impressive. It connected to my phone and my tablet without a second wasted. It looks good, sounds amazing and is going to be difficult to beat . It's fairly heavy for it's size which surprised me. It's really that good. You won't be disappointed if you buy one . It's versatility and functionality are as impressive as it's sound quality. I went for a ride in my hot rod Jeep CJ5 and had no problem hearing the speaker loud and clear. And my jeep isn't exactly quiet but I heard every note and verse without any problems. Can't wait until I get the 2nd one I just ordered. Im not exaggerating, it really is that good ! Update... I received the 2nd speaker and it is just as I expected as far as sound quality and performance. They sound fantastic and the difference between having a single speaker and having a 2nd speaker is significant but not as significant as I expected it to be. I thought that the bass and mid range sounds would increase and that would improve the only thing I think needs improvement with these speakers. That's the Bass and Midrange sound quality. They have Bass and Midrange sound but I think it could be or should have been much better with 2 speakers. There was a improvement but not as much as I expected There would be. There aren't 2 passive radiators on the rear that I can see. There's a long oval shaped thing that I guess is what they are calling w passive radiator. Even using my Dolby Sound app on my phone and the different sound levels and music type preset equalizer settings still produces little or no noticeable Bass or Midrange improvements in reality. 1 speaker sounds good and 2 sound much better than 1. But 2 don't improve the sound quality and range of performance the way I expected it to. The speakers are really good considering the price. They could even be described as Great. But they certainly could be better than they are . But at the current price point they are a fantastic bargain and are impressive without question. In a bedroom or small house they are undoubtedly going to be loud and sound great. But outside even having 2 of them turned up and separated by about 15 feet. They weren't as impressive or good as the 1st speaker led me to believe 2 of them would be. Definitely not bad , and a improvement over just 1 speaker. But definitely not the improvement as far as sound quality and overall volume one might anticipate. The stereo sound improved as it should have. But improvement in Bass or midrange sounds that I expected with the addition of another speaker just weren't what I expected or have experienced with other speakers in the past . Still a Great buy . But the addition of a second speaker linked to the first didn't provide the sound quality or volume I expected them to. They sound good but I expected there would be a more noticeable improvement in sound quality and volume with the 2nd speaker than I've observed.

title: JBL Charge 6 Portable Bluetooth Speaker, Waterproof, Drop-Proof - Blue

reviews.title: Reliable Performance with Refined Improvements
reviews.body: Overall Impression This is my second speaker from the JBL Charge line, and once again, I’m impressed. The Charge 6 builds on what already worked well in previous models while delivering dependable performance, strong sound quality, and easy usability. Design & Build Quality The speaker feels sturdy and well-constructed without being overly bulky. It’s portable, easy to move around, and sits securely on a variety of surfaces. Whether placed on a kitchen counter, coffee table, or taken outdoors, it feels durable enough for everyday use. Setup & Connectivity Setup is quick and straightforward. I’ve had no issues pairing the Charge 6 with any of my devices. Bluetooth connection is stable and reliable, something I really value, as I’ve owned other speakers that occasionally failed to appear or dropped connection. In this area, the Charge 6 performs consistently well. Sound Quality For a speaker in this price range, the sound quality is impressive. Volume: Gets surprisingly loud for its size. Clarity: Remains stable and clear even at higher volumes, with minimal distortion. Bass: Punchy and full without overpowering the mids and highs. Vocals: Crisp and easy to distinguish. The overall sound profile feels balanced and energetic, making it versatile for different genres of music. Compared to the JBL Charge 5 I upgraded from the Charge 5, which already delivered excellent sound. The difference here isn’t dramatic, but the Charge 6 feels slightly louder and punchier, with a bit more fullness at higher volumes. It’s more of a refinement than a complete redesign, but a noticeable and appreciated one. Ideal Use Cases This speaker is well-suited for small to medium-sized rooms and performs great for small outdoor gatherings or backyard settings. I liked it enough to purchase a second unit and place one in each corner of my living space for a more balanced, room-filling setup. The stereo pairing through the JBL Portable app is simple and works seamlessly. Whenever I have friends over, the sound quality consistently gets compliments. Battery Life JBL advertises up to 24 hours of playback (tested at 50% volume). In my experience, listening at around 60% volume yields approximately 17–19 hours on a single charge, which has been more than sufficient for daily use. If I had one minor critique, it would be that battery life drops more noticeably at very high volumes. For example, during an all-day beach trip or extended outdoor event where the speaker is running near maximum volume, you may need to recharge sooner than expected. That said, for normal day-to-day listening and typical gatherings, battery performance has been dependable and not a deal breaker for me. Final Verdict The JBL Charge 6 delivers strong, punchy sound, reliable connectivity, and solid battery performance in a durable, portable design. While the upgrade from the Charge 5 isn’t dramatic, it’s a meaningful refinement. Overall, it’s a great value for the performance it provides and an easy recommendation for anyone looking for a versatile Bluetooth speaker.

reviews.title: Great product. Arrived quickly!
reviews.body: This JBL waterproof speaker arrived well packaged and in perfect condition. The box was sealed, and everything was neatly packed inside. The charging cable and instructions were included. Setup was quick. Pairing with my phone took only a minute, and the Bluetooth connection has been stable. The buttons are easy to find and respond well. The speaker feels solid and well made. It has a durable exterior with a textured finish that provides a good grip. The compact size and handle make it easy to carry or toss into a backpack. Sound quality is impressive for the size. Voices are clear, and music has good balance with more bass than I expected. It gets plenty loud without sounding distorted at higher volumes. The waterproof design makes it a great choice for the patio, pool, beach, or shower. I also like that the battery lasts through several listening sessions before needing a recharge. Overall, this is a reliable portable speaker with excellent sound, simple controls, and solid build quality. It arrived exactly as described and has been easy to use from the first day. Great value for the money. I love how it arrived 2 hours after placing the order

reviews.title: The Ultimate Audio Wingman: Why the JBL Charge 6 Brings the Boom Without the Bulk!
reviews.body: We all know that feeling of finding the perfect piece of gear that just clicks with our lifestyle, and that is exactly what happened when I got my hands on the JBL Charge 6. In a sea of portable speakers that overpromise and underdeliver, this crisp, white beauty stands out as a true heavyweight in a surprisingly compact package. I am always on the move, whether I am out working in the garage, heading to the beach, or just kicking back by the backyard fire pit, and I need a device that can keep up. What struck me immediately about this particular model is how it completely redefines what a mid-sized portable speaker should be capable of handling. It is not just about making noise; it is about delivering a premium experience that seamlessly integrates into whatever crazy adventure my weekend throws at me. ​Let us talk about the absolute core of this device: the sound. The Bold JBL Pro Sound alone is phenomenal, but the real magic here is the AI Sound Boost technology. I have listened to countless audio setups, and I can confidently say that this proprietary audio processing algorithm fundamentally changes the game. It actively analyzes the music in real-time, pulling maximum acoustic performance out of the drivers while keeping distortion virtually non-existent, even when you crank the volume all the way up. The low-end bass kicks with a satisfying, punchy depth that you can feel in your chest, while the mids and highs remain exceptionally crisp and clear. Whether I am blasting classic rock anthems or heavy hip-hop tracks, the soundstage feels massive, filling up the entire patio or living room with rich, immersive audio that makes you forget you are listening to a portable unit. ​Now, an incredible-sounding speaker is useless to me if I have to baby it, which is why the rugged build of the Charge 6 is such a massive win. This thing is built like an absolute tank. It boasts serious waterproof and drop-proof credentials, meaning I never sweat it when a sudden rainstorm rolls in or when someone inevitably knocks it off the picnic table. I have watched it take a tumble directly onto hard concrete and brush it off like it was nothing, keeping the tunes rolling without a single hiccup. Adding to its utilitarian charm is the newly integrated, sturdy removable carrying strap. It sounds like a minor detail, but having that secure strap makes hauling it around infinitely easier. I can sling it over a bag, hang it from a hook in the workshop, or just keep a solid grip on it while hiking, all without compromising its sleek, streamlined white aesthetic. ​Perhaps the most crucial factor for a device that travels this much is endurance, and the battery life on the Charge 6 is nothing short of legendary. JBL packed this beast with up to 28 hours of playtime, and it absolutely delivers on that promise. I have taken it on multi-day camping trips and never once had to reach for a wall charger. But the absolute lifesaver is the built-in powerbank feature. We all know how fast smartphones drain when streaming high-quality music outdoors, so having the ability to plug my phone directly into the speaker to juice it back up while the playlist keeps pumping is incredibly practical. It is the ultimate two-in-one companion that ensures neither the party nor my phone dies prematurely. This speaker does not just meet my high standards for portable audio; it utterly shatters them.

reviews.title: Honest review of the JBL Charge 6 portable bluetooth speaker
reviews.body: At almost 60 years old, I’ve experienced just about every kind of audio system imaginable — component stereo systems, high-end car audio setups, premium headphones, earbuds, home theater systems, and portable speakers from many of the biggest brands. Because of that, it takes quite a bit to genuinely impress me when it comes to sound quality. The JBL Charge 6 absolutely impressed me. What JBL accomplished with this speaker is remarkable. The sound is incredibly powerful considering such a small footprint. This thing is compact enough to fit easily into almost any backpack, yet it produces bold, room-filling sound that feels much larger than the speaker itself. The audio quality is excellent. The highs are crystal clear, vocals sound clean and detailed, and the bass is deep, punchy, and robust without sounding muddy or distorted. Even at higher volumes, the sound remains balanced and enjoyable. The volume range is outstanding — this speaker gets surprisingly loud while still maintaining clarity. I’ve owned expensive audio equipment over the years, and honestly, the sound coming from this little speaker is shocking for its size. Whether indoors, outdoors, traveling, relaxing at home, or using it near water, the JBL Charge 6 consistently delivers an impressive listening experience. Bluetooth connectivity is fast and simple, and the portability is one of its biggest strengths. JBL also did a great job with durability. The waterproof and drop-proof design makes it ideal for everyday life, travel, and outdoor use without constantly worrying about damaging it. Battery life and durability seem to vary somewhat based on user experiences. Many people report excellent battery life that lasts all day, while others feel it could be better depending on usage and volume levels. Most users praise the rugged build quality, though a few have experienced durability concerns after heavy use. Overall, this speaker exceeded my expectations. After decades of owning and listening to high-end audio equipment, I can honestly say the JBL Charge 6 delivers an incredible amount of performance, clarity, and power for such a compact portable speaker. Small speaker. Massive sound. Very impressive product from JBL.

Connects to Bluetooth devices seamlessly. Its a great size for a small bathroom because it's not big or bulky. Really appreciate the small, slim design. We don't try to blast it for the neighborhood to hear it but sounds good outdoors around a group of friends by the fire or for background tunes while having a card night with buddies. Even works well and sounds good in the garage while working with power tools. Would probably even be great on a river float. Very happy and satisfied with this little speaker.

reviews.title: Powerful, Personal, Portable Flex Speaker
reviews.body: The Bose SoundLink Flex 2nd Gen speaker is hands down my favorite bluetooth speaker, though I do own the latest Beats Pill and love it for its capabilities. At present, I own eight of these 2nd Gen Flex speakers, one in each color variant. I do find that audiobooks, podcasts and spoken content sound best on the 2nd Gen Flex. Most Music does as well. Some reviewers report sound differences between the color variants. After initially suspecting this and repeatedly comparing the identical audio on each speaker, I found that the most likely explanation is how one is holding the speaker when audio is playing, as the audio does change based on the position of the speaker. Features I would like to see in the 3rd Gen model include: Much longer battery life. The technology and capabilities exist. The speaker is so excellent that paying a little more for much longer battery life, perhaps double, would be worth it. Lossless ability. When connecting the latest Bose Ultra headphones and even the Beats Pill to my iPhone with the Usb C to Usb C cables, each offer lossless streaming. The ability to connect the Flex to a CD player or some other audio device via the cable. There are Usb C to 3.5mm male and female cables on the market and this would be nice as I still have a small Bose CD player and plenty of CDs. While there are bluetooth transmitters such as the AirFly which make connectivity possible, direct wired connectivity is still nice for some of us. A detachable strap. The Beats Pill and the most excellent Bose SoundLink Micro 2nd Gen both offer a detachable strap. This would be a nice option for the Flex in the future. Pairing four Flex speakers in surround sound mode. While two Flex speakers are great in stereo, pairing four for surround sound would be next level great. The ability to change the volume of the obnoxious sounds the Flex puts out. I do like these sounds, particularly when the speaker connects to bluetooth. However, these are way too loud. The Beats Pill has the option of controlling the volume of its sounds. The same is true for the voice prompts. While some of the voice prompts can be disabled in the app, the volume cannot be changed. Even without these potential additions to a 3rd Gen Flex, this existing 2nd Gen Flex is a phenomenal bluetooth speaker that serves many purposes. The Alpine Sage color variant has been discontinued, as it was limited. However, the existing color options are excellent, particularly the Twilight Blue. Although the Flex and Beats Pill are both excellent and come down to personal preference when selecting one or the other, I would also go with the Flex if I did not have the luxury of owning both. In fact, I would go with the Flex over any other, even if it has yet to fulfill all its potential, which with the suggestions I mentioned for the 3rd Gen Flex, it would be an untouchable speaker. Highly recommend the 2nd Gen Flex to all reading this.

reviews.title: Bose Compact TV Subwoofer is a Great Value!
reviews.body: I recently bought this compact Bose soundbar on Amazon for $199.00. I can honestly say that it exceeds my expectations! Right out of the box you get the sense it’s a high quality product! The construction is solid and robust. My Bose soundbar is connected a recent model Samsung 32” QLED television via the HDMI Arc terminal. The audio quality is quite good IMO. Blindfolded you would swear the speaker was much larger. It’s got great high frequency response and the middle frequencies are crisp, balanced, possessing outside speech clarity. The bass is somewhat attenuated but given the compact size of the speaker it’s still very respectable. If you’re so inclined you can connect compatible Bose subwoofer to supplement the bass frequencies. I believe the Bose subwoofer represents a terrific value in the crowded home speaker market. I’m giving it 5 Stars since it exceeds my expectations!

reviews.title: Decent mini soundbar
reviews.body: Pros - compact, good size for a 40-55" TV - better sound than most built in TV speakers I've heard; not going to fool you into being in a theater without a sub or surrounds, but not meant to, so does the job it was built for - mostly easy setup, plug and play with a Samsung LCD TV from 2022 - does not require much space - good for bedroom TV or guest room TV Why not five stars? - power cable is way too short and plugs in at one side of back instead of center, making setup and positioning a pain - white power led on front is distracting - no bundled HDMI cable for eARC - remote uses coin battery instead of more common AAA - rubber feed to prevent vibration only at two sides, needed to add a middle foot to prevent rattle against TV stand since the stand was narrower than the speaker - otherwise I would need to position it well in front of the TV taking up more space - could do without silver Bose logo on top/front for a cleaner look - maybe make it gray or black - remote's "Bass" button has no visible or on screen feedback or menu to tell if it's on or off that I can find, and audio isn't different enough except for high volume movies to notice

reviews.title: INSANELY good for a small office/bedroom
reviews.body: I was looking for a small home office set up (10 X 12 room) and wanted something that was uncomplicated but also sounded really good given the room size. It's used primarily for music, but I'm often in meetings with up to 20 other people, so I wanted something with a voice clarity option. I figured I was going to have to sacrifice one for the other, but the speaker really delivers! What was most amazing to me was the level and quality of bass, which I didn't think was possible with a standalone sound bar, and a small sound bar at that. When I bought this, I also bought the bass module 500 which I've since returned, as it was completely unnecessary. The speaker produces a very balanced soundstage. I placed the soundbar across two studio monitor speaker stands with a 15 degree tilt, super highly recommended if you're planning to use this for a home office solution. This is absolutely not a speaker as a standalone in a larger room, but it's perfect for a small space. No subwoofer needed. You can literally feel the bass.

Bose dropped the ball on this one and seem to be living now off their name of top-quality products and service in the past and you know what starts to happen when you cut back on the quality, you start to lose your long time customers and no repurchase's from most new ones so business starts to decline, and we all know what has happened to big companies in the past. The Bluetooth is version is 4.2, that came out around 2011 or 12 so outdated, much cheaper brands even have the newer versions, heck the remote is not even Bluetooth! You have to make sure no other devices have Bluetooth on to connect to a single device you want par and listen two, a lot of others allow two at once so you can switch back and forth. There is absolutely no way to turn on or control the sound bar if you lose the remote, battery goes bad or if the remote goes bad, but we all know that does not happen now does it? For a 300-dollar soundbar especially from Bose I expected more, half was for the name and the other half for the actual worth of the unit and to get more bass I need to spend over $500.00 more when other top brand units come with a sound bar for under $300.00. I should be able to connect other subwoofer brands to this unit but from all my checking only a couple of people have gotten lucky, I have two and neither one will work with this unit when I connected them, so It's kind of like I gotcha from Bose if you want to upgrade your sound bar for $500.00 plus more to Bose. Yes, looks like this one is going back to Bose. Update: I decided to keep the speaker even as disappointed as I am with this so outdated speaker and mine was made in 2023 and then 28 days after using it just stopped working after being on for about a hour and a half, it only blinks the two lights white 3 times and turns the tv side light green and does this over and over again and will not turn off unless you unplug it, plug it back up and light off a couple of minutes then automatically turns back on and starts the same process over and over, So much for quality Bose I did not even get a months' worth of use and thank goodness I had two days left to return, never again for me Bose. Service is nonexistent never got a answer for a simple question I sent earlier so just imagine how it is with a real problem.

reviews.title: Excellent audio with consistent levels
reviews.body: This is my third and hopefully final soundbar in my hunt for something that just works. I did a bit of research that landed me on the Bose TV Speaker. This is for a living room with a 20' ceiling and a TV mounted above the fireplace. With young kids, the TV is usually on their shows during the day or mom and dad trying to watch something in the evening. We aren't looking to be fully immersed in booming action movies, dialogue is the focus. The last one I had would drown out dialogue with background music and I was always trying to adjust the levels. This is perfect, I don't have to fiddle with it and it does a great job of staying consistent and I never have an issue hearing dialogue. It connected easily to my Roku TV and even supports Roku TV integration, allowing me to adjust things through the TV interface. I like that it's relatively small while packing powerful audio. The only problem I had may have been due to my TV - when I connected to the Bose over Bluetooth it messed up the hdmi-arc connection and my TV was no longer powering the Bose on and off, I had to factory reset the TV to resolve this and I haven't tried the Bluetooth connection since. Bottom line is that I didn't want to spend more than $200 and I just wanted something that would just work - apparently that is a unicorn in today's age of soundbars - and the Bose TV Speaker is that unicorn

reviews.title: Finally, a simple solution to the madhouse of audio alternatives for television
reviews.body: I had a Bose one piece sound system many years ago. Really enjoyed it. It eventually gave up so I started down the dark hole of soundbars. In about 10 years I've had 3 and with each one there was always something that wouldn't sound right, mainly when someone talks and there's music in the background, only the music that's supposed to hang back instead blares like a foghorn and drowns out the dialogue. I have to admit the last one, a Vizio, soundbar only, no subwoofer or surround speakers, did it's best to keep the dialogue to within reach. It's main issue was it wouldn't cooperate with a Vizio TV, wouldn't maintain a setting if you had the ability to pay it. So, I'm back to the simple Bose TV Speaker. Ya got two settings, bass and dialogue. There are others but they don't involve audio. It plugs into my Vizio TV via HDMI eARC (cable not included), but it does come with an optical cable and I plugged it in but isn't required. ARC allows my TV remote and Fire Stick remote to control the soundbar volume which is the only thing you really need to control once you set the soundbar with it's own remote to be controlled by other devices and the sound setting you like (your choice of two or both at the same time, why not go for it). I can hear music, I can hear voices, I can hear them both at the same time and anyone who says you need a small room to use it in is probably wanting more than the bar can deliver regarding audio. It's plenty loud. Where I sit fairly far from the TV and the room is kind of open concept leading to not open concept, like rooms elsewhere. I can hear it through out the house. Good bass too. Okay I said two settings but the bass actually has 3 levels. The longest portion of the entire setup from unpacking to connection and listening was the unpacking. It's packed pretty well. Good things come in small packages they say, this is one of them. I recommend this to anyone who doesn't require sound bouncing from the holes in their shoes and from the coffee mug sitting beside them. It's a great sounding speaker that removes the requirement of having to take a course or two in sound engineering and makes listening to TV simple and comfortable and enjoyable again, you don't have to constantly change the audio settings to work with the video. It just works.

reviews.title: Big beautiful Bose sound
reviews.body: This is a truly excellent product that fully lives up to expectations. The sound is big and the complexity of setup is small, although to make it work with my older Sharp Aquos TV, which lacks HDMI ARC, I had to buy a dongle — an HDMI audio extractor that pulls the sound out of the main source HDMI and shunts it to an optical jack that can communicate properly with the Bose device using the supplied optical cable. More modern TVs won’t need that. For those whose TV had great video but the audio sucks, this is the cure. It would be worth it for full price but it was nice to get this one as a Prime Day door-buster sale item. I know the days of Bose products being made in Framingham are long gone but this particular item is built in Thailand, which is an ally or something like one. As an ABC shopper I’ll settle for that.

reviews.title: Great sound for the room — simple, reliable upgrade
reviews.body: I picked up the Bose TV Speaker to replace my old CineMate Bose system that finally died, and so far it’s been an excellent, hassle-free replacement. Setup was plug-and-play with my existing Bose TV’s optical out and it started working immediately. I haven’t used the Dialogue Enhancer feature, but even without it the speaker delivers clear, natural-sounding audio that suits my room very well. The unit is compact but sounds bigger than it looks. The bass has respectable weight for such a small speaker — not a home-theatre rumble, but enough to give action scenes and music some presence. The included remote is simple and intuitive, and overall build quality feels solid and understated like other Bose products. Pros: - Smooth setup — truly plug-and-play - Clear, balanced sound that fits the room nicely - Compact footprint; good for smaller living areas or bedrooms - Solid build and easy-to-use remote Cons: - Not a substitute for a full surround system if you want immersive multi-channel audio - Won’t match a dedicated subwoofer for deep bass Would recommend if you want an easy, reliable upgrade from an older compact Bose unit — great for improving everyday TV sound without fuss.

reviews.title: Under $80 Juggernaut (3 speaker battle)
reviews.body: was having a hard time choosing between this, and Oontz angle 3 Pro, and a Doss Soundbox Pro. Im looking for something primarily for the house to be used in a bedroom/office. EVERY SINGLE ONE WAS A WINNER and I wouldnt hesitate to choose any of the 3. Sound quality was very very....VERY comparable with each one and pretty much a wash (explained below). I dont like letting my batteries drain so I cant vouch for battery life on each one, but im not worried. Below is why I would choose each model, hopefully it helps you. Also if it matters, I listened to Radiohead-The National Anthem and Skrillex-Rumble to test the speakers. --Why I chose the Doss Soundbox Pro: I hate to admit it but the price....and I actually chose this one over the Tribit and Oontz after my sound tests. The sound was on par with the other 2 (similar wattage to the Oontz) and I liked this one just a hair more than the Oontz because it was a little crisper sounding where the Oontz was a little fuller...if that makes sense. So with the sound being the same, the fact that I could ALSO pair multiple Doss speakers for a multi speaker set up just like the Oontz (this is a great feature for when entertaining guests/having a small party/get-together), and considering I'd primarily be using this in a bedroom (where the powerbank wouldnt come in as handy like the Oontz has).....I had to choose this one. They dont list the wattage and this had the lowest wattage of the bunch at 10w compared to the other 2 at 20w/21w each.....but it was without a doubt equally as loud as the other two with trebles and bass being on par with the other two. Its not included but they have a bracket mount that clamps on to stuff.......not sure how it would hold up to movement and things like that but there is that option out there. reviews.title: A good unit with many features, and perhaps a tad pricey because of those features
reviews.body: In the world of Bluetooth speakers, this one struck me as a tad pricey, but not overly so. I am hoping for quality of build to let this thing last many years, and we'll see how that works. Meantime, the sound is nice. I use it mostly to listen to podcasts (including podcasts with music) and to stream stuff from Amazon music and Pandora, and the sound quality is OK for me for those purposes. I haven't used the bass emphasis button, finding I don't need that for what I listen to. The lighting feature is amusing, but I keep it off to lengthen battery life. The speakers provide a stereo sound, but I can't really discern a stereo result. Which is OK, I wasn't really expecting much in those regards, considering the speakers are so close to one another. The unit pairs with my iPhone extremely quickly. Haven't had it long enough to assess battery life (which can be a function of volume, use of lighting effects, use of the bass effect, and perhaps the phase of the moon). Overall, it meets my expectations fully and feels like it is well made.

reviews.title: Great little speaker!
reviews.body: This speaker is great. So far the battery life is superb and it gets very loud! I use this speaker in conjunction with a NUX Mighty Plug for guitar on the go. As expected with such a small speaker box the bass isn't extremely powerful but it sounds very crisp and full range if placed in the corner of a room with solid walls. I had a problem with the unit powering itself off at first until I realized it wasn't a low battery but an 'auto-off' feature when not playing anything. Searching this on the web, I didn't find anything on either their website or manual regarding an 'auto-off' feature for this model. Some suggested that DOSS has a firmware update available that disabled it. I spoke through email with a very nice person named Lizzie with their Customer Care team. Lizzie explained that units with the Version ID of VS3582 do not require any firmware updates to enable or disable this feature. If yours is a VS3582 then all you need to do in order to enable/disable the 'auto-off' feature is a button combo of Mode+Power and you'll see if flash red twice for off, green twice for on. Hold the bass button to cycle through lighting options (low, high, off). So far this little speaker has impressed me with what I intended to do with it and all my expectations are met. I am considering a 2nd one for stereo play! Hopefully Lizzie gets a raise soon

reviews.title: Stereopairing, Musik und Licht
reviews.body: VERPACKUNG: Nicht nur durch eine einfache Tüte wird die SoundBox Pro von DOSS geschützt, auch eine auf den Lautsprecher abgestimmte Kunststoffform ist im Karton. Ansonsten noch eine sehr gute Gebrauchsanweisung (auch Deutsch) ein USB A auf Micro USB Kabel und ein 3,5mm Klinke - Klinke Verbindungskabel. DESIGN: Der Lautsprecher ist umlaufend gummiert, an den kurzen Seiten könnte man Leder vermuten, es ist jedoch die Gummierung mit Ledermuster. Die Tasten sind gut erreichbar und haben einen gut spürbaren Druckpunkt. Kleine LEDs geben zusätzliche Info. Auf der Rückseite hinter der Gummideckung befinden sich Micro USB, 3,5mm Klinke und ein Micro SD Karten Anschluss. Vorn schützt ein Gitter die beiden aktiven und passiven Lautsprecher. Umlaufend befindet sich ein Kunststoffrahmen der von LEDs beleuchtet wird, sehr schick. FUNKTION: Vom Klang her ist die SoundBox Pro nicht zu unterschätzen. Die Lautstärke ist ordentlich und der Klang verzerrt minimal bei max Einstellung. Der Bass kommt gut rüber für so eine kleine Box, er ist eher mit einem Kickbass also knackig zu vergleichen. Langes gedröhne bekommt man wenn der Lautsprecher auf einer Unterlage platziert wird die etwas mitschwingen kann, z.B. Holztisch. Durch Equalizer Einstellungen am Handy kann man da aber noch einiges verändern. Das Stereopairing ist eine tolle Funktion die bei mir anstandslos funktioniert hat. Ich konnte keine Verzögerungen erkennen, es tritt auch kein Echo Effekt auf. Die Lichteffekte sind schön vor allem bei einer Gartenparty. Nachts kommen diese am besten zur Geltung. Für mich eine Funktion die sicherlich in einigen Situationen einen tollen Effekt hat (z.B. ruhige Musik abends auf dem Sofa mit pulsierenden LEDs). FAZIT: Ich möchte die Boxen nicht missen bei Kauf von zweien gab es einen Rabatt im Aktionszeitraum. Es macht auf jeden Fall Sinn hier zuzuschlagen und durch das Stereopairing eine tolle Klangkulisse zu schaffen. Sollte Bluetooth Mal nicht die richtige Wahl sein, kann man auch mit 3,5mm Klinge direkt verbinden (für Stereopairing immer mit dem master verbinden) oder alternativ Lieder auf Micro SD.

reviews.body: This is essentially the perfect bluetooth speaker. The sound quality, especially after dialing the EQ, is as good as it gets. Clear bass, sparkling highs, powerful mids. reviews.title: Durable, Great Sound Quality - Worth It
reviews.body: Fantastic speaker—well‑built, durable, and quick to charge. The size is perfect for pool days, parties, or tossing in a bag for travel. I bring it on trips for hotel‑room music, and around the house it never loses connection, even when I’m in another room or out in the backyard. It’s waterproof, so shower use is fair game. It charges via USB‑C, and that same port can top off your phone in a pinch. There’s also an AUX input if you ever need it. Multiple devices can connect via Bluetooth (though that can get chaotic), and it can pair with other Bose speakers. Once you’ve paired your device the first time, it reconnects automatically every time you power it on. Sound Quality: The sound is excellent. You can tweak the EQ in the app, the bass is strong and clean, and this thing gets loud without losing clarity. Treble stays crisp, and overall it’s one of the best‑sounding speakers in its size class. Is it worth the price? I’d say yes. Plenty of speakers check the same boxes, but if you want a bougie speaker that performs - this one is for you.

reviews.title: It brings the bass
reviews.body: As a long-time owner of the first-generation Bose SoundLink Mini, I had high expectations for the Bose SoundLink Max, and it did not disappoint. This review covers various aspects of the speaker, including sound quality, durability, ease of use, compatibility, setup, and design. The SoundLink Max lives up to the Bose name. After testing it with a myriad of musical genres, I was blown away by the fullness of the sound. The bass is so powerful that you can feel it, yet it does not drown out the mid and treble frequencies. It is worth noting that the initial EQ settings are flat, which might be why some users have complained about the lack of fullness. This could be addressed by repurposing the shortcut button for quick EQ adjustment. The SoundLink Max meets the IP67 standards, making it rugged, dustproof, and waterproof. Weighing nearly five pounds, it is heavy, but this is an acceptable trade-off for the durability it offers. In a pinch, you could even use it as a brick or a weapon for defending yourself from zombies! Using the SoundLink Max is straightforward. Press the power button, then play to start enjoying your music. When it’s time to change settings, the buttons are clearly labeled. The Max charges via a supplied USB-C cord and power block and can also serve as a portable power device. This is my main point of contention and it is not specifically with the Max, but with Bose as a whole. They have partnered with Qualcomm/Snapdragon for their HD Audio, which is currently confined to the Android ecosystem. As an iPhone user, I felt a little left out in the cold. Straight out-of-the-box, the Max was nearly ready to go. It took two seconds to pair and less than that to start charging, thanks to the included USB-C cable and power brick. The Bose app was easy to find and quick to install. I was able to set up an account and start using the app right away. While the setup was easy, more emphasis should be placed on the necessity of using the app to achieve the best sound, as the default EQ settings are a bit flat. The SoundLink Max boasts a sleek and simple design. There are no unnecessary lights or reminiscent designs to distract you—just a rugged exterior that protects the speakers while delivering excellent sound quality. The rope handle is a nice feature that accentuates the rugged yet simple design. They are easily changeable for other colored handles and shoulder straps, which are available at a steep premium on the Bose website. The Bose SoundLink Max is a phenomenal portable speaker that lives up to the high standards we expect from Bose. After several days of testing in various locations and with different music genres, I have not been disappointed. While there have been some reports of less-than-fantastic sound quality, this issue is easily resolved by adjusting the EQ settings in the Bose app. The final question is, is the SoundLink Max worth the $400 price tag? The simple answer is yes, it is worth every penny.

reviews.title: Sounds like a box of farts, and not in a good way. Maybe it is broken?
reviews.body: When I first unpacked this product and listened to it, I was completely won over. What an amazing first impression. Excellent soundstage. Wide, detailed, clear, everything you could want. Unfortunately, once you take the volume to even close to 50%, which you'd want to do in many situations and certainly outside, and it all falls apart. Hero to zero in the blink of an eye. The bass has a fart-like quality to it which ruins everything. The only way to make this sound acceptable is to use the EQ to take the bass pretty much to nothing or even a negative setting. In which case, you could buy almost any other Bluetooth speaker for less than half the price that is going to sound just as good. Many of the reviews talk about bass and presence, but that's only true at really low levels. At least assuming the unit I was sent is working to factory spec. And don't get me wrong, I'm not listening to music at window rattling levels designed to annoy the neighbors. I'm not even listening to tracks that I think are especially bass heavy. As an example I listened to Clocks by Coldplay. Hardly a hardcore bass fest. The opening bars sounded amazing. But as soon as the gentle bass chords joined the music, the speaker lost itself. I tried the product on a hard wooden stool. A hard wooden deck. A patio table. A different patio table. A few feet away. A few meters away. It really didn't matter. I played with numerous EQ settings. But the bottom line is that it just can't put out bass in any real capacity unless you are willing to lower the sound to a background volume. In which case, it's amazing. To me, the bass being available in such a quiet and tiny sweet spot, makes it kind of worthless to include it at all. I have a pair of B&O Explore speakers, that sound amazing and can be set as a stereo pair. If you buy them well you can have two of them for $100 less than this Bose. What they lack in bass, they more than make up for in incredible sound stage, stereo separation and can go toe to toe in terms of detail. The thing is, they also KNOW they can't do much bass, so they don't even try. Bose, is trying too hard to make bass happen that apparently isn't possible in this system. Just like I don't drive my car at 100 mph ever, I want it to be capable of that. I want it to accelerate from zero to sixty in under seven seconds, even though it's not how I drive. And when it comes to speakers, I want to know that if I want to turn up the volume a little, it isn't going to sound like a box of farts. I tried to give it every opportunity to impress, but it failed at everything except very quiet listening levels. I was mainly streaming from Apple Music, and I even looked for songs offered at their highest bitrate or including spacial audio technology. For the price they are charging, there is no way I keep this item. It is already in the box ready to go to UPS. Maybe it would be different if you have a different sound source, are using a different streaming service, are using AUX or Android. My tests were iOS based, and bluetooth streaming. Tracks that I have previously tested on my Marshall Woburn II speaker as an example, with the same source equipment.

reviews.title: Great Sounding Speaker ... If You Are Patient
reviews.body: *FIRST IMPRESSIONS: Listening to music as it comes out of the box, I had two impressions,something is missing from the music and what is that painful squeael in the treble area. while they may sound bad out of the box, the hardware is capable of greatness with the right tweaks. The rest of this review provides information about the basic setup and configuration of these speakers and what needs to be done to improve the sound. * PROS: Sound great; full spectrum with clear highs and lows, but takes work to bring it out. In fact, for the best sound, you'll need an equalizer. Once equalization has been applied, they can have the clarity found in a pair of much higher priced speakers; they have great lows, but can't match the 28Hz lows of the Cerwin Vega D-9s but the highs are reasonably close. Fairly easy to pair with another speaker but see below. * CONS: All detailed below with solutions: 1. Out of the box, it sounds much worse than it actually is. The default equalization was for marketing. The bass is pushed up 4 dB, the midrange down 2 dB and the highs up 5 dB. This may be impressive for a short time, but you may eventually be dissatisfied as the center has been cut out of the music and you'll cringe at the outlandish scream at 6.3 kHz. 2. Connecting to the Bose app involves an overlooked step, Bose should fix this. 3. Interconnecting speakers as a stereo pair is a bit tricky. 4. Serious power management problem which Bose should also fix. 5. Most buttons lack tactile icons for the visually impaired, but they are easy to find and count. For this device, there are six buttons arranged in a single horizontal row on the top front from left to right as follows: (1) power, (2) Bluetooth, (3) link, (4) Volume down, (5) Play/Pause, and (6) Volume up. Note that the function of the Play/Pause button may be affected by your music player and bluetooth configuration. Now for the details: * SETUP: - Connecting To The Bose App: It is hard to get The Bose app connected so you can take advantage of built-in features. This complaint appears often on the Google Playstore. - Getting Into The Configuration App: Download and install the Bose app from the web; it is in android and Apple download sites as well as the Bose web site. For best results, connect your phone to the speaker via bluetooth. Open the app and follow instructions until you get to a page that ought to be showing your device name and which contains the "Add Device" link. * NOTE: Before clicking this link be certain that notifications are enabled on your phone and that you will be alerted when a new notification arrives. Note to Bose, this ought to be stated on that page as a reminder to users. Assuming it has the right device, click the "Add Device" link. You will almost instantaneously get a notification. Open it and click the "Pair" link in that notification. If you are too late or something else happens, go back to that add device link and try again. * CONFIGURING THE SPEAKER: There are two areas of interest in the Bose app, one allows you to make some adjustments to the equalization for the speaker. The other allows you to control automatic power down parameters. - The Built In Equalizer: The built in equalizer has only three frequency bands for you to deal with, the bass, midrange and the treble. By default, these bands are set for marketing impact, to impress casual shoppers with the amazing highs and lows this speaker can produce, but you may find music reproduction very disappointing. If you want this primarily as a portable speaker, use the equalizer controls to produce a sound more to your liking. However, this won't clean up the sharp power spike at 6.3kHz., for that, an external equalizer is required. - Correcting The Frequency Response: If you have an Equalizer on your phone or computer, that equalizer will be far better than the one built into the speaker. Suggested Equalizations are given below. * POWER MANAGEMENT SETTING: Disguised as a profile area is the settings area (top right corner of the apps home page. The primary area of concern is the power setting. By default it is set to automatic. That means the speaker will turn off after 12 hours, even if plugged in. This is a battery safety feature. However, if you're using the speaker at home and have it always plugged in, you can set it to "Never," but be aware that this could be a problem if your power fails for you take it with you and fail to power it down first, the result could be a drained and if it goes long enough, damaged battery. The risk is yours, balance that risk against your convenience. Note to Bose, you should disregard the power down parameter if the speaker is plugged in. I consider not doing so a major engineering defect on your part especially as it could lead to battery problems. NOTE: Keep in mind Listening at high volumes or with very heavy bass will eventually cause the unit to shut down, even while plugged in. Also, under those conditions, the discharge time on full batteries without being plugged in is only three hours. To completely recharge the batteries after a shutdown will take about 5 hours. Recharge time from shutdown can take far longer if you try to turn it on again after a shutdown. * Personalizing The Sound: First, be aware that we all have different preferences in how music sounds, but here is what I did. I am using Equalizer APO on windows, but there are several similar apps for Android phones - Wavelet, Poweramp Equalizer, Echo Equalizer). For Mac users, you can achieve these same results using SoundSource (with an AU plugin) or the 'Expert' mode in eqMac. Unfortunately, iPhone users will have to buy and setup a dongle (an external Bluetooth transmitter with built-in DSP). to apply equalization parameters and transmit the sound via bluetooth. - Equalization Suggestions: The Bose Digital Signal Processor (DSP) is always active. It generally acts like the loudness contour in older amplifiers. It greatly increases the bass at low volumes and reduces the bass amplification as volume increases. It is also intended to produce the "Bose Sound" that is "full, meaning exagerated lows and highs." The response curves and filter/equalization settings below assume moderate volume. They work against the built in DSP settings to extend the frequency range where the response is considered "flat," that is, the range in which the volume stays between + or - 3dB. That is the normal standard for top grade amplifiers and speakers to ensure that you hear the music as intended by the artists who produced it. The following is the list of frequency and power level, in dB that I'm using to correct the factory tuning and achieve a more balanced, high-fidelity sound. I found the following frequency adjustments to be effective. These values help neutralize the sharp spikes and restore the midrange that is missing out of the box. NOTE: These values assume the default Bose equalization has not been changed. If you have altered them and don’t remember what they were, you can do a full reset on the speaker to put it back into factory configuration. This requires a very long simultaneous press of the volume up and volume down buttons. The Bose will eventually respond with a burp. - Equalization Suggestions: Preamp: -3.0 dB For Copy/Paste (Equalizer APO,) copy the following line exactly as written into your config file: GraphicEQ: 100 -2; 250 -3; 630 2; 1000 3.5; 1600 2.5; 4000 -3; 6300 -6; 10000 -4; 16000 -2 For Manual Entry (Mobile Apps & Screen Readers): 100 -2 250 -3 630 2 1000 3.5 1600 2.5 4000 -3 6300 -6 10000 -4 16000 -2 - Alternative Approach - Filters If the program you choose for the frequency corrections has the capability of specifying filter points, a more surgical approach, you might consider these filter specifications: Filter Set 1: Preamp: -3.0 dB Filter 1: ON PK Fc 100 Hz Gain -1.5 dB Q 1.0 Filter 2: ON PK Fc 250 Hz Gain -2.5 dB Q 1.5 Filter 3: ON PK Fc 1000 Hz Gain 2.0 dB Q 1.0 Filter 4: ON PK Fc 2500 Hz Gain 1.5 dB Q 2.0 Filter 5: ON PK Fc 4500 Hz Gain -1.5 dB Q 2.0 Filter 6: ON PK Fc 6300 Hz Gain -5.0 dB Q 3.0 Filter 7: ON HS Fc 10000 Hz Gain -1.0 dB -Alternative Filter Set: Filter set 2 In the following, the lines with the # sign are comments. They are the settings recommended on the internet, I found them to give a booming bass, so I substituted the lines that are not commented out. Make your own choice. Preamp: -6.5 dB #Filter 1: ON PK Fc 100 Hz Gain -1.5 dB Q 1.0 #Filter 2: ON PK Fc 250 Hz Gain -2.5 dB Q 1.5 Filter 1: ON PK Fc 100 Hz Gain -3.5 dB Q 1.0 Filter 2: ON PK Fc 250 Hz Gain -4.5 dB Q 1.5 Filter 3: ON PK Fc 1000 Hz Gain 2.0 dB Q 1.0 Filter 4: ON PK Fc 2500 Hz Gain 1.5 dB Q 2.0 Filter 5: ON PK Fc 4000 Hz Gain -3.0 dB Q 1.5 Filter 6: ON PK Fc 6300 Hz Gain -6.0 dB Q 3.0 Filter 7: ON PK Fc 10000 Hz Gain -4.0 dB Q 2.0 Filter 8: ON HS Fc 13000 Hz Gain 4.5 dB * A comparison of frequency response curves: Bose out of the box: Effective Range +/- 6dB; 60 Hertz to 14,000 Hertz • Using the Equalizer settings: Effective range +/- 3dB;110 Hertz to 5,000 Hertz., limited by that massive cut at 6.3 kHz. Using the first Filter settings: Effective range +/- 2.5dB; 55 Hertz to 15,500 Hertz. Using Filter settings #2: Effective range +/- 3dB; 52 Hz to 16,500 Hz Clearly, the filter settings are the winner. feel free to adjust the equalization values to your own satisfaction, and if you feel the need, you can supply intermediate values. If you increase the power too much, and get distortion from clipping, reduce the preamp value. * Making A Stereo Pair: This area is considered to be a bit flakey, perhaps because people forget critical details or their timing is a bit off. so be prepared to repeat if required. To make a stereo pair. On the speaker you want as the left speaker, do a long press and then a quick second press of the third button from the left (the Shortcut/Link button). After the speaker tells you to do so, do a single quick press of the third button from the left on the second speaker, this will be the right speaker. Be patient, the speakers takes longer than one would expect to respond to the button presses on each speaker; allow 30 to 45 seconds for each speaker. As a side note on volume, I normally listen to these speakers from 20 feet away with the volume set at 55%, so they have sufficient power to fill a large room. * Final Verdict: If you want a "plug and play" perfect experience, this might frustrate you. But if you are willing to spend 10 minutes in the settings and Equalizer , it is likely the best-sounding speaker in its size class.

reviews.title: Outstanding Sound
reviews.body: If there were two ratings, one for the speaker and one for the Seller (Amazon), Speaker gets 5 Stars and Amazon gets 2 Stars. The speaker doesn't deserve a low rating due to Amazon. I watched a lot of reviews and had a hard time to decide between JBL or Bose, only because of the Bose price. I already have 2 Bose Soundtouch 300s and 1 Bose Wave Sountouch, so I already knew the rich sound Bose puts out. Because of the sound quality of my previous Bose I figured I would take a chance on the Pricey Bose Soundlink Max. Before I go any further, I do need to say first, Amazon should be ashamed of themselves, selling OPEN BOX for BRAND NEW. I don't believe this is the fault of Bose, it is Amazon Re-Selling their returns, as I bought 2 Bose Soundlink Max's "Shipped by Amazon" and both were OPEN BOX which was not stated in the selling add. They were at a good sale price, but i dislike not being told they were OPEN BOX, especially when paying close to $400 CAD for 1 speaker. Even though the speakers are outstanding I am thinking of returning both speakers due to this unless Amazon can do something about it. 90% of my purchases are through Amazon, and having this done disgusts me. Back to the Bose Soundlink Max. This review is based on only one evening of trial. For starters I had no issues with the bluetooth, it was very easy to connect both my Samsung phone and Samsung tablet, and that was without the Bose App installed. Once I was linked, I started playing all types of music. Pop, Dance, Rock etc, and with a bit of bit of fine tuning with the built in EQ on Samsung, this little speaker fills the room with such amazing rich sound. I read a review once where it said this speaker sounds great out of the box. It sounds ok, but tune an EQ on it and it is amazing. I would shut the EQ off and On while playing and listening to this speaker through an EQ makes a world of difference, which BTW would be the same with any speaker. The build of the speaker is very nice. Does not have a cheap plastic feel. A good portion of the speaker has a grippy silicone feel. The weight of the speaker alone tells a lot about the build Quality, Not too heavy, but also not too light, its very solid. The carry handle is very sturdy and well connected as well. I still need to try the linking feature between the two speakers. Will update soon

reviews.title: Powerful, Personal, Portable Flex Speaker
reviews.body: The Bose SoundLink Flex 2nd Gen speaker is hands down my favorite bluetooth speaker, though I do own the latest Beats Pill and love it for its capabilities. At present, I own eight of these 2nd Gen Flex speakers, one in each color variant. I do find that audiobooks, podcasts and spoken content sound best on the 2nd Gen Flex. Most Music does as well. Some reviewers report sound differences between the color variants. After initially suspecting this and repeatedly comparing the identical audio on each speaker, I found that the most likely explanation is how one is holding the speaker when audio is playing, as the audio does change based on the position of the speaker. Features I would like to see in the 3rd Gen model include: Much longer battery life. The technology and capabilities exist. The speaker is so excellent that paying a little more for much longer battery life, perhaps double, would be worth it. Lossless ability. When connecting the latest Bose Ultra headphones and even the Beats Pill to my iPhone with the Usb C to Usb C cables, each offer lossless streaming. The ability to connect the Flex to a CD player or some other audio device via the cable. There are Usb C to 3.5mm male and female cables on the market and this would be nice as I still have a small Bose CD player and plenty of CDs. While there are bluetooth transmitters such as the AirFly which make connectivity possible, direct wired connectivity is still nice for some of us. A detachable strap. The Beats Pill and the most excellent Bose SoundLink Micro 2nd Gen both offer a detachable strap. This would be a nice option for the Flex in the future. Pairing four Flex speakers in surround sound mode. While two Flex speakers are great in stereo, pairing four for surround sound would be next level great. The ability to change the volume of the obnoxious sounds the Flex puts out. I do like these sounds, particularly when the speaker connects to bluetooth. However, these are way too loud. The Beats Pill has the option of controlling the volume of its sounds. The same is true for the voice prompts. While some of the voice prompts can be disabled in the app, the volume cannot be changed. Even without these potential additions to a 3rd Gen Flex, this existing 2nd Gen Flex is a phenomenal bluetooth speaker that serves many purposes. The Alpine Sage color variant has been discontinued, as it was limited. However, the existing color options are excellent, particularly the Twilight Blue. Although the Flex and Beats Pill are both excellent and come down to personal preference when selecting one or the other, I would also go with the Flex if I did not have the luxury of owning both. In fact, I would go with the Flex over any other, even if it has yet to fulfill all its potential, which with the suggestions I mentioned for the 3rd Gen Flex, it would be an untouchable speaker. Highly recommend the 2nd Gen Flex to all reading this.

reviews.title: Decent quality blades that are easy to keep sharp
reviews.body: The steel is arguably soft, but that is typical of european (particularly german) blades. The iron content of this stainless steel is high and the nickel content may be low. If left wet for long, it may develop rust spots. However, you should always clean and dry a knife after using it anyway. If taken care of, these blades will last many years. They will cut what you want and retain a nice shape. The chef's knife is great. It is the primary knife used in my kitchen. It is comfortable to use, slices through most anything with relative ease. After about ten to fifteen diced onions I like to hone the blade again to keep work quick and easy. A dull knife is much more dangerous than a sharp one they say. Despite frequent maintenance, it does an excellent job and doesn't fatigue me. The santokus are of decent quality, and feel excellent for everyday tasks. The larger one has a good weight and feeling allowing for prolonged veggie extermination, and the smaller one is light and maneuverable to really slice and shape whatever you need. The paring knife is a razor blade with a handle basically. If the chef knife is too big or unwieldy for a task, the lil guy will step up with no issue. The bread knife is sharp. It WILL cut bread. Cake too, I bet. There is another smaller serrated knife but I have yet to use it. The scissors are nothing special but provide you something to open any package of food. The steak knives are beautiful but have lesser quality steel than the bigger knives. These will straight up form rust spots if left in the sink overnight, esp along the handle and spine of the blade. reviews.title: A perfect addition to my kitchen
reviews.body: While visiting my sister, I used her set of Cuisinart knifes. She place the time of purchase somewhere between 5 and 7 years, and they were wonderful. Easy to handle, not to heavy, and a great variety of knives for cutting different types of foods. The steak knives are the best I have ever used, the Santoku (the blade is wide in height and snub nosed) cut a left over roast into very, very thin slices for hot roast beef sandwiches. In early July, I purchased the Classic Forged Triple Riveted set of 15 knives and the block, because the set held most of the knives I was looking for and they fit right into my kitchen décor. And, my struggle of 59 years in my kitchen, trying to cut vegetables, fruits, meats and breads and struggling with knives has come to an end. It is such a mental and physical relieve to start a meal knowing that cutting "whatever" will no longer be a struggle. My new knives are the best I have ever purchased and I have purchased a lot of knives. Wish I had know a long time ago about Cuisinart knives, didn't know that they made anything but electric appliances for the kitchen. A little bit of a down side, be prepared for a larger than normal knife holding block, and it is heavy, but again the length of the knives make it necessary and are worth the block size and weight. Would I recommend them to my best friend.....in a heart beat! But...would I purchase this set again, no, but I would purchase the solid metal handle set, as the paring knife handle has cracked from the rivet to the edge of the handle. I care for my knives, I hand wash and dry them and put them away, I am concerned that if one handle cracks after a month and a half of use, how long before another on cracks. Overall, I would have given this set of knives a 5 star except for the cracked handle.

reviews.body: This is a very nice mid-range kitchen knife set. The steel used is actually named and is a good solid stainless steel that's a good balance for a set like this. The handles are beautiful and look high-end. The only thing I find a little odd is the scissors. The little swivel lock fell out and the spring disappeared somewhere in the kitchen within the first week of use. They still work OK but seem a bit over-complicated for kitchen scissors. They blades are very sharp out of box - so be careful. A little warning for you all if you get these - and I'm embarrassed to even discuss this: When you fill the knife block with the knives - make sure the sharp side of the big knives are all turned to the middle of the block. Otherwise - the sharp end hangs out over the edge of the block and is a significant danger. I loaded the knives without thinking about that and reached around the block at one point and got the top of my right thumb with the heal of one of the big knives that I loaded backwards. It got me good. I'll always have a scar there now. It was stupid and completely my mistake - so don't do the same thing. Be careful. the only blades that shouldn't have the sharp end pointing to the middle of the block would be the steak knives at the bottom. Those can be loaded with the sharp end down. The block will cover the apex just fine when loaded that way. Anyhow - I would recommend this set. Check the price history because the price does seem to bounce around a bit. It's a great deal when the price is down.

First impressions & design: Right out of the box, the presentation is clean and modern. The block itself has a polished, minimalist look that actually elevates the countertop instead of cluttering it. The knives have a uniform, well-balanced design with a comfortable grip and a subtle weight that feels intentional—not cheap or flimsy. Performance & functionality: This is where the set really stands out. Every knife comes razor-sharp and ready to go—no need for immediate honing or sharpening. From slicing meats to dicing vegetables and even more delicate work like herbs or soft fruits, each blade performs consistently and cleanly. The chef’s knife in particular handles like a workhorse, while the smaller utility and paring knives offer great control for precision tasks. The variety in the set is also practical—not just filler pieces. Each knife actually has a purpose, and you find yourself using more of them than expected instead of defaulting to just one or two. Build quality & usability: The balance is excellent—there’s a solid feel in the hand without being overly heavy, which makes longer prep sessions much easier. Handles are ergonomic and don’t slip, even when wet. The blades hold their edge well so far, and maintenance has been straightforward. Everyday use: This set transitions effortlessly from quick meal prep to more involved cooking sessions. It’s reliable, sharp, and visually appealing—exactly what you want sitting out in your kitchen daily. Final verdict: For the price point, this set punches well above its weight. It delivers on aesthetics, performance, and practicality without cutting corners. Whether you’re upgrading from a basic set or starting fresh, this is a solid investment that actually feels like one. Highly recommend.

I am hand washing mine as I want the gold to stay fresh looking for years to come. But they are nicely made with a quality finish, and I do believe they would hold up fine in the dishwasher. The blade thickness for the price is quite impressive. In all honesty, I bought this set for the way it looked. My kitchen is very gold heavy on decor. But...I ended up being very surprised at the quality of the set for the price I paid. I own much more expensive knives, the workhorses you hide away in the drawers because they aren't aesthetically pleasing, but these are performing way above my expectations and feel as if they will have some real durability for some time to come. reviews.title: I received a damaged, recirculated returned item :(
reviews.body: I must’ve received the same set that’s been returned over and over again. Rather than continuing to recirculate a clearly defective return, why not send out a new, quality item? I purchased the green set, and as several other reviewers have mentioned, the color is not really Sage green—it’s much closer to avocado, although not quite that bright. More importantly, the oxidation and chipping on the gold metallic parts are very noticeable and simply shouldn’t be present on an item being sold as “new.” At a discounted price, this might be a reasonable thrift-store purchase. The actual steel quality seemed decent for a Chinese-made set, although the handles felt somewhat plasticky. That said, these obviously aren’t top-of-the-line pieces, so I wasn’t expecting premium construction. Ultimately, my main issue isn’t necessarily with the Martha Stewart brand itself, but with this particular vendor.

title: Cuisinart 15-Piece Stainless Steel Hollow Handle Block Set, C77SS-15PK

reviews.title: Sharp, Complete Set, and Looks Great on the Counter
reviews.body: I bought this Cuisinart 15-piece knife set because I wanted one complete set instead of having random knives from different brands taking over the kitchen drawer. The stainless steel design looks clean and modern, and the wooden block keeps everything organized and easy to reach. I also like that the set includes the sharpening steel and kitchen shears, so it covers more than just the basic knives. The knives feel balanced in the hand and came sharp enough for everyday prep like slicing vegetables, cutting meat, and handling general kitchen work. I definitely recommend using the sharpening steel regularly because even good knives need a little maintenance. The biggest improvement for me is organization. Now I actually know where the knife I need is instead of opening a drawer that looks like a culinary junkyard. 😂 Overall, a very complete, attractive, and practical knife set for everyday cooking.

reviews.title: I LOVE THESE KNIVES!! **UPDATE**
reviews.body: **it has been 3 wonderful years with these knives and they're still as sharp as the day they arrived! I have had no need to have them sharpened, and honestly, I still have no complaints. They. Are. AMAZING. I can't say enough good things about these knives. I recently moved into a new house and of course needed to upgrade some items. First on my list was a good knife set since I'm a avid cooker. Despite some bad reviews, I went ahead and ordered these. First things first; they are SHARP. I can only cut with one hand and these bad boys slice through tomatoes like nobody's business. One handed cutters dream!! Second, they are GORGEOUS. I am beyond proud of displaying them. Third, they have a wonderful balance to them. They are durable, there is nothing flimsy about them!! I have had several knife sets, but these are my absolute favourite!! Some people were complaining about them rusting, and fair, that COULD happen. But if treated right, they wont do that. My number one rule is these do NOT go in the dishwasher. In certain circumstances, they don't even see soap. They are washed immediately after use, thoroughly dried, and returned to the block. Should spots appear, I use stainless steel cleaner. They are still as beautiful as the day I took them out of the box. They also have required no sharpening since I got them. If stored and taken care of PROPERLY, these knives will never need replaced. They are every bit what I had hoped for and worth every penny spent. I highly recommend them to anyone who asks and even to those who don't!!! If you want knives you don't care about or you'll throw in the dishwasher, these are not for you. Take care of your knives, love them, respect them, and they will deliver excellent performance time and time again.

reviews.title: Excellent All‑Steel Knives That Perform Better Than Expected!!
reviews.body: I’ve owned several Cuisinart knives over the years, and this all–stainless steel set is definitely one of their winners. Each knife is forged from a single piece of steel, giving them a sleek, modern look and a sturdy feel. I’ll admit when I first saw the stainless steel handles, I assumed they would be slippery, especially when chopping veggies. Luckily, that wasn’t the case at all. They’re surprisingly comfortable, well‑balanced, and offer a secure grip even during longer prep sessions. The standout for me is the 7” Santoku knife (C77SS-7SAN-25K). It’s a Japanese style incredibly sharp, solidly built, and the longer blade length gives you great control. If you’re used to a 5" Santoku, it may feel a bit heavier and may take a little bit of getting used to, but once you do, it’s hard to go back. Like the rest of the knives in the set, this one arrives razor‑sharp and stays that way as long as you care for it properly. My next best favorite is the western style Chef's knife (C77SS-CF-25K) which is what most folks like including the chefs as it allows to cut a wide variety of vegetables and fruits. It has a curved edge("belly") with a pointed tip. My Third favorite cutting knife is the Slicing Knife (C77SS-SL-25K) which is specifically useful for slicing large cuts of either cooked meat or fish. It has a long, narrow blade with a pointed tip. I found this to be useful for cutting larger fruits like Watermelon, Melons or gourds etc. as the longer blade allows you to cut/slice them their vertical length. To keep these knives in top shape, here are a few care tips I personally follow: Use the right cutting surface: Stick to wood or plastic cutting boards. Harder surfaces like glass, stone, or metal will dull the blade quickly. Hand‑wash only: Clean with warm, soapy water and dry immediately with a soft cloth. Make sure the knife is completely dry before storing it. Avoid scraping with the sharp edge: If you need to move chopped ingredients, flip the knife over and use the back of the blade or a scraper. Store properly: Always use the included sheath. Storing knives loose in a drawer can damage the edge and create a safety hazard. If you follow these simple steps, these knives will stay sharp and serve you well for a long time. Overall, this is a great quality set that delivers excellent value and performance. Highly recommend!
